## button

### Notes and edge cases

- Zag ships no button machine: the closest things are the standalone `toggle` machine (a `type="button"` root with `aria-pressed`) and the per-component triggers, each of which sets `type="button"` explicitly rather than relying on a shared button primitive. (zag: packages/machines/toggle/src/toggle.connect.ts)
- Ark's button equivalent is the polymorphic `ark.button` produced by its factory, so button behavior is tested as factory and asChild behavior rather than as a component. (ark: packages/react/src/components/factory.test.tsx)
- Every trigger-like part across the machines sets `type="button"` (dialog, popover, menu, select, combobox trigger and clear-trigger, date-picker view and nav triggers, carousel controls, toast close and action triggers, tour action triggers, file-upload trigger, color-picker swatch, eyedropper and format triggers, number-input spinners, qr-code download trigger, timer action triggers, clipboard trigger, editable edit, submit and cancel triggers), which is the de facto button contract in this codebase. (zag: packages/machines/dialog/src/dialog.connect.ts; zag: packages/machines/number-input/src/number-input.connect.ts; zag: packages/machines/color-picker/src/color-picker.connect.ts)

## checkbox

### Roles and attributes

- Anatomy parts are root, label, control, indicator; every part element carries `data-scope="checkbox"` and `data-part="<part>"`. (zag: packages/machines/checkbox/src/checkbox.anatomy.ts)
- Root, label, control and indicator all receive the same state attribute block: `data-active`, `data-focus`, `data-focus-visible`, `data-readonly`, `data-hover`, `data-disabled`, `data-invalid`, `data-required`, and `data-state` with value `indeterminate`, `checked` or `unchecked`. (zag: packages/machines/checkbox/src/checkbox.connect.ts)
- The control part is `aria-hidden="true"` because the hidden native input carries the semantics. (zag: packages/machines/checkbox/src/checkbox.connect.ts)
- The indicator part is `hidden` whenever the checkbox is neither indeterminate nor checked. (zag: packages/machines/checkbox/src/checkbox.connect.ts)
- The hidden input is `type="checkbox"`, gets `aria-labelledby` pointing at the label id and `aria-invalid` from the invalid prop. (zag: packages/machines/checkbox/src/checkbox.connect.ts)
- Given the basic checkbox, when it is clicked, then `data-state="checked"` appears simultaneously on root, label and control. (zag: e2e/checkbox.e2e.ts: "should be checked when clicked")
- Given a checkbox rendered with `checked="indeterminate"`, then the control part has `data-state="indeterminate"`. (ark: packages/react/src/components/checkbox/tests/checkbox.test.tsx: "should handle indeterminate state properly"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/checkbox/tests/checkbox.test.tsx: "should handle indeterminate state properly"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/checkbox/tests/checkbox.test.ts: "should handle indeterminate state from example")

### Keyboard

- Given the hidden input is focused via Tab, when Space is pressed, then the checkbox becomes checked. (zag: e2e/checkbox.e2e.ts: "should be checked when spacebar is pressed while focused")

### Pointer

- Given a checkbox, when the root is clicked, then it toggles to checked. (zag: e2e/checkbox.e2e.ts: "should be checked when clicked")
- Given a checkbox with an onCheckedChange handler, when the label text is clicked, then the handler fires with `{ checked: true }`. (ark: packages/react/src/components/checkbox/tests/checkbox.test.tsx: "should invoke onCheckedChange")
- Given a Solid checkbox, when the control is clicked twice, then onCheckedChange fires with `{ checked: true }` and then `{ checked: false }` (Solid asserts the round trip that React only asserts one way). (ark: packages/solid/src/components/checkbox/tests/checkbox.test.tsx: "should invoke onCheckedChange")

### Focus management

- Given the page body is clicked first, when Tab is pressed, then the hidden input is focused and the control gets `data-focus=""`. (zag: e2e/checkbox.e2e.ts: "should be focused when page is tabbed")
- Given a disabled checkbox, when Tab is pressed, then the hidden input is not focused. (zag: e2e/checkbox.e2e.ts: "should not be focusable when disabled")
- Given a blur listener on the hidden input, when the label is clicked three times, then zero blur events fire, so label clicks never move focus off the input. (zag: e2e/checkbox.e2e.ts: "input is not blurred on label click")
- Given a checkbox inside Field.Root, when the field label is clicked, then the checkbox input receives focus. (ark: packages/react/src/components/checkbox/tests/checkbox.test.tsx: "should focus on input when label is clicked"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/checkbox/tests/checkbox.test.tsx: "should focus on input when label is clicked"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/checkbox/tests/checkbox.test.ts: "should focus on input when label is clicked")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given a controlled checkbox whose checked state lives in the host component, when an external "set checked" button is clicked, then the checkbox reflects checked. (ark: packages/react/src/components/checkbox/tests/checkbox.test.tsx: "should allow controlled usage"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/checkbox/tests/checkbox.test.tsx: "should allow controlled usage"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/checkbox/tests/checkbox.test.ts: "should allow controlled usage")
- In Vue the controlled fixture wires `ref` + `useForwardPropsEmits(props, emits)` and asserts synchronously after the click, where React and Solid wrap the assertion in `waitFor`. (ark: packages/vue/src/components/checkbox/tests/controlled-checkbox.test.vue)

### Forms

- Given a checkbox, when clicked, then the native `role="checkbox"` element reports checked to assistive tech and to `toBeChecked`. (ark: packages/react/src/components/checkbox/tests/checkbox.test.tsx: "should handle check and unchecked"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/checkbox/tests/checkbox.test.tsx: "should handle check and unchecked"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/checkbox/tests/checkbox.test.ts: "should handle check and unchecked")
- Given a disabled checkbox, then the hidden input is disabled. (zag: e2e/checkbox.e2e.ts: "should have disabled attributes when disabled")
- Given a checkbox inside a required Field, then the input is required. (ark: packages/react/src/components/checkbox/tests/checkbox.test.tsx: "should set checkbox as required"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/checkbox/tests/checkbox.test.tsx: "should set checkbox as required"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/checkbox/tests/checkbox.test.ts: "should set checkbox as required")
- Given a checkbox inside a disabled Field, then the input is disabled. (ark: packages/react/src/components/checkbox/tests/checkbox.test.tsx: "should set input as disabled"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/checkbox/tests/checkbox.test.tsx: "should set input as disabled"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/checkbox/tests/checkbox.test.ts: "should set input as disabled")
- Given a checkbox inside a readOnly Field, then the label carries `data-readonly`. (ark: packages/react/src/components/checkbox/tests/checkbox.test.tsx: "should set input as readonly"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/checkbox/tests/checkbox.test.tsx: "should set input as readonly"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/checkbox/tests/checkbox.test.ts: "should set input as readonly")
- Given a checkbox inside Field.Root, then Field.HelperText renders its text. (ark: packages/react/src/components/checkbox/tests/checkbox.test.tsx: "should display helper text"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/checkbox/tests/checkbox.test.tsx: "should display helper text"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/checkbox/tests/checkbox.test.ts: "should display helper text")
- Given a checkbox inside an invalid Field, then Field.ErrorText is rendered. (ark: packages/react/src/components/checkbox/tests/checkbox.test.tsx: "should display error text when error is present"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/checkbox/tests/checkbox.test.tsx: "should display error text when error is present"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/checkbox/tests/checkbox.test.ts: "should display error text when error is present")
- Given a checkbox inside a valid Field, then Field.ErrorText is absent from the DOM. (ark: packages/react/src/components/checkbox/tests/checkbox.test.tsx: "should not display error text when no error is present"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/checkbox/tests/checkbox.test.tsx: "should not display error text when no error is present"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/checkbox/tests/checkbox.test.ts: "should not display error text when no error is present")
- Given a Checkbox.Group with one disabled member, then only that member's input is disabled and its siblings stay enabled. (ark: packages/react/src/components/checkbox/tests/checkbox.test.tsx: "should allow individual checkbox to be disabled"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/checkbox/tests/checkbox.test.tsx: "should allow individual checkbox to be disabled"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/checkbox/tests/checkbox.test.ts: "should allow individual checkbox to be disabled")

### Accessibility tooling

- Given the basic checkbox, when axe runs over `[data-part=root]` with color-contrast disabled, then there are no violations. (zag: e2e/checkbox.e2e.ts: "should have no accessibility violation")
- Given the React checkbox example, when axe runs over the rendered container, then there are no violations. (ark: packages/react/src/components/checkbox/tests/checkbox.test.tsx: "should have no a11y violations")

## switch

### Roles and attributes

- Anatomy parts are root, label, control, thumb. (zag: packages/machines/switch/src/switch.anatomy.ts)
- Root, label, control and thumb receive `data-active`, `data-focus`, `data-focus-visible`, `data-readonly`, `data-hover`, `data-disabled`, `data-invalid`, `data-required` and `data-state` of `checked` or `unchecked` - the switch has no indeterminate state. (zag: packages/machines/switch/src/switch.connect.ts)
- Control and thumb are both `aria-hidden="true"`; the hidden input is `type="checkbox"` with `aria-labelledby` on the label id and `aria-invalid`. (zag: packages/machines/switch/src/switch.connect.ts)

### Keyboard

- Given the switch input is focused, when Space is pressed, then the switch becomes checked. (zag: e2e/switch.e2e.ts: "should be checked when spacebar is pressed while focused")

### Pointer

- Given a switch, when the root is clicked, then the input is checked. (zag: e2e/switch.e2e.ts: "should be checked when clicked")
- Given a switch with onCheckedChange, when the label is clicked, then the callback fires with `{ checked: true }`. (ark: packages/react/src/components/switch/tests/switch.test.tsx: "should toggle state when clicked"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/switch/tests/switch.test.tsx: "should toggle state when clicked"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/switch/tests/switch.test.ts: "should toggle state when clicked")
- Given a disabled switch, when the control is clicked, then onCheckedChange is never called. (ark: packages/react/src/components/switch/tests/switch.test.tsx: "should not toggle when disabled"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/switch/tests/switch.test.tsx: "should not toggle when disabled"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/switch/tests/switch.test.ts: "should not toggle when disabled")

### Focus management

- Given the switch input is focused, then the input reports focus and the control carries `data-focus=""`. (zag: e2e/switch.e2e.ts: "should be focused when page is tabbed")
- Given a disabled switch, when the label is clicked, then the input is not focused and the control has no `data-focus`. (zag: e2e/switch.e2e.ts: "should not be focusable when disabled")
- Given a blur listener on the input, when the label is clicked three times, then no blur fires. (zag: e2e/switch.e2e.ts: "input is not blurred on label click")
- Given a switch inside Field.Root, when the field label is clicked, then the switch input takes focus. (ark: packages/react/src/components/switch/tests/switch.test.tsx: "should focus on input when label is clicked"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/switch/tests/switch.test.tsx: "should focus on input when label is clicked"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/switch/tests/switch.test.ts: "should focus on switch when label is clicked")

### Forms

- Given a disabled switch, then the input is disabled and the control carries `data-disabled=""`. (zag: e2e/switch.e2e.ts: "should have disabled attributes when disabled")
- Given `invalid`, then the switch input exposes `aria-invalid="true"`. (ark: packages/react/src/components/switch/tests/switch.test.tsx: "should show invalid attribute when invalid"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/switch/tests/switch.test.tsx: "should show invalid attribute when invalid"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/switch/tests/switch.test.ts: "should show invalid attribute when invalid")
- Given `required`, then the switch input is required. (ark: packages/react/src/components/switch/tests/switch.test.tsx: "should be required when required is true"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/switch/tests/switch.test.tsx: "should be required when required is true"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/switch/tests/switch.test.ts: "should be required when required is true")
- Given a switch inside a required Field, then the input is required; inside a disabled Field, the input is disabled. (ark: packages/react/src/components/switch/tests/switch.test.tsx: "should set checkbox as required"; ark: packages/react/src/components/switch/tests/switch.test.tsx: "should set input as disabled"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/switch/tests/switch.test.ts: "should set switch as required"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/switch/tests/switch.test.ts: "should set switch as disabled")
- Given a switch inside Field.Root, then helper text renders, error text renders only when the field is invalid, and is absent otherwise. (ark: packages/react/src/components/switch/tests/switch.test.tsx: "should display helper text"; ark: packages/react/src/components/switch/tests/switch.test.tsx: "should display error text when error is present"; ark: packages/react/src/components/switch/tests/switch.test.tsx: "should not display error text when no error is present"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/switch/tests/switch.test.tsx: "should display helper text"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/switch/tests/switch.test.ts: "should display helper text")

### Accessibility tooling

- Given the basic switch, when axe runs over the root part, then there are no violations. (zag: e2e/switch.e2e.ts: "should have no accessibility violation"; ark: packages/react/src/components/switch/tests/switch.test.tsx: "should have no a11y violations")

## radio-group

### Roles and attributes

- Anatomy parts are root, label, item, itemText, itemControl, indicator. (zag: packages/machines/radio-group/src/radio-group.anatomy.ts)
- Root has `role="radiogroup"`, `aria-labelledby` on the label id, `aria-required`, `aria-disabled`, `aria-readonly`, `aria-orientation`, plus `data-orientation`, `data-disabled`, `data-invalid`, `data-required` and `dir`. (zag: packages/machines/radio-group/src/radio-group.connect.ts)
- Item, itemText and itemControl each get `data-focus`, `data-focus-visible`, `data-disabled`, `data-readonly`, `data-state` (`checked`/`unchecked`), `data-hover`, `data-invalid`, `data-orientation` and `data-ssr`; itemControl adds `data-active` and `aria-hidden="true"`. (zag: packages/machines/radio-group/src/radio-group.connect.ts)
- Each item's hidden input is `type="radio"` with `data-ownedby` set to the root id, `aria-labelledby` on the item label id and `aria-invalid`. (zag: packages/machines/radio-group/src/radio-group.connect.ts)
- The indicator part is hidden while no value is selected or its measured rect is empty, carries `data-disabled` and `data-orientation`, and exposes the CSS variables `--transition-property`, `--left`, `--top`, `--width`, `--height`, driving `transitionProperty`/`transitionDuration` from `--transition-duration` (default 150ms) and `--transition-timing-function`. (zag: packages/machines/radio-group/src/radio-group.connect.ts)
- Given the basic radio group, then the root's `aria-labelledby` equals the label part's generated id. (zag: e2e/radio-group.e2e.ts: "should have aria-labelledby on root")
- Given a radio is clicked, then `data-state="checked"` appears on that item's root, label and control at once. (zag: e2e/radio-group.e2e.ts: "should be checked when clicked")

### Keyboard

- Given the first radio is focused by tabbing, when Space is pressed, then that radio becomes checked. (zag: e2e/radio-group.e2e.ts: "should be checked when spacebar is pressed while focused")
- Given "apple" is checked, when ArrowDown is pressed three times, then selection follows focus to "grape". (zag: e2e/radio-group.e2e.ts: "should check items when navigating by arrows")

### Focus management

- Given the page main area is clicked, when Tab is pressed, then the first radio's input takes focus and its control gets `data-focus=""`. (zag: e2e/radio-group.e2e.ts: "should be focused when page is tabbed")
- Given "grape" is already checked, when the group is tabbed into, then focus lands on the checked radio rather than the first one. (zag: e2e/radio-group.e2e.ts: "should be focused on active radio item when page is tabbed")
- Given a disabled group, when the page is tabbed, then no radio input receives focus. (zag: e2e/radio-group.e2e.ts: "should not be focusable when disabled")
- Given focus arrived by keyboard, when ArrowDown moves through items, then the focused item keeps both `data-focus` and `data-focus-visible`. (zag: e2e/radio-group.e2e.ts: "should keep data-focus-visible when navigating by arrows")
- Given focus arrived by mouse click, then the clicked control has `data-focus` but not `data-focus-visible`, and `data-focus-visible` appears only once arrow keys are used - this pins the pointer-vs-keyboard focus-visible heuristic. (zag: e2e/radio-group.e2e.ts: "should apply data-focus-visible after mouse click then arrow navigation")

### Forms

- Given a disabled group, then each item control has `data-disabled=""` and each hidden input is disabled. (zag: e2e/radio-group.e2e.ts: "should have disabled attributes when disabled")
- Given a radio group, when an enabled option's label is clicked, then onValueChange fires once with that option's value. (ark: packages/react/src/components/radio-group/tests/radio-group.test.tsx: "should invoke onValueChange if another value has selected"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/radio-group/tests/radio-group.test.tsx: "should invoke onValueChange if another value has selected"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/radio-group/tests/radio-group.test.ts: "should invoke onValueChange if another value has selected")
- Given an option marked disabled in the items array, when its label is clicked, then onValueChange never fires. (ark: packages/react/src/components/radio-group/tests/radio-group.test.tsx: "should not invoke onValueChange if option is disabled"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/radio-group/tests/radio-group.test.tsx: "should not invoke onValueChange if option is disabled"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/radio-group/tests/radio-group.test.ts: "should not invoke onValueChange if option is disabled")

### Accessibility tooling

- Given the basic radio group, when axe runs over the root, then there are no violations; React and Solid wrap the initial render in `act` before running axe. (zag: e2e/radio-group.e2e.ts: "should have no accessibility violation"; ark: packages/react/src/components/radio-group/tests/radio-group.test.tsx: "should have no a11y violations"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/radio-group/tests/radio-group.test.tsx: "should have no a11y violations"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/radio-group/tests/radio-group.test.ts: "should have no a11y violations")

- Given a segment group, when an enabled segment's label is clicked, then onValueChange fires with that value. ## toggle

### Roles and attributes

- Anatomy parts are root and indicator. (zag: packages/machines/toggle/src/toggle.anatomy.ts)
- Root is `type="button"` with `aria-pressed`, `data-state` of `on`/`off`, `data-pressed` and `data-disabled`; the indicator repeats `data-state`, `data-pressed` and `data-disabled`. (zag: packages/machines/toggle/src/toggle.connect.ts)

### Notes and edge cases

- The standalone toggle machine ships no e2e spec, no unit test and no Ark test file; its contract is only the attribute set above. (zag: packages/machines/toggle/src/toggle.connect.ts)

## toggle-group

### Roles and attributes

- Anatomy parts are root and item. (zag: packages/machines/toggle-group/src/toggle-group.anatomy.ts)
- Root takes `role="radiogroup"` in single mode and `role="group"` in multiple mode, `data-disabled`, `data-orientation`, `data-focus` when any item is focused, and `tabIndex` of -1 while tabbing backward out of the group else 0. (zag: packages/machines/toggle-group/src/toggle-group.connect.ts)
- Item is `type="button"` with `data-ownedby` set to the root id, `data-focus`, `data-disabled`, `data-orientation`, `data-state` of `on`/`off`, and `role="radio"` + `aria-checked` in single mode versus `aria-pressed` in multiple mode; `tabIndex` is managed only when roving focus is on. (zag: packages/machines/toggle-group/src/toggle-group.connect.ts)
- Given single mode, when an item is clicked, then it gets `data-state="on"` and the previously selected item flips to `data-state="off"`. (zag: e2e/toggle-group.e2e.ts: "[single] should select on click")

### Keyboard

- Given focus is on an outside button, when Tab is pressed, then the first item receives focus. (zag: e2e/toggle-group.e2e.ts: "[keyboard] when no toggle is selected, focus first toggle")
- Given the first item is focused, when Shift+Tab is pressed, then focus leaves the group back to the outside button and no item is focused. (zag: e2e/toggle-group.e2e.ts: "[keyboard] when no toggle is selected, focus first toggle")
- Given focus moved to the second item with ArrowRight, when the group is tabbed out and back in, then focus returns to that same second item rather than the first. (zag: e2e/toggle-group.e2e.ts: "[keyboard] in and out tab press")
- Given the last item is focused, when ArrowRight is pressed, then focus loops to the first item. (zag: e2e/toggle-group.e2e.ts: "[keyboard] focus loop"; ark: packages/react/src/components/toggle-group/tests/toggle-group.test.tsx: "should loop focus by default"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/toggle-group/tests/toggle-group.test.tsx: "should loop focus by default"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/toggle-group/tests/toggle-group.test.ts: "should loop focus by default")
- Given `loopFocus={false}` and the last item focused, when ArrowRight is pressed, then focus stays on the last item. (ark: packages/react/src/components/toggle-group/tests/toggle-group.test.tsx: "should not loop focus if disabled"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/toggle-group/tests/toggle-group.test.tsx: "should not loop focus if disabled"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/toggle-group/tests/toggle-group.test.ts: "should not loop focus if disabled")
- The connect layer maps ArrowLeft/ArrowUp to focus-previous, ArrowRight/ArrowDown to focus-next, Home to focus-first, End to focus-last, and intercepts Shift+Tab to hand focus out of the group. (zag: packages/machines/toggle-group/src/toggle-group.connect.ts)

### Pointer

- Given single mode and an already-selected item, when it is clicked again, then it deselects. (zag: e2e/toggle-group.e2e.ts: "[single] should select and deselect")
- Given `multiple`, when two items are clicked, then both report `data-state="on"` and onValueChange reports the accumulated array. (zag: e2e/toggle-group.e2e.ts: "[multiple] should select multiple"; ark: packages/react/src/components/toggle-group/tests/toggle-group.test.tsx: "should handle multiple selection"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/toggle-group/tests/toggle-group.test.tsx: "should handle multiple selection"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/toggle-group/tests/toggle-group.test.ts: "should handle multiple selection")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given `defaultValue={['a']}`, then item A renders checked without any interaction; Solid expresses the same case with a `value` prop instead of `defaultValue`. (ark: packages/react/src/components/toggle-group/tests/toggle-group.test.tsx: "should handle default value"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/toggle-group/tests/toggle-group.test.tsx: "should handle default value"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/toggle-group/tests/toggle-group.test.ts: "should handle default value")
- Given an onValueChange handler, when item A is clicked, then it is called with an object containing `value: ['a']`. (ark: packages/react/src/components/toggle-group/tests/toggle-group.test.tsx: "should handle onValueChange"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/toggle-group/tests/toggle-group.test.tsx: "should handle onValueChange"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/toggle-group/tests/toggle-group.test.ts: "should handle onValueChange")

### Forms

- Given a disabled toggle group, then every item button is disabled. (ark: packages/react/src/components/toggle-group/tests/toggle-group.test.tsx: "should handle disabled state"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/toggle-group/tests/toggle-group.test.tsx: "should handle disabled state"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/toggle-group/tests/toggle-group.test.ts: "should handle disabled state")

### Accessibility tooling

- Given the basic toggle group, when axe runs, then there are no violations. (zag: e2e/toggle-group.e2e.ts: "should have no accessibility violation"; ark: packages/react/src/components/toggle-group/tests/toggle-group.test.tsx: "should have no a11y violations")

## slider

### Roles and attributes

- Anatomy parts are root, label, thumb, valueText, track, range, control, markerGroup, marker, draggingIndicator. (zag: packages/machines/slider/src/slider.anatomy.ts)
- Label, root, valueText, track, range and control all carry `data-disabled`, `data-orientation`, `data-dragging`, `data-invalid` and `data-focus`. (zag: packages/machines/slider/src/slider.connect.ts)
- Thumb has `role="slider"`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuetext`, `aria-orientation`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` falling back to the label part id, `aria-disabled`, `tabIndex` 0 unless disabled, plus `data-index`, `data-name`, `data-disabled`, `data-orientation`, and per-thumb `data-focus`/`data-dragging` that only apply to the focused index. (zag: packages/machines/slider/src/slider.connect.ts)
- markerGroup is `role="presentation"` and `aria-hidden`; each marker is `role="presentation"` with `data-value`, `data-disabled`, `data-orientation` and `data-state` describing its position relative to the value. (zag: packages/machines/slider/src/slider.connect.ts)
- draggingIndicator is `role="presentation"`, hidden unless dragging, and carries `data-state` of `open`/`closed` plus `data-orientation`. (zag: packages/machines/slider/src/slider.connect.ts)
- Root style exposes `--slider-thumb-offset-<index>` per thumb, `--slider-thumb-width`, `--slider-thumb-height`, `--slider-thumb-transform`, `--slider-range-start` and `--slider-range-end`; range positions itself from the two range variables, and thumb positions from its offset variable. (zag: packages/machines/slider/src/slider.style.ts)
- Thumb transform is `translateY(50%)` vertically, `translateX(50%)` in RTL and `translateX(-50%)` otherwise, so the same offset variables work in all three writing modes. (zag: packages/machines/slider/src/slider.style.ts)
- With `thumbAlignment="contain"` the thumb and markers are `visibility: hidden` until the thumb size has been measured, avoiding a first-paint jump. (zag: packages/machines/slider/src/slider.style.ts)
- Marker style sets `--translate-x`/`--translate-y` so markers center over their value, mirrored for RTL. (zag: packages/machines/slider/src/slider.style.ts)
- The hidden input per thumb is `type="text"` and `hidden`, carrying the value for form submission. (zag: packages/machines/slider/src/slider.connect.ts)

### Keyboard

- Given the thumb is focused, when ArrowRight is pressed twice, then the value text reads 1 then 2. (zag: e2e/slider.e2e.ts: "[keyboard] should work with arrow left/right keys")
- Given a value of 2, when Home then End are pressed, then the value snaps to the min 0 then the max 100. (zag: e2e/slider.e2e.ts: "[keyboard] should work with home/end keys")
- Given the thumb is focused, when Shift+ArrowRight then Shift+ArrowLeft are pressed, then the value moves by the default largeStep of 10 and back. (zag: e2e/slider.e2e.ts: "[keyboard] should work with shift key"; ark: packages/react/src/components/slider/tests/slider.test.tsx: "should step by the default largeStep (10 * step) when Shift is held"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/slider/tests/slider.test.tsx: "should step by the default largeStep (10 * step) when Shift is held"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/slider/tests/slider.test.ts: "should step by the default largeStep (10 * step) when Shift is held")
- Given the thumb is focused, when PageUp then PageDown are pressed, then the value moves by largeStep in each direction. (zag: e2e/slider.e2e.ts: "[keyboard] should work with page up/down keys"; ark: packages/react/src/components/slider/tests/slider.test.tsx: "should step by the default largeStep when PageUp/PageDown is pressed"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/slider/tests/slider.test.tsx: "should step by the default largeStep when PageUp/PageDown is pressed"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/slider/tests/slider.test.ts: "should step by the default largeStep when PageUp/PageDown is pressed")
- Given Meta, Control or Alt is held with an arrow key, then the value still moves by exactly one step and never by a fraction of a step, so modifier keys cannot leave the step grid. (zag: e2e/slider.e2e.ts: "[keyboard] should stay on the step grid regardless of modifier keys")
- Given `largeStep` is set to 5, when Shift+ArrowRight, PageUp and PageDown are pressed, then the value moves in increments of 5. (zag: e2e/slider.e2e.ts: "[keyboard] should respect a custom largeStep"; ark: packages/react/src/components/slider/tests/slider.test.tsx: "should use an explicit largeStep when Shift is held"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/slider/tests/slider.test.tsx: "should use an explicit largeStep when Shift is held"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/slider/tests/slider.test.ts: "should use an explicit largeStep when Shift is held")
- Given a two-thumb slider, when each thumb is focused and arrowed, then only that thumb's `aria-valuenow` changes. (ark: packages/react/src/components/slider/tests/slider.test.tsx: "should be possible to control it with the arrow keys"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/slider/tests/slider.test.tsx: "should be possible to control it with the arrow keys"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/slider/tests/slider.test.ts: "should be possible to control it with the arrow keys")
- Given a range slider, when the left thumb is driven to End, then it stops at the right thumb's value and a further ArrowRight does not move it, so thumbs cannot cross. (ark: packages/react/src/components/slider/tests/slider.test.tsx: "should not be possible to overlap the right thumb with the left thumb"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/slider/tests/slider.test.tsx: "should not be possible to overlap the right thumb with the left thumb")
- Given `orientation="vertical"`, when ArrowUp and ArrowDown are pressed, then the value increments and decrements respectively. (ark: packages/react/src/components/slider/tests/slider.test.tsx: "should be possible to control it with the arrow keys in vertical mode"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/slider/tests/slider.test.tsx: "should be possible to control it with the arrow keys in vertical mode")
- The connect layer maps ArrowUp/ArrowRight to increment, ArrowDown/ArrowLeft to decrement, PageUp/PageDown to large-step moves, and Home/End to min/max, resolving the key through a direction-aware `getEventKey`. (zag: packages/machines/slider/src/slider.connect.ts)

### Pointer

- Given the basic slider, when the track is pressed at 80 percent of its effective width, then the thumb takes focus and the value becomes 80. (zag: e2e/slider.e2e.ts: "[pointer] should set value on click track")
- Given a press at 80 percent, when the pointer is dragged to 90 percent and released, then the value ends at 90. (zag: e2e/slider.e2e.ts: "[pointer] should set the value on drag")

### Focus management

- Given a press on the track, then the nearest thumb receives focus as part of the same gesture. (zag: e2e/slider.e2e.ts: "[pointer] should set value on click track")
- The focused thumb gets `zIndex: 1` so it paints above its sibling when two thumbs overlap. (zag: packages/machines/slider/src/slider.style.ts)

### Forms

- Given a disabled slider, then every thumb exposes `aria-disabled="true"` and loses its tabIndex. (ark: packages/react/src/components/slider/tests/slider.test.tsx: "should handle disabled state"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/slider/tests/slider.test.tsx: "should handle disabled state"; zag: packages/machines/slider/src/slider.connect.ts)
- Given an onValueChange handler, when one arrow key is pressed, then it fires exactly once. (ark: packages/react/src/components/slider/tests/slider.test.tsx: "should emit correct onValueChange events"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/slider/tests/slider.test.tsx: "should emit correct onValueChange events")

### RTL and i18n

- Given the tree is wrapped in `LocaleProvider locale="ar-AE"`, when ArrowRight is pressed, then the value decreases and ArrowLeft increases it, mirroring the axis. (ark: packages/react/src/components/slider/tests/slider.test.tsx: "should be possible to control it with the arrow keys in rtl mode"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/slider/tests/slider.test.tsx: "should be possible to control it with the arrow keys in rtl mode")
- Range offsets and thumb offsets are computed against `isRtl`, swapping the `left`/`right` inset properties for the range part. (zag: packages/machines/slider/src/slider.style.ts)
- Vue keeps the RTL, vertical, disabled, thumb-overlap and onValueChange cases commented out, so the Vue adapter is only proven for LTR horizontal keyboard stepping. (ark: packages/vue/src/components/slider/tests/slider.test.ts)

### Accessibility tooling

- Given the basic slider, when axe runs over the root, then there are no violations; both React and Solid skip their axe case for the slider. (zag: e2e/slider.e2e.ts: "should have no accessibility violation"; ark: packages/react/src/components/slider/tests/slider.test.tsx: "should have no a11y violations")

### Notes and edge cases

- The e2e model computes track points from the control box minus the thumb size, because in `contain` thumb alignment the usable track is inset by half a thumb at each end. (zag: e2e/models/slider.model.ts)
- Ark's slider tests read thumbs with `getAllByRole('slider', { hidden: true })`, since the thumbs are inside a container that testing-library treats as hidden until measured. (ark: packages/react/src/components/slider/tests/slider.test.tsx)

## angle-slider

### Roles and attributes

- Anatomy parts are root, label, thumb, valueText, control, track, markerGroup, marker. (zag: packages/machines/angle-slider/src/angle-slider.anatomy.ts)
- Root carries `data-disabled`, `data-invalid`, `data-readonly` and the CSS variables `--value` (raw number) and `--angle` (`<n>deg`). (zag: packages/machines/angle-slider/src/angle-slider.connect.ts)
- Thumb has `role="slider"`, `aria-valuemin` 0, `aria-valuemax` 360, `aria-valuenow`, `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby` defaulting to the label id, `tabIndex` 0 when interactive or readonly, `data-disabled`, `data-invalid`, `data-readonly`, and rotates via `rotate: var(--angle)`. (zag: packages/machines/angle-slider/src/angle-slider.connect.ts)
- Control is `role="presentation"` with `data-disabled`, `data-invalid` and `data-readonly`; the hidden input is `type="hidden"`. (zag: packages/machines/angle-slider/src/angle-slider.connect.ts)
- Each marker carries `data-value`, `data-state`, `data-disabled` and the variables `--marker-value` and `--marker-display-value`, rotating by `calc(var(--marker-display-value) * 1deg)`. (zag: packages/machines/angle-slider/src/angle-slider.connect.ts)

### Keyboard

- The connect layer maps ArrowLeft/ArrowDown to decrement and ArrowRight/ArrowUp to increment by step, with Home and End jumping to the ends, resolved through a horizontal-orientation key lookup. (zag: packages/machines/angle-slider/src/angle-slider.connect.ts)

### Pointer

- Given the value is 0deg, when the control is clicked at the 90-degree point of its circle, then the value lands within 85-95deg. (zag: e2e/angle-slider.e2e.ts: "[pointer] should jump to clicked position on control")
- Given the value is 0deg, when the drag starts at the thumb's edge rather than its center and ends at the 90-degree point, then the value still lands within 85-95deg, so the grab offset is preserved instead of snapping the thumb center to the pointer. (zag: e2e/angle-slider.e2e.ts: "[pointer] should maintain relative position when dragging from thumb edge")
- Given the value is 45deg, when the thumb is dragged from its edge to the 180-degree point, then the value lands within 175-185deg, proving the angular offset holds across the whole drag. (zag: e2e/angle-slider.e2e.ts: "[pointer] should maintain offset throughout drag operation")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given the default angle slider, then the value text renders "0deg". (zag: e2e/angle-slider.e2e.ts: "[pointer] should jump to clicked position on control"; ark: packages/react/src/components/angle-slider/tests/angle-slider.test.tsx: "should display helper text")

### Forms

- Given `disabled`, then the slider thumb has `data-disabled=""`; given `readOnly`, then it has `data-readonly=""`. (ark: packages/react/src/components/angle-slider/tests/angle-slider.test.tsx: "should set angle slider as disabled"; ark: packages/react/src/components/angle-slider/tests/angle-slider.test.tsx: "should set angle slider as readonly")

### Accessibility tooling

- Given the basic angle slider, when axe runs over the root, then there are no violations; the React axe case is skipped. (zag: e2e/angle-slider.e2e.ts: "should have no accessibility violation"; ark: packages/react/src/components/angle-slider/tests/angle-slider.test.tsx: "should have no a11y violations")

## rating-group

### Roles and attributes

- Anatomy parts are root, label, item, control. (zag: packages/machines/rating-group/src/rating-group.anatomy.ts)
- Control is `role="radiogroup"` with `aria-orientation="horizontal"`, `aria-labelledby` on the label id, `aria-readonly`, `data-readonly` and `data-disabled`. (zag: packages/machines/rating-group/src/rating-group.connect.ts)
- Each item is `role="radio"` with `aria-roledescription="rating"`, `aria-label` from the value text translation, `aria-setsize` equal to count, `aria-posinset` equal to its index, `aria-checked`, `aria-disabled`, plus `data-checked`, `data-highlighted`, `data-half`, `data-disabled` and `data-readonly`. (zag: packages/machines/rating-group/src/rating-group.connect.ts)
- The hidden input is `type="text"` and `hidden`, and the label carries `data-disabled` and `data-required`. (zag: packages/machines/rating-group/src/rating-group.connect.ts)

### Keyboard

- Given item 3 is focused, when ArrowRight is pressed twice then ArrowLeft twice, then focus moves to item 4 and back to item 3 - arrow keys move by one rating per press. (zag: e2e/rating-group.e2e.ts: "should select value on arrow left/right")
- Given item 3 is focused, when Home is pressed, then item 1 is focused and highlighted, and End focuses and highlights item 5. (zag: e2e/rating-group.e2e.ts: "should select value on arrow home/end")
- Given item 3 is focused, when ArrowLeft is pressed five times so the value reaches 0, then Tab still finds item 1 focusable with `tabindex="0"`, so an empty rating keeps a tab stop. (zag: e2e/rating-group.e2e.ts: "should remain focusable when value is 0")
- The connect layer maps ArrowUp to the same handler as ArrowLeft and ArrowDown to the same as ArrowRight, and Space selects the focused index. (zag: packages/machines/rating-group/src/rating-group.connect.ts)

### Pointer

- Given the basic rating group, when item 4 is clicked, then the hidden input's value becomes "4". (zag: e2e/rating-group.e2e.ts: "should set value when item is clicked")
- Given an onValueChange handler, when the "5 stars" radio is clicked, then it fires with `{ value: 5 }` on the first call. (ark: packages/react/src/components/rating-group/tests/rating-group.test.tsx: "should trigger onValueChange on click"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/rating-group/tests/rating-group.test.tsx: "should trigger onValueChange on click"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/rating-group/tests/rating-group.test.ts: "should trigger onValueChange on click")
- Given a default value of 0, when the "5 stars" radio is clicked, then the hidden input value becomes "5". (ark: packages/react/src/components/rating-group/tests/rating-group.test.tsx: "should update rating on click"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/rating-group/tests/rating-group.test.tsx: "should update rating on click"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/rating-group/tests/rating-group.test.ts: "should update rating on click")
- Pointer-move within an item computes a horizontal percentage and reports `isMidway` when below 0.5, which is what drives the half-star `data-half` state. (zag: packages/machines/rating-group/src/rating-group.connect.ts)
- The hover-highlight behavior (hovering item 4 highlights 4, hovering out falls back to the selected 3) is written but skipped, so hover highlighting is currently unverified in e2e. (zag: e2e/rating-group.e2e.ts: "highlight when hovered")

### Focus management

- Given the basic rating group with value 3, when the label is clicked, then focus lands on the third item rather than the first. (zag: e2e/rating-group.e2e.ts: "clicking label should focus 3rd item"; ark: packages/react/src/components/rating-group/tests/rating-group.test.tsx: "should focus on rating group when label is clicked"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/rating-group/tests/rating-group.test.tsx: "should focus on rating group when label is clicked"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/rating-group/tests/rating-group.test.ts: "should focus on rating group when label is clicked")

## signature-pad

### Roles and attributes

- Anatomy parts are root, control, segment, segmentPath, guide, clearTrigger, label. (zag: packages/machines/signature-pad/src/signature-pad.anatomy.ts)

## progress

### Roles and attributes

- Anatomy parts are root, label, track, range, valueText, view, circle, circleTrack, circleRange. (zag: packages/machines/progress/src/progress.anatomy.ts)
- A shared block puts `role="progressbar"`, `aria-label` holding the formatted value, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, `aria-valuenow` (omitted when indeterminate), `data-max`, `data-orientation` and `data-state` on the semantic element. (zag: packages/machines/progress/src/progress.connect.ts)
- Root carries `data-max`, `data-value`, `data-state`, `data-orientation` and the CSS variable `--percent`, which is left undefined while indeterminate. (zag: packages/machines/progress/src/progress.connect.ts)
- valueText is `aria-live="polite"` so screen readers announce value changes. (zag: packages/machines/progress/src/progress.connect.ts)
- The circular variant computes `--radius` from `--size` and `--thickness`, then `--circumference` as `2 * pi * var(--radius)` and `--offset` as the remaining arc, setting `strokeDashoffset` from them and omitting `strokeDasharray` while indeterminate. (zag: packages/machines/progress/src/progress.connect.ts)
- A view part is `hidden` unless its declared `data-state` matches the machine's current state, giving per-state slots. (zag: packages/machines/progress/src/progress.connect.ts)

## timer

### Roles and attributes

- Anatomy parts are root, area, control, item, itemValue, itemLabel, actionTrigger, separator. (zag: packages/machines/timer/src/timer.anatomy.ts)
- The area part is `role="timer"` with `aria-atomic="true"` and a translated `aria-label` built from the current time and formatted time, so the whole time is re-announced as one unit. (zag: packages/machines/timer/src/timer.connect.ts)

- The public API exposes start, pause, resume, reset and restart. (zag: packages/machines/timer/src/timer.connect.ts)

## clipboard

### Roles and attributes

- Anatomy parts are root, control, trigger, indicator, input, label. (zag: packages/machines/clipboard/src/clipboard.anatomy.ts)
- Root, label, control, input and trigger all carry `data-copied` while the copied state is active. (zag: packages/machines/clipboard/src/clipboard.connect.ts)

- An indicator instance is `hidden` unless its declared `copied` prop matches the current copied state, which is how the "Copy"/"Copied!" swap is expressed declaratively. (zag: packages/machines/clipboard/src/clipboard.connect.ts)

## number-field

### Roles and attributes

- Anatomy parts are root, label, input, control, valueText, incrementTrigger, decrementTrigger, scrubber, under the scope name `numberInput`. (zag: packages/machines/number-input/src/number-input.anatomy.ts)
- Root, label, control and valueText all carry `data-disabled`, `data-focus`, `data-invalid` and `data-scrubbing`; label adds `data-required`. (zag: packages/machines/number-input/src/number-input.connect.ts)
- Control is `role="group"` with `aria-disabled` and `aria-invalid`. (zag: packages/machines/number-input/src/number-input.connect.ts)
- The input is `role="spinbutton"` with `aria-roledescription="numberfield"`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, `aria-valuenow` (omitted when the parsed value is NaN), `aria-valuetext`, `aria-invalid`, `type="text"`, `autoComplete="off"`, an `inputMode` from props, and a `pattern` that is dropped whenever `formatOptions` are in play. (zag: packages/machines/number-input/src/number-input.connect.ts)
- Increment and decrement triggers are `type="button"` with `tabIndex={-1}`, `aria-controls` pointing at the input id, a translated `aria-label`, and `data-disabled` computed from whether that direction is still possible. (zag: packages/machines/number-input/src/number-input.connect.ts)
- The scrubber is `role="presentation"` with `data-disabled` and `data-scrubbing`. (zag: packages/machines/number-input/src/number-input.connect.ts)
- Given a value above max while still focused, then the input reports `aria-invalid="true"` before any blur. (zag: e2e/number-input.e2e.ts: "should clamp value when blurred")

### Keyboard

- Given the value 5, when ArrowUp is pressed, then the value becomes 6. (zag: e2e/number-input.e2e.ts: "should increment with arrow up")
- Given the value 5, when ArrowDown is pressed twice, then the value becomes 3. (zag: e2e/number-input.e2e.ts: "should decrement the value")
- Given the value 5 and Enter already pressed, when ArrowDown then ArrowUp are pressed, then stepping still works after the commit. (zag: e2e/number-input.e2e.ts: "pressing enter should make up/down still work")
- Given the value 5, when Home then End are pressed, then the value jumps to min 0 then max 100. (zag: e2e/number-input.e2e.ts: "should set value to min/max on home/end keys")
- Given the value 0, when Shift+ArrowUp is pressed, then the value moves by the default largeStep of 10 and Shift+ArrowDown moves back. (zag: e2e/number-input.e2e.ts: "shift+arrowup: should change 10 steps"; ark: packages/react/src/components/number-input/tests/number-input.test.tsx: "should increment by the default largeStep (10 * step) when Shift is held"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/number-input/tests/number-input.test.tsx: "should increment by the default largeStep (10 * step) when Shift is held"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/number-input/tests/number-input.test.ts: "should increment by the default largeStep (10 * step) when Shift is held")
- Given the value 0, when Alt+ArrowUp is pressed twice, then the value moves by the default smallStep of 0.1 each time, and Alt+ArrowDown reverses it. (zag: e2e/number-input.e2e.ts: "alt+arrowup: should change by smallStep"; ark: packages/react/src/components/number-input/tests/number-input.test.tsx: "should increment by the default smallStep (step / 10) when Alt is held"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/number-input/tests/number-input.test.tsx: "should increment by the default smallStep (step / 10) when Alt is held"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/number-input/tests/number-input.test.ts: "should increment by the default smallStep (step / 10) when Alt is held")
- Given `largeStep` 5 and `smallStep` 0.25, when Shift+ArrowUp then Alt+ArrowUp then Alt+ArrowDown are pressed, then the value follows 5, 5.25, 5. (zag: e2e/number-input.e2e.ts: "should respect custom smallStep and largeStep"; ark: packages/react/src/components/number-input/tests/number-input.test.tsx: "should use an explicit largeStep when Shift is held"; ark: packages/react/src/components/number-input/tests/number-input.test.tsx: "should use an explicit smallStep when Alt is held"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/number-input/tests/number-input.test.tsx: "should use an explicit largeStep when Shift is held"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/number-input/tests/number-input.test.ts: "should use an explicit smallStep when Alt is held")
- Given an explicit `largeStep` of 5, when a bare ArrowUp is pressed, then the value moves by the ordinary step of 1, so largeStep applies only with Shift. (ark: packages/react/src/components/number-input/tests/number-input.test.tsx: "should not use largeStep when Shift is not held"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/number-input/tests/number-input.test.tsx: "should not use largeStep when Shift is not held"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/number-input/tests/number-input.test.ts: "should not use largeStep when Shift is not held")
- Given currency format options, when Enter is pressed after typing 555, then the input formats immediately to "$555.00". (zag: e2e/number-input.e2e.ts: "[formatOptions] pressing enter trigger format")
- The connect layer maps ArrowUp/ArrowDown to stepped increments that read Shift and Alt for large and small steps, Home/End to min/max, and Enter to a commit that carries the current selection. (zag: packages/machines/number-input/src/number-input.connect.ts)

### Pointer

- Given an empty input, when the increment trigger is clicked, then the value becomes 1. (zag: e2e/number-input.e2e.ts: "clicking increment"; zag: e2e/number-input.e2e.ts: "inc click: should increment value")
- Given the value 5, when the decrement trigger is clicked, then the value becomes 4. (zag: e2e/number-input.e2e.ts: "clicking decrement"; zag: e2e/number-input.e2e.ts: "dec click: should increment value")
- Given the value 20, when the decrement trigger is held down for roughly nine spin ticks and released, then the value lands near 9 within a tolerance of 1, so press-and-hold spins continuously after a 300ms delay at a 50ms interval. (zag: e2e/number-input.e2e.ts: "dec longpress: should spin value downwards")
- Given `step={5}`, when the increment button is clicked once, then the value becomes 5. (ark: packages/react/src/components/number-input/tests/number-input.test.tsx: "should increment value by step when using increment button"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/number-input/tests/number-input.test.tsx: "should increment value by step when using increment button"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/number-input/tests/number-input.test.ts: "should increment value by step when using increment button")
- Given `allowMouseWheel`, when the input is focused and a wheel event with negative deltaY arrives, then the value increments to 1. (ark: packages/react/src/components/number-input/tests/number-input.test.tsx: "should handle wheel event when allowMouseWheel is true"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/number-input/tests/number-input.test.tsx: "should handle wheel event when allowMouseWheel is true"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/number-input/tests/number-input.test.ts: "should handle wheel event when allowMouseWheel is true")
- The scrub-to-change gesture (drag on the scrubber updates the value) and the increment long-press spin are both written but skipped in e2e, so only the decrement long-press is actually verified. (zag: e2e/number-input.e2e.ts: "scrub: should update value on scrubbing"; zag: e2e/number-input.e2e.ts: "inc longpress: should spin value upwards")

### Focus management

- Given a number input inside a Field, when the field label is clicked, then the spinbutton receives focus. (ark: packages/react/src/components/number-input/tests/number-input.test.tsx: "should focus on input when label is clicked"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/number-input/tests/number-input.test.tsx: "should focus on input when label is clicked"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/number-input/tests/number-input.test.ts: "should focus on input when label is clicked")
- The increment and decrement triggers are removed from the tab order (`tabIndex: -1`), so Tab moves from the input straight past the spinners. (zag: packages/machines/number-input/src/number-input.connect.ts)

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given the value 12, when Backspace is pressed twice, then the input is allowed to hold the empty string rather than snapping to a number. (zag: e2e/number-input.e2e.ts: "should allow typing empty string value")
- Given 200 typed into a 0-100 field, when focus leaves, then the value clamps to 100. (zag: e2e/number-input.e2e.ts: "should clamp value when blurred")
- Given the input is emptied, when focus leaves, then the value stays empty rather than clamping to min. (zag: e2e/number-input.e2e.ts: "should clamp value when input is empty")
- Given `min` is 1 and the input is emptied, when focus leaves, then the value still stays empty, so an empty field is never coerced to a positive min. (zag: e2e/number-input.e2e.ts: "should not clamp empty value on blur when min is greater than 0")
- Given `clampValueOnBlur` with min 0, max 10 and a default of 15, when the input blurs, then the value clamps to 10. (ark: packages/react/src/components/number-input/tests/number-input.test.tsx: "should clamp value on blur when clampValueOnBlur is true"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/number-input/tests/number-input.test.tsx: "should clamp value on blur when clampValueOnBlur is true"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/number-input/tests/number-input.test.ts: "should clamp value on blur when clampValueOnBlur is true")
- Given `allowOverflow` with max 10 and a default of 15, then the input keeps 15. (ark: packages/react/src/components/number-input/tests/number-input.test.tsx: "should allow value to exceed max when allowOverflow is true"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/number-input/tests/number-input.test.tsx: "should allow value to exceed max when allowOverflow is true"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/number-input/tests/number-input.test.ts: "should allow value to exceed max when allowOverflow is true")
- Vue triggers the blur clamp with `user.tab()` where React uses `fireEvent.blur` and Solid calls `input.blur()` - three different ways to produce the same commit. (ark: packages/vue/src/components/number-input/tests/number-input.test.ts: "should clamp value on blur when clampValueOnBlur is true")

### Forms

- Given a non-numeric string typed character by character, then nothing is accepted, and "123xyz" yields "123". (zag: e2e/number-input.e2e.ts: "should not allow non-numeric characters")
- Given digits typed sequentially, then "123" then ".45" compose to "123.45", and "-67.89" is accepted whole. (zag: e2e/number-input.e2e.ts: "should allow numeric characters")
- Given "1.23" already typed, when ".45" is typed, then the extra separator is dropped and the value becomes "1.2345"; starting from ".5" and typing ".25" yields ".525". (zag: e2e/number-input.e2e.ts: "should prevent multiple decimal separators")
- Given "-12345" or "12345" or "0.30" or "-0.30" typed, then the native input reports `checkValidity()` true for each. (zag: e2e/number-input.e2e.ts: "should allow negative integer values"; zag: e2e/number-input.e2e.ts: "should allow positive integer values"; zag: e2e/number-input.e2e.ts: "should allow positive values with decimal point"; zag: e2e/number-input.e2e.ts: "should allow negative values with decimal point")
- Given "007" typed, then the raw text is preserved while editing and normalizes to "7" on blur; "000.45" normalizes to "0.45" and "000" to "0", while "0.123" is left as is. (zag: e2e/number-input.e2e.ts: "should handle leading zeros correctly")
- Given an input cleared to empty, when a new number is typed, then values round-trip cleanly for integers, decimals, negatives and leading-dot forms. (zag: e2e/number-input.e2e.ts: "should handle empty string to valid number transitions")
- Given "--5" typed, then only one sign survives as "-5"; "1a2b3" becomes "123"; "1.5x" becomes "1.5"; "123-" becomes "123"; and "5.-" keeps the trailing separator as "5.". (zag: e2e/number-input.e2e.ts: "should handle invalid number sequences")
- Given zero variants on blur, then "-0" stays "-0", "+0" becomes "0", "0.0" and ".0" and "0.00" all become "0", and "-0.0" becomes "-0", so negative zero is deliberately preserved. (zag: e2e/number-input.e2e.ts: "should handle zero variations")
- Given currency format options, when focus leaves after typing 555, then the value formats to "$555.00". (zag: e2e/number-input.e2e.ts: "[formatOptions] blurring should trigger format")
- Given `formatOptions={{ currency: 'USD' }}` and a default of "5", then the displayed value is "5" until a commit. (ark: packages/react/src/components/number-input/tests/number-input.test.tsx: "should handle custom format and parse functions"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/number-input/tests/number-input.test.tsx: "should handle custom format and parse functions"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/number-input/tests/number-input.test.ts: "should handle custom format and parse functions")
- Given min and max fraction digits of 2 and 3, then "1.00" renders initially and typing "1.1234" then blurring rounds to "1.123"; Vue skips this case. ### Notes and edge cases

- Given a currency-formatted "$555.00", when the caret is placed at index 4 and "5" is typed, then the value becomes "$5555.00", the caret lands at 5, and blurring regroups it to "$5,555.00" - the caret is mapped through the reformat rather than jumping to the end. (zag: e2e/number-input.e2e.ts: "[formatOptions] should maintain cursor position")
- Given an unchanged value, `getNextCursorPosition` returns the same caret index whether it sits at the start, middle or end. (zag: packages/machines/number-input/tests/cursor.test.ts: "cursor at start"; zag: packages/machines/number-input/tests/cursor.test.ts: "cursor in middle"; zag: packages/machines/number-input/tests/cursor.test.ts: "cursor at end")
- Given a caret at 0 and a value with no shared prefix or suffix, then the caret moves to the end of the new value, including when the old value was empty. (zag: packages/machines/number-input/tests/cursor.test.ts: "moves cursor to end"; zag: packages/machines/number-input/tests/cursor.test.ts: "different lengths - moves to end"; zag: packages/machines/number-input/tests/cursor.test.ts: "empty old value")
- Given characters appended at the end, then the caret stays at the end of the shared prefix. (zag: packages/machines/number-input/tests/cursor.test.ts: "appending characters - cursor stays at prefix end"; zag: packages/machines/number-input/tests/cursor.test.ts: "appending multiple characters - cursor stays at prefix end")
- Given characters prepended, then the caret shifts right by the number of inserted characters because the suffix is matched. (zag: packages/machines/number-input/tests/cursor.test.ts: "prepending characters"; zag: packages/machines/number-input/tests/cursor.test.ts: "prepending multiple characters")
- Given an insertion in the middle, then the caret stays just after the matched prefix. (zag: packages/machines/number-input/tests/cursor.test.ts: "inserting character - prefix preserved"; zag: packages/machines/number-input/tests/cursor.test.ts: "cursor after prefix, suffix preserved")
- Given "1000" becoming "1,000", then a caret at the end moves to 5 and a caret at index 2 moves to 3, so grouping separators shift the caret. (zag: packages/machines/number-input/tests/cursor.test.ts: "number gets comma formatting - cursor at end"; zag: packages/machines/number-input/tests/cursor.test.ts: "cursor in middle during formatting")
- Given "555" becoming "$555.00", then the caret moves to the end at 7. (zag: packages/machines/number-input/tests/cursor.test.ts: "currency formatting - prefix matches then suffix")
- Given deletions, then a caret past the new end clamps to the end, and a middle deletion keeps the caret after the prefix. (zag: packages/machines/number-input/tests/cursor.test.ts: "backspace at end"; zag: packages/machines/number-input/tests/cursor.test.ts: "delete in middle")
- Given the value is cleared entirely, then the caret returns to 0, and with both values empty it stays at 0. (zag: packages/machines/number-input/tests/cursor.test.ts: "empty new value"; zag: packages/machines/number-input/tests/cursor.test.ts: "both empty")
- Given only a partial prefix or suffix match, then the caret clamps to the length of the matched part. (zag: packages/machines/number-input/tests/cursor.test.ts: "partial prefix match only"; zag: packages/machines/number-input/tests/cursor.test.ts: "partial suffix match only")
- Given no prefix or suffix match at all, then the caret falls back to the same relative position, so a caret at 50 percent of the old value lands at 50 percent of the new one. (zag: packages/machines/number-input/tests/cursor.test.ts: "relative position fallback")
- Given "123.45", when the caret is placed before the decimal separator and Delete is pressed, then the separator is removed leaving "12345". (zag: e2e/number-input.e2e.ts: "deleting decimal point")
- Given "-123.45", when the caret is at 0 and Delete is pressed, then the minus sign is removed leaving "123.45". (zag: e2e/number-input.e2e.ts: "deleting negative sign")
- Given "123.45", when the caret is just after the separator and Backspace is pressed, then the separator is removed leaving "12345". (zag: e2e/number-input.e2e.ts: "backspacing through decimal point")
- Given "-123", when the caret is just after the sign and Backspace is pressed, then the sign is removed leaving "123". (zag: e2e/number-input.e2e.ts: "backspacing negative sign")
- Given "123.45", when digits either side of the separator are deleted in turn, then the value goes to "12.45" then "12.5". (zag: e2e/number-input.e2e.ts: "deleting digits around decimal")
- Given "007", when Backspace is pressed repeatedly, then the value steps "00", "0", "" without normalizing mid-edit. (zag: e2e/number-input.e2e.ts: "backspace on leading zero")
- Given "123.45", when all text is selected and "999" is typed, then the whole value is replaced. (zag: e2e/number-input.e2e.ts: "full selection and replacement")
- Given an empty input, when select-all is followed by typing, then the value is entered normally, and a second select-all replacement swaps "50.25" for "123.45". (zag: e2e/number-input.e2e.ts: "full selection replacement with decimal")
- Given "100.25", when the substring "100" is selected and "200" typed, then the value becomes "200.25". (zag: e2e/number-input.e2e.ts: "partial text selection and replacement")
- Given "123.45" with "123" selected, when "abc456def" is typed, then only the digits survive and the value becomes "456.45". (zag: e2e/number-input.e2e.ts: "filter invalid characters during selection replacement")
- Given "100.25" with the fractional "25" selected, when "75" is typed, then the value becomes "100.75". (zag: e2e/number-input.e2e.ts: "decimal portion selection and replacement")

## pin-input

### Roles and attributes

- Anatomy parts are root, label, input, control, under the scope name `pinInput`. (zag: packages/machines/pin-input/src/pin-input.anatomy.ts)
- Root carries `data-invalid`, `data-disabled`, `data-complete`, `data-readonly`; label adds `data-required`. (zag: packages/machines/pin-input/src/pin-input.connect.ts)
- Each input gets `data-index`, `data-ownedby` set to the root id, `data-filled` when that slot holds a character, `data-complete`, `data-disabled`, `data-invalid`, `aria-invalid`, a translated `aria-label` of the form "pin code N of M", `autoCapitalize="none"`, `inputMode` of `numeric` for otp or numeric types else `text`, `type` of `password` when masked, and `autoComplete` of `one-time-code` for otp else `off`. (zag: packages/machines/pin-input/src/pin-input.connect.ts)
- Each input's `enterKeyHint` is `done` on the last slot and `next` elsewhere, so mobile keyboards show the right action key. (zag: packages/machines/pin-input/src/pin-input.connect.ts; zag: e2e/pin-input.e2e.ts: "enterkeyhint: last input should have 'done', others 'next'")
- Only one input is tabbable at a time: `tabIndex` is 0 for the slot at the insertion point and -1 for the rest. (zag: packages/machines/pin-input/src/pin-input.connect.ts)
- The placeholder is blanked on the focused slot and shown on the others. (zag: packages/machines/pin-input/src/pin-input.connect.ts)
- The hidden input is `aria-hidden`, `type="text"` and `tabIndex={-1}`, carrying the joined value for forms. (zag: packages/machines/pin-input/src/pin-input.connect.ts)
- Given a filled first slot, then that input has `data-filled` while the empty second slot does not. (zag: e2e/pin-input.e2e.ts: "data-filled: should be set on filled inputs")
- Given three inputs, then their aria-labels read "pin code 1 of 3", "pin code 2 of 3" and "pin code 3 of 3". (ark: packages/react/src/components/pin-input/tests/pin-input.test.tsx: "should have the proper aria labels"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/pin-input/tests/pin-input.test.tsx: "should have the proper aria labels"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/pin-input/tests/pin-input.test.ts: "should have the proper aria labels")
- Given `otp`, then every input has `autocomplete="one-time-code"`; Solid has this case commented out. (ark: packages/react/src/components/pin-input/tests/pin-input.test.tsx: "should set one-time-code for autocomplete on fields"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/pin-input/tests/pin-input.test.ts: "should set one-time-code for autocomplete on fields"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/pin-input/tests/pin-input.test.tsx)

### Keyboard

- Given an empty pin input, when a character is typed into a slot, then focus advances to the next slot. (zag: e2e/pin-input.e2e.ts: "on type: should move focus to the next input"; ark: packages/react/src/components/pin-input/tests/pin-input.test.tsx: "should move focus to the next item when enter a value"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/pin-input/tests/pin-input.test.tsx: "should move focus to the next item when enter a value"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/pin-input/tests/pin-input.test.ts: "should move focus to the next item when enter a value")
- Given a slot receives two characters at once, then only the last character is kept. (zag: e2e/pin-input.e2e.ts: "on type: should not allow multiple keys at once")
- Given the third slot is focused and empty, when Backspace is pressed, then the previous slot is cleared and focused. (zag: e2e/pin-input.e2e.ts: "on backspace (empty): should delete prev char and move back"; ark: packages/react/src/components/pin-input/tests/pin-input.test.tsx: "should clear the previous input when pressing backspace"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/pin-input/tests/pin-input.test.ts: "should clear the previous input when pressing backspace")
- Given all slots filled, when Backspace is pressed, then the current slot is cleared and focus moves back. (zag: e2e/pin-input.e2e.ts: "on backspace (filled): should clear and move focus back")
- Given all slots filled, when ArrowLeft then ArrowRight are pressed, then focus steps between slots. (zag: e2e/pin-input.e2e.ts: "on arrow: should change focus between inputs")
- Given all slots filled, when Home then End are pressed, then focus lands on the first then the last slot. (zag: e2e/pin-input.e2e.ts: "home/end: should navigate to first and last filled")
- Given only the first two of three slots filled, when End is pressed, then focus lands on the last filled slot rather than the empty third. (zag: e2e/pin-input.e2e.ts: "home/end: end with partial fill goes to last filled")
- Given "1","2","3" with the middle slot focused, when Delete is pressed, then the remaining values shift left leaving "1","3","" with no hole. (zag: e2e/pin-input.e2e.ts: "delete: should splice and shift values left (no holes)")
- Given "1","2","3" with the middle slot focused, when Backspace is pressed, then focus moves to the first slot and the values shift left to "1","3","". (zag: e2e/pin-input.e2e.ts: "backspace: should splice and shift values left (no holes)")
- Given only the first slot is filled, when ArrowRight is pressed from the second slot, then focus stays at the insertion point and does not jump into empty slots. (zag: e2e/pin-input.e2e.ts: "arrow right: should not go past insertion point")
- Given the first slot is focused, when ArrowLeft is pressed, then focus stays on the first slot. (zag: e2e/pin-input.e2e.ts: "arrow left: should not go before first input")
- Given a slot already holding "1", when "1" is typed again, then the value is unchanged and focus still advances. (zag: e2e/pin-input.e2e.ts: "same key: should advance focus without changing value")
- Given two slots already filled, when the first slot is refocused and a different character is typed, then that slot holds only the new character. (zag: e2e/pin-input.e2e.ts: "[different] should allow only single character")
- Given a slot holding "1", when it is refocused and "1" typed again, then it still holds exactly one character. (zag: e2e/pin-input.e2e.ts: "[same] should allow only single character")
- Given all three slots filled, when the middle slot is refocused and a new character typed, then that slot takes the new value, the following slot keeps its old value, and focus advances to it. (zag: e2e/pin-input.e2e.ts: "[on edit] should allow to edit the existing value")
- Given numeric mode, when "a" or "!" is typed, then the slot stays empty and focus does not advance. (zag: e2e/pin-input.e2e.ts: "non-numeric chars should be rejected in numeric mode")
- Given `type="alphabetic"`, when "1" is typed then "a", then the digit is rejected and the letter is accepted with focus advancing. (zag: e2e/pin-input.e2e.ts: "alphabetic type: should reject numbers")
- Given the first slot is filled and focused, when Backspace is pressed, then focus stays on the first slot and its value is cleared. (zag: e2e/pin-input.e2e.ts: "backspace at index 0: should stay at first input")
- Given focus on an empty slot, when Delete is pressed, then nothing changes. (zag: e2e/pin-input.e2e.ts: "delete on empty slot: should do nothing")
- Given a filled slot, when Ctrl/Cmd+Backspace is used, then the slot clears, and Home followed by Delete also clears it - the native word-delete and forward-delete gestures are honored. (zag: e2e/pin-input.e2e.ts: "native delete keyboard behavior")
- Given "1","2","3" with the second slot selected, when Ctrl/Cmd+A then Ctrl/Cmd+X are pressed, then the cut splices the values left to "1","3","". (zag: e2e/pin-input.e2e.ts: "cut: should splice and shift values left (no holes)")
- Given all slots filled and the middle slot clicked, when a new character is typed, then it replaces that slot's value leaving the others intact. (zag: e2e/pin-input.e2e.ts: "complete then type: should replace focused value")
- The connect layer wires Backspace, Delete, ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, Enter, Home and End through a key map and also handles an "advance" path for same-key input. (zag: packages/machines/pin-input/src/pin-input.connect.ts)

### Pointer

- Given only the first slot is filled, when the third slot is clicked, then focus is redirected to the insertion point at slot two. (zag: e2e/pin-input.e2e.ts: "click: should redirect to insertion point when clicking past filled")
- Given all slots filled, when the first slot is clicked, then focus lands there, so filled slots stay directly clickable. (zag: e2e/pin-input.e2e.ts: "click: should allow clicking on filled slots")
- Given a filled pin input, when the clear button is clicked, then all values are cleared and focus returns to the first slot. (zag: e2e/pin-input.e2e.ts: "on clear: should clear values and focus first")
- Given clipboard permissions are granted and the first slot focused, when "123" is pasted, then every slot fills and focus lands on the last slot. (zag: e2e/pin-input.e2e.ts: "on paste: should autofill all fields")
- Given the first slot already holds a value, when "123" is pasted while it is focused, then the paste overwrites from the first slot. (zag: e2e/pin-input.e2e.ts: "on paste: should autofill when focused field is not empty")
- Given three slots, when a five-character string is pasted, then the value is truncated to the available slots. (zag: e2e/pin-input.e2e.ts: "on paste: should truncate to available slots")
- Given the first slot filled and focus on the second, when "89" is pasted, then the earlier value is preserved and the paste fills forward giving "1","8","9". (zag: e2e/pin-input.e2e.ts: "on paste: mid-sequence should preserve left values")
- Given a sanitizing example, when "1-2-3" is pasted, then dashes are stripped before filling. (zag: e2e/pin-input.e2e.ts: "sanitize value: should strip dashes before filling")

### Focus management

- Given the second slot is the insertion point, when Tab is pressed, then focus skips the remaining inputs and lands on the clear button. (zag: e2e/pin-input.e2e.ts: "roving tabindex: tab should skip remaining inputs")
- Given focus is on the clear button, when Shift+Tab is pressed, then focus re-enters at the insertion point. (zag: e2e/pin-input.e2e.ts: "roving tabindex: shift+tab should re-enter at insertion point")
- Given all slots are filled, when Shift+Tab re-enters the group, then focus lands on the last input. (zag: e2e/pin-input.e2e.ts: "roving tabindex: shift+tab with all filled should land on last input")
- Given `blurOnComplete`, when the last value is entered, then the last input is blurred. (zag: e2e/pin-input.e2e.ts: "blurOnComplete: should blur after entering last value")
- Given `blurOnComplete` and a completed pin, when the last input is clicked and Backspace pressed, then focus moves to the previous slot instead of blurring again. (zag: e2e/pin-input.e2e.ts: "blurOnComplete: backspace on last input should not blur")
- Given `autoFocus`, then the first input is focused on mount; Solid skips this case. (ark: packages/react/src/components/pin-input/tests/pin-input.test.tsx: "should autofocus the first input"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/pin-input/tests/pin-input.test.ts: "should autofocus the first input"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/pin-input/tests/pin-input.test.tsx: "should autofocus the first input")
- Given a pin input inside a Field, when the field label is clicked, then the first slot receives focus. (ark: packages/react/src/components/pin-input/tests/pin-input.test.tsx: "should focus on input when label is clicked"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/pin-input/tests/pin-input.test.ts: "should focus on input when label is clicked")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given a controlled pin input, when an external button sets the value, then all slots render "1","2","3". (zag: e2e/pin-input.e2e.ts: "should update inputs when value is set externally")
- Given an externally set value, when an external reset button is clicked, then all slots clear. (zag: e2e/pin-input.e2e.ts: "should clear inputs when reset externally")
- Given an externally set value, when a slot is clicked and retyped, then local typing still works after the external write. (zag: e2e/pin-input.e2e.ts: "should allow typing after external set")
- Given all slots are filled, then onValueComplete fires with both the array `['1','2','3']` and `valueAsString: '123'`. (ark: packages/react/src/components/pin-input/tests/pin-input.test.tsx: "should invoke onComplete when all inputs are filled out"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/pin-input/tests/pin-input.test.ts: "should invoke onValueComplete when all inputs are filled out")
- Given a completed pin, when the last slot is cleared and refilled with the same digit, then onValueComplete fires again. (ark: packages/react/src/components/pin-input/tests/pin-input.test.tsx: "should replace last input calls onComplete correctly"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/pin-input/tests/pin-input.test.ts: "should replace last input calls onValueComplete correctly")
- Solid has the backspace, onComplete, otp-autocomplete and replace-last cases commented out and its entire Field block commented out, so Solid only proves aria labels and forward focus movement. (ark: packages/solid/src/components/pin-input/tests/pin-input.test.tsx)
- Vue wraps every render in a `renderOnNextTick` helper that awaits `nextTick()` before asserting, because the machine's initial effects land after Vue's first flush. (ark: packages/vue/src/components/pin-input/tests/pin-input.test.ts)

### Forms

- Given all slots filled inside a form, then the form submits automatically and the handler logs, so completion triggers native submission. (zag: e2e/pin-input.e2e.ts: "auto submit: should submit form when all inputs filled")
- Given a pin input inside a Field, then required, disabled and readOnly reach the hidden input, helper text renders, and error text appears only when invalid.
