## editable

### Roles and attributes

- Anatomy parts are root, area, label, preview, input, editTrigger, submitTrigger, cancelTrigger, control. (zag: packages/machines/editable/src/editable.anatomy.ts)
- Area carries `data-focus` while editing, `data-disabled` and `data-placeholder-shown` when empty. (zag: packages/machines/editable/src/editable.connect.ts)
- Label carries `data-focus`, `data-invalid` and `data-required`. (zag: packages/machines/editable/src/editable.connect.ts)
- The input has a translated `aria-label`, the edit placeholder, `aria-invalid`, `data-invalid`, `data-disabled`, `data-readonly`, `data-autoresize`, and is `hidden` when not editing unless autoResize is on (in which case both preview and input stay mounted). (zag: packages/machines/editable/src/editable.connect.ts)
- The preview has `data-placeholder-shown`, `aria-readonly`, `data-readonly`, `data-disabled`, `aria-disabled`, `aria-invalid`, `data-invalid`, `data-autoresize`, a translated `aria-label`, `tabIndex` 0 when interactive, and is `hidden` while editing unless autoResize is on. (zag: packages/machines/editable/src/editable.connect.ts)
- The edit trigger is `type="button"` and hidden while editing; submit and cancel triggers are `type="button"` and hidden while not editing, each with a translated `aria-label`. (zag: packages/machines/editable/src/editable.connect.ts)
- The preview enters edit mode from click, focus or dblclick depending on activation mode, and each entry carries a distinct `src` so the machine can distinguish them. (zag: packages/machines/editable/src/editable.connect.ts)

### Keyboard

- Given edit mode entered from the preview, when Escape is pressed, then the current value is retained in the input. (zag: e2e/editable.e2e.ts: "on focus and blur, should retain current value")
- Given "Naruto" typed in edit mode, when Enter is pressed, then the preview shows "Naruto" and the input is no longer visible. (zag: e2e/editable.e2e.ts: "on type, should commit input value")
- Given "Naruto" typed in edit mode, when Escape is pressed, then the value reverts to "Hello World" and the input hides. (zag: e2e/editable.e2e.ts: "on type and esc, should revert value")
- The connect layer commits on Enter with an `src` of `keydown.enter` and cancels on Escape, with the Enter handling differing for multiline inputs. (zag: packages/machines/editable/src/editable.connect.ts)

### Pointer

- Given edit mode with "Naruto" typed, when the submit trigger is clicked, then the preview commits to "Naruto". (zag: e2e/editable.e2e.ts: "on type and click submit, should commit value")
- Given edit mode with "Naruto" typed, when a click lands outside, then the value is committed rather than discarded. (zag: e2e/editable.e2e.ts: "on type and click outside, should commit value")
- Given the edit trigger is clicked, then the input appears and takes focus. (zag: e2e/editable.e2e.ts: "on click edit, should enter edit mode")
- Given `activationMode="dblclick"`, when the preview is double-clicked and Escape pressed, then the value is retained. (zag: e2e/editable.e2e.ts: "[activationMode=dblclick] on focus and blur, should retain current value")
- Given `activationMode="dblclick"` and a placeholder preview, when it is double-clicked, then the input opens and a typed value plus Enter commits it. (ark: packages/react/src/components/editable/tests/editable.test.tsx: "should be possible to dbl click the placeholder to enter a value"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/editable/tests/editable.test.tsx: "should be possible to dbl click the placeholder to enter a value"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/editable/tests/editable.test.ts: "should be possible to dbl click the placeholder to enter a value")
- Given `activationMode="dblclick"` and an existing value, when the preview is double-clicked, the text cleared, a new value typed and Save clicked, then the new value is shown. (ark: packages/react/src/components/editable/tests/editable.test.tsx: "should be possible to edit an existing value"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/editable/tests/editable.test.tsx: "should be possible to edit an existing value"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/editable/tests/editable.test.ts: "should be possible to edit an existing value")
- Given edit mode, when the cancel trigger is clicked, then the input gains the `hidden` attribute, which is how "not editing" is expressed in the DOM. (ark: packages/react/src/components/editable/tests/editable.test.tsx: "should be possible to hide input if click EditableCancelTrigger "; ark: packages/solid/src/components/editable/tests/editable.test.tsx: "should be possible to hide input if click EditableCancelTrigger "; ark: packages/vue/src/components/editable/tests/editable.test.ts: "should be possible to hide input if click EditableCancelTrigger ")

### Focus management

## password-input

### Roles and attributes

- Anatomy parts are root, input, label, control, indicator, visibilityTrigger. (zag: packages/machines/password-input/src/password-input.anatomy.ts)
- Root, label, control and indicator carry `data-disabled`, `data-invalid` and `data-readonly`; label adds `data-required`. (zag: packages/machines/password-input/src/password-input.connect.ts)
- The input toggles `type` between `password` and `text`, exposes `data-state` of `hidden`/`visible`, sets `autoCapitalize="off"`, `spellCheck={false}`, `aria-invalid`, `data-disabled`, `data-invalid` and `data-readonly`. (zag: packages/machines/password-input/src/password-input.connect.ts)
- The visibility trigger is `type="button"` with `tabIndex={-1}`, `aria-controls` on the input id, `aria-expanded` reflecting visibility, `data-state`, `data-disabled`, `data-readonly` and a translated `aria-label` that changes with visibility. (zag: packages/machines/password-input/src/password-input.connect.ts)
- The indicator part is `aria-hidden` and mirrors `data-state`. (zag: packages/machines/password-input/src/password-input.connect.ts)
- The input carries password-manager opt-out attributes: `data-1p-ignore`, `data-lpignore="true"`, `data-bwignore="true"`, `data-form-type="other"` and `data-protonpass-ignore="true"`, which pin the quirks of 1Password, LastPass, Bitwarden, Dashlane and Proton Pass. (zag: packages/machines/password-input/src/password-input.connect.ts)

### Pointer

- Given a masked password input, when the visibility trigger is clicked, then the input type becomes `text`, and clicking again returns it to `password`. (zag: e2e/password-input.e2e.ts: "should toggle password visibility")

### Focus management

- Given "123456" typed and the caret moved one character left, when visibility is toggled twice, then the caret stays at position 5 both times, so the type swap does not reset the selection. (zag: e2e/password-input.e2e.ts: "preserve caret position when toggling password visibility")
- The visibility trigger is excluded from the tab order so Tab moves from the password field to the next control. (zag: packages/machines/password-input/src/password-input.connect.ts)

### Forms

- Given a password input inside an invalid Field, then the input has `aria-invalid="true"` and `data-invalid`, and the field's error message renders. (ark: packages/svelte/src/lib/components/password-input/tests/password-input-field.test.ts: "should propagate invalid state from Field.Root")

### Accessibility tooling

- Given the basic password input, when axe runs over the root, then there are no violations. (zag: e2e/password-input.e2e.ts: "should have no accessibility violation")

### Notes and edge cases

- Svelte is the only framework with a password-input test, and it covers only Field invalid propagation. (ark: packages/svelte/src/lib/components/password-input/tests/password-input-field.test.ts)

- The machine reads `aria-activedescendant` off the input to decide whether Enter should act on a highlighted tag or add a new one. (zag: packages/machines/tags-input/src/tags-input.connect.ts)
- Given a tag is added, then its text element carries `data-part="item-text"` and `data-scope="tags-input"`. ## autoresize

### Roles and attributes

- Autoresize is a utility (`@zag-js/auto-resize`) rather than a machine, so it has no anatomy and no data attributes; it adjusts the textarea height imperatively. (zag: packages/utilities/auto-resize/src)

### Pointer

- Given a textarea with a measured initial height, when six lines are typed, then the height grows by more than five pixels. (zag: e2e/autoresize.e2e.ts: "should grow textarea height as content increases")
- Given clipboard permissions, when six lines are pasted in one go, then the height also grows, so resize is not tied to keystrokes. (zag: e2e/autoresize.e2e.ts: "should grow textarea height when pasting multiline text")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given the controlled example, when text is typed, then both the textarea value and the rendered state value update. (zag: e2e/autoresize.e2e.ts: "should sync typed value to state")
- Given the controlled example, when text is pasted, then both the textarea value and the state value update. (zag: e2e/autoresize.e2e.ts: "should sync pasted value to state")
- Given "a" was typed then cleared through the clear button, when "a" is typed again, then the state value updates again rather than being swallowed as an unchanged value. (zag: e2e/autoresize.e2e.ts: "should update value after clear and retype same character")
- Given "a" was pasted then cleared, when "a" is pasted again, then the state value updates again. (zag: e2e/autoresize.e2e.ts: "should update value after clear and paste same text")

## file-upload

### Roles and attributes

- Anatomy parts are root, dropzone, item, itemDeleteTrigger, itemGroup, itemName, itemPreview, itemPreviewImage, itemSizeText, label, trigger, clearTrigger. (zag: packages/machines/file-upload/src/file-upload.anatomy.ts)
- Root carries `data-disabled`, `data-readonly` and `data-dragging`. (zag: packages/machines/file-upload/src/file-upload.connect.ts)
- The dropzone is `role="button"` by default and `role="application"` when `disableClick` is set, with a translated `aria-label`, `aria-disabled`, `data-invalid`, `data-disabled`, `data-readonly`, `data-dragging`, and `tabIndex` 0 unless disabled, readOnly or click-disabled. (zag: packages/machines/file-upload/src/file-upload.connect.ts)
- The trigger is `type="button"` with `data-disabled`, `data-readonly` and `data-invalid`. (zag: packages/machines/file-upload/src/file-upload.connect.ts)
- The hidden file input is `type="file"`, `aria-hidden`, `tabIndex={-1}`, with `accept` from the computed accept attribute and `multiple` set when multiple is true or maxFiles exceeds 1. (zag: packages/machines/file-upload/src/file-upload.connect.ts)
- Item group, item, itemName, itemSizeText, itemPreview, itemPreviewImage and itemDeleteTrigger all carry `data-disabled` and a `data-type` that distinguishes accepted from rejected files. (zag: packages/machines/file-upload/src/file-upload.connect.ts)
- The delete trigger per item is `type="button"` with a translated `aria-label` naming the file; the clear trigger is `type="button"` and hidden while there are no accepted files. (zag: packages/machines/file-upload/src/file-upload.connect.ts)
- The label carries `data-disabled`, `data-invalid` and `data-required`, and the api exposes `acceptedFiles`, `maxFilesReached` and `remainingFiles`. (zag: packages/machines/file-upload/src/file-upload.connect.ts)

### Keyboard

- Given the trigger is focused, when Enter opens the picker and Escape dismisses it, then only one filechooser event has fired across the next frame, so dismissing does not immediately reopen the picker. (zag: e2e/file-upload.e2e.ts: "should not reopen file picker after ESC key")

- Given the basic file upload, when the trigger is clicked, then the native file chooser opens. (zag: e2e/file-upload.e2e.ts: "should open file picker on trigger click")
- Given the file chooser is open, when a text file is selected, then the item list shows "text.txt" and a delete trigger appears. (zag: e2e/file-upload.e2e.ts: "should display chosen file"; zag: e2e/file-upload.e2e.ts: "should upload file via trigger click")

(ark: packages/react/src/components/file-upload/tests/file-upload.test.tsx: "should set file upload as required"; ark: packages/react/src/components/file-upload/tests/file-upload.test.tsx: "should set file upload as disabled"; ark: packages/react/src/components/file-upload/tests/file-upload.test.tsx: "should display helper text"; ark: packages/react/src/components/file-upload/tests/file-upload.test.tsx: "should display error text when error is present"; ark: packages/react/src/components/file-upload/tests/file-upload.test.tsx: "should not display error text when no error is present"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/file-upload/tests/file-upload.test.tsx: "should set file upload as required"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/file-upload/tests/file-upload.test.ts: "should set file upload as required")

(zag: e2e/file-upload.e2e.ts: "should have no accessibility violations"; ark: packages/react/src/components/file-upload/tests/file-upload.test.tsx: "should have no a11y violations")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given two files with different names in one batch, then both are accepted and nothing is rejected. (zag: packages/machines/file-upload/tests/get-event-files.test.ts: "accepts distinct files")
- Given the same file twice in one batch, then the second copy is rejected with the error `FILE_EXISTS`. (zag: packages/machines/file-upload/tests/get-event-files.test.ts: "rejects a file already accepted in the same batch")
- Given a file that matches one already accepted in an earlier batch, then it is rejected with `FILE_EXISTS`. (zag: packages/machines/file-upload/tests/get-event-files.test.ts: "rejects a file already accepted in an earlier batch")
- Given three files sharing a name but differing in size or type, then all three are accepted, because identity is the triple of name, size and type. (zag: packages/machines/file-upload/tests/get-event-files.test.ts: "treats name, size and type as the identity")
- Given a batch where the first file exceeds maxFileSize, then the later valid file is still accepted. (zag: packages/machines/file-upload/tests/get-event-files.test.ts: "a rejected file does not shadow a later valid one")
- Given a 50,000 file batch, then dedup completes in under a second, pinning the replacement of an O(n squared) dedup that previously took around 36 seconds. (zag: packages/machines/file-upload/tests/get-event-files.test.ts: "ingests a large directory without quadratic slowdown")
- Given every pair from a set of name/size/type variants, then `getFileKey` equality agrees exactly with `isFileEqual`. (zag: packages/machines/file-upload/tests/get-event-files.test.ts: "agrees with isFileEqual")
- The drag-and-drop e2e path has to prime the hidden input with `setInputFiles` and then build a DataTransfer from `input.files` inside the page, because Playwright cannot synthesize a real file drag. (zag: e2e/models/file-upload.model.ts)

## tabs

### Roles and attributes

- The anatomy declares the parts root, list, trigger, content and indicator, each emitting `data-scope="tabs"` and `data-part="<part>"`. (zag: packages/machines/tabs/src/tabs.anatomy.ts)
- Given a tabs root, when connect runs, then the root element carries the generated root id, `data-orientation` set to the orientation prop, `dir`, and `data-focus` while the machine is in the `focused` state. (zag: packages/machines/tabs/src/tabs.connect.ts)
- Given a tab list, when connect runs, then it carries `role="tablist"`, the generated list id, `dir`, `data-focus` while focused, `aria-orientation` and `data-orientation` both set to the orientation prop, and `aria-label` from `translations.listLabel`. (zag: packages/machines/tabs/src/tabs.connect.ts)
- Given a tab trigger, when connect runs, then it is normalized as a button with `role="tab"`, `type="button"`, `dir`, `data-orientation`, `data-value` set to the trigger value, `data-ownedby` set to the list id, and the generated trigger id. (zag: packages/machines/tabs/src/tabs.connect.ts)
- Given a disabled tab trigger, when connect runs, then it carries the native `disabled` attribute plus `data-disabled` and `aria-disabled`. (zag: packages/machines/tabs/src/tabs.connect.ts)
- Given a tab trigger whose value equals the selected value, when connect runs, then it carries `aria-selected="true"` and `data-selected`, and non-selected triggers carry `aria-selected="false"` with no `data-selected`. (zag: packages/machines/tabs/src/tabs.connect.ts)
- Given a tab trigger whose value equals the focused value, when connect runs, then it carries `data-focus`. (zag: packages/machines/tabs/src/tabs.connect.ts)
- Given a selected tab trigger, when connect runs, then `aria-controls` points at the matching content id, and unselected triggers omit `aria-controls` entirely. (zag: packages/machines/tabs/src/tabs.connect.ts)
- Given the machine is still in its SSR context, when connect runs, then the trigger carries `data-ssr`. (zag: packages/machines/tabs/src/tabs.connect.ts)
- Given the `composite` prop is true, when connect runs, then only the selected trigger has `tabIndex=0` and every other trigger has `tabIndex=-1`, implementing roving tabindex; when `composite` is false every trigger has `tabIndex=-1`. (zag: packages/machines/tabs/src/tabs.connect.ts)
- Given a tab content panel, when connect runs, then it carries `role="tabpanel"`, the generated content id, `aria-labelledby` pointing at its trigger id, `data-ownedby` set to the list id, `data-orientation`, `dir`, `data-selected` when selected, and the `hidden` attribute when not selected. (zag: packages/machines/tabs/src/tabs.connect.ts)
- Given the `composite` prop is true, when connect runs, then the content panel has `tabIndex=0`, otherwise `tabIndex=-1`. (zag: packages/machines/tabs/src/tabs.connect.ts)
- Given the indicator part, when connect runs, then it carries the generated indicator id, `dir`, `data-orientation`, and `hidden` whenever the tracked indicator rect is null or all of width, height, x and y are zero. (zag: packages/machines/tabs/src/tabs.connect.ts)
- Given the indicator part, when connect runs, then its inline style sets the custom properties `--transition-property` (to `left, right, top, bottom, width, height`), `--left`, `--top`, `--width` and `--height` (the tracked rect x/y/width/height converted to px). (zag: packages/machines/tabs/src/tabs.connect.ts)
- Given the indicator part, when connect runs, then its inline style sets `position: absolute`, `transitionTimingFunction: var(--transition-timing-function)`, and binds `left` to `var(--left)` for horizontal orientation or `top` to `var(--top)` for vertical orientation. (zag: packages/machines/tabs/src/tabs.connect.ts)
- Given indicator animation is enabled, when connect runs, then the indicator gets `willChange: var(--transition-property)`, `transitionProperty: var(--transition-property)` and `transitionDuration: var(--transition-duration, 150ms)`; when animation is disabled it gets `willChange: auto`, `transitionProperty: none` and `transitionDuration: 0ms`. (zag: packages/machines/tabs/src/tabs.connect.ts)
- Given a tabs widget rendered with triggers, an indicator and content panels, when axe analyses the root, then there are no accessibility violations. (zag: e2e/tabs.e2e.ts: "should have no accessibility violation"; ark: packages/react/src/components/tabs/tests/tabs.test.tsx: "should have no a11y violations")

### Keyboard

- Given a horizontal tab list with a focused tab, when ArrowRight is pressed, then focus and (in automatic activation mode) selection move to the next tab and its panel becomes visible. (zag: e2e/tabs.e2e.ts: "automatic: on arrow right, select + focus next tab")
- Given a horizontal tab list with a focused tab, when ArrowLeft is pressed, then focus and selection move to the previous tab and its panel becomes visible. (zag: e2e/tabs.e2e.ts: "automatic: on arrow left, select + focus the previous tab")
- Given a tab list, when Home is pressed, then focus moves to the first tab and, in automatic mode, that tab's panel becomes visible. (zag: e2e/tabs.e2e.ts: "on home key, select first tab")
- Given a tab list, when End is pressed, then focus moves to the last tab and, in automatic mode, that tab's panel becomes visible. (zag: e2e/tabs.e2e.ts: "on end key, select last tab")
- Given `activationMode="manual"`, when ArrowRight moves focus to the next tab, then that tab receives focus but its panel stays hidden. (zag: e2e/tabs.e2e.ts: "manual: on arrow right, focus but not select tab")
- Given `activationMode="manual"`, when Home moves focus to the first tab, then that tab receives focus but its panel stays hidden. (zag: e2e/tabs.e2e.ts: "manual: on home key, focus but not select tab")
- Given `activationMode="manual"` and focus moved by ArrowRight without selection, when Enter is pressed, then the focused tab is selected and its panel becomes visible. (zag: e2e/tabs.e2e.ts: "manual: on navigate, select on enter")
- Given `loopFocus=false` and the last tab focused, when ArrowRight is pressed, then focus stays on the last tab. (zag: e2e/tabs.e2e.ts: "loopFocus=false"; ark: packages/react/src/components/tabs/tests/tabs.test.tsx, packages/solid/src/components/tabs/tests/tabs.test.tsx, packages/vue/src/components/tabs/tests/tabs.test.ts: "should not loop focus if loop is false")
- Given loop focus is on by default and the last tab focused, when ArrowRight is pressed, then focus wraps to the first tab. (ark: packages/react/src/components/tabs/tests/tabs.test.tsx, packages/solid/src/components/tabs/tests/tabs.test.tsx, packages/vue/src/components/tabs/tests/tabs.test.ts: "should loop focus by default")
- Given `orientation="vertical"` and the first tab focused, when ArrowDown is pressed, then focus moves to the second tab. (ark: packages/react/src/components/tabs/tests/tabs.test.tsx, packages/solid/src/components/tabs/tests/tabs.test.tsx, packages/vue/src/components/tabs/tests/tabs.test.ts: "should handle orientation")
- Given loop focus is on and the first tab selected, when ArrowRight is pressed three times across three tabs, then focus and selection should return to the first tab, but the test is skipped as `@flaky` so the looping behavior is not actually verified. (zag: e2e/tabs.e2e.ts: "automatic: on arrow right, loop focus + selection")
- The list key handler maps ArrowDown/ArrowUp only when the orientation is vertical and ArrowLeft/ArrowRight only when the orientation is horizontal, plus Home and End in both orientations, and it calls `preventDefault()` for every handled key. (zag: packages/machines/tabs/src/tabs.connect.ts)
- Given a composition (IME) keydown event or an event whose target is outside the list, when the list key handler runs, then it returns without navigating. (zag: packages/machines/tabs/src/tabs.connect.ts)

### Pointer

- Given a tabs widget, when a tab trigger is clicked, then that tab is selected and its panel becomes visible. (zag: e2e/tabs.e2e.ts: "click tab, select tab", "automatic: should select the correct tab on click"; ark: packages/react/src/components/tabs/tests/tabs.test.tsx: "should show content when tab is activated"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/tabs/tests/tabs.test.tsx, packages/vue/src/components/tabs/tests/tabs.test.ts: "should show content when tab is activated")
- Given a tabs widget with an `onValueChange` callback, when a trigger is clicked, then the callback fires once with the clicked trigger's value. (ark: packages/react/src/components/tabs/tests/tabs.test.tsx, packages/solid/src/components/tabs/tests/tabs.test.tsx, packages/vue/src/components/tabs/tests/tabs.test.ts: "should activate tab on click")
- Given a disabled tab trigger, when it is clicked, then it does not receive focus and its content stays hidden. (ark: packages/react/src/components/tabs/tests/tabs.test.tsx, packages/solid/src/components/tabs/tests/tabs.test.tsx, packages/vue/src/components/tabs/tests/tabs.test.ts: "should not focus disabled tab")
- Given a trigger click that is a new-tab-opening click (modifier or middle click) or an already-prevented event, when the click handler runs, then no selection happens. (zag: packages/machines/tabs/src/tabs.connect.ts)
- Given Safari, when a tab trigger is clicked, then connect explicitly calls `focus()` on the trigger because Safari does not move focus to buttons on mouse down. (zag: packages/machines/tabs/src/tabs.connect.ts)

### Focus management

- Given a tab trigger, when it receives focus, then the machine records it as the focused value, and when it blurs to an element whose `role` is not `tab`, then the machine clears the focused value. (zag: packages/machines/tabs/src/tabs.connect.ts)
- Given the `api.focus()` method, when called, then it focuses the trigger for the currently selected value and does nothing when no value is selected. (zag: packages/machines/tabs/src/tabs.connect.ts)
- Given the arrow-key navigation moves selection in automatic mode, when navigation completes, then the newly selected trigger is the focused element (roving focus follows selection). (zag: e2e/tabs.e2e.ts: "automatic: on arrow right, select + focus next tab", "automatic: on arrow left, select + focus the previous tab")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given `deselectable=true`, when the already selected tab is clicked again, then its panel is hidden, and clicking it a third time selects it again. (zag: e2e/tabs.e2e.ts: "should deselect")
- Given a `defaultValue`, when the component mounts, then that tab's content is rendered and visible without interaction. (ark: packages/react/src/components/tabs/tests/tabs.test.tsx: "should render the content of tab when active"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/tabs/tests/tabs.test.ts: "should render the content of tab when active")
- Given a controlled `value` prop (Solid) or `modelValue` (Vue), when the component mounts, then the matching content is visible. (ark: packages/solid/src/components/tabs/tests/tabs.test.tsx: "should render the content of tab when active"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/tabs/tests/tabs.test.ts: "should render the content of tab when active")
- The imperative api exposes `setValue`, `clearValue`, `setIndicatorRect(value)`, `syncTabIndex()`, `selectNext(fromValue)`, `selectPrev(fromValue)` and `focus()`, plus the readable `value` and `focusedValue`. (zag: packages/machines/tabs/src/tabs.connect.ts)
- Vue's two tab tests share the name "should render the content of tab when active", one covering `defaultValue` and one covering `modelValue`, so the duplicated name hides two distinct behaviors. (ark: packages/vue/src/components/tabs/tests/tabs.test.ts: "should render the content of tab when active")

### Animation and presence

- Given `lazyMount`, when the component mounts, then the tab content is absent from the DOM and only appears after its trigger is clicked. (ark: packages/react/src/components/tabs/tests/tabs.test.tsx, packages/solid/src/components/tabs/tests/tabs.test.tsx, packages/vue/src/components/tabs/tests/tabs.test.ts: "should lazy mount a tab")
- Given `lazyMount` plus `unmountOnExit`, when a tab is opened and then another tab is clicked, then the first tab's content is removed from the DOM again. (ark: packages/react/src/components/tabs/tests/tabs.test.tsx, packages/solid/src/components/tabs/tests/tabs.test.tsx, packages/vue/src/components/tabs/tests/tabs.test.ts: "should lazy mount and unmount on exit a tab")
- Given the indicator element, when its CSS transition finishes, then an `INDICATOR_TRANSITION_END` event is sent, and transition-end events bubbled from descendants are ignored. (zag: packages/machines/tabs/src/tabs.connect.ts)
- Given a selected tab and a measured indicator, when an unrelated inactive tab's label text is replaced with much longer text so the tab list reflows, then the indicator re-measures and ends up aligned with the still-selected tab within a 2px tolerance, with all running animations awaited before asserting. (zag: e2e/tabs.e2e.ts: "indicator position updates when inactive tab changes size")

### RTL and i18n

- Every tabs part (root, list, trigger, content, indicator) receives the `dir` prop so RTL is propagated to each element. (zag: packages/machines/tabs/src/tabs.connect.ts)
- The list key handler resolves keys through `getEventKey` with both `dir` and `orientation`, so ArrowLeft and ArrowRight swap meaning under `dir="rtl"`. (zag: packages/machines/tabs/src/tabs.connect.ts)
- The tab list's `aria-label` comes from `translations.listLabel`, the only translated string in the component. (zag: packages/machines/tabs/src/tabs.connect.ts)

### SSR and hydration

- Given server rendering, when connect runs before hydration, then triggers carry `data-ssr` and the indicator is `hidden` because no rect has been measured yet. (zag: packages/machines/tabs/src/tabs.connect.ts)

### Notes and edge cases

- The e2e model reads the indicator through the attribute selector `[data-scope='tabs'][data-part='indicator']` rather than a test id, pinning the scope/part attribute pair as public contract. (zag: e2e/models/tabs.model.ts)
- The indicator alignment helpers compare only the x coordinate of the tab and indicator rects, with a fixed 2px tolerance constant. (zag: e2e/models/tabs.model.ts)

## steps

### Roles and attributes

- The anatomy declares the parts root, list, item, trigger, indicator, separator, content, nextTrigger, prevTrigger and progress, each emitting `data-scope="steps"` and `data-part="<part>"`. (zag: packages/machines/steps/src/steps.anatomy.ts)
- Given a steps root, when connect runs, then it carries the generated root id, `dir`, `data-orientation`, and an inline style setting the custom property `--percent` to the completion percentage followed by `%`. (zag: packages/machines/steps/src/steps.connect.ts)
- Given a steps list, when connect runs, then it carries `role="tablist"`, the generated list id, `dir`, `aria-owns` listing every step trigger id space-separated, `aria-orientation` and `data-orientation`. (zag: packages/machines/steps/src/steps.connect.ts)
- Given a step item, when connect runs, then it carries `dir`, `data-orientation`, `aria-current="step"` only on the current step, and `data-skippable` when `isStepSkippable(index)` returns true. (zag: packages/machines/steps/src/steps.connect.ts)
- Given a step trigger, when connect runs, then it is normalized as a button with `role="tab"`, `type="button"`, the generated trigger id, `dir`, `aria-selected` reflecting whether it is the current step, `aria-controls` pointing at its content id, `data-state` of `open` on the current step and `closed` otherwise, `data-orientation`, and the mutually exclusive `data-complete`, `data-current` and `data-incomplete` markers. (zag: packages/machines/steps/src/steps.connect.ts)
- Given the `linear` prop is true, when connect runs, then only the current step trigger has `tabIndex=0` and all others get `tabIndex=-1`; when `linear` is false every trigger has `tabIndex=0`. (zag: packages/machines/steps/src/steps.connect.ts)
- Given a step content panel, when connect runs, then it carries `role="tabpanel"`, its content id, `dir`, `tabIndex=0` unconditionally, `aria-labelledby` pointing at its trigger id, `data-state` open/closed, `data-orientation`, and the `hidden` attribute when it is not the current step. (zag: packages/machines/steps/src/steps.connect.ts)
- Given a step indicator, when connect runs, then it carries `aria-hidden="true"` plus `data-complete`, `data-current` and `data-incomplete`. (zag: packages/machines/steps/src/steps.connect.ts)
- Given a step separator, when connect runs, then it carries `dir`, `data-orientation`, `data-complete`, `data-current` and `data-incomplete`. (zag: packages/machines/steps/src/steps.connect.ts)
- Given the next trigger, when connect runs, then it is a `type="button"` element that is `disabled` whenever there is no next step; the prev trigger is `disabled` whenever there is no previous step. (zag: packages/machines/steps/src/steps.connect.ts)
- Given the progress part, when connect runs, then it carries `role="progressbar"`, `aria-valuenow` set to the completion percent, `aria-valuemin=0`, `aria-valuemax=100`, `aria-valuetext` of `"<percent>% complete"`, and `data-complete` once the percent reaches 100. (zag: packages/machines/steps/src/steps.connect.ts)

### Keyboard

- Steps exposes no key handler of its own; navigation happens only through trigger clicks and the next/prev trigger buttons, so there is no roving-focus or arrow-key contract to conform to. (zag: packages/machines/steps/src/steps.connect.ts)

### Pointer

- Given a non-linear steps widget, when a step trigger is clicked, then the machine jumps to that step index; when `linear` is true the click handler returns early and the step does not change. (zag: packages/machines/steps/src/steps.connect.ts)
- Given the next trigger, when clicked, then the machine advances one step; given the prev trigger, when clicked, then it goes back one step. Both handlers bail out on an already-prevented event. (zag: packages/machines/steps/src/steps.connect.ts)

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- The imperative api exposes `value`, `count`, `percent`, `hasNextStep`, `hasPrevStep`, `isCompleted`, `isStepValid(index)`, `isStepSkippable(index)`, `goToNextStep()`, `goToPrevStep()`, `resetStep()`, `setStep(value)` and `getItemState(props)`. (zag: packages/machines/steps/src/steps.connect.ts)
- Given an item index, when `getItemState` is called, then it reports `current`, `completed` (index below the step), `incomplete` (index above the step), `first`, `last` (index equal to `count - 1`), `skippable`, `isValid()`, the trigger id and the content id. (zag: packages/machines/steps/src/steps.connect.ts)
- `isStepValid(index)` defaults to true and `isStepSkippable(index)` defaults to false when the corresponding props are not supplied. (zag: packages/machines/steps/src/steps.connect.ts)

### RTL and i18n

- Every steps part receives the `dir` prop. Note the prev trigger spreads `dir` before its part attributes while every other part spreads it after, so a part-level `dir` would win there and not elsewhere. (zag: packages/machines/steps/src/steps.connect.ts)

### Accessibility tooling

- Steps has no Zag e2e spec and no Ark unit test in any of react, solid, vue or svelte, so none of its behavior or its progressbar/tablist wiring is covered by an executed test anywhere in either repo. (zag: packages/machines/steps/src/steps.connect.ts)

## pagination

### Roles and attributes

- The anatomy declares the parts root, item, ellipsis, firstTrigger, prevTrigger, nextTrigger and lastTrigger, each emitting `data-scope="pagination"` and `data-part="<part>"`. (zag: packages/machines/pagination/src/pagination.anatomy.ts)
- Given a pagination root, when connect runs, then it carries the generated root id, `dir`, and `aria-label` defaulting to `"pagination"`. (zag: packages/machines/pagination/src/pagination.connect.ts)
- Given an ellipsis, when connect runs, then it carries an index-scoped ellipsis id and `dir` and nothing else. (zag: packages/machines/pagination/src/pagination.connect.ts)
- Given a page item, when connect runs, then it carries a page-scoped item id, `dir`, `data-index` set to the page number, `data-selected` when it is the current page, `aria-current="page"` only on the current page, and `aria-label` from `translations.itemLabel`. (zag: packages/machines/pagination/src/pagination.connect.ts)
- The default `itemLabel` produces `"page <n>"`, and `"last page, page <n>"` when there is more than one page and `n` is the last page. (zag: packages/machines/pagination/src/pagination.connect.ts)
- Given `type="button"`, when connect runs, then every item and trigger gets `type="button"`; given `type="link"` with a `getPageUrl` prop, then each item and trigger gets an `href` computed from its target page and the current page size. (zag: packages/machines/pagination/src/pagination.connect.ts)
- Given the prev and first triggers, when connect runs, then each carries its own generated id, `dir`, `data-disabled` while on page 1, and `aria-label` of `"previous page"` / `"first page"`; under `type="button"` they also get the native `disabled` attribute on page 1. (zag: packages/machines/pagination/src/pagination.connect.ts)
- Given the next and last triggers, when connect runs, then each carries its own generated id, `dir`, `data-disabled` once the page is at or past the total page count, and `aria-label` of `"next page"` / `"last page"`; under `type="button"` they also get the native `disabled` attribute there. (zag: packages/machines/pagination/src/pagination.connect.ts)
- Given `type="link"`, when connect runs, then the prev trigger only gets an `href` if a previous page exists and the next trigger only if a next page exists, while the first trigger always links to page 1 and the last trigger always links to `totalPages`. (zag: packages/machines/pagination/src/pagination.connect.ts)
- Given a pagination widget with `count=100` and `pageSize=10`, when axe analyses it, then there are no accessibility violations. (zag: e2e/pagination.e2e.ts: "should have no accessibility violation"; ark: packages/react/src/components/pagination/tests/pagination.test.tsx: "should have no a11y violations")

### Pointer

- Given a pagination widget on page 1, when the item for page 2 is clicked, then that item gains `aria-current="page"` and page 1 loses it. (zag: e2e/pagination.e2e.ts: "should update page when item is clicked"; ark: packages/react/src/components/pagination/tests/pagination.test.tsx, packages/solid/src/components/pagination/tests/pagination.test.tsx, packages/vue/src/components/pagination/tests/pagination.test.ts: "should update page when item is clicked")
- Given a pagination widget, when a page item is clicked, then that item also gains the `data-selected` attribute. (zag: e2e/pagination.e2e.ts: "should update page when item is clicked")
- Given page 1 is current, when the next trigger is clicked, then page 2 becomes current. (zag: e2e/pagination.e2e.ts: "should update page when next button is clicked"; ark: packages/react/src/components/pagination/tests/pagination.test.tsx, packages/solid/src/components/pagination/tests/pagination.test.tsx, packages/vue/src/components/pagination/tests/pagination.test.ts: "should update page when next button is clicked")
- Given the next trigger is clicked four times from page 1, when page 5 is reached, then the item for page 5 carries `data-selected`, and clicking next once more then prev once returns to page 5. (zag: e2e/pagination.e2e.ts: "should update page when prev button is clicked")
- Given page 5 is current, when the prev trigger is clicked three times, then page 2 is current. (zag: e2e/pagination.e2e.ts: "should update page when prev button is clicked")
- Given page 2 is current, when the prev trigger is clicked, then page 1 becomes current. (ark: packages/react/src/components/pagination/tests/pagination.test.tsx, packages/solid/src/components/pagination/tests/pagination.test.tsx, packages/vue/src/components/pagination/tests/pagination.test.ts: "should update page when prev button is clicked")
- Given an `onPageChange` handler wired to a page output, when a page item is clicked, then the handler reports the clicked page number. (zag: e2e/pagination.e2e.ts: "should call onChange when item is clicked")
- Given an `onPageChange` handler, when the next trigger is clicked from page 1, then the handler reports page 2. (zag: e2e/pagination.e2e.ts: "should call onChange when next button is clicked")
- Given an `onPageChange` handler and page 5 selected, when the prev trigger is clicked, then the handler reports page 4. (zag: e2e/pagination.e2e.ts: "should call onChange when prev button is clicked")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- The imperative api exposes `count`, `page`, `pageSize`, `totalPages`, `pages`, `previousPage`, `nextPage`, `pageRange`, `slice(data)`, `setPageSize(size)`, `setPage(page)`, `goToNextPage()`, `goToPrevPage()`, `goToFirstPage()` and `goToLastPage()`. (zag: packages/machines/pagination/src/pagination.connect.ts)
- Given a data array, when `api.slice(data)` is called, then it returns the array sliced by the computed `pageRange.start` and `pageRange.end`. (zag: packages/machines/pagination/src/pagination.connect.ts)
- Given the `range(start, end)` util, when called with 1 and 5, then it returns `[1, 2, 3, 4, 5]`. (zag: packages/machines/pagination/tests/pagination.utils.test.ts: "range method")
- Given the `transform` util and the mixed input `[1, 2, "ellipsis", 3, 4]`, when called, then every number becomes `{ type: "page", value: n }` and the string becomes `{ type: "ellipsis" }` with no value key. (zag: packages/machines/pagination/tests/pagination.utils.test.ts: "transform method")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given `siblingCount=1`, `boundaryCount=1`, `totalPages=0` and page 0, when `getRange` is called, then it returns an empty array. (zag: packages/machines/pagination/tests/pagination.utils.test-cases.ts: "getRange method")
- Given `siblingCount=1`, `boundaryCount=1` and `totalPages=1`, when page is 1, then the range is `[1]`. (zag: packages/machines/pagination/tests/pagination.utils.test-cases.ts: "getRange method")
- Given `siblingCount=1`, `boundaryCount=1` and `totalPages=2`, when page is 1 or 2, then the range is `[1, 2]`. (zag: packages/machines/pagination/tests/pagination.utils.test-cases.ts: "getRange method")
- Given `siblingCount=1`, `boundaryCount=1` and `totalPages=3`, when page is 1, 2 or 3, then the range is `[1, 2, 3]`. (zag: packages/machines/pagination/tests/pagination.utils.test-cases.ts: "getRange method")
- Given `siblingCount=1`, `boundaryCount=1` and `totalPages=4`, when page is 1, then the range is `[1, 2, 3, 4]`. (zag: packages/machines/pagination/tests/pagination.utils.test-cases.ts: "getRange method")
- Given `siblingCount=1`, `boundaryCount=1` and `totalPages=4`, when page is 2 or 3, then the range is `[1, 2, 3, 4]`. (zag: packages/machines/pagination/tests/pagination.utils.test-cases.ts: "getRange method")
