## splitter

### Roles and attributes

- The anatomy declares the parts root, panel, resizeTrigger and resizeTriggerIndicator, each emitting `data-scope="splitter"` and `data-part="<part>"` with the resize trigger parts serialized as `resize-trigger` and `resize-trigger-indicator`. (zag: packages/machines/splitter/src/splitter.anatomy.ts)
- Given a splitter root, when connect runs, then it carries the generated root id, `dir`, `data-orientation`, `data-dragging` while the machine is dragging, and an inline style of `display: flex`, `flexDirection` row for horizontal or column for vertical, `height: 100%`, `width: 100%` and `overflow: hidden`. (zag: packages/machines/splitter/src/splitter.connect.ts)
- Given a panel, when connect runs, then it carries a panel-scoped id, `dir`, `data-orientation`, `data-dragging` while dragging, `data-id` set to the panel id, `data-index` set to its position in the panels array, and `data-ownedby` set to the root id. (zag: packages/machines/splitter/src/splitter.connect.ts)
- Given a resize trigger, when connect runs, then it carries `role="separator"`, a trigger-scoped id, `dir`, `data-id`, `data-ownedby`, `data-orientation` and `aria-orientation` both set to the orientation, and `tabIndex=0` unless the trigger is disabled, in which case `tabIndex` is omitted entirely. (zag: packages/machines/splitter/src/splitter.connect.ts)
- Given a resize trigger identified as `before:after`, when connect runs, then `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax` are the rounded percentage size of the panel before the handle and its allowed range, and `aria-controls` lists the ids of the panels on both sides space-separated. (zag: packages/machines/splitter/src/splitter.connect.ts; zag: packages/machines/splitter/src/utils/aria.ts)
- Given a handle id that names only one side, when connect resolves it, then it is completed into a `before:after` pair using the neighboring panel; when either side cannot be resolved, `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` and `aria-controls` are all left undefined. (zag: packages/machines/splitter/src/splitter.connect.ts; zag: packages/machines/splitter/src/utils/aria.ts)
- Given a set of panels, when aria values are calculated, then `aria-valuemax` is `min(currentMaxSize, 100 - sum of other panels' minSize)` and `aria-valuemin` is `max(currentMinSize, 100 - sum of other panels' maxSize)`, with panels defaulting to minSize 0 and maxSize 100. (zag: packages/machines/splitter/src/utils/aria.ts)
- Given a resize trigger, when connect runs, then it carries `data-focus` while focused or dragging, `data-dragging` while this specific handle is the drag target, and `data-disabled` when disabled. (zag: packages/machines/splitter/src/splitter.connect.ts)
- Given a resize trigger indicator, when connect runs, then it carries `data-orientation`, `data-ownedby`, and the same `data-focus`, `data-dragging` and `data-disabled` markers as its trigger. (zag: packages/machines/splitter/src/splitter.connect.ts)
- Given a resize trigger, when connect runs, then its inline style sets `touchAction: none`, `userSelect`/`WebkitUserSelect: none`, `flex: 0 0 auto`, and `minHeight: 0` for horizontal splitters or `minWidth: 0` for vertical ones. (zag: packages/machines/splitter/src/splitter.connect.ts)
- Given a resize trigger, when connect runs, then its cursor is `col-resize` for horizontal and `row-resize` for vertical, and is left unset when the trigger is disabled or when a registry is in use. (zag: packages/machines/splitter/src/splitter.connect.ts)
- Given a resize trigger, when connect runs, then `pointerEvents` is `none` if it is disabled, `none` if it is dragging but not focused, and otherwise unset. (zag: packages/machines/splitter/src/splitter.connect.ts)
- Given a drag in progress, when panel styles are computed, then every panel gets `pointerEvents: none` so nested iframes cannot swallow the drag. (zag: packages/machines/splitter/src/utils/panel.ts)
- Given `orientation="vertical"` is selected, when the tree re-renders, then the root, the first panel and the first resize trigger should each carry `data-orientation="vertical"`, but all three assertions are written without `await` in front of `expect(locator).toHaveAttribute(...)`, so they never actually run and the behavior is not verified. (zag: e2e/splitter.e2e.ts: "should manage splitter panels when vertical orientation")
- Given a two-panel splitter with one resize trigger, when the component renders, then both panel labels are present and a single element with `role="separator"` exists. (ark: packages/react/src/components/splitter/splitter.test.tsx: "should render the component")
- Given a two-panel splitter, when axe analyses it, then there are no accessibility violations. (zag: e2e/splitter.e2e.ts: "should have no accessibility violations"; ark: packages/react/src/components/splitter/splitter.test.tsx, packages/solid/src/components/splitter/tests/splitter.test.tsx: "should have no a11y violations")

### Keyboard

- Given a horizontal splitter and a focused resize trigger, when ArrowRight is pressed, then the handle moves by the resize step so the panel before it grows by that many percent and `aria-valuenow` increases by one step. (zag: e2e/splitter.e2e.ts: "should resize with keyboard when focused after hover")
- Given a pointer-focused resize trigger, when ArrowRight is pressed, then `aria-valuenow` increments by exactly one, confirming the default keyboard step of 1 percent. (zag: e2e/splitter.e2e.ts: "should keep pointer focus without showing keyboard focus styles")
- The keyboard step is 10 when Shift is held, otherwise the `keyboardResizeBy` prop when set, otherwise 1. (zag: packages/machines/splitter/src/splitter.connect.ts)
- Given a horizontal splitter, when ArrowLeft or ArrowRight is pressed on a handle, then the delta is applied on the horizontal axis and ArrowUp/ArrowDown produce a delta of zero; for a vertical splitter the axes swap. (zag: packages/machines/splitter/src/splitter.connect.ts)
- Given a focused handle, when Home is pressed, then a keyboard move of -100 is sent (collapse to one extreme) and End sends +100 (expand to the other extreme). (zag: packages/machines/splitter/src/splitter.connect.ts)
- Given a focused handle, when Enter is pressed, then an `ENTER` event is sent, which the machine uses to toggle a collapsible panel. (zag: packages/machines/splitter/src/splitter.connect.ts)
- Given a focused handle, when F6 is pressed, then a `FOCUS.CYCLE` event is sent carrying the Shift state so focus cycles forward or backward through handles. (zag: packages/machines/splitter/src/splitter.connect.ts)
- Every handled key calls `preventDefault()` after dispatching, and keys are resolved through `getEventKey` with `dir` and `orientation` so arrow semantics flip under RTL. (zag: packages/machines/splitter/src/splitter.connect.ts)
- Given a click on the splitter root, when Tab is pressed, then the next resize trigger should carry `data-focus`, but the assertion is written without `await` so it never runs; additionally the test targets the second trigger (`trigger-b:c`) while a single Tab from the root lands on the first one. (zag: e2e/splitter.e2e.ts: "should be focused on next splitter when tabbed")
- Given a three-panel splitter, when Tab then ArrowRight are pressed three times, then the second resize trigger should report `aria-valuenow="36"`, but the `expect` is not awaited so nothing is verified, and the expected value is inconsistent with growing the first panel (which shrinks the middle panel instead). (zag: e2e/splitter.e2e.ts: "should increase panel when arrow right pressed")
- Given a three-panel splitter, when Tab then ArrowLeft are pressed three times, then the second resize trigger should report `aria-valuenow="30"`, but again the `expect` is not awaited and the value looks swapped with the ArrowRight case. (zag: e2e/splitter.e2e.ts: "should decrease panel when arrow left pressed")
- Given a focused resize trigger and an `onResizeEnd` callback, when ArrowRight is pressed, then the callback should fire, but the test is skipped (and passes the handler to the wrong prop name), so resize callbacks are not verified. (ark: packages/react/src/components/splitter/splitter.test.tsx: "should call onResizeStart callback")

### Pointer

- Given a resize trigger, when a left-button pointer down occurs, then connect focuses the trigger with `preventScroll: true` and `focusVisible: false` before starting the drag, explicitly to work around Safari not focusing non-form elements on pointer down. (zag: packages/machines/splitter/src/splitter.connect.ts)
- Given a resize trigger, when the drag starts, then it calls `setPointerCapture` for the pointer id and both prevents default and stops propagation; pointer up releases the capture if it is still held. (zag: packages/machines/splitter/src/splitter.connect.ts)
- Given a non-left-button pointer down, when the handler runs, then nothing happens; on a disabled trigger the event is only prevented. (zag: packages/machines/splitter/src/splitter.connect.ts)
- Given a registry is configured, when pointer down fires, then connect focuses the trigger and returns, leaving pointer handling and hover tracking to the registry. (zag: packages/machines/splitter/src/splitter.connect.ts)
- Given a resize trigger, when the pointer moves over or leaves it, then `POINTER_OVER` and `POINTER_LEAVE` are sent unless the trigger is disabled or a registry is in use. (zag: packages/machines/splitter/src/splitter.connect.ts)
- Given a resize trigger dragged 20px to the right with a real mouse down, move and up, then the trigger keeps DOM focus but does not match `:focus-visible`, so keyboard focus rings stay hidden after a pointer resize, and a following ArrowRight still increments `aria-valuenow` by one. (zag: e2e/splitter.e2e.ts: "should keep pointer focus without showing keyboard focus styles")

### Focus management

- Given a button placed before the splitter and focused, when the first resize trigger is hovered and Tab is pressed, then the resize trigger becomes the focused element and is immediately keyboard-resizable, a regression guard for hover state stealing focus tracking. (zag: e2e/splitter.e2e.ts: "should resize with keyboard when focused after hover")
- Given a resize trigger, when it receives focus it sends `FOCUS` with its id and when it blurs it sends `BLUR`, and both handlers return early for a disabled trigger. (zag: packages/machines/splitter/src/splitter.connect.ts)
- A handle reports `focused` when it is the drag target, or when the machine is in the `focused` state and the keyboard state names that handle. (zag: packages/machines/splitter/src/splitter.connect.ts)

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- The imperative api exposes `dragging`, `orientation`, `getPanels()`, `getPanelById(id)`, `getItems()`, `getSizes()`, `setSizes(size)`, `resetSizes()`, `collapsePanel(id)`, `expandPanel(id, minSize)`, `resizePanel(id, size)`, `getPanelSize(id)`, `isPanelCollapsed(id)`, `isPanelExpanded(id)` and `getLayout()`. (zag: packages/machines/splitter/src/splitter.connect.ts)
- Given a list of panels, when `getItems()` is called, then it returns an alternating sequence of `{ type: "panel" }` and `{ type: "handle", id: "before:after" }` entries with no trailing handle after the last panel. (zag: packages/machines/splitter/src/splitter.connect.ts)
- Given a collapsible panel, when its resolved size fuzzily equals its `collapsedSize` (defaulting to 0), then `isPanelCollapsed` is true; `isPanelExpanded` is true for any non-collapsible panel or when the size is fuzzily greater than the collapsed size. (zag: packages/machines/splitter/src/splitter.connect.ts)
- Given `getLayout()`, when called, then it returns the panel ids sorted alphabetically and joined with `:`. (zag: packages/machines/splitter/src/utils/panel.ts)

### SSR and hydration

- Given a panel with `defaultSize="240px"`, `minSize="200px"` and `maxSize="360px"` and no resolved sizes yet, when the server-side flex style is computed, then it is `flexBasis: "clamp(200px, 240px, 360px)"`, `flexGrow: "0"`, `flexShrink: 0`, `minWidth: "200px"` and `maxWidth: "360px"`. (zag: packages/machines/splitter/tests/splitter.utils.test.ts: "serializes css unit sizes for server style fallback")
- Given a vertical panel with a numeric `defaultSize` of 35 and `minSize` 20 and no resolved sizes, when the server-side flex style is computed, then it is `flexBasis: 0`, `flexGrow: "35.0"`, `flexShrink: 1` and `minHeight: "20%"`, so percentage sizes become flex-grow weights rather than a basis. (zag: packages/machines/splitter/tests/splitter.utils.test.ts: "serializes percent sizes as flex grow for server style fallback")
- Given no layout size at all and no resolved size, when the flex style is computed, then `flexGrow` is `"1"`; a single-panel group always gets `flexGrow: "1"` regardless of its configured size. (zag: packages/machines/splitter/src/utils/panel.ts)
- Given mixed server sizes of `["240px", 60]` for two panels with no root element, when sizes are resolved, then the pixel value cannot be measured and the result is `[40, 60]`, the unmeasurable panel taking the remaining percentage. (zag: packages/machines/splitter/tests/splitter.utils.test.ts: "resolves missing server sizes to remaining percentages")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given a collapsible panel currently collapsed with `collapsedSize: 5`, `minSize: 10`, `maxSize: 20` and resolved sizes `[5, 95]`, when the flex style is computed, then the min constraint uses the collapsed size: `flexGrow: "5.00"`, `minWidth: "5%"`, `maxWidth: "20%"`. (zag: packages/machines/splitter/tests/splitter.utils.test.ts: "uses collapsedSize for min constraint when panel is collapsed")
- Given a collapsed panel whose sizes are CSS units (`collapsedSize: "40px"`, `minSize: "200px"`, `maxSize: "360px"`) and resolved sizes `[8, 92]`, when the flex style is computed, then it is `flexGrow: "8.00"`, `minWidth: "40px"` and `maxWidth: "360px"`. (zag: packages/machines/splitter/tests/splitter.utils.test.ts: "uses collapsedSize CSS units for min constraint when collapsed")
- Given the same collapsible panel while expanded with resolved sizes `[15, 85]`, when the flex style is computed, then the min constraint reverts to `minSize`: `flexGrow: "15.0"`, `minWidth: "10%"`, `maxWidth: "20%"`. (zag: packages/machines/splitter/tests/splitter.utils.test.ts: "uses minSize for min constraint when panel is expanded")
- Given `toCssPanelSize`, when called with the number 20 or the string `"20"`, then it returns `"20%"`; `"12rem"` passes through unchanged and `" 25vw "` is trimmed to `"25vw"`. (zag: packages/machines/splitter/tests/splitter.utils.test.ts: "normalizes css panel size values")
- Given a two-panel layout of `[25, 75]` where the first panel has `resizeBehavior: "preserve-pixel-size"`, when the group shrinks from 1000px to 500px, then the layout becomes `[50, 50]` because the fixed panel keeps its 250px while the relative panel absorbs the change. (zag: packages/machines/splitter/tests/splitter.utils.test.ts: "preserves fixed pixel-size panels across group resize")
- Given a previous or next group size of zero or below, when fixed panel sizes are preserved, then the previous layout is returned untouched; when no relative panels exist the fixed sizes are rescaled to total 100. (zag: packages/machines/splitter/src/utils/preserve-fixed-panel-sizes.ts)
- Panel flex sizes are serialized with `toPrecision(3)` by default, which is why the expected `flexGrow` strings in the unit tests are `"35.0"`, `"5.00"`, `"8.00"` and `"15.0"` rather than plain integers. (zag: packages/machines/splitter/src/utils/panel.ts)
- Every panel gets `overflow: hidden` so its content cannot force it wider than its computed size. (zag: packages/machines/splitter/src/utils/panel.ts)
- Ark vue ships a `splitter.test.vue` fixture with a two-panel splitter and a labeled resize trigger, but there is no sibling `splitter.test.ts` that mounts it, so the vue splitter has no executed tests at all. (ark: packages/vue/src/components/splitter/tests/splitter.test.vue)
- Ark solid covers only the axe check for splitter; no solid, vue or svelte test exercises dragging, keyboard resize, or collapse. (ark: packages/solid/src/components/splitter/tests/splitter.test.tsx: "should have no a11y violations")

## tree-view

### Roles and attributes

- The anatomy declares the parts branch, branchContent, branchControl, branchIndentGuide, branchIndicator, branchText, branchTrigger, item, itemIndicator, itemText, label, nodeCheckbox, nodeRenameInput, root and tree, each emitting `data-scope="tree-view"` and `data-part="<part>"` with camelCase names serialized as `branch-content`, `branch-control`, `branch-indent-guide`, `branch-indicator`, `branch-text`, `branch-trigger`, `item-indicator`, `item-text`, `node-checkbox` and `node-rename-input`. (zag: packages/machines/tree-view/src/tree-view.anatomy.ts)
- Given a tree-view root, when connect runs, then it carries the generated root id and `dir` only; the label part carries the label id and `dir`. (zag: packages/machines/tree-view/src/tree-view.connect.ts)
- Given the tree part, when connect runs, then it carries `role="tree"`, the tree id, `dir`, `aria-label` defaulting to `"Tree View"`, `aria-labelledby` pointing at the label id, and `tabIndex=-1` so the tree container itself is never in the tab sequence. (zag: packages/machines/tree-view/src/tree-view.connect.ts)
- Given `selectionMode="multiple"`, when connect runs, then the tree carries `aria-multiselectable="true"`; in single-selection mode the attribute is omitted entirely rather than set to false. (zag: packages/machines/tree-view/src/tree-view.connect.ts)
- Given a leaf node, when connect runs, then the item carries `role="treeitem"`, a node-scoped id, `dir`, `data-ownedby` set to the tree id, `data-path` (the index path joined with `/`), `data-value`, `aria-level` and `data-depth` set to the index-path length, and the custom property `--depth` set to the same depth. (zag: packages/machines/tree-view/src/tree-view.connect.ts)
- Given a branch node, when connect runs, then the branch element carries `role="treeitem"`, `dir`, `data-branch` set to the node value, `data-ownedby`, `data-value`, `data-path`, `aria-level`, `data-depth`, the custom property `--depth`, `aria-expanded` reflecting expansion, and `data-state` of `open` or `closed`. (zag: packages/machines/tree-view/src/tree-view.connect.ts)
- The tree ARIA contract omits `aria-setsize` and `aria-posinset` entirely: neither attribute appears anywhere in the tree-view package, so position-in-set information is not exposed to assistive technology. (zag: packages/machines/tree-view/src/tree-view.connect.ts)
- Given a selected node, when connect runs, then the item carries `aria-selected="true"`, `data-selected` and `aria-current="true"`; a branch carries `aria-selected` and `data-selected` but no `aria-current`. (zag: packages/machines/tree-view/src/tree-view.connect.ts)
- Given a disabled node, when connect runs, then `aria-selected` is omitted entirely (rather than set to false) and the node carries `aria-disabled` and `data-disabled`. (zag: packages/machines/tree-view/src/tree-view.connect.ts)
- Given the focused node, when connect runs, then it carries `data-focus` and `tabIndex=0` while every other node gets `tabIndex=-1`, and when no node has been focused yet the first visible node is treated as focused. (zag: packages/machines/tree-view/src/tree-view.connect.ts)
- Given a node being renamed, when connect runs, then the item and branch control carry `data-renaming`. (zag: packages/machines/tree-view/src/tree-view.connect.ts)
- Given checkbox support, when connect runs, then the item and branch control carry `data-checked` when fully checked and `data-indeterminate` when partially checked. (zag: packages/machines/tree-view/src/tree-view.connect.ts)
- Given a loading branch, when connect runs, then the branch carries `data-loading` and `aria-busy`, the branch control carries `data-loading` and `aria-busy`, the branch trigger carries `data-loading` plus the native `disabled` attribute, and the branch indicator and branch text carry `data-loading`. (zag: packages/machines/tree-view/src/tree-view.connect.ts)
- Given a branch control, when connect runs, then it carries `role="button"`, the node id, `dir`, `data-path`, `data-state` open/closed, `data-value`, `data-depth`, plus `data-disabled`, `data-selected`, `data-focus`, `data-renaming`, `data-checked` and `data-indeterminate`. (zag: packages/machines/tree-view/src/tree-view.connect.ts)
- Given a branch trigger, when connect runs, then it carries `role="button"`, `dir`, `data-disabled`, `data-state` open/closed, `data-value` and `data-loading`. (zag: packages/machines/tree-view/src/tree-view.connect.ts)
- Given branch content, when connect runs, then it carries `role="group"`, `dir`, `data-state` open/closed, `data-depth`, `data-path`, `data-value`, and the `hidden` attribute while collapsed. (zag: packages/machines/tree-view/src/tree-view.connect.ts)
- Given a branch indicator, when connect runs, then it carries `aria-hidden="true"`, `data-state`, `data-disabled`, `data-selected`, `data-focus` and `data-loading`. (zag: packages/machines/tree-view/src/tree-view.connect.ts)
- Given a branch indent guide, when connect runs, then it carries only `data-depth`. (zag: packages/machines/tree-view/src/tree-view.connect.ts)
- Given item text, when connect runs, then it carries `data-disabled`, `data-selected` and `data-focus`; branch text carries `data-disabled`, `data-state` and `data-loading`. (zag: packages/machines/tree-view/src/tree-view.connect.ts)
- Given an item indicator, when connect runs, then it carries `aria-hidden="true"`, `data-disabled`, `data-selected`, `data-focus`, and `hidden` unless the node is selected. (zag: packages/machines/tree-view/src/tree-view.connect.ts)
- Given a node checkbox, when connect runs, then it carries `role="checkbox"`, `tabIndex=-1`, `data-disabled`, `data-state` of `checked`, `unchecked` or `indeterminate`, and `aria-checked` of `"true"`, `"false"` or `"mixed"` to match. (zag: packages/machines/tree-view/src/tree-view.connect.ts)
- Given a rename input, when connect runs, then it is an `<input type="text">` with a rename-scoped id, `aria-label` defaulting to `"Rename tree item"`, and the `hidden` attribute unless that node is being renamed. (zag: packages/machines/tree-view/src/tree-view.connect.ts)
- Given a file-tree style tree view, when axe analyses it, then there are no accessibility violations. (zag: e2e/tree-view.e2e.ts: "should have no accessibility violation"; ark: packages/react/src/components/tree-view/tests/tree-view.test.tsx: "should not have any accessibility violations")
- Given a rendered tree, when a leaf node is queried by the treeitem role and its label, then it is visible, and the same holds for a branch node. (ark: packages/react/src/components/tree-view/tests/tree-view.test.tsx, packages/vue/src/components/tree-view/tests/tree-view.test.ts: "should render a leaf node correctly", "should render a branch node correctly"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/tree-view/tests/tree-view.test.tsx: "should render a leaf node correctly", "should render a branch node correctly")

### Keyboard

- Given the first branch control focused, when ArrowDown is pressed, then focus moves to the next visible node, and a second ArrowDown moves to the node after it, stepping over collapsed subtrees. (zag: e2e/tree-view.e2e.ts: "Arrow Down should move focus down")
- Given the last node focused, when ArrowUp is pressed twice, then focus moves up through the two preceding visible nodes. (zag: e2e/tree-view.e2e.ts: "Arrow Up should move focus up")
- Given a node deep in the tree focused, when Home is pressed, then focus moves to the first tree node. (zag: e2e/tree-view.e2e.ts: "Home: should move focus to first tree item")
- Given the first node focused, when End is pressed, then focus moves to the last visible tree node. (zag: e2e/tree-view.e2e.ts: "End: should move focus to last tree item")
- Given a collapsed branch focused, when ArrowRight is pressed, then the branch expands, and a second ArrowRight moves focus to its first child. (zag: e2e/tree-view.e2e.ts: "Branch: Arrow Right")
- Given focus inside an expanded branch, when ArrowLeft is pressed, then focus moves up to the parent branch control, and a second ArrowLeft collapses that branch. (zag: e2e/tree-view.e2e.ts: "Branch: Arrow Left")
- ArrowRight is handled only on branch nodes and is ignored on leaf nodes and on disabled nodes; ArrowLeft dispatches a branch-specific event on branches and a leaf-specific event on items, and is ignored on disabled nodes. (zag: packages/machines/tree-view/src/tree-view.connect.ts)
- ArrowDown, ArrowUp, Home and End are ignored whenever a modifier key other than Shift is held, and each carries the Shift state so it can extend selection. (zag: packages/machines/tree-view/src/tree-view.connect.ts)
- Given a focused leaf node, when the asterisk key is pressed, then every sibling branch at that level expands. (zag: e2e/tree-view.e2e.ts: "Asterisk key should select expand siblings")
- Given multiple selection and the first node focused, when Meta+A is pressed, then every currently visible node is selected, and after expanding a branch and pressing Meta+A again the newly revealed children are included too. (zag: e2e/tree-view.e2e.ts: "Ctrl + A should select all visible nodes")
- The select-all key handler checks only `event.metaKey`, so Ctrl+A does not select all on Windows or Linux even though pointer clicks accept either Ctrl or Meta as the toggle modifier. (zag: packages/machines/tree-view/src/tree-view.connect.ts)
- Given multiple selection and the first node focused, when Shift+ArrowDown is pressed twice, then the two nodes below the anchor are selected. (zag: e2e/tree-view.e2e.ts: "Shift + Arrow Down should extend selection down")
- Given multiple selection and the last node focused, when Shift+ArrowUp is pressed twice, then the two nodes above are selected. (zag: e2e/tree-view.e2e.ts: "Shift + Arrow Up should extend selection up")
- Given multiple selection, when Shift+ArrowDown extends the selection three nodes and then Shift+ArrowUp is pressed twice, then the selection shrinks back to just the first extended node rather than inverting. (zag: e2e/tree-view.e2e.ts: "Shift + Arrow Up + Arrow Down should modify")
- Given a node clicked to set an anchor, when Shift+ArrowDown extends selection twice and then Shift+ArrowUp is pressed three times, then the selection ends up on the anchor plus the node above it, showing the anchor is preserved while the range flips direction. (zag: e2e/tree-view.e2e.ts: "Shift + Arrow Up + Arrow Down should modify and preserve anchor")
- Given a focused node, when Enter is pressed, then a branch toggles and a leaf is selected, with `preventDefault()` called unless the node is an anchor element, and the key is ignored for disabled nodes or for a modifier-held Enter on an anchor. (zag: packages/machines/tree-view/src/tree-view.connect.ts)
- Given a focused node, when Space is pressed while a typeahead search is already in progress, then the space is appended to the search string instead of activating the node; otherwise Space behaves exactly like Enter. (zag: packages/machines/tree-view/src/tree-view.connect.ts)
- Given a focused node and a `canRename` prop that permits it, when F2 is pressed, then renaming starts for that node; without a `canRename` prop F2 does nothing, so renaming is opt-in. (zag: packages/machines/tree-view/src/tree-view.connect.ts)
- Given any other printable key that passes the typeahead validity check, when pressed on a focused node, then a typeahead search runs across visible nodes and `preventDefault()` is called. (zag: packages/machines/tree-view/src/tree-view.connect.ts)
- Given the first node focused, when "p" is typed, then focus should move to the node whose label starts with p, and after expanding a branch typing "z" should move focus into that branch, but the test is skipped with a note that it works in the browser and not in Playwright, so typeahead is not actually verified end to end. (zag: e2e/tree-view.e2e.ts: "typeahead should move focus to matching item")
- Given a key event during IME composition, or a key event originating inside an editable element within the tree, when the tree key handler runs, then it returns without navigating so typing in an inline input is not hijacked. (zag: packages/machines/tree-view/src/tree-view.connect.ts)
- Given a key event whose target is not inside a branch control or item, when the handler runs, then it returns; when the closest node has no `data-value`, a console warning is logged and the key is ignored. (zag: packages/machines/tree-view/src/tree-view.connect.ts)
- Given the rename input focused, when Escape is pressed, then renaming is cancelled; when Enter is pressed the input's current value is submitted as the new label. Both prevent default, and every key event stops propagation so tree navigation never runs while renaming. (zag: packages/machines/tree-view/src/tree-view.connect.ts)
- Given the rename input, when a key arrives during IME composition, then the handler returns immediately so composition keystrokes cannot submit or cancel the rename. (zag: packages/machines/tree-view/src/tree-view.connect.ts)

### Pointer

- Given a tree view, when a leaf node is clicked, then that node becomes selected with `aria-selected="true"`. (zag: e2e/tree-view.e2e.ts: "clicking on a node selects it")
- Given multiple selection, when three nodes (two leaves and one branch control) are clicked with the Meta modifier held, then all three end up selected, so the modifier toggles selection additively. (zag: e2e/tree-view.e2e.ts: "Ctrl + Click should toggle selection")
- Given multiple selection and a branch clicked to set the anchor, when a later leaf is Shift-clicked, then the whole visible range from the anchor to the clicked node is selected, including the branch's revealed children. (zag: e2e/tree-view.e2e.ts: "Shift + Click should extend selection from anchor node to clicked node")
- Given multiple selection and no prior click, when a node is Shift-clicked, then the range from the first visible node to the clicked node is selected. (zag: e2e/tree-view.e2e.ts: "Shift + Click should extend selection without anchor node")
- Given a node, when it is clicked with a non-left button, then nothing happens; a modifier-held click on an anchor node is left to the browser so open-in-new-tab still works. (zag: packages/machines/tree-view/src/tree-view.connect.ts)
- Given a node click, when the handler runs, then either `metaKey` or `ctrlKey` counts as the toggle modifier, the Shift state is forwarded, propagation is stopped, and `preventDefault()` is called for non-anchor nodes. (zag: packages/machines/tree-view/src/tree-view.connect.ts)
- Given a branch control, when clicked, then the branch toggles and propagation stops; clicks are ignored while the branch is disabled or loading. (zag: packages/machines/tree-view/src/tree-view.connect.ts)
- Given a branch trigger, when clicked, then only the expand/collapse toggle fires (no selection) and propagation stops. (zag: packages/machines/tree-view/src/tree-view.connect.ts)
- Given a node checkbox, when clicked with the left button, then the checked state toggles, propagation stops, and focus is moved to the enclosing `role="treeitem"` element with `preventScroll: true`. (zag: packages/machines/tree-view/src/tree-view.connect.ts)
- Given a collapsed branch, when its branch control button is clicked, then the subtree expands and a child leaf becomes visible. (ark: packages/react/src/components/tree-view/tests/tree-view.test.tsx, packages/solid/src/components/tree-view/tests/tree-view.test.tsx, packages/vue/src/components/tree-view/tests/tree-view.test.ts: "should expand branch node to reveal child leaf node")
- Given an "Expand all" button wired to `api.expand()`, when clicked, then every branch including nested ones reports `aria-expanded="true"`. (zag: e2e/tree-view.e2e.ts: "expand/collapse all button")
- Given an "Expand all" then a "Collapse all" button, when each is clicked, then no branch is left with `aria-expanded="false"` after expanding and no branch is left with `aria-expanded="true"` after collapsing. (zag: e2e/tree-view.e2e.ts: "expand all button")
- Given multiple selection and a "Select all" button, when clicked, then every visible top-level node is selected. (zag: e2e/tree-view.e2e.ts: "select all button")

### Focus management

- Given a tree with no selection, when it first renders, then the first node's branch control has `tabindex="0"` and is the single tab stop into the tree. (zag: e2e/tree-view.e2e.ts: "If no selection, first node should be added to tab sequence")
- Given a node has been clicked and selected, when focus leaves the tree by clicking outside, then that selected node keeps `tabindex="0"` so returning by Tab restores the last position. (zag: e2e/tree-view.e2e.ts: "If selection exists, first selected node should be added to tab sequence")
- Given a node or branch control, when it receives focus, then a focus event is sent for that node value and propagation is stopped so nested nodes do not double-report. (zag: packages/machines/tree-view/src/tree-view.connect.ts)
- Given the rename input, when it blurs, then the current value is submitted as the new label rather than discarded. (zag: packages/machines/tree-view/src/tree-view.connect.ts)

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- The imperative api exposes `collection`, `expandedValue`, `selectedValue`, `checkedValue`, `toggleChecked(value, isBranch)`, `setChecked(value)`, `clearChecked()`, `getCheckedMap()`, `expand(value)`, `collapse(value)`, `select(value)`, `deselect(value)`, `getVisibleNodes()`, `focus(value)`, `selectParent(value)`, `expandParent(value)`, `setExpandedValue(value)`, `setSelectedValue(value)`, `startRenaming(value)`, `submitRenaming(value, label)` and `cancelRenaming()`. (zag: packages/machines/tree-view/src/tree-view.connect.ts)
- Given `api.expand()` with no argument, when called, then all branches expand; with a value it expands just that branch. The same holds for `collapse`, `select` and `deselect`, which clear everything when called without a value. (zag: packages/machines/tree-view/src/tree-view.connect.ts)
- Given `setExpandedValue` or `setSelectedValue`, when called, then the incoming array is de-duplicated before being committed. (zag: packages/machines/tree-view/src/tree-view.connect.ts)
- Given `selectParent(value)` or `expandParent(value)`, when the node has no parent, then the call is a no-op; otherwise the parent is added to the existing selection or expansion set. (zag: packages/machines/tree-view/src/tree-view.connect.ts)
- A node counts as visible only when every ancestor on its value path is in the expanded set, which is how the first focusable node and the visible-node list are computed. (zag: packages/machines/tree-view/src/tree-view.connect.ts)

### RTL and i18n

- The root, tree, item, branch, branch control, branch trigger, branch text and branch content parts all receive the `dir` prop, and the key handler resolves keys through `getEventKey` with `dir` so ArrowLeft and ArrowRight swap under RTL. (zag: packages/machines/tree-view/src/tree-view.connect.ts)
- Translated strings are limited to `treeLabel` (default `"Tree View"`) for the tree's `aria-label` and `renameInputLabel` (default `"Rename tree item"`) for the rename input. (zag: packages/machines/tree-view/src/tree-view.connect.ts)

### Notes and edge cases

- The e2e model locates leaf and branch nodes by the `treeitem` role and accessible name, but locates branch elements by `[data-part=branch][data-value="..."]` and branch controls by `[data-part=branch-control][data-value="..."]`, pinning both the role contract and the part/value attribute pair. (zag: e2e/models/tree-view.model.ts)
- The model's `clickBranch` actually clicks the branch control part, not the branch trigger part, so branch toggling in the e2e suite is exercised through the control and never through the dedicated trigger. (zag: e2e/models/tree-view.model.ts)
- The "expand all" assertions check `aria-expanded` on the branch element, and the whole-tree assertions count `[role="treeitem"][aria-expanded="..."]` inside `[role="tree"]`, so branch elements must carry both the role and the expansion state on the same node. (zag: e2e/models/tree-view.model.ts)
- Multi-select e2e tests use the `Meta` modifier rather than `Control`, so the Windows/Linux Ctrl path through the same handlers is untested. (zag: e2e/tree-view.e2e.ts: "Ctrl + Click should toggle selection", "Ctrl + A should select all visible nodes")
- The Ark tree-view suites are thin: only render-a-leaf, render-a-branch and expand-to-reveal-child in react, solid and vue, plus an axe check in react. No framework tests selection, checkboxes, renaming, keyboard navigation, or the `createTreeCollection` node-to-value/node-to-string mapping directly. (ark: packages/react/src/components/tree-view/tests/tree-view.test.tsx, packages/solid/src/components/tree-view/tests/tree-view.test.tsx, packages/vue/src/components/tree-view/tests/tree-view.test.ts)
- The Ark react fixture builds its tree with `createTreeCollection` passing `nodeToValue: (node) => node.id` and `nodeToString: (node) => node.name`, and renders nodes through a recursive `TreeView.NodeProvider` plus `TreeView.NodeContext` render prop that receives `nodeState` (used here to swap the folder icon on `nodeState.expanded`), so the node-to-collection API and the indexPath threading are exercised only indirectly by those three tests. (ark: packages/react/src/components/tree-view/examples/basic.tsx)
- Ark has no `json-tree-view` test file in any framework, so that component is entirely untested. (ark: packages/react/src/components/tree-view/tests/tree-view.test.tsx)
- Solid's tree-view expand test calls the DOM `click()` directly instead of going through user-event, and asserts with `findByText`, so it does not exercise real pointer event sequencing. (ark: packages/solid/src/components/tree-view/tests/tree-view.test.tsx: "should expand branch node to reveal child leaf node")

## scroll-area

### Roles and attributes

- The anatomy declares the parts root, viewport, content, scrollbar, thumb and corner, each emitting `data-scope="scroll-area"` and `data-part="<part>"`. (zag: packages/machines/scroll-area/src/scroll-area.anatomy.ts)
- Given a scroll-area root, when connect runs, then it carries the generated root id, `dir`, `role="presentation"`, and `data-overflow-x` / `data-overflow-y` whenever the corresponding scrollbar is not hidden. (zag: packages/machines/scroll-area/src/scroll-area.connect.ts)
- Given a scroll-area root, when connect runs, then its inline style sets `position: relative` and the custom properties `--corner-width`, `--corner-height`, `--thumb-width` and `--thumb-height`, each the measured size converted to px. (zag: packages/machines/scroll-area/src/scroll-area.connect.ts)
- Given the viewport, when connect runs, then it carries `role="presentation"`, the viewport id, `data-ownedby` set to the root id, `data-at-top`, `data-at-bottom`, `data-at-left` and `data-at-right` reflecting which edges the scroll position has reached, `data-overflow-x`, `data-overflow-y`, and `overflow: auto`. (zag: packages/machines/scroll-area/src/scroll-area.connect.ts)
- Given the viewport, when both axes overflow, then it gets `tabIndex=0` so it is keyboard scrollable; when either scrollbar is hidden the `tabIndex` is omitted entirely. (zag: packages/machines/scroll-area/src/scroll-area.connect.ts)
- Given the content part, when connect runs, then it carries the content id, `role="presentation"`, `data-overflow-x`, `data-overflow-y` and `minWidth: fit-content`. (zag: packages/machines/scroll-area/src/scroll-area.connect.ts)
- Given a scrollbar, when connect runs, then it carries `data-ownedby`, `data-orientation` (defaulting to vertical), `data-scrolling` while that axis is scrolling, `data-hover` while the root is hovered, `data-dragging` while a thumb drag is in progress, and `data-overflow-x` / `data-overflow-y`. (zag: packages/machines/scroll-area/src/scroll-area.connect.ts)
- Given a scrollbar, when connect runs, then its inline style sets `position: absolute`, `touchAction: none` and `userSelect`/`WebkitUserSelect: none`; a vertical scrollbar is pinned with `top: 0`, `bottom: var(--corner-height)` and `insetInlineEnd: 0`, and a horizontal one with `insetInlineStart: 0`, `insetInlineEnd: var(--corner-width)` and `bottom: 0`. (zag: packages/machines/scroll-area/src/scroll-area.connect.ts)
- Given a thumb, when connect runs, then it carries `data-ownedby`, `data-orientation`, `data-hover`, `data-dragging`, and its size is driven by `height: var(--thumb-height)` for vertical or `width: var(--thumb-width)` for horizontal. (zag: packages/machines/scroll-area/src/scroll-area.connect.ts)
- Given the corner, when connect runs, then it carries `data-ownedby`, `data-hover`, `data-state` of `hidden` or `visible`, `data-overflow-x`, `data-overflow-y`, and a style of `position: absolute`, `bottom: 0`, `insetInlineEnd: 0`, `width: var(--corner-width)` and `height: var(--corner-height)`. (zag: packages/machines/scroll-area/src/scroll-area.connect.ts)

### Pointer

- Given the root, when a pointer enters or moves over it (with the event target inside the root), then a hover event is sent carrying the `pointerType`, so touch and mouse can be distinguished; a pointer leave that goes to an element outside the root clears hover. (zag: packages/machines/scroll-area/src/scroll-area.connect.ts)
- Given a scrollbar track, when a left-button pointer down lands directly on the track (not on a descendant such as the thumb), then a track pointer-down is sent with the event point and propagation stops; pointer up sends a track pointer-up for that orientation. (zag: packages/machines/scroll-area/src/scroll-area.connect.ts)
- Given a thumb, when a left-button pointer down occurs, then a thumb pointer-down is sent with the event point to begin the drag; other buttons are ignored. (zag: packages/machines/scroll-area/src/scroll-area.connect.ts)
- Given the viewport, when the user wheels, touch-moves, pointer-moves, pointer-enters or presses a key on it, then a user-scroll event is sent so the machine can distinguish user scrolling from programmatic scrolling, and native scroll events report the scrolling element. (zag: packages/machines/scroll-area/src/scroll-area.connect.ts)

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- The imperative api exposes `isAtTop`, `isAtBottom`, `isAtLeft`, `isAtRight`, `hasOverflowX`, `hasOverflowY`, `getScrollProgress()`, `scrollToEdge({ edge, behavior })`, `scrollTo(details)` and `getScrollbarState({ orientation })`. (zag: packages/machines/scroll-area/src/scroll-area.connect.ts)
- Given `getScrollbarState`, when called for an orientation, then it reports `hovering`, `dragging`, `scrolling` for that axis, and `hidden` for that axis. (zag: packages/machines/scroll-area/src/scroll-area.connect.ts)
- Given `scrollToEdge`, when called, then it resolves the edge against the current `dir` prop so `start` and `end` follow the writing direction. (zag: packages/machines/scroll-area/src/scroll-area.connect.ts)

### Accessibility tooling

- Scroll area has no Zag e2e spec and no Ark unit test in react, solid, vue or svelte, so none of its scrollbar, thumb, corner or edge-detection behavior is verified by an executed test in either repo. (zag: packages/machines/scroll-area/src/scroll-area.connect.ts)

## toc

### Roles and attributes

- The anatomy declares the parts root, title, list, item, link and indicator, each emitting `data-scope="toc"` and `data-part="<part>"`. (zag: packages/machines/toc/src/toc.anatomy.ts)
- Given a toc root, when connect runs, then it carries the generated root id, `dir`, `aria-labelledby` pointing at the title id, and the custom properties `--top`, `--left`, `--width` and `--height` set from the tracked indicator rect in px. (zag: packages/machines/toc/src/toc.connect.ts)
- Given the title and list parts, when connect runs, then each carries its generated id and `dir` and nothing else. (zag: packages/machines/toc/src/toc.connect.ts)
- Given a toc item, when connect runs, then it carries a value-scoped id, `dir`, `data-value`, `data-depth` as a string, `data-active` while the item is in the active set, `data-first` when it is the first active item, `data-last` when it is the last active item, and the custom property `--depth`. (zag: packages/machines/toc/src/toc.connect.ts)
- Given a toc link, when connect runs, then it carries a value-scoped link id, `dir`, `data-value`, `data-active` while active, and `aria-current="location"` while active (omitted otherwise). (zag: packages/machines/toc/src/toc.connect.ts)
- Given the indicator, when connect runs, then it carries the indicator id, `position: absolute`, and the `hidden` attribute whenever the tracked rect is null or all of width, height, x and y are zero. (zag: packages/machines/toc/src/toc.connect.ts)
- Given the Ark toc, when rendered, then `Toc.Nav` produces a `navigation` landmark and `Toc.Content` produces an `article` element, neither of which exists as a Zag anatomy part. (ark: packages/react/src/components/toc/tests/toc.test.tsx: "should render Nav as a nav landmark", "should render Content as an article"; ark: packages/svelte/src/lib/components/toc/toc.test.ts: "should render Nav as a nav landmark", "should render Content as an article")
- Given the Ark toc, when rendered, then the navigation landmark, the article and the title text are all present in one pass. (ark: packages/solid/src/components/toc/tests/toc.test.tsx: "should render correct semantic landmarks")
- Given the Ark toc, when rendered, then the title slot's text is in the document. (ark: packages/react/src/components/toc/tests/toc.test.tsx, packages/svelte/src/lib/components/toc/toc.test.ts: "should render the title")
- Given the Ark toc, when rendered, then `data-part` attributes exist for title, list, item, link and indicator. (ark: packages/react/src/components/toc/tests/toc.test.tsx, packages/svelte/src/lib/components/toc/toc.test.ts: "should apply data-part attributes to all parts")
- Given the Ark toc indicator, when rendered, then the element carries `data-part="indicator"`. (ark: packages/react/src/components/toc/tests/toc.test.tsx, packages/svelte/src/lib/components/toc/toc.test.ts: "should render the indicator")
- Given five items, when the Ark solid toc renders, then exactly five `listitem` elements exist, so items are real list items inside the list part. (ark: packages/solid/src/components/toc/tests/toc.test.tsx: "should render the correct number of items")
- Given items whose values are heading ids, when the toc renders, then each link's `href` is the `#`-prefixed item value. (ark: packages/react/src/components/toc/tests/toc.test.tsx, packages/svelte/src/lib/components/toc/toc.test.ts: "should render all links with correct hrefs"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/toc/tests/toc.test.tsx: "should have correct hrefs for links")
- Given the Ark solid toc, when rendered, then each link's text content matches its item label in item order. (ark: packages/solid/src/components/toc/tests/toc.test.tsx: "should have correct text content for links")
- Given the Ark solid toc content, when rendered, then the headings inside `Toc.Content` appear in item order with matching text. (ark: packages/solid/src/components/toc/tests/toc.test.tsx: "should have correct heading structure")
- Given a toc, when axe analyses it, then there are no accessibility violations. (ark: packages/react/src/components/toc/tests/toc.test.tsx, packages/svelte/src/lib/components/toc/toc.test.ts: "should have no a11y violations")

### Pointer

- Given a toc link whose href is a same-page hash, when it is clicked and a `scrollEl` is configured, then the matching heading is scrolled into view, the default is prevented, and the hash is pushed onto history with a synthetic `hashchange` event dispatched carrying the old and new URLs. (zag: packages/machines/toc/src/toc.connect.ts)
- Given a toc link click, when no `scrollEl` is configured, then the handler returns immediately and the browser handles the anchor natively. (zag: packages/machines/toc/src/toc.connect.ts)
- Given a toc link click that is already prevented, is a download click, or opens in a new tab, when the handler runs, then it returns without scrolling. (zag: packages/machines/toc/src/toc.connect.ts)
- Given a link whose href points to a different origin, pathname or search string, when clicked, then it is not treated as a same-page hash and no scroll or history push happens; a malformed percent-encoded hash is also rejected. (zag: packages/machines/toc/src/toc.connect.ts)
- Given `api.scrollTo(value)`, when no `scrollEl` is configured, then the heading is scrolled with the native `scrollIntoView({ block: "start" })` using the resolved behavior; with a `scrollEl` it scrolls that element instead and reports whether the scroll happened. (zag: packages/machines/toc/src/toc.connect.ts)

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- The imperative api exposes `activeIds`, `activeItems`, `items`, `setActiveIds(value)`, `scrollTo(value, details)` and `getItemState(props)`. (zag: packages/machines/toc/src/toc.connect.ts)
- Given `getItemState`, when called, then it reports `active` (the item value is in the active set), `first` (it is the first active id), `last` (it is the last active id) and `depth`. (zag: packages/machines/toc/src/toc.connect.ts)
- Given `defaultActiveIds={['usage']}`, when the toc renders, then the usage link carries `data-active=""` and the introduction link has no `data-active`. (ark: packages/react/src/components/toc/tests/toc.test.tsx, packages/svelte/src/lib/components/toc/toc.test.ts: "should set data-active on the link matching defaultActiveIds")
- Given two default active ids, when the toc renders, then both matching links carry `data-active` and an unlisted link does not, so scroll-spy supports several simultaneously visible headings. (ark: packages/react/src/components/toc/tests/toc.test.tsx, packages/svelte/src/lib/components/toc/toc.test.ts: "should support multiple defaultActiveIds")
- Given a controlled `activeIds` prop, when the toc renders, then only the listed link is active. (ark: packages/react/src/components/toc/tests/toc.test.tsx, packages/svelte/src/lib/components/toc/toc.test.ts: "should reflect controlled activeIds")
- Given a controlled `activeIds` prop, when it changes on rerender, then the newly listed link becomes active and the previous one loses `data-active`. (ark: packages/react/src/components/toc/tests/toc.test.tsx, packages/svelte/src/lib/components/toc/toc.test.ts: "should update active link when controlled activeIds change")
- Given a `Toc.Context` render prop, when the toc has one default active id, then the render prop receives an `activeIds` array of length 1. (ark: packages/react/src/components/toc/tests/toc.test.tsx: "should expose activeIds via Context render prop")

### Notes and edge cases

- All Ark toc active-state tests drive the active set through props rather than scrolling, so the intersection-based scroll-spy that actually computes `activeIds` from heading positions is never exercised; the solid fixture is the only one that wires a real `scrollEl`, and its tests only check static structure. (ark: packages/react/src/components/toc/tests/toc.test.tsx: "should reflect controlled activeIds"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/toc/tests/basic.tsx)
- The svelte toc fixture accepts an `onActiveChange` prop but no svelte test asserts it fires, and the react controlled tests pass a `vi.fn()` purely to satisfy the controlled-prop requirement without asserting on it. (ark: packages/svelte/src/lib/components/toc/tests/basic.svelte; ark: packages/react/src/components/toc/tests/toc.test.tsx: "should reflect controlled activeIds")
- The react and svelte toc suites are line-for-line the same eleven tests minus the react-only Context render-prop case, which makes toc the one component in this group with real cross-framework parity. (ark: packages/react/src/components/toc/tests/toc.test.tsx; ark: packages/svelte/src/lib/components/toc/toc.test.ts)
- Toc has no Zag e2e spec and no vue test, so scroll-spy activation is unverified in every framework. (zag: packages/machines/toc/src/toc.connect.ts)

## marquee

### Roles and attributes

- The anatomy declares the parts root, viewport, content, edge and item, each emitting `data-scope="marquee"` and `data-part="<part>"`. (zag: packages/machines/marquee/src/marquee.anatomy.ts)
- Given a marquee root, when connect runs, then it carries the generated root id, `dir`, `role="region"`, `aria-roledescription="marquee"`, `aria-live="off"`, `aria-label` defaulting to `"Marquee content"`, `data-state` of `paused` or `idle`, `data-orientation`, and `data-paused` while paused. (zag: packages/machines/marquee/src/marquee.connect.ts)
- Given a marquee root, when connect runs, then its inline style sets `display: flex`, `flexDirection` column for vertical or row for horizontal, `position: relative`, `overflow: hidden` to clip the scrolling content, and `contain: layout style paint`. (zag: packages/machines/marquee/src/marquee.connect.ts)
- Given a marquee root, when connect runs, then its inline style sets the custom properties `--marquee-duration` (the computed duration in seconds), `--marquee-spacing` (the `spacing` prop verbatim), `--marquee-delay` (the `delay` prop in seconds), `--marquee-loop-count` (the `loopCount` prop, or the keyword `infinite` when it is 0) and `--marquee-translate`. (zag: packages/machines/marquee/src/marquee.connect.ts)
- Given `side="top"`, then `--marquee-translate` is `-100%`; given `side="bottom"` it is `100%`; for the horizontal sides it is `-100%` for `start` in LTR and `end` in RTL, and `100%` otherwise. (zag: packages/machines/marquee/src/marquee.utils.ts)
- Given the viewport, when connect runs, then it carries the viewport id, an explicit `data-part="viewport"`, `data-orientation` and `data-side`, plus a style of `display: flex`, full `height` for vertical or full `width` for horizontal. (zag: packages/machines/marquee/src/marquee.connect.ts)
- Given `side="bottom"` or `side="end"`, when the viewport style is computed, then its flex direction is reversed (`column-reverse` or `row-reverse`) so clones land on the correct side. (zag: packages/machines/marquee/src/marquee.connect.ts)
- Given a content element, when connect runs, then it carries an index-scoped id, `dir`, an explicit `data-part="content"`, `data-index`, `data-orientation`, `data-side`, `data-reverse` as an empty attribute when the `reverse` prop is set, and `data-clone` for every index above zero. (zag: packages/machines/marquee/src/marquee.connect.ts)
- Given a cloned content element (index above zero), when connect runs, then it also carries `role="presentation"` and `aria-hidden="true"` so duplicated text is not read twice; the original at index 0 carries neither. (zag: packages/machines/marquee/src/marquee.connect.ts)
- Given a content element, when connect runs, then its style sets `display: flex`, the matching `flexDirection`, `flexShrink: 0`, `backfaceVisibility`/`WebkitBackfaceVisibility: hidden` and `transform: translateZ(0)` to force a compositor layer against animation-reset flicker, `contain: paint` specifically to avoid Firefox subpixel flicker, `minWidth: auto` for vertical or `minHeight: auto` for horizontal, and `willChange` of `transform` while running or `auto` while paused. (zag: packages/machines/marquee/src/marquee.connect.ts)
- Given an edge element, when connect runs, then it carries `dir`, an explicit `data-part="edge"`, `data-side`, `data-orientation`, `pointerEvents: none`, `position: absolute`, and side-specific insets: `start` uses `top: 0`, `insetInlineStart: 0`, `height: 100%`; `end` uses `top: 0`, `insetInlineEnd: 0`, `height: 100%`; `top` uses `top: 0`, `insetInline: 0`, `width: 100%`; `bottom` uses `bottom: 0`, `insetInline: 0`, `width: 100%`. (zag: packages/machines/marquee/src/marquee.connect.ts; zag: packages/machines/marquee/src/marquee.utils.ts)
- Given an item, when connect runs, then it carries `dir` and a margin of `calc(var(--marquee-spacing) / 2)` applied as `marginBlock` for vertical or `marginInline` for horizontal. (zag: packages/machines/marquee/src/marquee.connect.ts)

### Pointer

- Given `pauseOnInteraction`, when the pointer enters the root then the marquee pauses, and when it leaves the marquee resumes; without the prop neither handler is attached at all. (zag: packages/machines/marquee/src/marquee.connect.ts)

### Focus management

- Given `pauseOnInteraction`, when any descendant of the root receives focus, then the marquee pauses so focus does not travel with moving content; a focus event on the root itself is ignored. (zag: packages/machines/marquee/src/marquee.connect.ts)
- Given `pauseOnInteraction`, when focus leaves the marquee entirely (the new focus target is not contained in the root), then it resumes; moving focus between two children keeps it paused. (zag: packages/machines/marquee/src/marquee.connect.ts)

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- The imperative api exposes `paused`, `orientation`, `side`, `multiplier`, `contentCount` (the multiplier plus one), `pause()`, `resume()`, `togglePause()` and `restart()`. (zag: packages/machines/marquee/src/marquee.connect.ts)

### Animation and presence

- Given the viewport, when an animation iteration completes on the content element at index 0 only, then `onLoopComplete` fires; iterations on the clones are ignored. (zag: packages/machines/marquee/src/marquee.connect.ts)
- Given the viewport, when the animation ends on the content element at index 0 only, then `onComplete` fires; animation-end on the clones is ignored. (zag: packages/machines/marquee/src/marquee.connect.ts)
- Given a 1000px viewport, 100px of content and a speed of 100, when the duration is calculated without autoFill, then it is 1 second, because each content element translates by 100% of its own size so the distance is the content size and not the viewport size (regression for issue 3231, where the same input produced 10 seconds). (zag: packages/machines/marquee/tests/marquee.utils.test.ts: "uses content size for the distance when content is smaller than the viewport")
- Given a 500px viewport, 1000px of content and a speed of 100, when the duration is calculated without autoFill, then it is 10 seconds. (zag: packages/machines/marquee/tests/marquee.utils.test.ts: "keeps the configured speed when content is larger than the viewport")
- Given a speed of 100 and the viewport/content pairs 1000/100, 1000/2000 and 300/300, when the duration is calculated, then `contentSize / duration` equals 100 in every case, so the configured speed is the real pixel speed regardless of viewport size. (zag: packages/machines/marquee/tests/marquee.utils.test.ts: "actual pixel speed equals the configured speed regardless of viewport size")
- Given autoFill with a multiplier of 10, a 1000px viewport, 100px of content and a speed of 100, when the duration is calculated, then it is 10 seconds because the distance is scaled by the multiplier. (zag: packages/machines/marquee/tests/marquee.utils.test.ts: "autoFill scales the distance by the multiplier")

### RTL and i18n

- Given `dir="rtl"`, when the translate value is computed, then the sign flips for the horizontal sides, so `side="end"` scrolls in the negative direction and `side="start"` in the positive one, the mirror of LTR. (zag: packages/machines/marquee/src/marquee.utils.ts)
- The only translated string is the root label, defaulting to `"Marquee content"`. (zag: packages/machines/marquee/src/marquee.connect.ts)

### Accessibility tooling

- Marquee has no Zag e2e spec and no Ark unit test in react, solid, vue or svelte, so its `role="region"` plus `aria-roledescription="marquee"` wiring, the clone `aria-hidden` handling, and pause-on-interaction are covered only by the duration unit tests. (zag: packages/machines/marquee/src/marquee.connect.ts)

## accordion

### Roles and attributes

- The anatomy declares parts `root`, `item`, `itemTrigger`, `itemContent`, `itemIndicator`, and every part renders `data-scope="accordion"` plus `data-part="<part>"`. (zag: packages/machines/accordion/src/accordion.anatomy.ts)
- Given a rendered accordion, the root element carries `dir`, `id` defaulting to `accordion:<id>`, and `data-orientation` set to the `orientation` prop. (zag: packages/machines/accordion/src/accordion.connect.ts; zag: packages/machines/accordion/src/accordion.dom.ts)
- Given a rendered item, it carries `dir`, `id` defaulting to `accordion:<id>:item:<value>`, `data-state="open"` when expanded and `data-state="closed"` otherwise, `data-focus` when it is the focused value, `data-disabled` when the item or the root is disabled, and `data-orientation`. (zag: packages/machines/accordion/src/accordion.connect.ts)
- Given a rendered item content, it carries `role="region"`, `id` defaulting to `accordion:<id>:content:<value>`, `aria-labelledby` pointing at the item trigger id, the `hidden` attribute while collapsed, `data-state`, `data-disabled`, `data-focus` and `data-orientation`. (zag: packages/machines/accordion/src/accordion.connect.ts)
- Given a rendered item indicator, it carries `aria-hidden="true"`, `dir`, `data-state`, `data-disabled` and `data-orientation`, and no id. (zag: packages/machines/accordion/src/accordion.connect.ts)
- Given a rendered item trigger, it is a `type="button"` element with `id` defaulting to `accordion:<id>:trigger:<value>`, `aria-controls` and `data-controls` both set to the item content id, `aria-expanded` reflecting the expanded state, the native `disabled` attribute when disabled, `data-ownedby` set to the root id, plus `data-state`, `data-focus` and `data-orientation`. (zag: packages/machines/accordion/src/accordion.connect.ts)
- Given a rendered accordion, keyboard navigation only walks triggers matching `[data-controls][data-ownedby="<root id>"]:not([disabled])` inside the root element, so disabled items are skipped from arrow, Home and End traversal. (zag: packages/machines/accordion/src/accordion.dom.ts)
- Given a default Ark accordion, when rendered, then the first item trigger has `aria-expanded="false"`. (ark: packages/react/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.tsx, packages/solid/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.tsx, packages/vue/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.ts: "should not have an expanded item by default")
- Given an Ark accordion whose third item is declared `disabled`, when rendered, then that item's trigger has the native `disabled` attribute while the others do not. (ark: packages/react/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.tsx, packages/solid/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.tsx: "should disable a single item")
- Given an Ark accordion with `disabled` on the root, when rendered, then all four item triggers have the native `disabled` attribute. (ark: packages/react/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.tsx, packages/solid/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.tsx: "should disable all items when disabled is true")
- Given a Vue accordion with `disabled` on the root, when rendered, then the React item trigger has the native `disabled` attribute (Vue asserts only the first trigger). (ark: packages/vue/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.ts: "should disable all items when disabled is true")
- Given an Ark accordion with `lazyMount`, when rendered before any click, then the item trigger has no `aria-controls` attribute, and after clicking the trigger the attribute appears. (ark: packages/react/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.tsx, packages/solid/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.tsx, packages/vue/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.ts: "should not have aria-controls if lazy mounted")

### Keyboard

- Given a vertical accordion, when `ArrowDown` is pressed on a trigger, then focus moves to the next enabled trigger and the event is default-prevented; `ArrowRight` and `ArrowLeft` are ignored in vertical orientation. (zag: packages/machines/accordion/src/accordion.connect.ts)
- Given a horizontal accordion, when `ArrowRight` or `ArrowLeft` is pressed on a trigger, then focus moves to the next or previous enabled trigger, and `ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp` are ignored. (zag: packages/machines/accordion/src/accordion.connect.ts)
- Given any orientation, when `Home` or `End` is pressed on a trigger, then focus moves to the first or last enabled trigger and the event is default-prevented. (zag: packages/machines/accordion/src/accordion.connect.ts)
- Given a trigger whose keydown event is already default-prevented, or whose item is disabled, when a key is pressed, then no navigation event is sent. (zag: packages/machines/accordion/src/accordion.connect.ts)
- Given focus on the "home" trigger, when `ArrowDown` is pressed, then the "about" trigger is focused. (zag: e2e/accordion.e2e.ts: "arrow down, focus next trigger")
- Given focus on the "home" trigger after one `ArrowDown`, when `ArrowUp` is pressed, then the "home" trigger is focused again. (zag: e2e/accordion.e2e.ts: "arrow up, focus previous trigger")
- Given focus on the "about" trigger, when `Home` is pressed, then the first trigger ("home") is focused. (zag: e2e/accordion.e2e.ts: "home key, focus first trigger")
- Given focus on the "home" trigger, when `End` is pressed, then the last trigger ("contact") is focused. (zag: e2e/accordion.e2e.ts: "end key, focus last trigger")
- Given an accordion with `multiple` enabled, when `Enter` is pressed on the focused "home" trigger, `ArrowDown` moves focus, and `Enter` is pressed again, then both the "home" and "about" contents are visible. (zag: e2e/accordion.e2e.ts: "[multiple=true] on arrow down, focus next trigger")
- Given an Ark accordion with the first trigger clicked, when `{arrowdown}` is typed on it then `{arrowup}` on the second trigger, then focus moves to the second trigger and back to the first. (ark: packages/react/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.tsx, packages/solid/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.tsx, packages/vue/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.ts: "should focus the next/previous item on arrow up & down")
- Given an Ark accordion with the last trigger clicked, when `{home}` is typed then `{end}`, then focus moves to the first trigger and then to the last trigger. (ark: packages/react/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.tsx, packages/solid/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.tsx, packages/vue/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.ts: "should focus the first/last item on home & end")
- Given an Ark accordion with the first trigger focused, when `{tab}` is typed, then focus moves to the next item trigger rather than into the expanded content. (ark: packages/react/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.tsx, packages/solid/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.tsx, packages/vue/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.ts: "should move the focus to the next element when pressing tab")

### Pointer

- Given a single-select accordion, when the "home" trigger is clicked, then the "home" content becomes visible. (zag: e2e/accordion.e2e.ts: "should show content")
- Given the "home" item already expanded in a non-collapsible single accordion, when its trigger is clicked again, then the content stays visible. (zag: e2e/accordion.e2e.ts: "then clicking the same trigger again: should not close the content")
- Given the "home" item expanded in a single accordion, when the "about" trigger is clicked, then the "about" content is visible and the "home" content is hidden. (zag: e2e/accordion.e2e.ts: "then clicking another trigger: should close the previous content")
- Given an accordion with `multiple` enabled, when the "home" trigger and then the "about" trigger are clicked, then both contents remain visible. (zag: e2e/accordion.e2e.ts: "clicking another trigger, should close the previous content")
- Given a disabled item, when its trigger is clicked, then no toggle event is sent. (zag: packages/machines/accordion/src/accordion.connect.ts)

### Focus management

- Given a trigger receiving focus, then `TRIGGER.FOCUS` is sent with the item value and the item gains `data-focus`; on blur `TRIGGER.BLUR` clears the focused value. Disabled items send neither. (zag: packages/machines/accordion/src/accordion.connect.ts)
- Given Safari, when a trigger is clicked, then the connect layer explicitly calls `focus()` on the clicked trigger before toggling, because Safari does not focus buttons on mousedown (browser quirk). (zag: packages/machines/accordion/src/accordion.connect.ts)
- Given an Ark accordion with `onFocusChange`, when the first trigger is focused programmatically, then the trigger has focus and `onFocusChange` is called. (ark: packages/react/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.tsx, packages/solid/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.tsx, packages/vue/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.ts: "should call onFocusChange when focus changes")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given a single-select accordion, when `setValue` is called with more than one value, then only the first value is kept. (zag: packages/machines/accordion/src/accordion.connect.ts)
- Given an Ark accordion with `defaultValue={['Solid']}`, when rendered, then the Solid trigger has `aria-expanded="true"`. (ark: packages/react/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.tsx, packages/solid/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.tsx: "should open item specified in defaultValue")
- Given a Vue accordion, the same default-open case is expressed as `modelValue: ['Solid']` forwarded through `useForwardPropsEmits`, and the Solid trigger has `aria-expanded="true"`. (ark: packages/vue/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.ts, packages/vue/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.vue: "should open item specified in defaultValue")
- Given an Ark accordion with `collapsible`, when the first trigger is clicked twice, then `aria-expanded` goes `true` then `false`. (ark: packages/react/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.tsx, packages/solid/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.tsx, packages/vue/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.ts: "should collapse an expanded item when collapsible is true")
- Given an Ark accordion with `collapsible={false}`, when the first trigger is clicked twice, then `aria-expanded` stays `"true"`. (ark: packages/react/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.tsx, packages/solid/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.tsx, packages/vue/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.ts: "should not collapse the current visible item")
- Given an Ark accordion with `multiple`, when the React trigger and the Vue trigger are clicked, then both have `aria-expanded="true"`. (ark: packages/react/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.tsx, packages/solid/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.tsx, packages/vue/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.ts: "should allow multiple items to be expanded when multiple is true")

(ark: packages/react/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.tsx, packages/solid/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.tsx, packages/vue/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.ts: "should call onValueChange when an item is clicked")
- Given the Svelte basic accordion example with `defaultValue={['ark-ui']}`, when rendered, then the "ark-ui" content is visible and the "getting-started" content is not visible. (ark: packages/svelte/src/lib/components/accordion/accordion.test.ts: "should show default expanded item")

### Animation and presence

- Given an Ark accordion with `lazyMount` and `collapsible`, when rendered, then the item content is absent from the DOM; after clicking the trigger it is visible; after clicking again it becomes not visible but stays mounted. (ark: packages/react/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.tsx, packages/solid/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.tsx, packages/vue/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.ts: "should lazy mount an accordion item")
- Given an Ark accordion with `lazyMount`, `unmountOnExit` and `collapsible`, when the trigger is clicked open and then clicked closed, then the content is first absent, then visible, then removed from the DOM again. (ark: packages/react/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.tsx, packages/solid/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.tsx, packages/vue/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.ts: "should lazy mount and unmount on exit an accordion item")

### RTL and i18n

- Given arrow keys on a trigger, the pressed key is resolved through `getEventKey` with the current `dir` and `orientation`, so in a horizontal RTL accordion `ArrowRight` moves to the previous trigger and `ArrowLeft` to the next. (zag: packages/machines/accordion/src/accordion.connect.ts)
- Given an Ark accordion wrapped in `LocaleProvider locale="ar-AE"`, when rendered, then the item trigger has `dir="rtl"`. (ark: packages/react/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.tsx, packages/solid/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.tsx: "should render text direction based on dir prop")

### Accessibility tooling

- Given the accordion basic story, when axe runs over `[data-part=root]` with the color-contrast rule disabled, then there are no violations. (zag: e2e/accordion.e2e.ts: "should have no accessibility violations")
- Given a rendered Ark accordion, when axe runs over the container, then there are no violations. (ark: packages/react/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.tsx: "should have no a11y violations"; ark: packages/svelte/src/lib/components/accordion/accordion.test.ts: "should have no accessibility violations")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given the Svelte basic accordion example, when rendered, then all item trigger titles are present in the document. (ark: packages/svelte/src/lib/components/accordion/accordion.test.ts: "should render accordion items")
- The Solid accordion suite has no axe test, and the Svelte accordion suite covers only axe, rendering and the default expanded item; keyboard, multiple, disabled and lazy-mount coverage exists only in React, Solid and Vue. (ark: packages/solid/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.tsx, packages/svelte/src/lib/components/accordion/accordion.test.ts)
- Vue drives the accordion under test through `defineProps<AccordionRootProps>()` plus `useForwardPropsEmits`, so every root prop and emit is forwarded from the test wrapper; Solid renders items through `<For>` so item props are accessor-backed. (ark: packages/vue/src/components/accordion/tests/accordion.test.vue, packages/solid/src/components/accordion/tests/basic.tsx)

## collapsible

### Roles and attributes

- The anatomy declares parts `root`, `trigger`, `content`, `indicator`, and every part renders `data-scope="collapsible"` plus `data-part="<part>"`. (zag: packages/machines/collapsible/src/collapsible.anatomy.ts)
- Given a rendered collapsible, the root carries `id` defaulting to `collapsible:<id>`, `dir`, and `data-state="open"` only while the machine is in the `open` state, otherwise `data-state="closed"`. (zag: packages/machines/collapsible/src/collapsible.connect.ts; zag: packages/machines/collapsible/src/collapsible.dom.ts)
- Given a rendered trigger, it carries `id` defaulting to `collapsible:<id>:trigger`, `type="button"`, `dir`, `aria-controls` set to the content id, `aria-expanded` set to `visible || false` where `visible` is true in both the `open` and `closing` states, plus `data-state` and `data-disabled`. (zag: packages/machines/collapsible/src/collapsible.connect.ts)
- Given a rendered content, it carries `id` defaulting to `collapsible:<id>:content`, the marker attribute `data-collapsible=""`, `data-disabled`, `data-has-collapsed-size` when `collapsedHeight` or `collapsedWidth` is set, `dir`, and the `hidden` attribute when it is neither visible nor has a collapsed size. (zag: packages/machines/collapsible/src/collapsible.connect.ts)
- Given content that is open and not on its initial render, `data-state` is omitted entirely so the enter animation is skipped, otherwise it is `"open"` or `"closed"`. (zag: packages/machines/collapsible/src/collapsible.connect.ts)
- Given a rendered content, it always exposes the CSS custom properties `--height`, `--width`, `--collapsed-height` and `--collapsed-width` in pixels from the measured size and the collapsed size props. (zag: packages/machines/collapsible/src/collapsible.connect.ts)
- Given a closed content with `collapsedHeight` set, inline styles add `overflow: hidden`, `minHeight` and `maxHeight` pinned to the collapsed height; with `collapsedWidth` set they pin `minWidth` and `maxWidth` instead. (zag: packages/machines/collapsible/src/collapsible.connect.ts)
- Given a rendered indicator, it carries `dir`, `data-state` and `data-disabled`, and no id. (zag: packages/machines/collapsible/src/collapsible.connect.ts)

### Keyboard

- Given a collapsible whose content was opened and closed again, when `Tab` is pressed, then focus lands on the trigger button and not on anything inside the collapsed content. This case is skipped in repo via test.skip. (zag: e2e/collapsible.e2e.ts: "[closed] content should not be reachable via tab key")

### Pointer

- Given a closed collapsible, when the trigger is clicked, then the content becomes visible, and clicking the trigger again hides it. (zag: e2e/collapsible.e2e.ts: "[toggle] should be open when clicked")
- Given a trigger whose click event is already default-prevented, or a disabled collapsible, when clicked, then no open or close event is sent. (zag: packages/machines/collapsible/src/collapsible.connect.ts)
- Given a default Ark collapsible, when the Toggle button is clicked, then the content goes from not visible to visible. (ark: packages/react/src/components/collapsible/tests/collapsible.test.tsx, packages/solid/src/components/collapsible/tests/collapsible.test.tsx: "should toggle")
- Given a default Ark Vue collapsible, when the Toggle button is clicked and clicked again, then the content becomes visible and then not visible while staying mounted. (ark: packages/vue/src/components/collapsible/collapsible.test.ts: "should control presence when not lazy mounting and not unmounting on exit")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- The api exposes `open`, `visible` (open or closing), `disabled`, `measureSize()` to re-measure the content, and `setOpen(next)` which sends `open`/`close` with `replaces: "open"` so repeated calls in one tick collapse to the last one. (zag: packages/machines/collapsible/src/collapsible.connect.ts)
- Given an Ark collapsible with `open={true}`, when the Toggle button is clicked, then the content stays visible because the open state is fully controlled. (ark: packages/react/src/components/collapsible/tests/collapsible.test.tsx: "should be fully controlled (true)")
- Given an Ark collapsible with `open={false}`, when the Toggle button is clicked, then the content stays not visible. (ark: packages/react/src/components/collapsible/tests/collapsible.test.tsx: "should be fully controlled (false)")

### Animation and presence

- Given an Ark collapsible with `lazyMount`, when rendered, then the content is absent from the DOM, and after clicking Toggle it is visible.
