(ark: packages/react/src/components/collapsible/tests/collapsible.test.tsx, packages/solid/src/components/collapsible/tests/collapsible.test.tsx: "should lazy mount")
- Given an Ark Vue collapsible with `lazyMount`, when Toggle is clicked open then closed, then the content starts absent, becomes visible, and ends up not visible but still mounted. (ark: packages/vue/src/components/collapsible/collapsible.test.ts: "should control presence when lazy mounting and not unmounting on exit")
- Given an Ark collapsible with `unmountOnExit`, when rendered the content is mounted but not visible, after clicking Toggle it is visible, and after clicking again it is removed from the DOM. (ark: packages/react/src/components/collapsible/tests/collapsible.test.tsx, packages/solid/src/components/collapsible/tests/collapsible.test.tsx: "should unmount on exit "; ark: packages/vue/src/components/collapsible/collapsible.test.ts: "should control presence when not lazy mounting and unmounting on exit ")
- Given an Ark collapsible with both `lazyMount` and `unmountOnExit`, when Toggle is clicked open then closed, then the content is absent, then visible, then removed from the DOM again. (ark: packages/react/src/components/collapsible/tests/collapsible.test.tsx, packages/solid/src/components/collapsible/tests/collapsible.test.tsx: "should lazy mount and unmount on exit"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/collapsible/collapsible.test.ts: "should control presence when lazy mounting and unmounting on exit")
- Given a React Ark collapsible with `defaultOpen` and `hideMode="display-none"` whose content runs a 100ms interval, when the content is collapsed by clicking Toggle and fake timers advance 300ms, then the interval keeps ticking, so effects inside hidden content stay alive. (ark: packages/react/src/components/collapsible/tests/collapsible.test.tsx: "keeps effects alive when hideMode is display-none")
- Given a React Ark collapsible with `defaultOpen` and `hideMode="activity"` whose content runs a 100ms interval, when the content is collapsed by clicking Toggle and fake timers advance 300ms, then the tick count stops changing, so React 19 `<Activity mode="hidden">` pauses effects inside collapsed content. (ark: packages/react/src/components/collapsible/tests/collapsible.test.tsx: "pauses effects when hideMode is activity")

### Accessibility tooling

- Given the collapsible basic story, when axe runs over `[data-part=root]` with the color-contrast rule disabled, then there are no violations. (zag: e2e/collapsible.e2e.ts: "should have no accessibility violation")
- Given a rendered Ark React collapsible, when axe runs over the container, then there are no violations. (ark: packages/react/src/components/collapsible/tests/collapsible.test.tsx: "should have no a11y violations")

### Notes and edge cases

- The Solid collapsible suite has no axe, controlled-open or `hideMode` tests; the Vue suite only covers the four lazyMount/unmountOnExit combinations and names them after presence rather than collapsing. (ark: packages/solid/src/components/collapsible/tests/collapsible.test.tsx, packages/vue/src/components/collapsible/collapsible.test.ts)
- Vue drives the collapsible under test with `defineProps<CollapsibleRootProps>()` plus `useForwardPropsEmits`, so `lazyMount` and `unmountOnExit` arrive as root props through `v-bind`. (ark: packages/vue/src/components/collapsible/tests/collapsible.test.vue)
- There is no Svelte collapsible test file; Svelte ships collapsible examples only. (ark: packages/svelte/src/lib/components/collapsible)

## presence

### Roles and attributes

- Presence has no anatomy file and emits no parts or attributes of its own; `packages/machines/presence/src/index.ts` exports only `connect`, `machine`, the prop list and the types, so every attribute is set by the consumer from the returned api. (zag: packages/machines/presence/src/index.ts)
- The api surface is `skip` (true until the first presence change has been committed), `present`, `setNode(node)` to register the animated element, and `unmount()` to force the unmounted state. (zag: packages/machines/presence/src/presence.connect.ts; zag: packages/machines/presence/src/presence.types.ts)
- The machine has three states, `mounted`, `unmountSuspended` and `unmounted`; `present` is true in `mounted` and `unmountSuspended`, and the initial state is `mounted` only when the `present` prop is true on first render. (zag: packages/machines/presence/src/presence.machine.ts; zag: packages/machines/presence/src/presence.connect.ts)
- The accepted props are `present`, `onEnterComplete`, `onExitComplete` and `immediate`. (zag: packages/machines/presence/src/presence.props.ts; zag: packages/machines/presence/src/presence.types.ts)
- Consumers of presence set exactly two things on the node: `data-state="open"` when present and `data-state="closed"` when not, suppressed entirely when `api.skip` is true and `skipAnimationOnMount` is requested, and the `hidden` attribute when not present. (zag: packages/machines/presence/src/presence.connect.ts; ark: packages/react/src/components/presence/use-presence.ts, packages/solid/src/components/presence/use-presence.ts)
- Ark's `Presence` component additionally stamps `data-scope="presence"` and `data-part="root"` on the rendered element. (ark: packages/react/src/components/presence/presence.tsx, packages/svelte/src/lib/components/presence/presence.svelte, packages/vue/src/components/presence/presence.vue)

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given the `present` prop changes, a `PRESENCE.CHANGED` event runs `setInitial` then `syncPresence`; `setInitial` flips the internal `initial` flag to true inside a `queueMicrotask`, so the very first presence change reports `skip: true` and can be rendered without an enter animation. (zag: packages/machines/presence/src/presence.machine.ts)
- Given `present` flips to true from any state, the machine transitions to `mounted` and records the current animation name as `prevAnimationName` on the next frame. (zag: packages/machines/presence/src/presence.machine.ts)
- Given `unmount()` is called while mounted or unmount-suspended, the machine goes straight to `unmounted`, clears `prevAnimationName`, calls `onExitComplete` and dispatches the `exitcomplete` event. (zag: packages/machines/presence/src/presence.connect.ts; zag: packages/machines/presence/src/presence.machine.ts)
- Given a node is registered twice with the same element, `setupNode` returns early; registering a different element replaces both the node ref and the cached `getComputedStyle` result, and machine exit clears both refs. (zag: packages/machines/presence/src/presence.machine.ts)

### Animation and presence

- Given `present` flips to false, the machine waits one `requestAnimationFrame`, re-checks the `present` prop (bailing out if it flipped back to true during the frame), then reads the cached computed style's `animationName` into `unmountAnimationName`. (zag: packages/machines/presence/src/presence.machine.ts)
- Given the resolved exit `animationName` is `"none"`, equals the recorded `prevAnimationName`, or the node's computed `display` is `"none"`, or its `animationDuration` is `"0s"`, then the machine unmounts immediately with `src: "presence.changed"` instead of suspending. (zag: packages/machines/presence/src/presence.machine.ts)
- Given `present` flips to false while the owner document's `visibilityState` is `"hidden"`, then the machine unmounts immediately with `src: "visibilitychange"` and never waits for an animation. (zag: packages/machines/presence/src/presence.machine.ts)
- Given the node has a real exit animation, the machine enters `unmountSuspended`, sets `animationFillMode: "forwards"` on the node for the duration, and restores the previous inline style on the next tick when the effect is cleaned up. (zag: packages/machines/presence/src/presence.machine.ts)
- Given the suspended state, an `animationstart` whose target is the node re-records `prevAnimationName`, an `animationend` unmounts only when the target is the node, the current animation name still equals `unmountAnimationName` and `present` is still false (`src: "animationend"`), and an `animationcancel` on the node unmounts with `src: "animationcancel"`. (zag: packages/machines/presence/src/presence.machine.ts)
- Given `onEnterComplete` is supplied and `initial` is already true, the enter tracker retries each frame until the node is connected, then calls `onEnterComplete` immediately when the animation name is `"none"`, display is `"none"` or the duration is `"0s"`, and otherwise on the first `animationend` targeting the node while still present. (zag: packages/machines/presence/src/presence.machine.ts)
- Given the node is present on first render, the enter-animation tracker is skipped entirely so `onEnterComplete` does not fire for the initial mount. (zag: packages/machines/presence/src/presence.machine.ts)
- Given the machine reaches `unmounted`, it calls `onExitComplete` and dispatches a non-bubbling `exitcomplete` `CustomEvent` on the registered node. (zag: packages/machines/presence/src/presence.machine.ts)
- Given an Ark `Presence` with neither `lazyMount` nor `unmountOnExit`, when the toggle button flips `present` to true then back to false, then the box goes from not visible to visible and back to not visible while staying mounted the whole time. (ark: packages/react/src/components/presence/presence.test.tsx, packages/solid/src/components/presence/presence.test.tsx, packages/vue/src/components/presence/tests/presence.test.ts, packages/svelte/src/lib/components/presence/presence.test.ts: "should control presence when not lazy mounting and not unmounting on exit")
- Given an Ark `Presence` with `lazyMount`, when rendered the box is absent from the DOM, after toggling present it is visible, and after toggling back it is not visible but stays mounted. (ark: packages/react/src/components/presence/presence.test.tsx, packages/solid/src/components/presence/presence.test.tsx, packages/vue/src/components/presence/tests/presence.test.ts, packages/svelte/src/lib/components/presence/presence.test.ts: "should control presence when lazy mounting and not unmounting on exit")
- Given an Ark `Presence` with `unmountOnExit`, when rendered the box is mounted but not visible, after toggling present it is visible, and after toggling back it is removed from the DOM. (ark: packages/react/src/components/presence/presence.test.tsx, packages/solid/src/components/presence/presence.test.tsx, packages/vue/src/components/presence/tests/presence.test.ts, packages/svelte/src/lib/components/presence/presence.test.ts: "should control presence when not lazy mounting and unmounting on exit ")
- Given an Ark `Presence` with both `lazyMount` and `unmountOnExit`, when toggled present then not present, then the box is absent, then visible, then removed from the DOM again. (ark: packages/react/src/components/presence/presence.test.tsx, packages/solid/src/components/presence/presence.test.tsx, packages/vue/src/components/presence/tests/presence.test.ts, packages/svelte/src/lib/components/presence/presence.test.ts: "should control presence when lazy mounting and unmounting on exit")
- Given a React Ark `Presence` with `hideMode="display-none"` wrapping a 100ms interval probe, when present flips to false and fake timers advance 50ms, then the box has `data-state="closed"` and the `hidden` attribute, and after a further 300ms the interval has kept ticking. (ark: packages/react/src/components/presence/presence.test.tsx: "keeps effects alive when hideMode is display-none")
- Given a React Ark `Presence` with `hideMode="activity"` wrapping a 100ms interval probe, when present flips to false and fake timers advance 50ms, then the box has `data-state="closed"` but no `hidden` attribute, and after a further 300ms the tick count is unchanged because React 19 `<Activity mode="hidden">` pauses the effect. (ark: packages/react/src/components/presence/presence.test.tsx: "pauses effects when hideMode is activity")

### Accessibility tooling

- Given a rendered Ark React `Presence` in the not-present state, when axe runs over the container, then there are no violations. (ark: packages/react/src/components/presence/presence.test.tsx: "should have no a11y violations")

### Notes and edge cases

- Ark computes `unmounted` as `(!present && never-was-present && lazyMount) || (unmountOnExit && !present && was-ever-present)`, so `lazyMount` only suppresses the first mount and `unmountOnExit` only removes after a presence cycle. (ark: packages/react/src/components/presence/use-presence.ts, packages/solid/src/components/presence/use-presence.ts)
- Ark resolves `hideMode: "activity"` back to `"display-none"` when the running React version does not provide `<Activity>`, so the `hidden` attribute is the fallback hiding mechanism. (ark: packages/react/src/components/presence/use-presence.ts, packages/react/src/components/presence/presence-gate.tsx)
- React tracks "was ever present" with a `useRef` mutated during render, Solid with a `createSignal` inside a `createEffect`, Vue with a `ref` inside a `watch` on the connected api, and Svelte with runes plus `$derived` over `splitPresenceProps`; Svelte registers the node with an `{@attach}` callback instead of a ref prop. (ark: packages/react/src/components/presence/use-presence.ts, packages/solid/src/components/presence/use-presence.ts, packages/vue/src/components/presence/use-presence.ts, packages/svelte/src/lib/components/presence/presence.svelte)
- Vue exposes the enter and exit completion hooks as the `enterComplete` and `exitComplete` emits rather than props, and declares `immediate`, `lazyMount`, `present`, `skipAnimationOnMount` and `unmountOnExit` with `undefined` defaults so unset booleans stay undefined instead of becoming `false`. (ark: packages/vue/src/components/presence/presence.vue, packages/vue/src/components/presence/use-presence.ts)
- Every Ark `Presence` accepts `asChild` (React/Solid `PolymorphicProps`, Vue `:as-child`, Svelte `PolymorphicProps<'div'>`) so the presence attributes can be merged onto a consumer element instead of the default `div`. (ark: packages/react/src/components/presence/presence.tsx, packages/vue/src/components/presence/presence.vue, packages/svelte/src/lib/components/presence/presence.svelte)
- The Solid, Vue and Svelte presence suites have no axe test and no `hideMode` tests; the `hideMode` contract is only pinned in React. (ark: packages/solid/src/components/presence/presence.test.tsx, packages/vue/src/components/presence/tests/presence.test.ts, packages/svelte/src/lib/components/presence/presence.test.ts)

## dialog

### Roles and attributes

- The anatomy declares parts `trigger`, `backdrop`, `positioner`, `content`, `title`, `description`, `closeTrigger`, and every part renders `data-scope="dialog"` plus `data-part="<part>"`. (zag: packages/machines/dialog/src/dialog.anatomy.ts)
- Default ids are `dialog:<id>:positioner`, `dialog:<id>:backdrop`, `dialog:<id>:content`, `dialog:<id>:trigger` (or `dialog:<id>:trigger:<value>` for a valued trigger), `dialog:<id>:title`, `dialog:<id>:description` and `dialog:<id>:close`, each overridable through the `ids` prop; the trigger id override may be a function of the trigger value. (zag: packages/machines/dialog/src/dialog.dom.ts)
- Given a rendered trigger, it is a `type="button"` element with `dir`, its id, `data-ownedby` set to the machine scope id, `data-value` set to the trigger value, `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-controls` set to the content id, `data-state="open"|"closed"`, `data-current` when it is the active trigger, and `aria-expanded` equal to `open` for a valueless trigger or `open && isCurrent` for a valued trigger. (zag: packages/machines/dialog/src/dialog.connect.ts)
- Given a rendered backdrop, it carries `dir`, its id, `data-state`, and the `hidden` attribute while the dialog is closed. (zag: packages/machines/dialog/src/dialog.connect.ts)
- Given a rendered positioner, it carries `dir`, its id, and inline `pointer-events: none` whenever the dialog is closed or `modal` is false. (zag: packages/machines/dialog/src/dialog.connect.ts)
- Given a rendered content, it carries `dir`, `role` from the `role` prop (`"dialog"` or `"alertdialog"`), its id, `tabIndex={-1}`, `data-state`, `aria-modal` from the `modal` prop, the `hidden` attribute while closed, and inline `pointer-events: auto` when `modal` is false. (zag: packages/machines/dialog/src/dialog.connect.ts)
- Given content with a rendered title and no `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` points at the title id; when `aria-label` is supplied it is used instead and `aria-labelledby` is omitted; when no title part is rendered `aria-labelledby` is omitted. (zag: packages/machines/dialog/src/dialog.connect.ts)
- Given content with a rendered description part, `aria-describedby` points at the description id, otherwise it is omitted. (zag: packages/machines/dialog/src/dialog.connect.ts)
- Given a rendered close trigger, it is a `type="button"` element with `dir` and its id, and its click handler stops propagation before closing so it does not re-trigger an ancestor. (zag: packages/machines/dialog/src/dialog.connect.ts)
- Given the multiple-trigger story with trigger 2 open, then trigger 2 has `aria-expanded="true"` while triggers 1 and 3 have `aria-expanded="false"`. (zag: e2e/dialog-multiple-trigger.e2e.ts: "should scope aria-expanded to the active trigger")
- Given the multiple-trigger story with trigger 2 open, then trigger 2 has `data-current=""` and trigger 1 has no `data-current` attribute. (zag: e2e/dialog-multiple-trigger.e2e.ts: "should set data-current only on the active trigger")
- Given an Ark dialog with `lazyMount`, when rendered before opening, then the trigger has no `aria-controls` attribute. (ark: packages/react/src/components/dialog/tests/dialog.test.tsx, packages/solid/src/components/dialog/tests/dialog.test.tsx: "should not have aria-controls if lazy mounted")

### Keyboard

- Given the multiple-trigger story with trigger 2 focused, when `Enter` is pressed, then the dialog opens showing Bob Smith's content. (zag: e2e/dialog-multiple-trigger.e2e.ts: "should open dialog with Enter key")
- Given the multiple-trigger story with trigger 3 focused, when `Space` is pressed, then the dialog opens showing Carol Davis's content. (zag: e2e/dialog-multiple-trigger.e2e.ts: "should open dialog with Space key")
- Given the multiple-trigger story with trigger 1 focused, when `Tab` moves focus to trigger 2 and `Enter` opens the dialog, then the content shows Bob Smith, and pressing `Escape` closes it and returns focus to trigger 2. (zag: e2e/dialog-multiple-trigger.e2e.ts: "should return focus to correct trigger after keyboard navigation")

### Focus management

- Given the nested dialog story, when the parent trigger is clicked, then the parent dialog's close button receives focus. (zag: e2e/dialog.e2e.ts: "should focus on close button when dialog is open")
- Given the parent dialog open, when the child trigger is clicked (with a 17ms click delay), then the child dialog's close button receives focus. (zag: e2e/dialog.e2e.ts: "[nested] should focus close button")
- Given an open dialog, when `Escape` closes it, then focus returns to the dialog trigger. (zag: e2e/dialog.e2e.ts: "should close modal on escape")
- Given a nested dialog pair, when the child is dismissed with `Escape`, then focus returns to the child dialog's trigger. This case is marked test.fixme, known failing. (zag: e2e/dialog.e2e.ts: "[nested] focus return to child dialog trigger")
- Given the multiple-trigger story opened from trigger 4, when `Escape` closes the dialog, then trigger 4 regains focus. (zag: e2e/dialog-multiple-trigger.e2e.ts: "should focus trigger on close")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- The api exposes `open`, `setOpen(next)` which sends `OPEN`/`CLOSE` with `replaces: "open"`, `triggerValue` and `setTriggerValue(value)`. (zag: packages/machines/dialog/src/dialog.connect.ts)
- Given an open dialog and a valued trigger that is not the current one, when that trigger is clicked, then the machine sends `TRIGGER_VALUE.SET` to swap the content instead of toggling the dialog closed. (zag: packages/machines/dialog/src/dialog.connect.ts)
- Given the setOpen story, when `setOpen(true)` is invoked from a button and then `setOpen(false)` from inside the content, then the content shows and hides and the change log reads `true,false`. (zag: e2e/dialog-set-open.e2e.ts: "should open and close through the api")
- Given the setOpen story, when `setOpen(true)` and `setOpen(false)` are called in the same tick, then the resolved open state is `false`, the content stays hidden, and `onOpenChange` is never called (empty log). (zag: e2e/dialog-set-open.e2e.ts: "should close when setOpen(false) follows setOpen(true) in the same tick")
- Given the setOpen story, when `setOpen(false)` and `setOpen(true)` are called in the same tick, then the resolved open state is `true`, the content is visible, and `onOpenChange` logs a single `true`. (zag: e2e/dialog-set-open.e2e.ts: "should open when setOpen(true) follows setOpen(false) in the same tick")
- Given the setOpen story, when `setOpen(true)` is called repeatedly, then the open state is `true` and `onOpenChange` logs exactly one `true`. (zag: e2e/dialog-set-open.e2e.ts: "should invoke onOpenChange once when setOpen is repeated")
- Given a closed dialog, when `setOpen(false)` is clicked twice, then the open state stays `false` and `onOpenChange` is never invoked (empty log). (zag: e2e/dialog-set-open.e2e.ts: "should not invoke onOpenChange when closing an already closed dialog")
- Given an Ark dialog with `open` and an `onOpenChange` spy, when the close button is clicked, then `onOpenChange` is called exactly once. (ark: packages/react/src/components/dialog/tests/dialog.test.tsx: "should invoke onOpenChange if dialog is closed"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/dialog/tests/dialog.test.tsx: "should invoke onClose if dialog is closed")
- Given an Ark dialog with `open={true}`, when the close button is clicked, then the close button is still visible because the open state is fully controlled. (ark: packages/react/src/components/dialog/tests/dialog.test.tsx: "should be fully controlled (true)")
- Given an Ark dialog with `open={false}`, when the trigger is clicked, then no close button ever enters the DOM. (ark: packages/react/src/components/dialog/tests/dialog.test.tsx: "should be fully controlled (false)")

### Dismissal and layering

- Given an open dialog, when `Escape` is pressed, then the content is no longer visible. (zag: e2e/dialog.e2e.ts: "should close modal on escape"; zag: e2e/dialog-multiple-trigger.e2e.ts: "should close dialog on escape")
- Given a parent dialog with a child dialog open, when a close button inside the child that targets the parent is clicked, then both the child and the parent close and focus returns to the parent trigger. (zag: e2e/dialog.e2e.ts: "[nested] should close parent modal from child")
- Given the multiple-trigger story opened from trigger 2, when the close trigger part is clicked, then the content is hidden. (zag: e2e/dialog-multiple-trigger.e2e.ts: "should close dialog on close trigger click")
- Given an Ark dialog, when the trigger is clicked the title is visible, and when Close is clicked the title becomes not visible. (ark: packages/react/src/components/dialog/tests/dialog.test.tsx, packages/solid/src/components/dialog/tests/dialog.test.tsx: "should show dialog content when opened")
- Given a Vue Ark dialog, when the trigger is clicked and then Close is clicked (each wrapped in `waitFor` because Vue applies the change on the next tick), then the title becomes visible and then not visible. (ark: packages/vue/src/components/dialog/tests/dialog.test.ts: "should show dialog content when opened")

### Animation and presence

- Given an Ark dialog with `lazyMount`, when rendered the positioner is absent from the DOM, after clicking the trigger it becomes visible, and after clicking Close it stays in the DOM. (ark: packages/react/src/components/dialog/tests/dialog.test.tsx, packages/solid/src/components/dialog/tests/dialog.test.tsx: "should be able to lazy mount")
- Given an Ark dialog with `lazyMount` and `unmountOnExit`, when the trigger is clicked and then Close, then the positioner goes absent, present, and absent again. (ark: packages/react/src/components/dialog/tests/dialog.test.tsx: "should lazy mount and unmount on exit")
- Given an Ark React dialog with `hideMode="display-none"`, when opened then closed, then the dialog element keeps the `hidden` attribute while the positioner stays mounted. (ark: packages/react/src/components/dialog/tests/dialog.test.tsx: "applies hidden attribute when hideMode is display-none")
- Given an Ark React dialog with `hideMode="activity"`, when opened then closed, then the positioner stays mounted and the dialog element has no `hidden` attribute. (ark: packages/react/src/components/dialog/tests/dialog.test.tsx: "keeps content mounted without hidden attribute when hideMode is activity")
- Given a Vue Ark dialog with an `onExitComplete` handler, when the dialog is opened and then closed, then the `exitComplete` emit fires after the close animation resolves. (ark: packages/vue/src/components/dialog/tests/dialog.test.ts: "should emit exitComplete when close animation completes")

### Accessibility tooling

- Given the nested dialog story with the parent dialog open, when axe runs over `[role=dialog]` with the color-contrast rule disabled, then there are no violations. (zag: e2e/dialog.e2e.ts: "should have no accessibility violation")
- Given a rendered Ark React dialog, when axe runs over the container, then there are no violations. (ark: packages/react/src/components/dialog/tests/dialog.test.tsx: "should have no a11y violations")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given the multiple-trigger story, when trigger 1 is clicked the content shows Alice Johnson, and after closing with `Escape` and clicking trigger 3 the same content element shows Carol Davis, so a single dialog instance is reused across triggers. (zag: e2e/dialog-multiple-trigger.e2e.ts: "should open dialog from different triggers")
- Trigger discovery for multiple triggers queries `[data-scope="dialog"][data-part="trigger"][data-ownedby="<scope id>"]` across the root node, and the "active trigger" for focus restore falls back to the first such element when no trigger value is set. (zag: packages/machines/dialog/src/dialog.dom.ts)
- Given a Vue dialog created through `useDialog(computed(() => ({ id: 'test-id' })))` and rendered with `Dialog.RootProvider`, when opened by calling `dialog.setOpen(true)`, then the dialog element's id contains `test-id`, proving computed props reach the machine through the root provider. (ark: packages/vue/src/components/dialog/tests/dialog-root-provider-computed-props.test.vue, packages/vue/src/components/dialog/tests/dialog.test.ts: "should apply computed props when using root provider with useDialog")
- The React and Solid dialog fixtures render backdrop, positioner and content inside a `Portal`, and the Vue fixture inside `<Teleport to="body">`, so every dialog assertion is made against portalled content. (ark: packages/react/src/components/dialog/tests/basic.tsx, packages/solid/src/components/dialog/tests/basic.tsx, packages/vue/src/components/dialog/tests/dialog.test.vue)
- The Solid dialog suite covers only open/close, `onOpenChange`, `lazyMount` and the missing `aria-controls`; controlled open, `unmountOnExit` and `hideMode` are pinned only in React, and `exitComplete` and the computed-props root provider only in Vue. (ark: packages/solid/src/components/dialog/tests/dialog.test.tsx, packages/react/src/components/dialog/tests/dialog.test.tsx, packages/vue/src/components/dialog/tests/dialog.test.ts)
- There is no Svelte dialog test file; Svelte ships dialog examples only. (ark: packages/svelte/src/lib/components/dialog)

## drawer

### Roles and attributes

- The anatomy declares parts `positioner`, `content`, `title`, `description`, `trigger`, `backdrop`, `grabber`, `grabberIndicator`, `closeTrigger`, `swipeArea`, and every part renders `data-scope="drawer"` plus `data-part="<part>"`. (zag: packages/machines/drawer/src/drawer.anatomy.ts)
- Default ids are `drawer:<id>:content`, `:positioner`, `:title`, `:description`, `:trigger` (or `:trigger:<value>`), `:backdrop`, `:header`, `:grabber`, `:grabber-indicator`, `:close-trigger` and `:swipe-area`, each overridable through `ids`; the trigger id override may be a function of the trigger value. (zag: packages/machines/drawer/src/drawer.dom.ts)
- Given a rendered positioner, it carries its id, `dir`, `hidden` while the machine is in the `closed` state, `data-state="open"|"closed"`, `data-swipe-direction` set to the direction resolved against `dir`, and inline `pointer-events: none` while closing or when `modal` is false. (zag: packages/machines/drawer/src/drawer.connect.ts)
- Given a rendered content, it carries `dir`, its id, `tabIndex={-1}`, `role` from the `role` prop (`"dialog"` or `"alertdialog"`), `aria-modal` from `modal`, `aria-labelledby` only when a title part is rendered, `aria-describedby` only when a description part is rendered, and `hidden` while not open. (zag: packages/machines/drawer/src/drawer.connect.ts)
- Given a rendered content, it carries `data-state`, `data-expanded=""` when the active snap point resolves to zero offset, `data-swipe-direction`, `data-swiping=""` while dragging or swiping open, `data-dragging=""` only while a drag offset exists, `data-nested-drawer-open=""` when a nested drawer is open, and `data-nested-drawer-swiping=""` when a nested drawer is being swiped. (zag: packages/machines/drawer/src/drawer.connect.ts)
- Given a rendered content, its inline transform is always `translate3d(var(--drawer-translate-x, 0px), var(--drawer-translate-y, 0px), 0)` with `will-change: transform`, `transition-duration: 0s` while dragging or swiping open, `visibility: hidden` while swiping open before the first drag offset arrives, and `pointer-events: auto` when `modal` is false. (zag: packages/machines/drawer/src/drawer.connect.ts)
- Given a rendered content, it emits the CSS custom properties `--drawer-translate` (the vertical translate in px, kept for backwards compatibility), `--drawer-translate-x`, `--drawer-translate-y`, `--drawer-snap-point-offset-x`, `--drawer-snap-point-offset-y`, `--drawer-swipe-movement-x`, `--drawer-swipe-movement-y`, `--drawer-swipe-strength`, `--nested-drawers` (the nested open count), `--drawer-height` and `--drawer-frontmost-height`. (zag: packages/machines/drawer/src/drawer.connect.ts)
- Given a vertical swipe direction, `--drawer-translate-x`, `--drawer-snap-point-offset-x` and `--drawer-swipe-movement-x` are pinned to `0px` and the offset lives on the y axis; given a horizontal direction the axes swap. (zag: packages/machines/drawer/src/drawer.connect.ts)
- Given a negative swipe direction (`up` or `left`), the sign of the offsets, snap point offsets and movements is flipped so the translate is negative. (zag: packages/machines/drawer/src/drawer.connect.ts)
- Given `--drawer-height` and `--drawer-frontmost-height`, they are emitted only when the corresponding nested metric is greater than zero, otherwise the property is omitted entirely. (zag: packages/machines/drawer/src/drawer.connect.ts)
- Given a rendered trigger, it is a `type="button"` element with `dir`, its id, `data-ownedby` set to the scope id, `data-value`, `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-controls` set to the content id, `data-state`, `data-current` when it is the active trigger, and `aria-expanded` equal to `open` for a valueless trigger or `open && isCurrent` for a valued trigger. (zag: packages/machines/drawer/src/drawer.connect.ts)
- Given a rendered backdrop, it carries its id, `data-state`, `data-swiping=""` while dragging or swiping open, `hidden` when closed or while swiping open before the first drag offset, plus inline `will-change: opacity`, `pointer-events: none` while closing, and the custom properties `--drawer-swipe-progress` and `--drawer-swipe-strength`. (zag: packages/machines/drawer/src/drawer.connect.ts)
- `--drawer-swipe-progress` is `abs(signed movement) / contentSize` clamped to 0..1 while actively swiping, `1` while swiping open before the content size has been measured, and `0` at rest. (zag: packages/machines/drawer/src/drawer.connect.ts)
- Given a rendered grabber, it carries its id and inline `touch-action: none` so the browser does not scroll while dragging it. (zag: packages/machines/drawer/src/drawer.connect.ts)
- Given a rendered grabber indicator, it carries only its id and the part attributes. (zag: packages/machines/drawer/src/drawer.connect.ts)
- Given a rendered close trigger, it is a `type="button"` element with its id whose click sends `CLOSE`. (zag: packages/machines/drawer/src/drawer.connect.ts)
- Given a rendered swipe area, it carries its id, `role="presentation"`, `aria-hidden="true"`, `data-state`, `data-swiping=""` while swiping open, `data-swipe-direction` set to the resolved opening direction (the opposite of the drawer's swipe direction unless overridden), and `data-disabled=""` when disabled. (zag: packages/machines/drawer/src/drawer.connect.ts)
- Given a rendered swipe area, its inline `touch-action` is `pan-x` for a vertical opening direction and `pan-y` for a horizontal one, and its `pointer-events` is `none` when disabled or when the drawer is open and not currently swiping open. (zag: packages/machines/drawer/src/drawer.connect.ts)
- Given the drawer stack's indent parts, they carry `data-active=""` when any drawer is open and `data-inactive=""` otherwise, and emit `--drawer-swipe-progress` (clamped 0..1) and `--drawer-frontmost-height` in px, omitting the height when it is not greater than zero; `getIndentBackgroundProps` returns the identical prop object. (zag: packages/machines/drawer/src/drawer.stack.ts)
- The api exposes `open`, `dragging`, `setOpen`, `snapPoints`, `swipeDirection`, `snapPoint`, `setSnapPoint`, `triggerValue`, `setTriggerValue`, `getOpenPercentage()` (`1 - currentOffset / contentSize` clamped 0..1, `0` when closed or unmeasured), `getSnapPointIndex()` (`-1` when no snap point is active) and `getContentSize()`. (zag: packages/machines/drawer/src/drawer.connect.ts)

### Keyboard

- Given an open drawer, when `Escape` is pressed, then the content is hidden and focus returns to the trigger. (zag: e2e/drawer.e2e.ts: "should close on escape")
- Given a drawer opened by swiping up from the swipe area, when `Escape` is pressed, then the content is hidden. (zag: e2e/drawer-swipe-area.e2e.ts: "should close on escape after swipe open")
- Given the indent-effect story with the drawer open, when `Escape` is pressed, then the content is hidden, the indent and indent background flip back to `data-inactive=""`, and `--drawer-swipe-progress` is back to `0`. (zag: e2e/drawer-indent.e2e.ts: "should orchestrate indent/effect visual state during swipe")

### Pointer

- Given a closed drawer, when the trigger is clicked, then both the content and the backdrop become visible. (zag: e2e/drawer.e2e.ts: "should open when trigger is clicked")
- Given an open drawer whose enter animation has finished, when the grabber is mouse-dragged down 200px over 100ms (a fast swipe past `swipeVelocityThreshold`, default 700 px/s), then the drawer closes. (zag: e2e/drawer.e2e.ts: "should close when dragged down past swipeVelocityThreshold")
- Given an open drawer, when the grabber is mouse-dragged down by 55 percent of the content's visible height over the default 500ms (past the default `closeThreshold` of 0.25), then the drawer closes. (zag: e2e/drawer.e2e.ts: "should close when dragged down past closeThreshold")
- Given an open drawer, when the grabber is mouse-dragged down only 100px over 500ms, then the drawer stays open. (zag: e2e/drawer.e2e.ts: "should stay open when dragged down slightly")
- Given an open drawer, when the grabber is dragged down 100px with synthesized `touchstart`/`touchmove`/`touchend` events, then after the snap animation settles the visible height is within 4px of its original value, so the drawer snaps back and remains interactive. (zag: e2e/drawer.e2e.ts: "should stay interactive on touch drag")
- Given an open drawer, when the grabber is dragged down 100px with synthesized `pointerdown`/`pointermove`/`pointerup` events whose `pointerType` is `"touch"`, then after the snap settles the visible height is within 4px of its original value. (zag: e2e/drawer.e2e.ts: "should stay interactive on touch pointer drag")
- Given an open drawer at its maximum snap point, when the grabber is mouse-dragged up 150px, then the visible height is unchanged, so over-drag past the open position is clamped. (zag: e2e/drawer.e2e.ts: "should no effect when dragged up")
- Given an open drawer with a scrollable region inside the content, when the region is scrolled by 200px, then its `scrollTop` is no longer zero, so content scrolling is not swallowed by the drag handler. (zag: e2e/drawer.e2e.ts: "should allow scrolling within content")
- Given an open drawer with an element marked `data-no-drag`, when that element is dragged down 100px without releasing, then the visible height does not change at all, and after releasing the mouse the drawer is still open at exactly its original height. (zag: e2e/drawer.e2e.ts: "should not allow dragging from no-drag area")
- Given an open drawer whose title text has been selected with a DOM Range, when the content is mouse-dragged down 100px, then the visible height is unchanged, so a drag is not started while a text selection exists inside the content. (zag: e2e/drawer.e2e.ts: "should not start dragging when text is selected in content")
- Given the `draggable=false` story, when the content is mouse-dragged down 100px without releasing, then the visible height does not change, but after releasing and dragging the grabber down 100px the visible height drops by exactly 100px, so only the grabber is draggable. (zag: e2e/drawer.e2e.ts: "sheet content should not be draggable")
- Given a content part rendered with `getContentProps({ draggable: false })`, its pointerdown handler returns immediately so no drag session starts. (zag: packages/machines/drawer/src/drawer.connect.ts)
- Given the swipe-area story with the drawer closed, when a 300px upward touch swipe is performed on the swipe area, then the content and the backdrop become visible. (zag: e2e/drawer-swipe-area.e2e.ts: "should open when swiped up from swipe area")
- Given the swipe-area story, when the mouse is pressed on the swipe area, held 200ms and released without moving, then the drawer does not open. (zag: e2e/drawer-swipe-area.e2e.ts: "should not open on pointer down without swipe")
- Given the swipe-area story, when a 3px upward swipe is performed, then the drawer does not open. (zag: e2e/drawer-swipe-area.e2e.ts: "should not open on small swipe")
- Given a drawer opened by swiping up from the swipe area, when the grabber is mouse-dragged down 200px over 100ms, then the content and the backdrop are both hidden. (zag: e2e/drawer-swipe-area.e2e.ts: "should close when swiped down after swipe open")
- Given a drawer opened by swiping up from the swipe area, when the `close-trigger` part is clicked, then the content and the backdrop are both hidden. (zag: e2e/drawer-swipe-area.e2e.ts: "should close via close button after swipe open")
- Given the swipe area's pointerdown handler, it ignores non-left buttons, ignores events whose `pointerType` is `"touch"` (those are handled by `touchstart` instead), ignores everything while the drawer is open and not swiping open, and calls `preventDefault()` on cancelable events. (zag: packages/machines/drawer/src/drawer.connect.ts)
- Given the swipe area's touchstart handler, it uses the first touch point and is ignored when disabled or when the drawer is already open and not swiping open. (zag: packages/machines/drawer/src/drawer.connect.ts)
- Given a drag session on the content or grabber, it is only committed when the machine has the `open` tag and is not in the `closing` state. (zag: packages/machines/drawer/src/drawer.connect.ts)

### Focus management

- Given an open drawer, when `Escape` closes it, then focus returns to the drawer trigger. (zag: e2e/drawer.e2e.ts: "should close on escape")
- Focus behavior is governed by the `trapFocus` (default true), `restoreFocus` (default true), `initialFocusEl` and `finalFocusEl` props. (zag: packages/machines/drawer/src/drawer.types.ts)

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- `setOpen(next)` sends `OPEN`/`CLOSE` with `replaces: "open"` and `setSnapPoint(point)` sends `SNAP_POINT.SET` with `replaces: "snapPoint"`, so repeated calls within one tick collapse to the last value. (zag: packages/machines/drawer/src/drawer.connect.ts)
- Given an open drawer and a valued trigger that is not the current one, when that trigger is clicked, then `TRIGGER_VALUE.SET` swaps the content rather than closing the drawer; otherwise the click toggles open/closed. (zag: packages/machines/drawer/src/drawer.connect.ts)
- Given the setSnapPoint story reset to 20rem, when `setSnapPoint("30rem")` is invoked, then the rendered snap point reads `30rem` and `onSnapPointChange` logs `30rem`. (zag: e2e/drawer-set-snap-point.e2e.ts: "should set the snap point through the api")
- Given the setSnapPoint story at 20rem, when `setSnapPoint("30rem")` then `setSnapPoint("20rem")` are called in the same tick, then the snap point stays `20rem` and `onSnapPointChange` is never invoked (empty log). (zag: e2e/drawer-set-snap-point.e2e.ts: "should keep the last snap point set in the same tick")
- Given the setSnapPoint story, when `setSnapPoint("30rem")` then `setSnapPoint(1)` are called in the same tick, then only the last one applies: the snap point reads `1` and the log reads `1`. (zag: e2e/drawer-set-snap-point.e2e.ts: "should apply only the last snap point when two are set in the same tick")
- Given the setSnapPoint story, when `setSnapPoint("30rem")` is called repeatedly, then the snap point reads `30rem` and `onSnapPointChange` logs it exactly once. (zag: e2e/drawer-set-snap-point.e2e.ts: "should invoke onSnapPointChange once when the same value is set repeatedly")
- Given a drawer stack, `register(id)` creates an entry with an incrementing order and `unregister(id)` removes it, notifying only when the entry actually existed. (zag: packages/machines/drawer/src/drawer.stack.ts)
- Given a stack with one registered drawer, when it is marked open, then the snapshot is `{ active: true, openCount: 1, swipeProgress: 0, frontmostHeight: 0 }`. (zag: packages/machines/drawer/tests/drawer.stack.test.ts: "tracks open state and count")
- Given a stack with drawer "a" open at height 180 and a later-registered drawer "b" open at height 320, then the snapshot's `frontmostHeight` is 320, so the height comes from the highest-order open drawer. (zag: packages/machines/drawer/tests/drawer.stack.test.ts: "resolves frontmost height from latest open drawer")
- Given a stack whose frontmost open drawer reports a swipe progress of 5, then `swipeProgress` clamps to 1, and once a later drawer "b" is registered, opened and reports a progress of -1, then `swipeProgress` clamps to 0. (zag: packages/machines/drawer/tests/drawer.stack.test.ts: "uses frontmost swiping progress and clamps range")
- Given a stack with one subscriber, when `register`, `setOpen`, `setHeight` and `setSwipe` are all called synchronously, then the listener has not fired yet, and after a microtask flush it has fired exactly once with the snapshot `{ active: true, openCount: 1, swipeProgress: 0.4, frontmostHeight: 200 }`. (zag: packages/machines/drawer/tests/drawer.stack.test.ts: "batches notifications in the same tick")
- Given a stack subscriber that has been notified once, when it unsubscribes and the drawer is then closed, then the listener is not called again. (zag: packages/machines/drawer/tests/drawer.stack.test.ts: "supports unsubscribe")
- Given a stack entry, `setOpen(false)` also resets that entry's `swiping` flag and `swipeProgress` to zero, and `setHeight` coerces non-finite or non-positive heights to `0`. (zag: packages/machines/drawer/src/drawer.stack.ts)
- Given a stack write that produces an identical snapshot, no notification is scheduled, and the published snapshot object is frozen. (zag: packages/machines/drawer/src/drawer.stack.ts)

### Dismissal and layering

- Given an open drawer whose enter animation has finished, when the page body is clicked at (5, 5), then the content and the backdrop are both hidden. (zag: e2e/drawer.e2e.ts: "should close when clicked outside")
- Given a drawer opened by swiping up from the swipe area, when the page body is clicked outside, then the content and the backdrop are both hidden. (zag: e2e/drawer-swipe-area.e2e.ts: "should close when clicked outside after swipe open")
- Dismissal is governed by `closeOnInteractOutside` (default true), `closeOnEscape` (default true), `modal` (default true) and `preventScroll` (default true). (zag: packages/machines/drawer/src/drawer.types.ts)

### Positioning

- Given the snap-points story, when the drawer is opened, then its visible height starts within 4px of 20rem (the first snap point measured against the root font size). (zag: e2e/drawer.e2e.ts: "should snap to defined positions")
- Given the snap-points story at 20rem, when the grabber is dragged up 250px, then the visible height grows by more than 80px, and dragging back down 250px returns it to within 4px of 20rem. (zag: e2e/drawer.e2e.ts: "should snap to defined positions")
- Given the snap-points story with `snapToSequentialPoints` enabled, when the grabber is dragged up only 100px, then the visible height grows by more than 50px because the drawer advances exactly one snap point. (zag: e2e/drawer.e2e.ts: "should advance one step on swipe up")
- Given the snap-points story with `snapToSequentialPoints` enabled and the drawer expanded to full height, when the grabber is swiped down 150px, then the drawer snaps to the lower snap point and stays visible instead of dismissing. (zag: e2e/drawer.e2e.ts: "should not dismiss on fast swipe down from full height, should snap instead")
- Snap resolution is driven by `snapPoints` (default `[1]`), `defaultSnapPoint` (default `1`), `snapToSequentialPoints` (default false), `swipeDirection` (default `"down"`), `swipeVelocityThreshold` (default 700 px/s), `closeThreshold` (default 0.25) and `preventDragOnScroll` (default true). (zag: packages/machines/drawer/src/drawer.types.ts)

### Animation and presence

- Given the indent-effect story before the drawer is opened, then the indent and indent background both have `data-inactive=""` and `--drawer-swipe-progress` is `0`. (zag: e2e/drawer-indent.e2e.ts: "should orchestrate indent/effect visual state during swipe")
- Given the indent-effect story after the drawer opens and settles, then the indent and indent background both have `data-active=""`, `--drawer-swipe-progress` is `0`, and `--drawer-frontmost-height` is a positive px value. (zag: e2e/drawer-indent.e2e.ts: "should orchestrate indent/effect visual state during swipe")
- Given the indent-effect story with the drawer open, when the grabber is dragged down 120px over 300ms without releasing, then `--drawer-swipe-progress` rises above `0` and the indent's computed transform differs from its resting transform. (zag: e2e/drawer-indent.e2e.ts: "should orchestrate indent/effect visual state during swipe")
- Given the indent-effect story mid-swipe, when the mouse is released and the snap animation settles, then `--drawer-swipe-progress` returns to `0` and the indent transform differs from its mid-swipe value. (zag: e2e/drawer-indent.e2e.ts: "should orchestrate indent/effect visual state during swipe")
- Test helpers wait for the drawer's enter and snap animations by awaiting `Promise.allSettled` over `element.getAnimations()`, and the closed state is detected by `data-state="closed"` on the content, so the drawer's open and snap transitions are Web Animations based. (zag: e2e/models/drawer.model.ts)
- Visible height is derived as `content.clientHeight - parseFloat(--drawer-translate)`, so the translate custom property is the observable drag position. (zag: e2e/models/drawer.model.ts)

### RTL and i18n

- The swipe direction is resolved through `resolveSwipeDirection(swipeDirection, dir)` before being written to `data-swipe-direction` and before signs are applied, so a logical direction maps to the mirrored physical direction in RTL. (zag: packages/machines/drawer/src/drawer.connect.ts)
- The swipe area's default opening direction is `oppositeSwipeDirection[swipeDirection]`, itself resolved against `dir`, and can be overridden per swipe area with its own `swipeDirection` prop. (zag: packages/machines/drawer/src/drawer.connect.ts)

### Accessibility tooling

- Given the drawer basic story with the drawer open, when axe runs over `[data-part=content]` with the color-contrast and `scrollable-region-focusable` rules disabled, then there are no violations. (zag: e2e/drawer.e2e.ts: "should have no accessibility violations")

### Notes and edge cases

- While swiping open before any drag offset has been recorded, the offset falls back to a sentinel of 9999px (or the measured content size once known), the content gets `visibility: hidden` and the backdrop gets `hidden`, so the drawer is off-screen rather than flashing at rest position. (zag: packages/machines/drawer/src/drawer.connect.ts)
- There are no Ark UI drawer tests in any framework package; the drawer contract is covered only by the Zag e2e specs and the stack unit test. (ark: packages/react/src/components, packages/solid/src/components, packages/vue/src/components/drawer, packages/svelte/src/lib/components/drawer)
- Scroll-blocking candidates are discovered by walking every descendant of the content and collecting those whose `scrollHeight > clientHeight` or `scrollWidth > clientWidth`, split per axis. (zag: packages/machines/drawer/src/drawer.dom.ts)
- A pointer event counts as "inside" the drawer when its target is contained by either the content or the swipe area subtree. (zag: packages/machines/drawer/src/drawer.dom.ts)

## popover

### Roles and attributes

- Anatomy parts are arrow, arrowTip, anchor, trigger, indicator, positioner, content, title, description, closeTrigger. (zag: packages/machines/popover/src/popover.anatomy.ts)
- The trigger is `type="button"` with `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-controls` on the content id, `aria-expanded`, `data-state` of open/closed, `data-placement`, `data-side`, `data-ownedby` set to the machine scope id, `data-value` for multi-trigger setups, and `data-current` on the active trigger. (zag: packages/machines/popover/src/popover.connect.ts)
- With multiple triggers, `aria-expanded` is only true on the trigger whose value matches the open one, and false on the rest. (zag: e2e/popover-multiple-trigger.e2e.ts: "should scope aria-expanded to the active trigger")
- With multiple triggers, only the active trigger carries `data-current=""`. (zag: e2e/popover-multiple-trigger.e2e.ts: "should set data-current only on the active trigger")
- The content is `role="dialog"` with `tabIndex={-1}`, `aria-modal` when modal, `hidden` while closed, `data-state`, `data-expanded`, `data-placement`, `data-side`, plus `aria-labelledby`/`aria-describedby` wired only when a title or description part is actually rendered. (zag: packages/machines/popover/src/popover.connect.ts)
- The indicator mirrors `data-state`, the close trigger is `type="button"` with a translated `aria-label`, and every part receives `dir`. (zag: packages/machines/popover/src/popover.connect.ts)
- Positioner styles come from the shared popper utility, which writes `--x`, `--y`, `--z-index`, `--reference-width`, `--reference-height`, `--available-width`, `--available-height` and `--transform-origin` onto the floating element, plus `--arrow-size`, `--arrow-size-half`, `--arrow-background` and `--arrow-offset` for the arrow. (zag: packages/utilities/popper/src/get-placement.ts; zag: packages/utilities/popper/src/middleware.ts)
- Given `lazyMount`, then the trigger has no `aria-controls` until the content exists; Vue has this case skipped with a TODO. (ark: packages/react/src/components/popover/tests/popover.test.tsx: "should not have aria-controls if lazy mounted"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/popover/tests/popover.test.tsx: "should not have aria-controls if lazy mounted"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/popover/tests/popover.test.ts: "should not have aria-controls if lazy mounted")

### Keyboard

- Given the trigger is focused, when Enter is pressed, then the popover opens. (zag: e2e/popover.e2e.ts: "[keyboard] should open the Popover on press `Enter`"; zag: e2e/popover-multiple-trigger.e2e.ts: "should open popover with Enter key")
- Given a focused trigger in a multi-trigger list, when Space is pressed, then the popover opens with that trigger's content. (zag: e2e/popover-multiple-trigger.e2e.ts: "should open popover with Space key")
- Given the popover is open, when Escape is pressed, then it closes and focus returns to the trigger. (zag: e2e/popover.e2e.ts: "[keyboard] should close the Popover on press `Escape`"; zag: e2e/popover-multiple-trigger.e2e.ts: "should close popover on escape"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/popover/tests/popover.test.tsx: "should hide the popover when escape is pressed")
- Vue skips its Escape-closes-popover case, so that path is unverified in Vue. (ark: packages/vue/src/components/popover/tests/popover.test.ts: "should hide the popover when escape is pressed")

### Pointer

- Given a closed popover, when the trigger is clicked, then it opens, and clicking the trigger again closes it. (zag: e2e/popover.e2e.ts: "[pointer] should to open/close a popover on trigger click")
- Given an open popover, when the close trigger is clicked, then it closes and focus returns to the trigger. (zag: e2e/popover.e2e.ts: "[pointer] close the popover on click close button"; zag: e2e/popover-multiple-trigger.e2e.ts: "should close popover on close trigger"; ark: packages/react/src/components/popover/tests/popover.test.tsx: "should open and close the popover"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/popover/tests/popover.test.tsx: "should open and close the popover"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/popover/tests/popover.test.ts: "should open and close the popover")
- Given a multi-trigger popover opened from the last trigger, when another trigger is clicked, then the popover stays open and swaps to that trigger's content. (zag: e2e/popover-multiple-trigger.e2e.ts: "should switch triggers while popover is open")
- Given a popover opened from trigger 1, then its content shows that trigger's payload. (zag: e2e/popover-multiple-trigger.e2e.ts: "should open popover from trigger")

### Focus management

- Given `autoFocus` is on, when the popover opens, then focus moves to the first focusable element inside the content. (zag: e2e/popover.e2e.ts: "[autoFocus=true] should move focus inside the popover content to the first focusable element"; ark: packages/react/src/components/popover/tests/popover.test.tsx: "should focus the first focusable element"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/popover/tests/popover.test.tsx: "should focus the first focusable element"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/popover/tests/popover.test.ts: "should focus the first focusable element")
- Given `autoFocus` is false, when the popover opens, then the content itself is not focused. (zag: e2e/popover.e2e.ts: "[autoFocus=false] should not focus the content")
- Given `modal` and an open popover, when Tab is pressed three times, then focus cycles back to the first link inside the content, so focus is trapped. (zag: e2e/popover.e2e.ts: "[keyboard / modal] on tab: should trap focus within popover content")
- Given a modal popover whose content has a single effective tab stop (a checked radio in a group), when Tab and then Shift+Tab are pressed, then focus stays on that radio - the trap handles a one-stop content without escaping. (zag: e2e/popover.e2e.ts: "[keyboard / modal] should trap focus when content has a single effective tab stop")
- Given a non-modal popover, when Tab is pressed past the end of the content, then focus moves to the next tabbable element after the trigger in document order. (zag: e2e/popover.e2e.ts: "[keyboard / non-modal] on tab outside: should move focus to next tabbable element after button")
- Given a non-modal popover, when Shift+Tab is pressed from the first content element, then focus returns to the trigger and the popover stays open. (zag: e2e/popover.e2e.ts: "[keyboard / non-modal] on shift-tab outside: should move focus to trigger")
- Given a non-modal popover whose trigger is the last tabbable element on the page, when Tab moves past the content's last element, then focus leaves the popover entirely rather than looping back into the content. (zag: e2e/popover.e2e.ts: "[keyboard / non-modal] when trigger is last tabbable: tab out should not loop into content")
- Given an open popover, when a focusable element outside is clicked, then the popover closes and focus stays on the clicked element rather than returning to the trigger. (zag: e2e/popover.e2e.ts: "[pointer] when clicking outside on focusable element, should not re-focus the button")
- The refocus-the-trigger-after-outside-click case is skipped, so that path is not verified. (zag: e2e/popover.e2e.ts: "[pointer] when clicking outside, should re-focus the button")
- Given keyboard navigation moved focus from trigger 1 to trigger 2 before opening, when Escape closes the popover, then focus returns to trigger 2. (zag: e2e/popover-multiple-trigger.e2e.ts: "should return focus to correct trigger after keyboard navigation")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given `defaultOpen`, then the dialog is present on first render. (ark: packages/react/src/components/popover/tests/popover.test.tsx: "should open by default")
- Given a controlled popover, when an external toggle button is clicked twice, then the popover opens and closes; Vue skips this case. (ark: packages/react/src/components/popover/tests/popover.test.tsx: "should allow controlled usage"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/popover/tests/popover.test.tsx: "should allow controlled usage"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/popover/tests/popover.test.ts: "should allow controlled usage")

### Positioning

- Given a popover opened from the last trigger, when a higher trigger is clicked, then the positioner's Y coordinate decreases, so the floating element repositions to the new anchor. (zag: e2e/popover-multiple-trigger.e2e.ts: "should reposition when switching triggers")

### Animation and presence

- Given `lazyMount`, then the positioner is absent until first open and stays mounted after closing. (ark: packages/react/src/components/popover/tests/popover.test.tsx: "should be able to lazy mount"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/popover/tests/popover.test.tsx: "should be able to lazy mount"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/popover/tests/popover.test.ts: "should be able to lazy mount")
- Given `lazyMount` with `unmountOnExit`, then the positioner mounts on open and is removed again after close. (ark: packages/react/src/components/popover/tests/popover.test.tsx: "should lazy mount and unmount on exit"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/popover/tests/popover.test.tsx: "should lazy mount and unmount on exit"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/popover/tests/popover.test.ts: "should lazy mount and unmount on exit")

### Accessibility tooling

- Given the basic popover, when axe runs over the root, then there are no violations; React must wrap the render in `act` first. (zag: e2e/popover.e2e.ts: "should have no accessibility violations"; ark: packages/react/src/components/popover/tests/popover.test.tsx: "should have no a11y violations")

## hover-card

### Roles and attributes

- Anatomy parts are arrow, arrowTip, trigger, positioner, content, under the scope name `hoverCard`. (zag: packages/machines/hover-card/src/hover-card.anatomy.ts)
- The trigger carries `data-placement`, `data-side`, `data-state`, `data-ownedby`, `data-value` and `data-current`, and listens for pointer-enter, pointer-leave, focus and blur. (zag: packages/machines/hover-card/src/hover-card.connect.ts)
- The content is `hidden` while closed, has `tabIndex={-1}`, `data-state`, `data-placement` and `data-side`, and keeps the card open through its own pointer-enter and pointer-leave handlers. (zag: packages/machines/hover-card/src/hover-card.connect.ts)
- With multiple triggers, only the hovered trigger carries `data-current=""`. (zag: e2e/hover-card-multiple-trigger.e2e.ts: "should set data-current on the active trigger")

### Pointer

- Given a hover card, then the content is not visible on load. (zag: e2e/hover-card.e2e.ts: "content should be hidden by default")
- Given the trigger is hovered, then the content becomes visible after the open delay. (zag: e2e/hover-card.e2e.ts: "should be opened after hovering trigger"; zag: e2e/hover-card-multiple-trigger.e2e.ts: "should open hover card on hover"; ark: packages/react/src/components/hover-card/tests/hover-card.test.tsx: "should open on hover"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/hover-card/tests/hover-card.test.tsx: "should open on hover"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/hover-card/tests/hover-card.test.ts: "should open on hover")
- Given the card is open, when the pointer moves from the trigger onto the content, then the card stays open, so the gap between them does not close it. (zag: e2e/hover-card.e2e.ts: "should remain open after moving from trigger to content")
- Given the pointer is over the content, when it moves back onto the trigger, then the card stays open. (zag: e2e/hover-card.e2e.ts: "should remain open after moving from content back to trigger")
- Given the card is open by hover, when the pointer leaves entirely, then the card closes. (zag: e2e/hover-card-multiple-trigger.e2e.ts: "should close hover card on mouse leave"; ark: packages/react/src/components/hover-card/tests/hover-card.test.tsx: "should open on hover")
- Given a multi-trigger hover card open on trigger 1, when trigger 3 is hovered, then the content swaps to trigger 3's payload without closing. (zag: e2e/hover-card-multiple-trigger.e2e.ts: "should switch triggers on hover")

### Focus management

- Given the trigger is focused programmatically, then the card opens. (zag: e2e/hover-card.e2e.ts: "should be opened after focusing trigger")
- Given the card was opened by focus, when the trigger is blurred, then the card closes after roughly 500ms. (zag: e2e/hover-card.e2e.ts: "should be closed after blurring trigger")
- Given the card was opened by tabbing to the trigger, when Tab moves focus away, then the card closes. (zag: e2e/hover-card.e2e.ts: "should be closed after blurring trigger with keyboard")
- Given the card was opened by pointer and then also focused, when the trigger is blurred, then the card stays open, and only moving the pointer elsewhere closes it - pointer intent outranks focus intent. (zag: e2e/hover-card.e2e.ts: "should remain open after blurring trigger if pointer opens card")
- Given keyboard modality is established by a Shift+Tab, when trigger 1 receives focus, then the card opens with its content. (zag: e2e/hover-card-multiple-trigger.e2e.ts: "should open hover card on keyboard focus")
- Given trigger 1 is focused, when Tab moves to trigger 2, then the open card switches to trigger 2's content. (zag: e2e/hover-card-multiple-trigger.e2e.ts: "should switch triggers on keyboard navigation")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given `defaultOpen`, then the content is visible on first render. (ark: packages/react/src/components/hover-card/tests/hover-card.test.tsx: "should open by default")
- Given an onOpenChange handler, when the trigger is hovered, then it fires exactly once. (ark: packages/react/src/components/hover-card/tests/hover-card.test.tsx: "should invoke onOpenChange"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/hover-card/tests/hover-card.test.tsx: "should invoke onOpenChange"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/hover-card/tests/hover-card.test.ts: "should invoke onOpenChange")

### Dismissal and layering

- Given an open hover card, when Escape is pressed, then it closes. (zag: e2e/hover-card-multiple-trigger.e2e.ts: "should close hover card on escape")

### Positioning

- Given side-by-side triggers, when the hovered trigger changes, then the positioner's X coordinate changes. (zag: e2e/hover-card-multiple-trigger.e2e.ts: "should reposition when switching triggers")

### Animation and presence

- Given `lazyMount`, then the positioner is absent until the first hover. (ark: packages/react/src/components/hover-card/tests/hover-card.test.tsx: "should lazy mount"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/hover-card/tests/hover-card.test.tsx: "should lazy mount"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/hover-card/tests/hover-card.test.ts: "should lazy mount")
- Given `lazyMount` with `unmountOnExit`, then the positioner mounts on hover and unmounts on unhover. (ark: packages/react/src/components/hover-card/tests/hover-card.test.tsx: "should lazy mount and unmount on exit"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/hover-card/tests/hover-card.test.tsx: "should lazy mount and unmount on exit"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/hover-card/tests/hover-card.test.ts: "should lazy mount and unmount on exit")
- The Vue hover-card fixture wraps its content in `<Teleport to="body">`, so Vue proves the portalled path where React and Solid use the inline one. (ark: packages/vue/src/components/hover-card/tests/hover-card.test.vue)

### Accessibility tooling

- Given the hover card, when axe runs over the trigger, then there are no violations; when the card is open, axe over the content is also clean. (zag: e2e/hover-card.e2e.ts: "should have no accessibility violation"; zag: e2e/hover-card.e2e.ts: "should have no accessibility violation in content"; ark: packages/react/src/components/hover-card/tests/hover-card.test.tsx: "should have no a11y violations")

## tooltip

### Roles and attributes

- Anatomy parts are trigger, arrow, arrowTip, positioner, content. (zag: packages/machines/tooltip/src/tooltip.anatomy.ts)
- The trigger carries `data-expanded`, `data-state`, `data-ownedby`, `data-value`, `data-current`, and `aria-describedby` pointing at the content only while open. (zag: packages/machines/tooltip/src/tooltip.connect.ts)
- The content is `role="tooltip"` unless the consumer passed an `aria-label`, in which case the role is dropped; it is `hidden` while closed and carries `data-state`, `data-placement`, `data-side` and `data-instant` for the no-delay case. (zag: packages/machines/tooltip/src/tooltip.connect.ts)
- With multiple triggers, only the active trigger carries `data-current=""`. (zag: e2e/tooltip-multiple-trigger.e2e.ts: "should set data-current on active trigger")
- Given `interactive={false}`, then the content has `pointer-events: none` so the pointer can never enter it. (ark: packages/react/src/components/tooltip/tests/tooltip.test.tsx: "should have pointer-events none style if interactive is set to false"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/tooltip/tests/tooltip.test.tsx: "should have pointer-events none style if interactive is set to false"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/tooltip/tests/tooltip.test.ts: "should have pointer-events none style if interactive is set to false")

### Pointer

- Given the trigger is hovered for the open delay (the model waits 1000ms), then the tooltip shows, and moving the pointer to the corner hides it. (zag: e2e/tooltip.e2e.ts: "should open tooltip on hover interaction"; zag: e2e/tooltip-multiple-trigger.e2e.ts: "should open tooltip on hover"; ark: packages/react/src/components/tooltip/tests/tooltip.test.tsx: "should show the tooltip on pointerover and close on pointer leave"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/tooltip/tests/tooltip.test.tsx: "should show the tooltip on pointerover and close on pointer leave"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/tooltip/tests/tooltip.test.ts: "should show the tooltip on pointerover and close on pointer leave")
- Given tooltip 1 is open, when tooltip 2's trigger is hovered without waiting, then tooltip 1 closes and tooltip 2 opens immediately, because a shared store allows only one open tooltip at a time. (zag: e2e/tooltip.e2e.ts: "should show only one tooltip at a time")
- Given an open tooltip, when pointerdown fires on its trigger, then it closes - pressing the trigger dismisses rather than keeping it open. (zag: e2e/tooltip.e2e.ts: "closes on pointerdown")
- Given an open tooltip, when the pointer moves away to (0,0), then it hides. (zag: e2e/tooltip-multiple-trigger.e2e.ts: "should close tooltip on mouse leave")
- Given a multi-trigger tooltip open on trigger 1, when trigger 3 is hovered, then the content swaps to trigger 3's text. (zag: e2e/tooltip-multiple-trigger.e2e.ts: "should switch triggers on hover")
- Given `disabled={false}` is passed explicitly, then hovering still opens the tooltip. (ark: packages/react/src/components/tooltip/tests/tooltip.test.tsx: "should show on pointerover if isDisabled has a falsy value"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/tooltip/tests/tooltip.test.tsx: "should show on pointerover if isDisabled has a falsy value"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/tooltip/tests/tooltip.test.ts: "should show on pointerover if isDisabled has a falsy value")
- The trigger listens to pointermove rather than pointerenter for opening, and to pointerleave plus click and blur for closing, and the content has its own pointermove and pointerleave handlers for the interactive case. (zag: packages/machines/tooltip/src/tooltip.connect.ts)

### Focus management

- Given the page is clicked and Tab focuses the first trigger, then that tooltip opens, and clicking outside closes it. (zag: e2e/tooltip.e2e.ts: "should work with focus/blur")
- Given tooltip 1 is open from focus, when Tab moves to the next trigger, then tooltip 1 closes and tooltip 2 opens. (zag: e2e/tooltip.e2e.ts: "should work with focus/blur for multiple tooltips"; zag: e2e/tooltip-multiple-trigger.e2e.ts: "should switch triggers on keyboard navigation")
- Given keyboard modality established by Shift+Tab, when a trigger receives focus, then its tooltip opens. (zag: e2e/tooltip-multiple-trigger.e2e.ts: "should open tooltip on keyboard focus")

### Dismissal and layering

- Given a tooltip opened by keyboard, when Escape is pressed, then it closes. (zag: e2e/tooltip.e2e.ts: "closes on esc press"; zag: e2e/tooltip-multiple-trigger.e2e.ts: "should close tooltip on escape"; ark: packages/react/src/components/tooltip/tests/tooltip.test.tsx: "should hide the tooltip when escape is pressed"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/tooltip/tests/tooltip.test.tsx: "should hide the tooltip when escape is pressed"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/tooltip/tests/tooltip.test.ts: "should hide the tooltip when escape is pressed")
- Given `closeOnEscape={false}`, when Escape is pressed, then the tooltip stays open. (ark: packages/react/src/components/tooltip/tests/tooltip.test.tsx: "should not hide the tooltip when escape is pressed if closeOnEsc is set to false"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/tooltip/tests/tooltip.test.tsx: "should not hide the tooltip when escape is pressed if closeOnEsc is set to false"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/tooltip/tests/tooltip.test.ts: "should not hide the tooltip when escape is pressed if closeOnEsc is set to false")

### Positioning

- Given a tooltip opened from the last trigger, when the first trigger is hovered, then the positioner's Y coordinate decreases. (zag: e2e/tooltip-multiple-trigger.e2e.ts: "should reposition when switching triggers")

### Animation and presence

- Given `lazyMount`, then no tooltip element exists until the first hover, and it is hidden again after Escape. (ark: packages/react/src/components/tooltip/tests/tooltip.test.tsx: "should lazy render the tooltip"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/tooltip/tests/tooltip.test.tsx: "should lazy render the tooltip"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/tooltip/tests/tooltip.test.ts: "should lazy render the tooltip")
- Given `lazyMount` with `unmountOnExit`, then the tooltip is removed from the DOM after it closes; Vue closes it by unhovering where React and Solid press Escape. (ark: packages/react/src/components/tooltip/tests/tooltip.test.tsx: "should lazy mount and unmount on exit"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/tooltip/tests/tooltip.test.tsx: "should lazy mount and unmount on exit"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/tooltip/tests/tooltip.test.ts: "should lazy mount and unmount on exit")

### Accessibility tooling

- Given the tooltip example, when axe runs over `main`, then there are no violations; React wraps the render in `act`. (ark: packages/react/src/components/tooltip/tests/tooltip.test.tsx: "should have no a11y violations"; zag: e2e/models/tooltip.model.ts)

## toast

### Roles and attributes

- Anatomy parts are group, root, title, description, actionTrigger, closeTrigger. (zag: packages/machines/toast/src/toast.anatomy.ts)
- Each toast root is `role="status"` with `aria-atomic="true"`, `tabIndex={0}`, `aria-labelledby`/`aria-describedby` wired only when a title or description exists, and the attribute block `data-state` (open/closed), `data-type`, `data-placement`, `data-align`, `data-side`, `data-mounted`, `data-paused`, `data-first` on the frontmost toast, `data-sibling` on the rest, `data-stack` when expanded and `data-overlap` when collapsed. (zag: packages/machines/toast/src/toast.connect.ts)
- The group region is `role="region"` with `tabIndex={-1}`, `aria-live="polite"`, `aria-relevant="additions text"`, `aria-atomic="false"`, `data-placement`, `data-side`, `data-align`, and an `aria-label` that spells out the label, placement and the hotkey combination. (zag: packages/machines/toast/src/toast-group.connect.ts)
- Ghost-before and ghost-after elements carry `data-ghost` of `before`/`after`, giving the region hit-area padding so the pointer can travel between toasts. (zag: packages/machines/toast/src/toast.connect.ts)
- The group sets `--gap`, `--first-height`, and `--viewport-offset-top/right/bottom/left` on the region. (zag: packages/machines/toast/src/toast.utils.ts)
- Each toast sets `--opacity`, `--remove-delay`, `--duration`, `--initial-height`, `--offset`, `--index`, `--z-index`, `--lift-amount` (computed as `var(--lift) * var(--gap)`), `--x`, `--y`, `--sign`, `--lift`, `--height`, `--base-scale` and `--scale`, with the sign and lift flipping by placement so the same animation works top and bottom. (zag: packages/machines/toast/src/toast.utils.ts)
- The action trigger and close trigger are both `type="button"`, the close trigger carrying a translated `aria-label`, and both dismiss with a `user` source. (zag: packages/machines/toast/src/toast.connect.ts)

### Keyboard

- Given two toasts, when the Alt+T hotkey is pressed, then the region takes focus, all toasts pause and the stack expands; clicking outside collapses it again. (zag: e2e/toast.e2e.ts: "focus on region on hotkey press")
- Each toast handles Escape from its own root to dismiss with a `keyboard` source. (zag: packages/machines/toast/src/toast.connect.ts)

### Pointer

- Given three error toasts on the stacked example, when the pointer enters the region, then every toast reports `data-paused=""`, and when the pointer leaves they resume and eventually all dismiss. (zag: e2e/toast.e2e.ts: "should pause on hover region")
- Given the overlap example, when one error toast is created, then it shows its title and later removes itself. (zag: e2e/toast.e2e.ts: "should render/remove error toast")
- Given three toasts on the overlap example, then all three exist and each carries `data-overlap=""`. (zag: e2e/toast.e2e.ts: "should overlap toasts by default")
- Given three loading toasts, when the pointer enters the region, then every toast switches to `data-stack=""`, and leaving the region collapses them back to `data-overlap=""`. (zag: e2e/toast.e2e.ts: "hover on region should expand region")
- Given two toasts, when Pause All is clicked, then all report paused, and Resume All lets them finish and disappear. (zag: e2e/toast.e2e.ts: "should pause all toast on click pause")
- Given two paused toasts, when Close All is clicked, then no toasts remain. (zag: e2e/toast.e2e.ts: "close all")
- Given four expanded loading toasts, when the third toast's close button is hovered and clicked, then the remaining toasts stay expanded one frame later rather than collapsing mid-interaction. (zag: e2e/toast.e2e.ts: "closing a toast should keep it expanded")
- Given a created toast, when its Close control is clicked, then the title and description leave the DOM. (ark: packages/react/src/components/toast/tests/toast.test.tsx: "should show and hide a toast message"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/toast/tests/toast.test.tsx: "should show and hide a toast message")

### Dismissal and layering

- Given a loading toast and an open dialog, when the toast's close button is clicked, then the dialog stays open and only the toast is removed, so a toast click is not treated as an outside-click for the dialog; this case runs only when FRAMEWORK is react. (zag: e2e/toast.e2e.ts: "interacting with toast does not close dialog")

### Accessibility tooling

- Given the React toast example, when axe runs, then there are no violations. (ark: packages/react/src/components/toast/tests/toast.test.tsx: "should have no a11y violations")

## tour

### Roles and attributes

- Anatomy parts are content, actionTrigger, closeTrigger, progressText, title, description, positioner, arrow, arrowTip, backdrop, spotlight. (zag: packages/machines/tour/src/tour.anatomy.ts)
- The content is `role="alertdialog"` with `aria-modal="true"`, `aria-live="polite"`, `aria-atomic="true"`, `tabIndex={-1}`, `hidden` while closed, `aria-labelledby` and `aria-describedby` on the title and description ids, and the attributes `data-state`, `data-type` (the step type), `data-placement`, `data-side` and `data-step` naming the current step id. (zag: packages/machines/tour/src/tour.connect.ts)
- Title and description carry `data-placement` of `center` when the step has no target, else the resolved placement and side. (zag: packages/machines/tour/src/tour.connect.ts)
- The backdrop is hidden while closed, carries `data-state` and `data-type`, and sits at `--tour-layer: 0`; the spotlight sits at layer 1 and exposes `--spotlight-x`, `--spotlight-y`, `--spotlight-width` and `--spotlight-height` from the measured target rect; the positioner sits at layer 2 with `--x`, `--y` and a `--z-index` of `calc(var(--tour-layer) + var(--tour-z-index))`. (zag: packages/machines/tour/src/tour.connect.ts)
- The spotlight is hidden when the tour is closed or the current step has no target. (zag: packages/machines/tour/src/tour.connect.ts)
- Action triggers are `type="button"` and take `data-type` of next, prev, close, skip or custom, with `data-disabled` when there is no next or previous step and translated aria-labels. (zag: packages/machines/tour/src/tour.connect.ts)
- The public api covers next, prev, dismiss, skip, setStep, start, addStep, removeStep, updateStep and setSteps. (zag: packages/machines/tour/src/tour.connect.ts)

### Keyboard

- Given the tour is open, when ArrowRight is pressed repeatedly, then it advances through step-0 (centered, no target), step-1 (a data-fetching step with a spotlight), step-2 (a target inside an overflow container), step-2a (a target inside an iframe, resolved through a frame locator), step-3 (near the bottom of the page), step-4 (at the very bottom) and step-5 (the final step with its own title), showing a spotlight over each target.
