- Given `multiple` enabled, when Enter selects `Badakhshān`, the highlight is walked with ArrowLeft plus eight ArrowDown presses into China to select `Guangxi`, and then walked back with ArrowLeft plus eight ArrowUp presses to press Enter on `Badakhshān` again, then the trigger reads `Badakhshān, Guangxi` and finally just `Guangxi`, so Enter toggles an already selected leaf off. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "advanced selection behavior > keyboard selection behavior > should support keyboard multiple selection toggle")
- Given the open dropdown whose first column contains the disabled `Antarctica`, when Home, ArrowDown and ArrowUp are pressed, then the highlight lands on `Africa`, skips `Antarctica` to reach `Asia`, and skips it again coming back to `Africa`. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "disabled items > should skip disabled items during keyboard navigation")
- The trigger keydown map handles ArrowUp, ArrowDown (with `altKey` opening instead of stepping), ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, Enter and Space, and calls `preventDefault` for each; unlike select there is no typeahead fallback on the trigger. (zag: packages/machines/cascade-select/src/cascade-select.connect.ts)
- The content keydown map handles ArrowDown, ArrowUp, ArrowRight, ArrowLeft, Home, End, Enter and the literal `" "` key, calls `preventDefault`, only acts when the event target is the content itself (`isSelfTarget`), blocks Tab unless `isValidTabEvent` allows it, and bails out for editable targets. (zag: packages/machines/cascade-select/src/cascade-select.connect.ts)

### Pointer

- Given the closed cascade select, when the trigger is clicked, then the content and the depth-0 list are visible, and clicking the trigger again hides the content. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "basic functionality > should toggle dropdown on trigger click")
- Given `allowParentSelection` and no value, then the clear trigger is not visible; after clicking `Africa` the trigger reads `Africa` and the clear trigger becomes visible. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "basic functionality > should show clear trigger when value is selected")
- Given `allowParentSelection` with `Africa` selected, when the clear trigger is clicked, then the trigger falls back to `Select a location` and the clear trigger is hidden again. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "basic functionality > should clear value when clear trigger is clicked")
- Given the open dropdown showing only the depth-0 list, when `Africa` is clicked then `Algeria` is clicked, then depth-1 appears and then depth-2 appears, so each branch click adds exactly one column. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "navigation and lists > should show multiple lists when navigating into parent items")
- Given the default `highlightTrigger` of click, when `Africa` and then `Algeria` are clicked, then each clicked item becomes highlighted and opens the next depth list. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "click highlighting (default) > should highlight items on click for navigation")
- Given the default click highlight trigger, when `Africa` is hovered, then no item has `data-highlighted`; only clicking it highlights it. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "click highlighting (default) > should not highlight on hover with click trigger")
- Given `highlightTrigger="hover"`, when `Africa` is hovered then `Algeria` is hovered, then `Africa` is highlighted with depth-1 visible, and then two items are highlighted at once (the whole path) with depth-2 visible. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "hover highlighting > should highlight parent items on hover")
- Given `highlightTrigger="hover"` with the pointer resting over `Algeria`, when End moves the highlight to `Zimbabwe` and the mouse is moved again to the same unchanged coordinates, then the highlight stays on `Zimbabwe` (and is in the viewport), and a fresh hover on `Zambia` then moves it; the test comment pins the WebKit behaviour of emitting a pointermove at an unchanged position when content scrolls under a resting cursor. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "hover highlighting > should keep keyboard highlight when content scrolls under a resting pointer")
- Given `highlightTrigger="hover"` and the path `Africa > Algeria` hovered open, when `Africa` is hovered again, then only one item stays highlighted and the depth-2 list is hidden, so hovering an ancestor collapses the deeper path. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "hover highlighting > should collapse the path when hovering back to a parent item")
- Given `highlightTrigger="hover"` and the path hovered down to the states column, when the leaf `Adrar` is hovered, then only two items are highlighted (`Africa` and `Algeria`), so leaves are not added to the highlighted path. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "hover highlighting > should not highlight full path for leaf items")
- Given `highlightTrigger="hover"` with `Africa` highlighted, when the pointer moves out to the content's (0, 0) corner, then `Africa` stays highlighted because of the grace area. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "hover highlighting > should support grace area for smooth navigation")
- Given `multiple` with two leaf selections made by clicking, when the clear trigger is clicked, then the trigger resets to `Select a location` and the clear trigger is hidden. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "advanced selection behavior > interaction with other features > should clear value and maintain consistency")
- Given `highlightTrigger="hover"`, `allowParentSelection`, `multiple` and `closeOnSelect=false`, when `Africa` is hovered then clicked and `Asia` is hovered then clicked, then hover drives the highlight while the clicks accumulate the value to `Africa, Asia`. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "advanced selection behavior > interaction with other features > should handle complex selection with hover highlighting")
- Given the open dropdown, when the disabled `Antarctica` item is force-clicked, then the trigger still reads `Select a location` and the dropdown stays open. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "disabled items > should not respond to clicks on disabled items")
- Given `highlightTrigger="hover"`, when the disabled `Antarctica` item is hovered, then no item is highlighted. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "disabled items > should not respond to hover on disabled items when hover highlighting is enabled")
- Item `onPointerMove` sends `ITEM.POINTER_ENTER` with the value, index path and `clientX`/`clientY` only for mouse pointers under `pointer` interaction modality, skipping disabled items and the already highlighted value; `onPointerLeave` sends `ITEM.POINTER_LEAVE` with the same coordinates, which is how the grace area is computed. (zag: packages/machines/cascade-select/src/cascade-select.connect.ts)
- The content part has its own `onPointerMove` that forwards `clientX`, `clientY` and `target` as a `POINTER_MOVE` event so the machine can track the pointer between columns. (zag: packages/machines/cascade-select/src/cascade-select.connect.ts)
- An item's `onDoubleClick` sends `CLOSE` for non-disabled items. (zag: packages/machines/cascade-select/src/cascade-select.connect.ts)

### Focus management

- Given the cascade select, when the label is clicked, then the trigger receives focus, because the label `onClick` focuses the trigger with `preventScroll: true` unless disabled. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "accessibility > clicking the label should focus control"; zag: packages/machines/cascade-select/src/cascade-select.connect.ts)
- Given the trigger focused and Enter pressed to open, when ArrowDown is pressed, then `Asia` becomes highlighted, so keyboard focus stays inside the dropdown after opening rather than moving to an item element. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "focus management > should maintain focus within dropdown during navigation")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given `allowParentSelection`, when the branch `Africa` is clicked, then the trigger reads `Africa` and the dropdown stays open. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "selection behavior > should select valid continent when parent selection is allowed")
- Given `allowParentSelection`, when `Africa` then `Algeria` are clicked, then the trigger reads the path `Africa / Algeria` and the dropdown stays open. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "selection behavior > should select country when parent selection is allowed")
- Given default settings, when `Africa`, `Algeria` and the leaf `Adrar` are clicked, then the trigger reads `Africa / Algeria / Adrar` and the dropdown closes. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "selection behavior > should navigate to state list without parent selection")
- Given `multiple` and `closeOnSelect=false`, when two leaves from different paths (`Adrar` and `Badakhshān`) are clicked, then the trigger reads `Adrar, Badakhshān` and the dropdown stays open. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "selection behavior > should support multiple selection")
- Given `allowParentSelection`, when the branch `Africa` is clicked, then it stays highlighted and its child list stays open; clicking `Algeria` likewise keeps `Algeria` highlighted with the depth-2 list open. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "advanced selection behavior > parent selection allowed > should allow selecting parent items and keep them highlighted")
- Given `allowParentSelection` and the path navigated to a leaf, when the leaf `Adrar` is clicked, then the trigger reads `Africa / Algeria / Adrar` and no item is highlighted any more. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "advanced selection behavior > parent selection allowed > should clear highlighting when selecting leaf items")
- Given `allowParentSelection`, `multiple` and `closeOnSelect=false` with `Africa` already selected, when the descendant `Algeria` is selected, then the trigger reads only `Algeria` because the ancestor is dropped on conflict. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "advanced selection behavior > parent selection allowed > should resolve parent/child conflicts in multiple mode")
- Given `allowParentSelection`, `multiple` and `closeOnSelect=false` with `Algeria` selected, when `Africa` is clicked to navigate back and clicked again to select it, then the trigger reads only `Africa` because the descendant is dropped on conflict. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "advanced selection behavior > parent selection allowed > should remove child when parent is selected in multiple mode")
- Given `allowParentSelection`, `multiple` and `closeOnSelect=false`, when `Algeria` and then `Afghanistan` (different continents) are selected, then the trigger reads `Algeria, Afghanistan`, so non-overlapping paths coexist. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "advanced selection behavior > parent selection allowed > should handle multiple non-conflicting selections")
- Given the default `allowParentSelection=false`, when `Africa` and then `Algeria` are clicked, then the trigger keeps reading `Select a location` while each click opens the next depth list and highlights the clicked branch, so branch clicks navigate without selecting. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "advanced selection behavior > parent selection not allowed (default) > should navigate through parents without selecting them")
- Given the default `allowParentSelection=false`, when the leaf `Adrar` is clicked, then the trigger reads `Africa / Algeria / Adrar` and the dropdown closes. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "advanced selection behavior > parent selection not allowed (default) > should only select leaf items")
- Given `multiple` and `closeOnSelect=false`, when leaves `Adrar` and `Badakhshān` are selected and then `Adrar` is navigated to and clicked again, then the trigger goes `Adrar`, `Adrar, Badakhshān`, and finally just `Badakhshān`, so clicking a selected leaf toggles it off. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "advanced selection behavior > parent selection not allowed (default) > should support multiple leaf selections with toggle")
- Given `multiple`, `closeOnSelect=false` and `Adrar` already selected, when `Asia` is clicked, then the depth-1 list shows Asian countries, so navigation resumes from the most recent selection's path as its base. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "advanced selection behavior > parent selection not allowed (default) > should use most recent selection as base for navigation in multiple mode")
- Given default settings, when a leaf is selected through the path, then the trigger formats the single selection as the slash-joined full path `Africa / Algeria / Adrar`. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "advanced selection behavior > value formatting > should format single selection as full path")
- Given `multiple` and `closeOnSelect=false`, when two leaves are selected, then the trigger formats them as comma-separated leaf names `Adrar, Badakhshān` rather than full paths. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "advanced selection behavior > value formatting > should format multiple selections as comma-separated leaf names")
- Given `allowParentSelection`, `multiple` and `closeOnSelect=false`, when the parents `Africa` and `Asia` are selected, then the trigger reads `Africa` and then `Africa, Asia`. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "advanced selection behavior > value formatting > should format parent selections correctly when allowed")
- Given `allowParentSelection`, when the disabled `Antarctica` is force-clicked, then the trigger still reads `Select a location`, and a following click on `Africa` does set the trigger to `Africa`. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "advanced selection behavior > interaction with other features > should handle disabled items during selection attempts")
- Given `allowParentSelection` with `Africa` selected, when the dropdown is closed and reopened from the trigger, then `Africa` is highlighted again and the depth-1 countries list is shown, so the highlighted path is restored from the value. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "advanced selection behavior > interaction with other features > should maintain selection state when reopening dropdown")
- Given `disabled`, when the trigger is force-clicked, then the content never becomes visible. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "disabled and readonly states > should not open dropdown when disabled")
- Given `readOnly`, when the trigger is clicked, then the content never becomes visible. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "disabled and readonly states > should not open dropdown when readonly")
- `getItemState` computes `highlighted` by prefix-comparing the item's value path against `highlightedValue`, `selected` via deep `isEqual` against any entry of `value`, `hasChildren` from `collection.isBranchNode`, plus `depth`, `highlightedChild` and `highlightedIndex` for the item's own column. (zag: packages/machines/cascade-select/src/cascade-select.connect.ts)

### Forms

- The hidden form input is an `input` (not a native `select` as in select) with `name`, `form`, `disabled`, `multiple`, `required`, `readOnly`, `hidden`, `aria-hidden="true"`, an `id` the label's `htmlFor` points at, `aria-labelledby` the label id, and a `defaultValue` taken from `context.hash("value")`. (zag: packages/machines/cascade-select/src/cascade-select.connect.ts)

### Dismissal and layering

- Given the open dropdown, when Escape is pressed, then the content is hidden and focus returns to the trigger. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "keyboard navigation > should close dropdown with Escape")
- Given `allowParentSelection` and `closeOnSelect=true`, when the branch `Africa` is selected, then the dropdown stays open, so `closeOnSelect` only applies to leaves. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "advanced selection behavior > close on select behavior > should not close when selecting parent items")
- Given `closeOnSelect=true`, when the leaf `Adrar` is selected, then the dropdown closes. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "advanced selection behavior > close on select behavior > should close when selecting leaf items")
- Given `closeOnSelect=false`, when the leaf `Adrar` is selected, then the dropdown stays open. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "advanced selection behavior > close on select behavior > should respect closeOnSelect false for leaf items")

### Accessibility tooling

- Given the basic cascade select example, when axe runs over the `.cascade-select` subtree with `color-contrast` disabled, then there are no violations. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "accessibility > should have no accessibility violation")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given `multiple` and `closeOnSelect=false`, when three leaves from three different continents are clicked back to back without waiting (`Adrar`, `Badakhshān`, `Auvergne`), then the trigger reads `Adrar, Badakhshān, Auvergne`. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "advanced selection behavior > edge cases > should handle rapid selections correctly")
- Given `allowParentSelection`, when `Africa` then `Algeria` then the leaf `Adrar` are clicked, then each branch stays highlighted in turn and the highlight is fully cleared once the leaf is selected. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "advanced selection behavior > edge cases > should maintain correct highlighting during complex navigation")
- Given `allowParentSelection`, `multiple` and `closeOnSelect=false`, when `Africa`, then `Algeria`, then `Adrar` are each selected in sequence, then the value collapses each time to the deepest node (`Africa`, `Algeria`, `Adrar`), and selecting `Asia` afterwards yields `Adrar, Asia`. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "advanced selection behavior > edge cases > should handle conflicting paths correctly in complex scenarios")
- Given `allowParentSelection`, `multiple` and `closeOnSelect=false`, when `Algeria` and then its sibling `Egypt` are selected, then the trigger reads `Algeria, Egypt`, so same-level siblings do not conflict. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts: "advanced selection behavior > edge cases > should handle same-level selections in multiple mode")
- The connect API exposes `collection`, `open`, `focused`, `multiple`, `disabled`, `value`, `highlightedValue`, `highlightedItems`, `selectedItems`, `hasSelectedItems`, `empty`, `valueAsString`, plus `reposition`, `focus`, `setOpen`, `setHighlightValue`, `clearHighlightValue`, `setValue`, `selectValue`, `clearValue(value?)` and `getItemState`. (zag: packages/machines/cascade-select/src/cascade-select.connect.ts)
- The machine prop surface adds the cascade-specific `allowParentSelection`, `highlightTrigger` (click or hover), `formatValue` and `collection` of tree nodes on top of the usual `closeOnSelect`, `loopFocus`, `multiple`, `scrollToIndexFn`, `positioning`, `readOnly`, `required`, `invalid` and the `onHighlightChange`/`onValueChange`/`onOpenChange`/`onFocusOutside`/`onInteractOutside`/`onPointerDownOutside` callbacks. (zag: packages/machines/cascade-select/src/cascade-select.props.ts)
- There is no Ark test file for cascade-select in any framework, so its Ark-level contract (asChild/render, RootProvider, Field integration, form submission) is untested. (zag: e2e/cascade-select.e2e.ts)
- The e2e model resolves items by an exact-match regex on the nested `[data-part=item-text]` rather than on the item itself, because `hasText` on the item would let `Africa` match `South Africa` and `Central African Republic`. (zag: e2e/models/cascade-select.model.ts)

## combobox

### Roles and attributes

- Anatomy parts are root, clearTrigger, content, control, input, item, itemGroup, itemGroupLabel, itemIndicator, itemText, label, list, positioner, trigger. (zag: packages/machines/combobox/src/combobox.anatomy.ts)
- Root carries `data-invalid` and `data-readonly`; the label adds `data-readonly`, `data-disabled`, `data-invalid`, `data-required` and `data-focus`; the control carries `data-state`, `data-focus`, `data-disabled` and `data-invalid`. (zag: packages/machines/combobox/src/combobox.connect.ts)
- The input is `role="combobox"` `type="text"` with `aria-autocomplete` of `both` when autocompleting else `list`, `aria-controls` on the content id, `aria-expanded`, `aria-activedescendant` naming the highlighted item, `aria-invalid`, `data-state`, `data-invalid`, `data-autofocus`, `autoComplete="off"` and `spellCheck="false"`. (zag: packages/machines/combobox/src/combobox.connect.ts)
- The trigger is `type="button"` with `aria-haspopup` of `listbox` (or `dialog` when not composite), `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` only while open, `aria-label` from translations, `data-state`, `data-invalid`, `data-readonly`, `data-disabled`, `data-focusable`, and `tabIndex={-1}` unless explicitly made focusable. (zag: packages/machines/combobox/src/combobox.connect.ts)
- The content is `role="listbox"` when composite and `role="dialog"` otherwise, with `tabIndex={-1}`, `hidden` while closed, `aria-labelledby` on the label, `aria-multiselectable` when multiple and composite, `data-state`, `data-placement`, `data-side` and `data-empty` when the collection is empty. (zag: packages/machines/combobox/src/combobox.connect.ts)
- When not composite the list part takes `role="listbox"` and the multiselectable flag instead, so the roles migrate between content and list depending on composition. (zag: packages/machines/combobox/src/combobox.connect.ts)
- Each item is `role="option"` with `tabIndex={-1}`, `aria-selected`, `aria-disabled`, `data-highlighted`, `data-state` of checked/unchecked, `data-disabled` and `data-value`; itemText mirrors state and highlight, and itemIndicator is `aria-hidden` and hidden unless selected. (zag: packages/machines/combobox/src/combobox.connect.ts)
- The item group is `role="group"` with `aria-labelledby` on its label, and the group label is `role="presentation"`. (zag: packages/machines/combobox/src/combobox.connect.ts)
- The clear trigger is `type="button"` with `tabIndex={-1}`, a translated `aria-label`, `aria-controls` on the input, `data-invalid`, and is `hidden` whenever the value is empty. (zag: packages/machines/combobox/src/combobox.connect.ts)
- Given the trigger is clicked, then it reports `aria-expanded="true"` and the options become visible. (ark: packages/react/src/components/combobox/tests/combobox.test.tsx: "should show options on click"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/combobox/tests/combobox.test.tsx: "should show options on click"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/combobox/tests/combobox.test.ts: "should show options on click")

### Keyboard

- Given the input is focused, when "c" is typed, then the list opens and focus stays in the input; typing "an" highlights "Canada" and Enter commits it into the input and closes the list. (zag: e2e/combobox.e2e.ts: "[keyboard] should open combobox menu when typing")
- Given the list is open, when Escape is pressed, then the list closes. (zag: e2e/combobox.e2e.ts: "[keyboard] Escape should close content")
- Given a closed combobox with loop enabled, when ArrowDown is pressed, then the list opens with the first enabled option highlighted, and ArrowUp from there wraps to the last option. (zag: e2e/combobox.e2e.ts: "[keyboard / loop] on arrow down, open and highlight first enabled option")
- Given `loopFocus` is false, when ArrowDown opens the list and ArrowUp is pressed at the first option, then the highlight stays on the first option. (zag: e2e/combobox.e2e.ts: "[keyboard / no-loop] on arrow down, open and highlight first enabled option")
- Given a closed combobox, when ArrowUp is pressed, then the list opens with the last enabled option highlighted, with or without looping. (zag: e2e/combobox.e2e.ts: "[keyboard / loop] on arrow up, open and highlight last enabled option"; zag: e2e/combobox.e2e.ts: "[keyboard / no-loop] on arrow up, open and highlight last enabled option")
- Given an open list, when Home and End are pressed, then the first and last options are highlighted. (zag: e2e/combobox.e2e.ts: "[keyboard / open] on home and end, when open, focus first and last option")
- Given the list has been closed with Escape while the input holds "an", when Home and End are pressed, then the caret moves to offset 0 and 2 instead of moving a highlight, so the keys switch meaning with the open state. (zag: e2e/combobox.e2e.ts: "[keyboard / closed] on home and end, caret moves to start and end")
- Given the filtered list from typing "mal" with loop on, when ArrowDown is pressed past the last match, then the highlight wraps to the first match. (zag: e2e/combobox.e2e.ts: "[keyboard / arrowdown / loop]")
- Given the same filtered list with loop off, when ArrowDown is pressed at the last match, then the highlight stays there. (zag: e2e/combobox.e2e.ts: "[keyboard / arrowdown / no-loop]")
- Given the filtered list, when ArrowUp is pressed first, then the last match is highlighted with loop on and the first match with loop off. (zag: e2e/combobox.e2e.ts: "[keyboard / arrowup / loop]"; zag: e2e/combobox.e2e.ts: "[keyboard / arrowup / no-loop]")
- The input key map handles ArrowDown and ArrowUp (with Alt turning them into plain open and close), Home, End, Enter and Escape, each carrying a `src` so the machine can distinguish key-driven from pointer-driven transitions. (zag: packages/machines/combobox/src/combobox.connect.ts)

### Pointer

- Given a closed combobox, when the trigger arrow is clicked, then the list opens and the input takes focus. (zag: e2e/combobox.e2e.ts: "[pointer] should open combobox menu when arrow is clicked")
- Given an open list, when an option is hovered it becomes highlighted, and clicking it writes its label into the input and closes the list. (zag: e2e/combobox.e2e.ts: "[pointer / selection]"; ark: packages/react/src/components/combobox/tests/combobox.test.tsx: "should handle item selection"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/combobox/tests/combobox.test.tsx: "should handle item selection"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/combobox/tests/combobox.test.ts: "should handle item selection")
- Given a value already selected, when the list is reopened and another option clicked, then the input takes the new value. (zag: e2e/combobox.e2e.ts: "[pointer] select and select again")
- Given `openOnClick`, when the input itself is clicked, then the list opens. (zag: e2e/combobox.e2e.ts: "[pointer / open-on-click]")
- Given an option is clicked, then it reports `data-state="checked"`. (zag: e2e/combobox.e2e.ts: "selects value on click")
- Given a selected value, when the clear trigger is clicked, then the input empties and the option is no longer checked. (zag: e2e/combobox.e2e.ts: "can clear value")
- Given autocomplete mode with "mal" typed, when an option is hovered, then the input value stays "mal" - hovering never rewrites the input. (zag: e2e/combobox.e2e.ts: "[pointer] hovering an option should not update input value")
- Given `readOnly`, when the trigger is clicked, then no options become visible. (ark: packages/react/src/components/combobox/tests/combobox.test.tsx: "should be read-only when readOnly is true"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/combobox/tests/combobox.test.tsx: "should be read-only when readOnly is true"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/combobox/tests/combobox.test.ts: "should be read-only when readOnly is true")

### Focus management

- Given the list is opened by clicking the trigger, then focus remains on the input rather than moving into the list. (zag: e2e/combobox.e2e.ts: "[pointer] should open combobox menu when arrow is clicked")
- Given a combobox inside a Field, when the field label is clicked, then the input receives focus. (ark: packages/react/src/components/combobox/tests/combobox.test.tsx: "should focus on combobox when label is clicked"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/combobox/tests/combobox.test.tsx: "should focus on combobox when label is clicked"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/combobox/tests/combobox.test.ts: "should focus on combobox when label is clicked")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given `selectionBehavior="clear"`, when a filtered item is committed with Enter, then the input value is cleared rather than filled with the label. (zag: e2e/combobox.e2e.ts: "[selection=clear] should clear input value")
- Given an option is selected, then onValueChange reports the selected item objects, clearing empties that list, and selecting a different option replaces rather than appends the previous item. (zag: e2e/combobox.e2e.ts: "[callback] onValueChange should include selected item in items"; zag: e2e/combobox.e2e.ts: "[callback] onValueChange items should be empty after clearing"; zag: e2e/combobox.e2e.ts: "[callback] onValueChange items should track latest selected item")
- Given `inputBehavior="none"` and no selection, when a custom string is typed and Enter pressed, then the input is cleared because the value is rejected. (zag: e2e/combobox.e2e.ts: "[no value] enter behavior for custom values")
- Given a value already selected, when the input text is replaced with junk and Enter pressed, then the input reverts to the selected item's label. (zag: e2e/combobox.e2e.ts: "[value] enter reverts the value")
- Given an item is selected, then onValueChange fires exactly once. (ark: packages/react/src/components/combobox/tests/combobox.test.tsx: "should call onValueChange when item is selected"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/combobox/tests/combobox.test.tsx: "should call onValueChange when item is selected"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/combobox/tests/combobox.test.ts: "should call onValueChange when item is selected")
- Given the trigger is clicked, then onOpenChange fires exactly once. (ark: packages/react/src/components/combobox/tests/combobox.test.tsx: "should open menu when onOpenChange is called"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/combobox/tests/combobox.test.tsx: "should open menu when onOpenChange is called"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/combobox/tests/combobox.test.ts: "should open menu when onOpenChange is called")
- Given a controlled example that ignores incoming value changes, when "Vue" is clicked, then the reported selected items stay at the controlled "React" and never include "Vue", proving the machine does not drift from a controlled value. (zag: e2e/combobox.e2e.ts: "[composition] controlled-ignore should keep selectedItems aligned with controlled value")
- Given an external button sets the value to "Solid" after the user has typed and dismissed the list, then the input shows "Solid" and reopening the list shows that item as `data-state="checked"`. (zag: e2e/combobox.e2e.ts: "[composition] external value change should keep item selection in sync")
- Given multiple mode, when the same item is committed twice with Enter, then it is selected and then deselected. (zag: e2e/combobox.e2e.ts: "should toggle the same item")
- Given multiple mode with `removeSelected`, when the same item is committed twice, then it stays selected because the selected item is removed from the list instead of being toggled. (zag: e2e/combobox.e2e.ts: "[removeSelected=true] should not toggle the same item")

### Forms

- Given the form example with `inputBehavior="none"`, when Enter commits a highlighted item, then the value is selected, the list closes and the form is not submitted. (zag: e2e/combobox.e2e.ts: "[keyboard] Enter on highlighted item selects and does not submit form")
- Given no highlighted item and a typed value that will be rejected, when Enter is pressed, then the form still does not submit. (zag: e2e/combobox.e2e.ts: "[no highlight / rejected value] Enter does not submit when typed value won't be accepted")
- Given `inputBehavior="autohighlight"`, when "z" is typed and Enter pressed, then the auto-highlighted item is selected and the form does not submit. (zag: e2e/combobox.e2e.ts: "[autoHighlight] Enter selects auto-highlighted item and does not submit")
- Given `allowCustomValue` with an item highlighted, when Enter is pressed, then the highlighted item wins and the form does not submit. (zag: e2e/combobox.e2e.ts: "[allowCustomValue + highlight] Enter selects highlighted item and does not submit")
- Given `allowCustomValue` with nothing highlighted, when Enter is pressed on a custom string, then the form submits once with that custom value on the first press. (zag: e2e/combobox.e2e.ts: "[allowCustomValue] Enter submits custom value on first press")
- Given `alwaysSubmitOnEnter` with an item highlighted, when Enter is pressed, then the item is selected and the form also submits. (zag: e2e/combobox.e2e.ts: "[alwaysSubmitOnEnter / highlight] Enter selects highlighted item and submits form")
- Given `alwaysSubmitOnEnter` with `allowCustomValue` and no highlight, when Enter is pressed, then the custom value is submitted. (zag: e2e/combobox.e2e.ts: "[alwaysSubmitOnEnter + allowCustomValue] Enter submits custom value with no highlight")
- Given a combobox inside a Field, then required, disabled and readOnly reach the combobox input, helper text renders, and error text appears only when invalid. (ark: packages/react/src/components/combobox/tests/combobox.test.tsx: "should set combobox as required"; ark: packages/react/src/components/combobox/tests/combobox.test.tsx: "should set combobox as disabled"; ark: packages/react/src/components/combobox/tests/combobox.test.tsx: "should set combobox as readonly"; ark: packages/react/src/components/combobox/tests/combobox.test.tsx: "should display helper text"; ark: packages/react/src/components/combobox/tests/combobox.test.tsx: "should display error text when error is present"; ark: packages/react/src/components/combobox/tests/combobox.test.tsx: "should not display error text when no error is present"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/combobox/tests/combobox.test.tsx: "should set combobox as required"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/combobox/tests/combobox.test.ts: "should set combobox as required")

### Animation and presence

- Given `lazyMount`, then the items are absent until the list first opens. (ark: packages/react/src/components/combobox/tests/combobox.test.tsx: "should be able to lazy mount its items"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/combobox/tests/combobox.test.tsx: "should be able to lazy mount its items"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/combobox/tests/combobox.test.ts: "should be able to lazy mount its items")
- Given `lazyMount` with `unmountOnExit`, then the positioner is removed again once the list closes. (ark: packages/react/src/components/combobox/tests/combobox.test.tsx: "should be able to lazy mount and unmount its items"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/combobox/tests/combobox.test.tsx: "should be able to lazy mount and unmount its items"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/combobox/tests/combobox.test.ts: "should be able to lazy mount and unmount its items")

### Accessibility tooling

- Given the basic combobox, when axe runs over the root, then there are no violations. (zag: e2e/combobox.e2e.ts: "should have no accessibility violations"; ark: packages/react/src/components/combobox/tests/combobox.test.tsx: "should have no a11y violations")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given autocomplete mode, when "mal" is typed, then nothing is highlighted until ArrowDown, after which Enter commits the highlighted match. (zag: e2e/combobox.e2e.ts: "[keyboard] should autocomplete")
- Given autocomplete mode, when ArrowDown walks past the last filtered option, then the input returns to the previously typed text and no option is highlighted, so the list cycles back through the raw input. (zag: e2e/combobox.e2e.ts: "[keyboard / loop] should loop through the options and previous input value")
- Given a selected value, then reopening the list highlights it and scrolls it into the content viewport. (zag: e2e/combobox.e2e.ts: "should scroll selected option into view")
- Given a scrolling list with a hovered item, when End is pressed, then the last item is highlighted and scrolled into view even though the pointer has not moved. (zag: e2e/combobox.e2e.ts: "on end key, keep highlight when scroll moves content under the cursor")
- Given the highlight was moved by keyboard after a scroll, when the pointer is moved onto another item, then hover regains control of the highlight. (zag: e2e/combobox.e2e.ts: "after keyboard scroll, hover still moves the highlight")
- The Vue combobox fixture builds its collection with `createListCollection`, binds through `v-model` and teleports the positioner to `body`, while React and Solid pass the collection as a prop and render inline. (ark: packages/vue/src/components/combobox/tests/combobox.test.vue)

## carousel

### Roles and attributes

- Anatomy parts are root, itemGroup, item, control, nextTrigger, prevTrigger, indicatorGroup, indicator, autoplayTrigger, progressText. (zag: packages/machines/carousel/src/carousel.anatomy.ts)
- The root is `role="region"` with `aria-roledescription="carousel"`, `data-orientation`, and the CSS variables `--slides-per-page`, `--slide-spacing` and `--slide-item-size`, which is how the slide width is derived in CSS rather than in JS. (zag: packages/machines/carousel/src/carousel.connect.ts)
- The item group carries `data-orientation`, `data-dragging` and `aria-live` of `off` while autoplaying and `polite` otherwise, and it is the scroll container that emits user-scroll events. (zag: packages/machines/carousel/src/carousel.connect.ts)
- Each item is `role="group"` with `aria-roledescription="slide"`, a translated `aria-label` naming its index and the total, `data-index`, `data-inview` when visible, `data-orientation`, and `aria-hidden` when out of view. (zag: packages/machines/carousel/src/carousel.connect.ts)
- Previous and next triggers are `type="button"` with translated aria-labels, `aria-controls` on the item group id and `data-orientation`, and they are disabled at the boundaries when looping is off. (zag: packages/machines/carousel/src/carousel.connect.ts)
- Each indicator is `type="button"` with `data-index`, `data-current` on the active page, `data-readonly` and a translated `aria-label`. (zag: packages/machines/carousel/src/carousel.connect.ts)
- The autoplay trigger is `type="button"` with `data-pressed` while playing and an `aria-label` that switches between the start and stop translations. (zag: packages/machines/carousel/src/carousel.connect.ts)
- Given the basic carousel, then six items render, the first indicator is current, slides 0 and 1 are `data-inview` and slide 2 is not. (zag: e2e/carousel.e2e.ts: "renders correctly")
- Given the example, then buttons named "Next slide" and "Previous slide" exist. (ark: packages/react/src/components/carousel/carousel.test.tsx: "should have the correct disabled / enabled states for control buttons")

### Keyboard

- Given an indicator is focused, when ArrowRight is pressed, then the carousel advances so the next slide is in view. (zag: e2e/carousel.e2e.ts: "indicator keyboard navigation")
- The indicator group key map wires ArrowRight/ArrowDown to the next page, ArrowLeft/ArrowUp to the previous page, and Home/End to the first and last page, with the horizontal keys swapped in RTL. (zag: packages/machines/carousel/src/carousel.connect.ts)

### Pointer

- Given the first page, then the previous trigger is disabled; clicking next makes indicator 1 current and enables the previous trigger. (zag: e2e/carousel.e2e.ts: "next/prev buttons navigate carousel")
- Given the basic carousel, when indicator 2 is clicked, then it becomes current and slides 4 and 5 come into view. (zag: e2e/carousel.e2e.ts: "clicking indicator scrolls to correct slide")
- Given an external "Scroll to 4" button, when it is clicked, then slide 4 comes into view, exercising the imperative scroll API. (zag: e2e/carousel.e2e.ts: "scroll to a specific index via button")
- Given a 400px left swipe on the item group, then slide 3 is in view and slides 0 and 1 are not. (zag: e2e/carousel.e2e.ts: "dragging behavior")
- Given a 20px drag held for 40ms and released, then the page does not change and the original slides stay in view, so a tiny drag is treated as a no-op. (zag: e2e/carousel.e2e.ts: "tiny drag and release keeps current page")
- Given a drag released and immediately followed by a second drag, then the carousel settles on the second drag's target page rather than the first. (zag: e2e/carousel.e2e.ts: "drag interruption and immediate restart resolves to final drag target")
- Given a drag that is still settling, when an indicator is clicked, then the indicator target wins over the drag's settle target. (zag: e2e/carousel.e2e.ts: "indicator click during settling wins over drag settle target")
- Given a wheel scroll that advances one page, when a drag follows, then the final page is the drag's target and the indicator stays in sync. (zag: e2e/carousel.e2e.ts: "wheel scroll followed by drag updates to the correct final page")
- Given two rapid clicks on the next trigger, then the carousel settles on the last page with the next trigger disabled and no indicator desync. (zag: e2e/carousel.e2e.ts: "rapid next trigger clicks settle on the last page without desync")
- Given a drag held for 180ms and released, then the indicator matches the snapped page immediately. (zag: e2e/carousel.e2e.ts: "drag release after hold keeps indicator in sync with snapped page")
- Given page 2 and a right drag held and released, then the carousel moves back exactly one snap point. (zag: e2e/carousel.e2e.ts: "dragging back after hold updates page to previous snap point")
- Given three successive drag-hold-release cycles in mixed directions, then the page state stays coherent throughout. (zag: e2e/carousel.e2e.ts: "repeated drag-hold-release cycles maintain page state")
- Given clicks and drags used interchangeably, then both paths converge on the same page and in-view slides. (zag: e2e/carousel.e2e.ts: "click and drag navigation converge to the same page state")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given `loop` is false, then dragging and wheeling past either boundary leaves the page clamped at the first or last page and the corresponding trigger disabled. (zag: e2e/carousel.e2e.ts: "loop=false boundary stress keeps page clamped at first and last pages")
- Given `loop` is true, then the previous trigger is enabled at the first page, clicking previous wraps to the last page and clicking next wraps back to the first. (zag: e2e/carousel.e2e.ts: "loop=true wraps both directions at boundaries with coherent indicator state"; zag: e2e/carousel.e2e.ts: "[loop=true] should loop slides")
- Given page 2, when `slidesPerPage` is changed to 3 at runtime, then the page clamps to 1 with slides 3-5 in view and the next trigger disabled, and changing it back to 1 keeps a coherent page with both triggers enabled. (zag: e2e/carousel.e2e.ts: "changing slidesPerPage at runtime clamps and preserves coherent page state")
- Given `slidesPerMove="auto"`, then each next click advances by a whole page. (zag: e2e/carousel.e2e.ts: "slidesPerMove='auto' advances by slidesPerPage")
- Given `slidesPerMove="1"`, then each next click advances exactly one slide. (zag: e2e/carousel.e2e.ts: "slidesPerMove='1' advances one slide per page transition")
- Given `slidesPerMove="2"`, then each next click advances two slides. (zag: e2e/carousel.e2e.ts: "slidesPerMove='2' advances two slides per page transition")
- Given page 4 under `slidesPerMove="1"`, when the prop changes to 2, then the page clamps to a valid page with the same slides in view and the next trigger disabled. (zag: e2e/carousel.e2e.ts: "changing slidesPerMove at runtime while mid-page clamps to valid page and keeps controls in sync")
- The autoplay start and stop case is skipped (it relies on Playwright's clock install), so autoplay timing is not verified in e2e. (zag: e2e/carousel.e2e.ts: "[loop=true] autoplay start/stop")
- Solid and Vue both skip their only carousel test, so the trigger disabled-state contract is proven only in React. (ark: packages/solid/src/components/carousel/carousel.test.tsx: "should have the correct disabled / enabled states for control buttons"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/carousel/carousel.test.ts: "should have the correct disabled / enabled states for control buttons")

### RTL and i18n

- Given `dir="rtl"`, then the next trigger, ArrowLeft on an indicator and wheel scrolling all advance in the mirrored direction and stay in sync, and the previous trigger walks back. (zag: e2e/carousel.e2e.ts: "rtl mode keeps trigger, keyboard, and wheel navigation in sync")
- Given page 1 in LTR, when `dir` is switched to rtl at runtime, then the page is preserved and ArrowLeft now advances; switching back to ltr preserves the page and remaps the keys again. (zag: e2e/carousel.e2e.ts: "switching dir while mid-page preserves page and remaps keyboard navigation")

### Accessibility tooling

- Given the basic carousel, when axe runs, then there are no violations; React wraps the render in `act` first. (zag: e2e/carousel.e2e.ts: "should have no accessibility violations"; ark: packages/react/src/components/carousel/carousel.test.tsx: "should have no a11y violations")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given `orientation="vertical"`, then the next trigger, ArrowDown on an indicator, wheel deltaY and a downward drag all move pages, and the boundary disables the next trigger. (zag: e2e/carousel.e2e.ts: "vertical orientation supports wheel, drag, and keyboard page updates")
- Given page 2, when the orientation is switched to vertical and back, then the page state and trigger disabled states survive both switches. (zag: e2e/carousel.e2e.ts: "switching orientation while on page 2 keeps page state and navigation coherent")
- The e2e model's settle helper prefers the native `scrollend` event and falls back to polling `scrollLeft`/`scrollTop` for three stable frames, because `scrollend` is not available in every browser. (zag: e2e/models/carousel.model.ts)

## async-list

### Roles and attributes

- async-list has no anatomy and emits no DOM attributes; it is a headless data machine whose api exposes `items`, `filterText`, `cursor`, `sortDescriptor`, `loading`, `sorting`, `empty`, `hasMore`, `error`, `abort`, `reload` and load-more, and it is designed to feed a combobox or listbox collection. (zag: packages/machines/async-list/src/async-list.types.ts; zag: packages/machines/async-list/src/async-list.connect.ts)

### Notes and edge cases

- Given the async combobox example with the SWAPI endpoint stubbed, when "lan" is typed, then only the server-matching person is listed and the non-matching ones are absent, so filtering happens server-side rather than over a local collection. (zag: e2e/combobox.e2e.ts: "[composition] async list should filter server results as user types")
- Given the async example, when a fetched item is clicked, then the input takes its label and the reported selected value matches, proving items fetched at runtime are selectable. (zag: e2e/combobox.e2e.ts: "[composition] async list should select fetched item")
- async-list ships no unit tests of its own; its behavior is covered only through the two combobox async e2e cases. (zag: packages/machines/async-list/src)

## date-picker

### Roles and attributes

- Anatomy parts are clearTrigger, content, control, input, label, monthSelect, nextTrigger, positioner, presetTrigger, prevTrigger, rangeText, root, table, tableBody, tableCell, tableCellTrigger, tableHead, tableHeader, tableRow, trigger, view, viewControl, viewTrigger, yearSelect. (zag: packages/machines/date-picker/src/date-picker.anatomy.ts)
- Root carries `data-state`, `data-disabled`, `data-readonly` and `data-empty`; the control carries `data-disabled`, `data-placeholder-shown` and `data-invalid`; the label adds `data-index`, `data-state`, `data-disabled`, `data-readonly` and `data-invalid`. (zag: packages/machines/date-picker/src/date-picker.connect.ts)
- The content is `role="application"` with `aria-roledescription="datepicker"`, a translated `aria-label`, `tabIndex={-1}`, `hidden` while closed, `data-state`, `data-placement`, `data-side` and `data-inline` for the inline variant. (zag: packages/machines/date-picker/src/date-picker.connect.ts)
- The table is `role="grid"` with `aria-roledescription` naming the current view, `aria-readonly`, `aria-disabled`, `aria-multiselectable` when the selection mode is not single, `data-view`, `data-columns` and `tabIndex={-1}`. (zag: packages/machines/date-picker/src/date-picker.connect.ts)
- Day cells are `role="gridcell"` with `aria-disabled` from selectability, `aria-selected` true when selected or inside a range, `aria-invalid`, `aria-current="date"` on today, and `data-value` holding the ISO date. (zag: packages/machines/date-picker/src/date-picker.connect.ts)
- Each day cell trigger is `role="button"` with a translated `aria-label`, roving `tabIndex` (0 only on the focused cell, -1 when disabled), and the attribute set `data-disabled`, `data-selectable`, `data-selected`, `data-value`, `data-view="day"`, `data-today`, `data-focus`, `data-unavailable`, `data-range-start`, `data-range-end`, `data-in-range`, `data-outside-range`, `data-weekend`, `data-in-hover-range`, `data-hover-range-start` and `data-hover-range-end`. (zag: packages/machines/date-picker/src/date-picker.connect.ts)
- Month and year cell triggers repeat the same contract with `data-view="month"` or `data-view="year"`, their own `aria-label` from the cell's value text, and the same range and hover-range attributes. (zag: packages/machines/date-picker/src/date-picker.connect.ts)
- The table head is `aria-hidden`; week-number header and cells carry `data-type="week-number"`, the cell being `role="rowheader"` with a translated label and `data-week-index`. (zag: packages/machines/date-picker/src/date-picker.connect.ts)
- The trigger is `type="button"` with `aria-haspopup="grid"`, `aria-controls`, `aria-expanded`, an `aria-label` that changes with the open state, `data-state`, `data-placement`, `data-side` and `data-placeholder-shown`. (zag: packages/machines/date-picker/src/date-picker.connect.ts)
- Previous and next triggers are `type="button"` with view-aware translated labels and `data-disabled` when that direction is out of range; the view trigger is a button whose label names the next view; the view part is `hidden` unless it matches the current view. (zag: packages/machines/date-picker/src/date-picker.connect.ts)
- The clear trigger is `type="button"` with a translated label and is `hidden` when nothing is selected; preset triggers are buttons labelled with their value. (zag: packages/machines/date-picker/src/date-picker.connect.ts)
- Each input carries `data-index`, `data-state`, `data-placeholder-shown`, `aria-invalid` and `data-invalid`, and its change handler runs the typed text through `ensureValidCharacters` with the locale's separator. (zag: packages/machines/date-picker/src/date-picker.connect.ts)
- Month and year selects carry translated aria-labels and drive the focused date rather than the value. (zag: packages/machines/date-picker/src/date-picker.connect.ts)
- Given a range picker where a start date is committed with Enter, then the start cell has `data-range-start=""` and the next focusable day has `data-in-hover-range=""`, so the band previews before the end is chosen. (zag: e2e/date-picker.e2e.ts: "selecting a range start with Enter previews the range band")

### Keyboard

- Given the calendar is open on today, when ArrowRight or ArrowLeft is pressed, then focus moves one day forward or back. (zag: e2e/date-picker.e2e.ts: "navigates to next day on ArrowRight key press"; zag: e2e/date-picker.e2e.ts: "navigates to previous day on ArrowLeft key press")
- Given the calendar is open, when ArrowUp or ArrowDown is pressed, then focus moves seven days back or forward, one grid row. (zag: e2e/date-picker.e2e.ts: "navigates to previous week on ArrowUp key press"; zag: e2e/date-picker.e2e.ts: "navigates to next week on ArrowDown key press")
- Given the calendar is open, when Home or End is pressed, then focus moves to the first or last day of the visible month. (zag: e2e/date-picker.e2e.ts: "navigates to first day of the month on Home key press"; zag: e2e/date-picker.e2e.ts: "navigates to last day of the month on End key press")
- Given the month view, when End then Home are pressed from the first month cell, then focus lands on December then January. (zag: e2e/date-picker-month.e2e.ts: "[keyboard] should move focus to the ends of the year")
- Given the year view, when End then Home are pressed from the first year cell, then focus lands on the last and first year of the visible decade. (zag: e2e/date-picker-year.e2e.ts: "[keyboard] should move focus to the ends of the decade")
- Given a date typed into the input, when Enter is pressed, then the value is committed and formatted back into the input. (zag: e2e/date-picker.e2e.ts: "keyboard selection")
- Given a committed date, when five characters are deleted and Enter pressed again, then the previous value is restored rather than left partial. (zag: e2e/date-picker.e2e.ts: "keyboard selection + re-selection")
- The table key map wires Enter, ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, ArrowUp, ArrowDown, PageUp, PageDown (each honoring Shift for the larger jump) and Home and End, all view-aware and column-count-aware. (zag: packages/machines/date-picker/src/date-picker.connect.ts)

### Pointer

- Given the trigger is clicked, then the calendar opens and focus lands on today's cell. (zag: e2e/date-picker.e2e.ts: "opens the calendar on click trigger and focus on current date")
- Given the calendar is open, when today's cell is clicked, then the popup closes and focus returns to the input. (zag: e2e/date-picker.e2e.ts: "selecting a date with pointer")
- Given the calendar is open, when any day cell is clicked, then the popup closes. (zag: e2e/date-picker.e2e.ts: "should close datepicker popup upon click on a date")
- Given the month-range example, when month 3 is clicked and month 7 hovered, then months 3 through 7 all report the hover-range attribute. (zag: e2e/date-picker-month.e2e.ts: "[pointer] should show the hovered range ahead of the anchor")
- Given the month-range example, when month 7 is clicked and month 5 hovered, then months 5 through 7 are in the hover range, so the band works backwards from the anchor. (zag: e2e/date-picker-month.e2e.ts: "[pointer] should show the hovered range behind the anchor")
- Given month 10 clicked and the next year navigated to, when month 3 is hovered, then months 1 through 3 of the new year are in the hover range, so the band spans a year boundary. (zag: e2e/date-picker-month.e2e.ts: "[pointer] should carry the range across years")
- Given the year-range example, when 2022 is clicked and 2027 hovered, then 2022 through 2027 are in the hover range, and hovering 2021 instead gives 2021 through 2022. (zag: e2e/date-picker-year.e2e.ts: "[pointer] should show the hovered range ahead of the anchor"; zag: e2e/date-picker-year.e2e.ts: "[pointer] should show the hovered range behind the anchor")
- Given 2022 clicked and the next decade navigated to, when 2033 is hovered and clicked, then 2030 through 2033 preview and the committed value is the 2022-2033 pair. (zag: e2e/date-picker-year.e2e.ts: "[pointer] should carry the range across decades")
- Given the year-inline example, when a year outside the visible decade is clicked, then the decade in view shifts to contain it. (zag: e2e/date-picker-year.e2e.ts: "should move the decade in view when one of them is clicked")
- Given the month-inline example constrained to March through September, when a month inside the range is clicked, then a value is selected. (zag: e2e/date-picker-month.e2e.ts: "should select a month within the range")

### Focus management

- Given a date is selected by clicking a cell, then focus moves to the input. (zag: e2e/date-picker.e2e.ts: "selecting a date with pointer")
- Given the calendar is open on a committed range, then focus lands on the range's start date rather than today. (zag: e2e/date-picker.e2e.ts: "Enter on a completed range starts a new range instead of keeping the old end")
- Cell triggers use roving tabindex (only the focused cell is tabbable) and the whole table is `tabIndex={-1}`. (zag: packages/machines/date-picker/src/date-picker.connect.ts)

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given the input is cleared by hand, then both the input and the reported selected value become empty, and picking a day afterwards sets a value again. (zag: e2e/date-picker.e2e.ts: "clearing input field should clear the date picker value")
- Given nonsense digits are typed, when Enter is pressed, then the picker clamps to a valid date ("01/01/9999") instead of crashing. (zag: e2e/date-picker.e2e.ts: "entering invalid date should not crash the datepicker")
- Given min 2025-07-01 and max 2025-09-30, when a later date is typed and the input is blurred, then the value is constrained down to the max, and the reported selected value matches. (zag: e2e/date-picker.e2e.ts: "constrains date to max value on blur when out-of-range date entered")
- Given the same bounds, when an earlier date is typed and blurred, then the value is constrained up to the min. (zag: e2e/date-picker.e2e.ts: "constrains date to min value on blur when out-of-range date entered")
- Given the same bounds, when out-of-range dates are committed with Enter instead of blur, then they are clamped to max and min respectively, so both commit paths agree. (zag: e2e/date-picker.e2e.ts: "constrains date to max value on Enter when out-of-range date entered"; zag: e2e/date-picker.e2e.ts: "constrains date to min value on Enter when out-of-range date entered")
- Given the same bounds, when an in-range date is committed, then it is left untouched. (zag: e2e/date-picker.e2e.ts: "allows valid dates within range")
- Given the range example, when the end input is filled first and blurred, then the value is set without crashing, pinning issue 2809. (zag: e2e/date-picker.e2e.ts: "should not crash when typing end date first")
- Given an end date typed first, when the calendar is opened and a start date clicked, then both values land correctly without crashing. (zag: e2e/date-picker.e2e.ts: "should allow selecting dates after typing end date first")
- Given an end date typed first, when the end input is focused and blurred a second time, then nothing crashes and the value survives, pinning issue 2840. (zag: e2e/date-picker.e2e.ts: "should not crash when blurring end date input twice after typing end date first")
- Given an end date typed first, when it is selected and retyped with a new year, then the new value is committed without crashing, pinning issue 2864. (zag: e2e/date-picker.e2e.ts: "should not crash when changing end date after typing end date first")
- Given a start later than the end typed through the two inputs, when both are blurred, then the dates are swapped so the range is ordered, matching the Enter and click paths, pinning issue 3186. (zag: e2e/date-picker.e2e.ts: "normalizes reversed range dates entered via input on blur")
- Given a complete range, when the calendar is reopened and Enter pressed on a new day, then the range resets to a single new start, the end clears, the calendar stays open and focus advances to the following day. (zag: e2e/date-picker.e2e.ts: "Enter on a completed range starts a new range instead of keeping the old end")
- Given only a start date was committed before closing, when the calendar is reopened and another date clicked, then the range is completed rather than restarted. (zag: e2e/date-picker.e2e.ts: "reopening with only a start date resumes range selection")
- Given `open={false}` alongside a `defaultOpen`, then the content stays closed, so the controlled prop wins. (zag: e2e/date-picker.e2e.ts: "controlled open={false} wins over defaultOpen")
- Given `minView="month"`, when the calendar opens, then the month view table is the visible one. (zag: e2e/date-picker.e2e.ts: "defaults to the month view when minView is month")
- Given a multi-month picker with a max of two selected dates, when a third month is clicked, then it is rejected without throwing and the first two stay selected. (zag: e2e/date-picker.e2e.ts: "selecting beyond the max does not crash")
- Given `open={true}`, then the close button stays visible even after being clicked; given `open={false}`, then clicking the open button never mounts the content, so Ark treats `open` as fully controlled. (ark: packages/react/src/components/date-picker/tests/date-picker.test.tsx: "should be fully controlled (true)"; ark: packages/react/src/components/date-picker/tests/date-picker.test.tsx: "should be fully controlled (false)"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/date-picker/tests/date-picker.test.tsx: "should be fully controlled (true)"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/date-picker/tests/date-picker.test.tsx: "should be fully controlled (false)")

### Forms

- Given `disabled`, then day cells are `tabindex="-1"`, and force-clicking a day leaves the value unchanged; Playwright normally refuses the click because the grid is aria-disabled. - Given `readOnly`, then arrow keys still move focus through the calendar but Enter does not select, and clicking a day does not change the value. - Given a committed value and `readOnly` switched on, when the clear trigger is clicked, then the value is kept. (zag: e2e/date-picker.e2e.ts: "clear trigger does not clear the value when readOnly")

### RTL and i18n

- Given locale `cs-CZ`, when "28.02.2024" is typed with dot separators and Enter pressed, then the value commits and reformats as "28. 02. 2024" in both the input and the reported value. (zag: e2e/date-picker.e2e.ts: "cs-CZ locale: typing date with dot separators commits correctly")
- Given the `fa-IR` custom-calendar example, when Persian digits are typed, then the input accepts them and keeps native numerals, pinning issue 3165 where non-ASCII numbering systems were rejected. (zag: e2e/date-picker.e2e.ts: "accepts the locale's native numerals typed into the input")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given the month-inline example constrained to March through September, then January, February, October, November and December are disabled while March, June and September are not. (zag: e2e/date-picker-month.e2e.ts: "should only disable months outside min and max")
- Given the year view, then exactly ten years render and the span from first to last is nine, so the view is a decade. (zag: e2e/date-picker-year.e2e.ts: "should render exactly the decade in view")
- Given the year view without min or max, then no year cell is disabled. (zag: e2e/date-picker-year.e2e.ts: "should not disable any year without min or max")
- Given the year-inline example, then years outside min and max are disabled while the boundary years are not. (zag: e2e/date-picker-year.e2e.ts: "should only disable years outside min and max")
- Given the year-inline example, then a year outside the visible decade carries the outside-range attribute yet stays selectable. (zag: e2e/date-picker-year.e2e.ts: "should keep years outside the decade in view selectable")
