## date-input

### Roles and attributes

- Anatomy parts are root, label, control, segmentGroup, segment, hiddenInput. (zag: packages/machines/date-input/src/date-input.anatomy.ts)
- Root, label and control all carry `data-disabled`, `data-readonly` and `data-invalid`; the control adds `data-focus` while any segment inside it is focused. (zag: packages/machines/date-input/src/date-input.connect.ts)
- Each segment group is `role="group"` with `aria-labelledby` on its own label id, `data-disabled`, `data-readonly`, `data-invalid` and `data-focus` only on the group whose index is active, which is how a range input marks exactly one side as focused. (zag: packages/machines/date-input/src/date-input.connect.ts)
- Each editable segment is `role="spinbutton"` with `tabIndex` 0 unless disabled, `contentEditable` when editable, `spellCheck="false"`, an `inputMode` derived from the segment type, `enterKeyHint="next"`, a type-derived `aria-label`, `aria-valuenow` (omitted while showing the placeholder), `aria-valuetext` (the placeholder text while empty, else the rendered text), `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, `aria-invalid`, `aria-readonly` and `aria-disabled`. (zag: packages/machines/date-input/src/date-input.connect.ts)
- Each segment also carries `data-value`, `data-type` naming the segment (month, day, year, hour, minute, second, dayPeriod, era, timeZoneName, literal), `data-readonly`, `data-disabled`, `data-editable` only when it is editable and neither readonly nor disabled, and `data-placeholder-shown` while empty. (zag: packages/machines/date-input/src/date-input.connect.ts)
- Literal separators are rendered as non-interactive segments that are `aria-hidden` with `data-readonly=""` and `data-disabled=""`. (zag: packages/machines/date-input/src/date-input.connect.ts)
- The hidden input is `type="hidden"` and one is rendered per value index, so a range input submits two fields. (zag: packages/machines/date-input/src/date-input.connect.ts)
- Given the basic date input, then exactly three spinbutton segments render alongside the label. (ark: packages/react/src/components/date-input/tests/date-input.test.tsx: "should render label and exactly three spinbutton segments"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/date-input/tests/date-input.test.tsx: "should render label and exactly three spinbutton segments"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/date-input/tests/date-input.test.ts: "should render label and exactly three spinbutton segments")
- Given a default value, then month, day and year segments expose `aria-valuenow` of 6, 15 and 2024. (ark: packages/react/src/components/date-input/tests/date-input.test.tsx: "should display defaultValue"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/date-input/tests/date-input.test.tsx: "should display defaultValue"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/date-input/tests/date-input.test.ts: "should display defaultValue")
- Given `invalid`, then the root carries `data-invalid`. (ark: packages/react/src/components/date-input/tests/date-input.test.tsx: "should mark segments invalid when invalid prop is passed"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/date-input/tests/date-input.test.tsx: "should mark segments invalid when invalid prop is passed"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/date-input/tests/date-input.test.ts: "should mark segments invalid when invalid prop is passed")
- Given a ZonedDateTime value with minute granularity, then each literal segment renders its own text (both "/" and ":" appear) rather than repeating the first literal. (ark: packages/solid/src/components/date-input/tests/date-input.test.tsx: "should render each literal segment with its own text, not the first literal"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/date-input/tests/date-input.test.ts: "should render each literal segment with its own text, not the first literal")

### Keyboard

- Given the month segment is focused, when ArrowRight is pressed twice, then focus moves to day and then to year. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[keyboard] ArrowRight moves focus to next segment")
- Given the year segment is focused, when ArrowLeft is pressed twice, then focus moves to day and then to month. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[keyboard] ArrowLeft moves focus to previous segment")
- Given the first segment is focused, when ArrowLeft is pressed, then focus stays there; given the last segment, ArrowRight also stays put. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[keyboard] ArrowLeft on first segment stays on first segment"; zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[keyboard] ArrowRight on last segment stays on last segment")
- Given a filled month segment, when ArrowUp is pressed, then the month increments, and ArrowDown decrements it. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[input] ArrowUp increments the segment value"; zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[input] ArrowDown decrements the segment value")
- Given an empty month segment showing its placeholder, when ArrowUp is pressed, then the segment is seeded with a value and no longer shows the placeholder. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[input] ArrowUp on placeholder sets the value")
- Given the month segment is focused, when Home is pressed, then it takes the minimum value 1, and End takes the maximum 12. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[input] Home sets segment to minimum value"; zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[input] End sets segment to maximum value")
- Given a filled segment, when Backspace is pressed, then it returns to the placeholder and focus stays on it. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[input] Backspace on filled segment clears it to placeholder"; zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[input] Backspace on filled month clears it to placeholder")
- Given a segment already showing the placeholder, when Backspace is pressed, then focus moves to the previous segment. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[input] Backspace on placeholder moves to previous segment")
- Given a partially typed segment ("0"), when Backspace is pressed, then the partial entry is discarded and focus stays put. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[input] Backspace during partial entry clears it without moving")
- Given a month of 12, when Backspace is pressed, then the trailing digit is removed leaving "1", and a second Backspace returns to the placeholder. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[input] Backspace removes last character (12 -> 1)"; zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[input] Backspace twice clears two digits (12 -> 1 -> placeholder)")
- Given the first segment is empty, when Backspace is pressed, then focus stays on it and it remains a placeholder. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[input] Backspace on first segment when empty stays on first segment")
- Given a complete date, when the year is cleared with four Backspaces, then one more Backspace moves to day and two more clear it. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[input] Backspace clears day after clearing year")
- Given a default value and the month segment focused, when Backspace is pressed, then that segment loses `aria-valuenow` entirely. (ark: packages/react/src/components/date-input/tests/date-input.test.tsx: "should clear value on Backspace")
- The segment key map handles ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, ArrowUp, ArrowDown (with a larger adjust amount for page keys), Backspace and Delete (both routed to the same clear handler), Home and End, and routes printable input through a separate segment-input event. (zag: packages/machines/date-input/src/date-input.connect.ts)

### Pointer

- Given the date input, when a segment is clicked, then that segment takes focus and the control gains `data-focus`. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[focus] clicking a segment focuses it"; ark: packages/react/src/components/date-input/tests/date-input.test.tsx: "should focus segment on click"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/date-input/tests/date-input.test.tsx: "should focus segment on click"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/date-input/tests/date-input.test.ts: "should focus segment on click")
- Given a focused segment, when a click lands outside, then the control loses `data-focus`. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[focus] clicking outside blurs the segments")

### Focus management

- Given the range example, when the start date is completed, then focus moves to the end group's first segment, and Backspace on that empty segment returns focus to the start group's year. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[input] completing start date moves focus to end date, backspace returns focus to start date")
- Given the range example, when a segment in the start group is focused, then only group 0 carries `data-focus`; focusing the end group moves the attribute to group 1. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[focus] focusing start date group marks only group 0 with data-focus"; zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[focus] focusing end date group marks only group 1 with data-focus")
- Given a focused range input, when focus leaves, then no group carries `data-focus`. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[focus] blurring range input removes data-focus from all groups")
- Given the range example with the start year focused, when ArrowRight is pressed, then focus crosses into the end group's first segment. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[keyboard] ArrowRight on last start segment moves focus to first end segment")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given the month segment is focused, when two digits are typed, then the segment commits and focus auto-advances to day; the same holds from day to year. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[input] typing a complete month advances to day segment"; zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[input] typing a complete day advances to year segment")
- Given all three segments are typed in order, then each shows its value and the committed value reads "1/25/2025". (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[input] typing a full date sets the value")
- Given a first digit high enough that no second digit could keep the value in range (month "2"), then the segment commits immediately and focus advances. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[input] typing a high first digit auto-advances (e.g. month=2 pads to 02)")
- Given non-numeric characters are typed into a numeric segment, then they are ignored and the segment stays a placeholder. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[input] typing non-numeric input is ignored")
- Given a month segment updated by typing, then the value is reflected without any explicit commit key. (ark: packages/react/src/components/date-input/tests/date-input.test.tsx: "should update month segment on typing")
- Given a single digit typed into the month segment, then both its `aria-valuenow` and its rendered text update immediately while the entry is still partial. (ark: packages/vue/src/components/date-input/tests/date-input.test.ts: "should update the displayed segment text while typing")
- Given `granularity="hour"`, then the hour segment renders, is focusable, starts as a placeholder and is seeded by ArrowUp; the same holds for minute and second granularity, with two typed digits completing those segments. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[input] hour granularity"; zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[input] minute granularity"; zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[input] seconds granularity")
- Given `placeholderValue` 2019-04-10, when ArrowUp is pressed on each empty segment, then the first press seeds that segment from the placeholder date and the second press increments from it. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[input] ArrowUp value starts from the placeholder date")
- Given the same placeholder, when ArrowDown is pressed on each empty segment, then the first press seeds from the placeholder and the second decrements. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[input] ArrowDown value starts from the placeholder date")
- Given `placeholderValue` is changed to a new date, then subsequent ArrowUp presses on empty segments seed from the new base date. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[input] changing placeholderValue prop updates the base date for editing")
- Given a placeholder of year 1, when ArrowDown cycles past year 1 AD, then the era segment flips to BC with year 1 and the committed value has year 0. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[input] ArrowDown on year:1 should show year:1 era:BC and selected value should have 0 year set")
- Given year 1 BC, when ArrowDown is pressed again, then it becomes year 2 BC and the committed value has year -1, so the era arithmetic follows the proleptic convention. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[input] ArrowDown on year:1 era:BC should show year:2 era:BC and selected value should have -1 year set")
- Given a complete valid input, then `placeholderValue` is not mutated by the commit. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[placeholderValue] is not changed after a complete valid input")
- Given only one segment typed, then the other segments still show placeholders and `placeholderValue` is unchanged, because the partial state lives in a separate editing value. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[placeholderValue] is not changed while typing partial segments")
- Given a committed date cleared segment by segment with Backspace, then `placeholderValue` still holds its original date. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[placeholderValue] is not changed after clearing all segments via backspace")
- Given 11/11/1111 typed and only the year cleared, then month and day still display the user's typed 11 and 11 rather than falling back to the placeholder's 04/10. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[editingValue] clearing one segment preserves the other typed segments")
- Given a committed date, when the same segments are retyped, then the new digits are visible before blur and the value commits to the new date on blur. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[editingValue] re-typing over a committed date shows the new digits before blur")
- Given a previously typed year that is then cleared, when ArrowUp or ArrowDown is pressed, then the value starts from the placeholder year rather than a stale edited year, and the untouched month and day keep their typed values. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[placeholderValue] ArrowUp after clearing a previously typed year starts from placeholder year"; zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[placeholderValue] ArrowDown after clearing a previously typed year starts from placeholder year")
- Given a previously typed day that is cleared, then ArrowUp seeds from the placeholder day and increments from there, and ArrowDown seeds then decrements. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[placeholderValue] ArrowUp after clearing a previously typed day starts from placeholder day"; zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[placeholderValue] ArrowDown after clearing a previously typed day starts from placeholder day")
- Given a previously typed month that is cleared, then ArrowUp and ArrowDown likewise restart from the placeholder month. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[placeholderValue] ArrowUp after clearing a previously typed month starts from placeholder month"; zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[placeholderValue] ArrowDown after clearing a previously typed month starts from placeholder month")
- Given a partial edit in progress, when `placeholderValue` changes, then the editing base resets so an ArrowUp on a still-empty segment seeds from the new placeholder. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[placeholderValue] changing the prop while mid-edit resets the editing base")
- Given month and day already typed, when `placeholderValue` changes, then those entered segments are preserved rather than reset. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[placeholderValue] changing the prop preserves already-entered segments")
- Given month and day typed, when granularity changes to minute, then the entered segments stay visible and the new time segments appear as placeholders. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[granularity] changing granularity preserves already-entered segments")
- Given a fully committed date, when granularity changes, then the date segments keep their committed values and only the new time segments are placeholders. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[granularity] changing granularity preserves a fully committed date")
- Given `granularity="minute"`, when the dayPeriod segment is focused and "p" typed, then it becomes PM, and typing "a" returns it to AM. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[granularity] typing 'P' on dayPeriod sets PM"; zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[granularity] typing 'A' on dayPeriod sets AM")
- Given the dayPeriod segment, when ArrowUp and ArrowDown are pressed, then it toggles between PM and AM. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[granularity] switching to minute granularity allows ArrowUp/ArrowDown to toggle dayPeriod")
- Given hour or minute granularity, then ArrowUp and ArrowDown both initialise an empty hour or minute segment from the placeholder. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[granularity] switching to hour granularity allows ArrowUp to initialise hour segment"; zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[granularity] switching to minute granularity allows ArrowUp to initialise minute segment"; zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[granularity] switching to hour granularity allows ArrowDown to initialise hour segment")
- Given `hourCycle=12`, then a dayPeriod segment renders and toggles with ArrowUp. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[hourCycle=12] dayPeriod segment renders and toggles")
- Given `hourCycle=24`, then no dayPeriod segment exists at all and the hour segment cycles through 0-23. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[hourCycle=24] no dayPeriod segment renders; hour cycles 0-23")
- Given 09:30 PM entered under `hourCycle=12`, when the cycle switches to 24 then back to 12, then the hour reads 21 in between, the dayPeriod segment disappears and reappears as PM, and the hour returns to 9. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[hourCycle] switching 12 → 24 → 12 preserves hour and re-shows dayPeriod")
- Given the hour-cycle example, then `hourCycle=24` forces 24-hour time regardless of locale and no dayPeriod segment renders. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[hour-cycle] hourCycle=24 forces 24-hour time regardless of locale")

### RTL and i18n

- Given locale `sr-Latn-RS`, then the segment placeholders use the Latin-script forms dd, mm and gggg, so a language-script match wins over the bare language. (zag: packages/machines/date-input/tests/placeholders.test.ts: "uses language-script placeholders before falling back to language")
- Given locale `sr-RS` with no script subtag, then the placeholders fall back to the Cyrillic language defaults дд, мм and гггг. (zag: packages/machines/date-input/tests/placeholders.test.ts: "falls back to language placeholders without a matching script")
- Given a naive `CalendarDateTime` of 00:00, then `createFormatFn` renders "00:00" under every formatter time zone from UTC through Pacific/Kiritimati, so a typed wall-clock time is never shifted, pinning issue 3187. (zag: packages/machines/date-input/tests/timezone.test.ts: "createFormatFn preserves the typed hour across formatter time zones")
- Given a naive `CalendarDate`, then it formats as the same 03/15/2024 across all formatter zones. (zag: packages/machines/date-input/tests/timezone.test.ts: "createFormatFn preserves a naive date across formatter time zones")
- Given a consumer-supplied formatter, then `getValueAsString` still returns the typed hour unshifted. (zag: packages/machines/date-input/tests/timezone.test.ts: "getValueAsString preserves the typed hour with a consumer formatter")
- Given a true `ZonedDateTime`, then its absolute instant is respected and the formatter's zone is honored, so only naive values are protected. (zag: packages/machines/date-input/tests/timezone.test.ts: "ZonedDateTime instants are unaffected (absolute, formatter zone honored)")
- `toFormatterDate` anchors a naive value to the formatter's zone so the wall clock round-trips, and leaves a ZonedDateTime's instant intact. (zag: packages/machines/date-input/tests/timezone.test.ts: "anchors a naive value to the formatter's zone so wall-clock round-trips"; zag: packages/machines/date-input/tests/timezone.test.ts: "keeps a ZonedDateTime's absolute instant intact")
- Given the segment processor, then the hour segment's rendered text is the typed value under every formatter zone. (zag: packages/machines/date-input/tests/timezone.test.ts: "hour segment shows the typed value regardless of the formatter's zone")
- Given the timezone example, then a `timeZoneName` segment renders showing the zone abbreviation alongside the date and time segments. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[timezone] timeZoneName segment renders with the zone abbreviation"; ark: packages/react/src/components/date-input/tests/date-input.test.tsx: "should render timeZoneName segment for ZonedDateTime values"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/date-input/tests/date-input.test.tsx: "should render timeZoneName segment for ZonedDateTime values"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/date-input/tests/date-input.test.ts: "should render timeZoneName segment for ZonedDateTime values")
- Given the timezone example, when ArrowRight is pressed from dayPeriod, then the read-only timeZoneName segment receives focus, and ArrowLeft from it returns to dayPeriod. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[timezone] ArrowRight from dayPeriod focuses the read-only timeZoneName"; zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[timezone] ArrowLeft from timeZoneName focuses dayPeriod")
- Given the timezone example, when "p" is typed on dayPeriod, then it becomes PM and focus advances to timeZoneName. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[timezone] typing 'P' on dayPeriod advances focus to timeZoneName")
- Given `hideTimeZone` is toggled on and off, then the timeZoneName segment is removed and restored. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[timezone] hideTimeZone hides the timeZoneName segment"; ark: packages/react/src/components/date-input/tests/date-input.test.tsx: "should hide timeZoneName segment when hideTimeZone is true"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/date-input/tests/date-input.test.tsx: "should hide timeZoneName segment when hideTimeZone is true")

- Given the basic date input and the range example, when axe runs over the root, then there are no violations. ### Notes and edge cases

- Given the range example, then a start date can be entered segment by segment and commits as a single value. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[input] can enter a start date")
- Given both range dates typed as 11/11/1111, when the end date is deleted segment by segment and one digit of the start year is also deleted, then all three end segments show placeholders instead of leaving partial values behind. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[issue] backspacing end date should not leave partial values in end date segments")
- Given an ISO date string pasted while a segment is focused, then the whole value is parsed and committed. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[paste] pasting a valid ISO date string sets the value")
- Given a non-date string pasted, then nothing is committed and all segments stay placeholders. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[paste] pasting an invalid string is a no-op")
- Given the min-max example, then a date inside the range commits exactly as typed. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[min/max] typing a full date within range sets the value correctly")
- Given the min-max example, when a year is typed digit by digit, then month and day keep their values through every intermediate digit and the value commits only once the year is complete. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[min/max] typing year digit-by-digit does not reset month and day")
- Given a partially typed year, when focus leaves, then the partial year is completed against the constraint without disturbing month and day. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[min/max] partial year entry does not disrupt other segments on blur")
- Given a partially typed year, when Backspace is pressed, then month and day are untouched. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[min/max] backspace during partial year entry does not reset other segments")
- Given a date below the minimum, then the out-of-range value is shown while editing and clamped to the min only on blur; the same holds above the maximum. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[min/max] typing a date below min is unclamped during edit, segment-clamped on blur"; zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[min/max] typing a date above max is unclamped during edit, segment-clamped on blur")
- Given a completed year, when Backspace removes a digit, then only the year is truncated and month and day survive. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[min/max] backspace on completed year does not reset month/day")
- Given a year of 1990 with one digit removed, when a new digit is typed, then it extends the partial value to 1995 rather than starting a fresh entry. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[min/max] backspace then retype extends the partial value (does not start fresh)")
- Given a year at the minimum boundary, when ArrowDown pushes it below the min, then the segment shows the out-of-range year during editing, month and day are untouched, and blur clamps back to the boundary value. (zag: e2e/date-input.e2e.ts: "[min/max] arrow-down on year at boundary does not reset month/day")

## time-picker

### Notes and edge cases

- Neither repo ships a time-picker machine or component: Zag has no `packages/machines/time-picker` and Ark has no `time-picker` component directory in react, solid, vue or svelte. Time entry is covered instead by date-input's hour, minute, second, dayPeriod and timeZoneName segments under the `granularity` and `hourCycle` props. (zag: packages/machines/date-input/src/date-input.connect.ts)

## color-picker

### Roles and attributes

- Anatomy parts are root, label, control, trigger, positioner, content, area, areaThumb, valueText, areaBackground, channelSlider, channelSliderLabel, channelSliderTrack, channelSliderThumb, channelSliderValueText, channelInput, transparencyGrid, swatchGroup, swatchTrigger, swatchIndicator, swatch, eyeDropperTrigger, formatTrigger, formatSelect. (zag: packages/machines/color-picker/src/color-picker.anatomy.ts)
- Root carries `data-disabled`, `data-readonly`, `data-invalid` and exposes the current color as the CSS variable `--value`. (zag: packages/machines/color-picker/src/color-picker.connect.ts)
- Label and control carry `data-disabled`, `data-readonly`, `data-invalid`, `data-focus`, with the label adding `data-required` and the control adding `data-state`. (zag: packages/machines/color-picker/src/color-picker.connect.ts)
- The trigger is `type="button"` with an `aria-label` that spells out the current color, `aria-controls`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-haspopup="dialog"` (dropped in inline mode), `data-state`, `data-placement`, `data-side`, `data-focus`, `data-disabled`, `data-readonly` and `data-invalid`. (zag: packages/machines/color-picker/src/color-picker.connect.ts)
- The content is `role="dialog"` (no role in inline mode) with `tabIndex={-1}`, `hidden` while closed, `data-state`, `data-placement` and `data-side`. (zag: packages/machines/color-picker/src/color-picker.connect.ts)
- The area is `role="group"` with `data-invalid`, `data-disabled` and `data-readonly`; its thumb is `role="slider"` with `aria-roledescription="2d slider"`, `aria-valuemin` 0, `aria-valuemax` 100, `aria-valuenow` from the x channel, an `aria-label` naming both channels, an `aria-valuetext` spelling out both channel values, `aria-disabled`, `tabIndex` 0 unless disabled, and a `--color` CSS variable. (zag: packages/machines/color-picker/src/color-picker.connect.ts)
- Each channel slider is `role="presentation"` with `data-channel` and `data-orientation`; its track is `role="group"`; its thumb is `role="slider"` with `aria-label` naming the channel, `aria-orientation`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuetext`, `aria-disabled`, `data-channel`, `data-orientation`, `data-disabled` and `tabIndex` 0 unless disabled. (zag: packages/machines/color-picker/src/color-picker.connect.ts)
- Channel inputs are `type="text"` for the hex-style text field and `type="number"` otherwise, with `data-channel`, `aria-label` naming the channel, `data-disabled`, `data-invalid` and `data-readonly`; the hidden form input is `type="text"` with `tabIndex={-1}`. (zag: packages/machines/color-picker/src/color-picker.connect.ts)
- Swatch triggers are `type="button"` with an `aria-label` naming the color, `data-state` of checked/unchecked, `data-value`, `data-disabled` and a `--color` variable; the swatch indicator is hidden unless checked; the swatch itself repeats `data-state`, `data-value` and `--color`. (zag: packages/machines/color-picker/src/color-picker.connect.ts)
- The transparency grid exposes a `--size` variable; the eye-dropper trigger is a button labelled "Pick a color from the screen"; the format trigger's label names the next format and the format select is labelled "change color format". (zag: packages/machines/color-picker/src/color-picker.connect.ts)
- Given `disabled` on the inline picker, then the area thumb and each channel slider thumb expose `aria-disabled="true"`. (zag: e2e/color-picker.e2e.ts: "[disabled] area thumb should expose aria-disabled"; zag: e2e/color-picker.e2e.ts: "[disabled] channel slider thumb should expose aria-disabled")

### Keyboard

- Given the picker is open with the area thumb focused, when Tab is pressed, then focus moves to the hue slider thumb and then to the alpha slider thumb. (zag: e2e/color-picker.e2e.ts: "keyboard focus movement")
- Given the picker is open, when Escape is pressed, then it closes and focus returns to the trigger. (zag: e2e/color-picker.e2e.ts: "should close picker on Escape after opening with trigger")
- The area thumb key map handles ArrowUp, ArrowDown, ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, PageUp and PageDown with a step; channel slider thumbs additionally handle Home and End. (zag: packages/machines/color-picker/src/color-picker.connect.ts)

### Pointer

- Given a closed picker, when the trigger is clicked, then the content opens, and clicking the trigger again closes it and returns focus to the trigger. (zag: e2e/color-picker.e2e.ts: "click on trigger should open picker"; zag: e2e/color-picker.e2e.ts: "clicking trigger twice should close picker")
- Given the picker is open, when the first swatch is clicked, then the hex input takes that swatch's value. (zag: e2e/color-picker.e2e.ts: "[swatch] should set value on click swatch")
- Given the picker is open, when the hue bar is clicked at its center, then the value text reports a hue of 180. (zag: e2e/color-picker.e2e.ts: "[slider] should change hue when clicking the hue bar")
- Given the picker is open, when the alpha bar is clicked at its center, then the value text reports an alpha of 0.5. (zag: e2e/color-picker.e2e.ts: "[slider] should change alpha when clicking the alpha bar")
- Given the picker is open, when the area thumb is dragged past the area's bounds and released outside it, then the picker stays open, so a scrub that ends outside is not treated as an outside click. (zag: e2e/color-picker.e2e.ts: "[pointer] pointer up after area scrub should not close picker")

### Focus management

- Given the picker is opened from the trigger, then the area thumb receives focus. (zag: e2e/color-picker.e2e.ts: "opening the picker should focus area")
- Given the picker is open, when a click lands outside, then the picker closes and focus returns to the trigger. (zag: e2e/color-picker.e2e.ts: "should re-focus trigger on outside click")
- Given a color picker inside a Field, when the field label is clicked, then the hex channel input receives focus. (ark: packages/react/src/components/color-picker/tests/color-picker.test.tsx: "should focus on input when label is clicked"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/color-picker/tests/color-picker.test.tsx: "should focus on input when label is clicked"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/color-picker/tests/color-picker.test.ts: "should focus on input when label is clicked")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given the closed picker, when "pink" is typed and committed, then the input shows `#FFC0CB`, so named CSS colors are parsed and normalized. (zag: e2e/color-picker.e2e.ts: "[closed] typing different native css colors should update color")
- Given the closed picker, when 0.3 is typed into the alpha input and committed, then the value text reads `hsla(0, 100%, 50%, 0.3)`. (zag: e2e/color-picker.e2e.ts: "[closed] typing in alpha should update color")
- Given `defaultValue={parseColor('#ff00ff')}`, then the swatch trigger renders that color; React skips this case and Vue asserts on the inline style string rather than a computed background color. (ark: packages/react/src/components/color-picker/tests/color-picker.test.tsx: "should render with default value"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/color-picker/tests/color-picker.test.ts: "should render with default value")

### Forms

- Given a color picker inside a Field, then required, disabled and readOnly reach the hidden textbox, helper text renders, and error text appears only when invalid. ## image-cropper

### Roles and attributes

- Anatomy parts are root, viewport, image, selection, handle, grid. (zag: packages/machines/image-cropper/src/image-cropper.anatomy.ts)
- The root is `role="group"` with a translated `aria-roledescription`, `aria-label`, `aria-description`, `aria-live="polite"`, `aria-controls` listing the viewport and selection ids, `aria-busy="true"` until the image is ready, plus `data-fixed`, `data-shape`, `data-pinch`, `data-dragging` and `data-panning`. (zag: packages/machines/image-cropper/src/image-cropper.connect.ts)
- The root exposes the CSS variables `--crop-width`, `--crop-height`, `--crop-x`, `--crop-y`, `--image-zoom`, `--image-rotation`, `--image-offset-x` and `--image-offset-y`, so the whole crop geometry is drivable from CSS. (zag: packages/machines/image-cropper/src/image-cropper.connect.ts)
- The viewport is `role="presentation"` with `data-ownedby` on the root id and `data-disabled` when the crop area is fixed. (zag: packages/machines/image-cropper/src/image-cropper.connect.ts)
- The image is `role="presentation"` and `aria-hidden`, with `data-ownedby`, `data-ready`, `data-flip-horizontal` and `data-flip-vertical`, and it reports its natural size back to the machine on load. (zag: packages/machines/image-cropper/src/image-cropper.connect.ts)
- The selection is the focusable element: `tabIndex={0}`, `role="slider"`, with translated `aria-label`, `aria-roledescription`, `aria-description` carrying usage instructions, `aria-valuemin` 0, `aria-valuemax` derived from the measured viewport, `aria-valuenow` the crop x, an `aria-valuetext` describing the whole crop, plus `data-disabled`, `data-shape`, `data-measured`, `data-dragging` and `data-panning`. (zag: packages/machines/image-cropper/src/image-cropper.connect.ts)
- Each handle is `role="presentation"` and `aria-hidden` with `data-position` naming its axis and `data-disabled`; grid lines are `aria-hidden` with `data-axis`, `data-dragging` and `data-panning`. (zag: packages/machines/image-cropper/src/image-cropper.connect.ts)
- The public api covers setZoom, zoomBy, setRotation, rotateBy, setFlip, toggling each flip axis, resizeCrop by handle position and delta, and reset. (zag: packages/machines/image-cropper/src/image-cropper.connect.ts)
- Given the basic example after the image loads, then both the image and the crop selection are visible. (zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "should display image and crop selection")

### Keyboard

- Given the selection is focused, when ArrowRight and ArrowDown are pressed, then the crop moves one pixel in each direction and its size is unchanged. (zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[keyboard] should move crop selection with arrow keys")
- Given the selection is focused, when Alt+ArrowRight then Alt+ArrowLeft are pressed, then the crop width grows and shrinks by one pixel while its x stays put. (zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[keyboard] should resize width using Alt+Arrow keys")
- Given the selection is focused, when Alt+ArrowDown then Alt+ArrowUp are pressed, then the crop height grows and shrinks by one pixel while its y stays put. (zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[keyboard] should resize height using Alt+Arrow keys")
- Given the selection is focused, when Alt+Ctrl+ArrowLeft or Alt+Meta+ArrowLeft is pressed, then the width changes by the largest step of 50 pixels, so Ctrl and Meta are equivalent accelerators. (zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[keyboard] should use largest step with ctrl modifier when resizing"; zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[keyboard] should use largest step with meta modifier when resizing")
- Given a larger step with the Shift modifier, then resizing moves by that intermediate step rather than one pixel. (zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[keyboard] should use larger step with shift modifier when resizing")
- Given min width 100 and min height 80, when Alt+Ctrl+ArrowLeft and Alt+Ctrl+ArrowUp are pressed ten times each, then the crop stops exactly at the minimum size. (zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[keyboard] should respect minimum size constraints when resizing")
- Given max width 250 and max height 200, when Alt+Ctrl+ArrowRight and Alt+Ctrl+ArrowDown are pressed ten times each, then the crop stops at the smaller of the maximum and the viewport size. (zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[keyboard] should respect maximum size constraints when resizing")
- Given the selection is focused, when Ctrl+ArrowLeft and Ctrl+ArrowUp are pressed ten times, then the crop clamps flush to the viewport's top-left corner and never leaves it. (zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[keyboard] should not move selection outside viewport bounds")
- Given the fixed-crop example, when "+" is pressed, then the image zoom scale grows above 1. (zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[keyboard] should zoom with +/- keys")
- Given the fixed-crop example zoomed in, when ArrowRight and ArrowDown are pressed, then the image translate moves by one pixel each way while the crop selection itself does not move. (zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[keyboard] should remain focusable and pan the image with arrow keys")
- Given the fixed-crop example, when Alt+ArrowRight is pressed, then neither the crop size nor its position changes, so resize keys are inert in fixed mode. (zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[keyboard] should not resize the crop with Alt+Arrow keys")
- The selection's key handler routes zoom keys, pan nudges, resize nudges and move nudges as separate machine events, each carrying the pressed key and the shift, ctrl and meta modifiers. (zag: packages/machines/image-cropper/src/image-cropper.connect.ts)

### Pointer

- Given the basic example, when the selection is dragged by (50, 30), then its position moves by exactly that and its size is unchanged. (zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[pointer] should move crop selection by dragging")
- Given the basic example, when the south-east handle is dragged by (10, 15), then width and height grow by exactly those amounts. (zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[pointer] should resize crop selection using corner handle")
- Given the east handle is dragged horizontally, then only the width changes. (zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[pointer] should resize crop selection using side handle")
- Given the north handle is dragged upward by 20, then the height grows by 20, so the top edge moves rather than the bottom. (zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[pointer] should resize crop selection using top handle")
- Given the wheel is scrolled up over the viewport, then the image scale becomes 1.1, and scrolling back down returns it to 1. (zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[zoom] should zoom in using wheel"; zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[zoom] should zoom out using wheel")
- Given the image is zoomed to 1.1, when the overlay is dragged by (50, 30), then the image translate becomes half of that in each axis, reflecting the zoom-relative pan mapping. (zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[pan] should pan image when dragging overlay")
- Given `aspectRatio=1`, when the south-east handle is dragged by (60, 60), then the resulting crop is exactly square. (zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[aspectRatio] should maintain aspect ratio when resizing with constraint")
- Given no aspect-ratio constraint, when the south-east handle is dragged with Shift held, then the original aspect ratio is preserved to two decimal places. (zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[keyboard + pointer] should lock aspect ratio with shift key during resize")
- Given min width 80 and min height 60, when the south-east handle is dragged far inward, then the crop stops at exactly the minimum size. (zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[minSize] should respect minimum crop size")
- Given max width 200 and max height 150, when the handle is dragged far outward, then the crop stops at the smaller of the maximum and the viewport size. (zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[maxSize] should respect maximum crop size")
- Given the fixed-crop example, when the selection is dragged, then its position does not change. (zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "should prevent crop area from moving when fixed")
- Given the circle example, then the crop is square on load and stays square when the south-east handle is dragged by mismatched deltas. (zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "should display the crop area in 1:1 aspect ratio"; zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "should keep the crop area in 1:1 aspect ratio when resizing")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given the rotation slider is set to 45, then the image's computed matrix decodes to a 45 degree rotation. (zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[rotation] should rotate image")
- Given the zoom slider is set to 2, then the image's matrix decodes to a scale of exactly 2 on both axes. (zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[zoom] should allow programmatic zoom changes")
- Given the flip checkboxes, when each is checked and unchecked, then the reported flip state and the checkbox checked state stay in sync in both directions. (zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[flip] should set flips via checkboxes")
- Given the flip action buttons, when horizontal is toggled twice and vertical once, then the state follows each toggle, and the reset action clears both axes. (zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[flip] should toggle and reset flips with actions")
- Given the resize API with a handle and a step chosen, then growing and shrinking each of the four side handles moves only the expected edge: east grows width keeping x, west grows width and moves x, south grows height keeping y, north grows height and moves y, with the mirrored behavior on shrink. (zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[api] should grow selection using right handle"; zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[api] should shrink selection using right handle"; zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[api] should grow selection using left handle"; zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[api] should shrink selection using left handle"; zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[api] should grow selection using bottom handle"; zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[api] should shrink selection using bottom handle"; zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[api] should grow selection using top handle"; zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[api] should shrink selection using top handle")
- Given the resize API with a corner handle, then growing and shrinking each of the four corners changes both dimensions by the step and moves x and y only for the corners that own those edges. (zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[api] should grow selection using bottom-right corner handle"; zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[api] should shrink selection using bottom-right corner handle"; zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[api] should grow selection using top-left corner handle"; zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[api] should shrink selection using top-left corner handle"; zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[api] should grow selection using top-right corner handle"; zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[api] should shrink selection using top-right corner handle"; zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[api] should grow selection using bottom-left corner handle"; zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[api] should shrink selection using bottom-left corner handle")
- Given a 500px step through the resize API, then shrinking stops at the configured minimum and growing stops at the configured maximum clamped to the viewport. (zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[api] should respect minimum size when shrinking"; zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[api] should respect maximum size when growing")

### Accessibility tooling

- Given the basic image cropper, when axe runs, then there are no violations. (zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "should have no accessibility violation")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given the viewport shrinks to 80 percent or grows to 120 percent, then the crop keeps exactly the same width and height ratio relative to the viewport. (zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[viewport] should scale crop proportionally when viewport shrinks"; zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[viewport] should scale crop proportionally when viewport grows")
- Given `aspectRatio=1.5`, when the viewport is resized to 70 percent, then the crop still has that ratio to two decimal places. (zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[viewport] should maintain aspect ratio during resize when aspectRatio is set")
- Given the crop is pushed flush to the viewport's bottom-right corner, when the viewport shrinks to 60 percent, then the crop stays entirely within the new bounds. (zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[viewport] should keep crop within bounds after resize")
- Given min or max size constraints, when the viewport is resized, then the crop still honors them afterwards. (zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[viewport] should respect minSize constraints after resize"; zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[viewport] should respect maxSize constraints after resize")
- Given a shrink, a grow and a return to the original viewport size in sequence, then the crop tracks each change and ends within a pixel of its original size. (zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[viewport] should handle multiple sequential resizes")
- Given a stubbed four-quadrant SVG image, when the crop is moved and a horizontal flip applied, then exporting produces a data URL whose center pixel is the expected quadrant color and whose pixel dimensions match the crop scaled into natural pixels; the same holds after a 90 degree rotation, pinning issue 3238. (zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts: "[export] should match the crop after flip and rotation (#3238)")
- `computeMoveCrop` clamps a move to the viewport, so a large negative x lands at 0 and a large positive y stops at the bottom edge. (zag: packages/machines/image-cropper/tests/crop.test.ts: "computeMoveCrop keeps the crop inside the viewport")
- `computeResizeCrop` honors aspect ratio and max size together: a 2:1 crop dragged far out becomes 300 by 150 rather than 300 by 300. (zag: packages/machines/image-cropper/tests/crop.test.ts: "computeResizeCrop preserves the aspect ratio and maximum size")
- `clampOffset` computes the pan limits from the rotated image's bounding box, so at 90 degrees a (200, 200) offset clamps to (0, 100). (zag: packages/machines/image-cropper/tests/crop.test.ts: "clampOffset accounts for the rotated image bounds")
- `clampOffset` with `fixedCropArea` keeps the fixed crop fully covered, clamping an extreme offset to (250, -300). (zag: packages/machines/image-cropper/tests/crop.test.ts: "clampOffset keeps a fixed crop covered")
- `getCropSourceRect` is the identity when natural size equals viewport size, scales the crop into natural pixels when the image is larger, and handles non-uniform scale where the display aspect ratio differs from the natural one. (zag: packages/machines/image-cropper/tests/transform.test.ts: "identity: natural size equals viewport size"; zag: packages/machines/image-cropper/tests/transform.test.ts: "scales crop into natural pixels when image is larger than viewport"; zag: packages/machines/image-cropper/tests/transform.test.ts: "handles non-uniform scale (display aspect ratio differs from natural)")
- Zoom shrinks the sampled source region, pan shifts it, pan offsets are themselves scaled into natural pixels, and zoom with pan composes consistently. (zag: packages/machines/image-cropper/tests/transform.test.ts: "zoom shrinks the sampled source region"; zag: packages/machines/image-cropper/tests/transform.test.ts: "offset (pan) shifts the sampled source region"; zag: packages/machines/image-cropper/tests/transform.test.ts: "offset is scaled into natural pixels"; zag: packages/machines/image-cropper/tests/transform.test.ts: "zoom and offset combine consistently")
- The source-rect math guards against an unmeasured (zero-sized) viewport and against a zero zoom rather than dividing by zero. (zag: packages/machines/image-cropper/tests/transform.test.ts: "guards against an unmeasured (zero) viewport"; zag: packages/machines/image-cropper/tests/transform.test.ts: "guards against zero zoom")
- Horizontal and vertical flips mirror the sampled source region, and `viewportToNaturalPoint` round-trips a flipped source pixel, all three pinning issue 3238. (zag: packages/machines/image-cropper/tests/transform.test.ts: "horizontal flip mirrors the sampled source region (#3238)"; zag: packages/machines/image-cropper/tests/transform.test.ts: "vertical flip mirrors the sampled source region (#3238)"; zag: packages/machines/image-cropper/tests/transform.test.ts: "viewportToNaturalPoint round-trips a flipped source pixel (#3238)")
- The mapping uses the rendered image position and size rather than assuming the image fills the viewport, maps crop corners through rotation, flip, zoom and pan together, and expands the source rect to the oriented crop's axis-aligned bounding box under rotation. (zag: packages/machines/image-cropper/tests/transform.test.ts: "uses the rendered image position and size"; zag: packages/machines/image-cropper/tests/transform.test.ts: "maps crop corners through rotation, flip, zoom, and pan"; zag: packages/machines/image-cropper/tests/transform.test.ts: "rotation expands the source rect to the oriented crop's AABB")
- `getCropOutputSize` keeps natural resolution under zoom and caps at the configured maximum dimensions. (zag: packages/machines/image-cropper/tests/transform.test.ts: "getCropOutputSize keeps natural resolution under zoom"; zag: packages/machines/image-cropper/tests/transform.test.ts: "getCropOutputSize respects the maximum dimensions")
- The preview transform serializes to a canonical CSS matrix string, which is what the e2e tests decode to read scale, rotation and translate. (zag: packages/machines/image-cropper/tests/transform.test.ts: "serializes the canonical preview transform as a CSS matrix")
- No Ark framework package ships image-cropper tests, so its contract is pinned only by Zag's e2e and unit suites. (zag: e2e/image-cropper.e2e.ts)

## collection

### Keyboard

- Given a list collection of react, vue, solid (disabled), angular, when getNextValue is called with a value, then it returns the following value in list order, and returns null for the last value so forward navigation does not wrap by default. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/list-collection.test.ts: "next item")
- Given the same list, when getPreviousValue is called with a value, then it returns the preceding value in list order, and returns null for the first value so backward navigation does not wrap by default. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/list-collection.test.ts: "prev item")
- Given getNextValue or getPreviousValue lands on a disabled item, when the scan continues, then the walker keeps stepping in the same direction until it reaches an enabled item, so disabled items are never returned as the next or previous value. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/list-collection.ts)
- Given getNextValue or getPreviousValue is called with a step other than 1, when clamp is false, then the index may run past either end and the result is null, and when clamp is true the index is pinned to the last index or to 0 so the first or last value is returned instead of null. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/list-collection.ts)
- Given a value that is not in the collection, when getNextValue or getPreviousValue is called with it, then the result is null because the starting index resolves to -1. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/list-collection.ts)
- Given a list whose first item is enabled and whose last item is enabled, when firstValue and lastValue are read, then they return react and angular, and the getters walk inward past any disabled item at either end. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/list-collection.test.ts: "first and last value"; zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/list-collection.ts)
- Given a typeahead state of { keysSoFar: "", timer: -1 } with no current value and a 350ms timeout, when search is called with "r", then it returns react because matching is a case-insensitive prefix match on the stringified label. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/list-collection.test.ts: "search finds a value based on a query")
- Given a typeahead search, when the accumulated query is the same character repeated (for example "aaa"), then the query collapses to that single character so repeated presses of one key cycle through items starting with it rather than searching for the literal repeated string. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/list-collection.ts)
- Given a typeahead search with a current value, when the query is a single character, then the scan starts at the item after the current value and skips the current value itself, so pressing the same letter advances to the next match instead of re-selecting the current item. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/list-collection.ts)
- Given a typeahead search, when candidate items are scanned, then disabled items are skipped and the scan wraps around the end of the list back to the start. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/list-collection.ts)
- Given a typeahead search, when a key is accepted, then keysSoFar is set to the accumulated query and a timer is armed to reset it to the empty string after the timeout (default 350ms), and any previously armed timer is cleared first. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/list-collection.ts)
- Given a 3-column grid of 11 items where svelte at row 1 column 1 is disabled, when getNextRowValue is called with ts (row 2, column 1), then it returns go, the cell directly below. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/grid-collection.test.ts: "get next row")
- Given the same grid, when getNextRowValue is called with js (row 2, column 2) and the last row has only two cells, then the column clamps to the last enabled column of that row and the result is go. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/grid-collection.test.ts: "get next row")
- Given the same grid, when getNextRowValue is called with deno (row 2, column 0), then it returns rust, the cell directly below. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/grid-collection.test.ts: "get next row")
- Given the same grid, when getNextRowValue is called with vue (row 0, column 1) and the cell directly below is the disabled svelte, then the search continues down further rows in the same column and returns ts. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/grid-collection.test.ts: "get next row")
- Given the same grid, when getPreviousRowValue is called with ts (row 2, column 1) and the cell directly above is the disabled svelte, then the search continues upward in the same column and returns vue. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/grid-collection.test.ts: "get prev row")
- Given the same grid, when getPreviousRowValue is called with js (row 2, column 2), then it returns node, the cell directly above. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/grid-collection.test.ts: "get prev row")
- Given the same grid, when getPreviousRowValue is called with deno (row 2, column 0), then it returns angular, the cell directly above. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/grid-collection.test.ts: "get prev row")
- Given the same grid and loop defaulting to false, when getPreviousRowValue is called with vue in the top row, then the row index does not wrap and the call returns vue itself, so vertical navigation at the top edge is a no-op rather than a jump to the bottom row. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/grid-collection.test.ts: "get prev row")
- Given a grid, when getNextRowValue or getPreviousRowValue is called with loop set to true, then the row index wraps from the last row to the first and from the first row to the last while keeping the column, still skipping disabled cells. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/grid-collection.ts)
- Given a grid where every candidate cell in a column is disabled, when getNextRowValue exhausts the row scan, then it falls back to lastValue, and getPreviousRowValue falls back to firstValue. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/grid-collection.ts)
- Given a grid and a value that is not in the collection, when getNextRowValue or getPreviousRowValue is called, then the result is null because getValueCell returns null. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/grid-collection.ts)
- Given a tree with root ROOT, branch1 containing child1-1, child1-2, child1-3 and branch1-1 (which contains child2-1), then child1 and child2, when getFirstNode is called, then it returns branch1, the first non-root node in document order, and getLastNode returns child2, the last non-root node in document order. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "visit the tree")
- Given a tree with only one top-level branch whose last child is itself a branch, when getLastNode is called, then it returns child2-2, the deepest last child in document order, and getFirstNode returns branch1, so last does not mean last top-level child. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "one branch scenario")
- Given the tree, when getNextNode is called with branch1, then it returns child1-1, so forward navigation descends into a branch's children rather than skipping to the next sibling. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "visit the tree")
- Given the tree, when getPreviousNode is called with child1-2, then it returns child1-1, the previous node in document order. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "visit the tree")
- Given a tree whose root children are child1, child2 (disabled), child3 and child4 (disabled), when getFirstNode, getLastNode, getNextNode("child1") and getPreviousNode("child3") are called, then they return child1, child3, child3 and child1, so all four traversal entry points skip disabled nodes at the ends and in the middle. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "skips disabled nodes")
- Given a tree of node_modules, src and loose files with only node_modules marked expanded, when getNextNode is called with node_modules and a skip predicate that rejects any node with an unexpanded ancestor, then it returns node_modules/zag-js, so next-node navigation models a tree where collapsed subtrees are invisible. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-skip.test.ts: "next node")
- Given the same tree with node_modules and node_modules/@types expanded, when getPreviousNode is called with src and the same skip predicate, then it returns node_modules/@types/react-dom, the last visible node before src, so backward navigation enters expanded nested branches but not collapsed ones. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-skip.test.ts: "previous node")
- Given getNextNode with a skip predicate that skips the node currently holding the value, when traversal reaches that node, then the node is still recorded as found before the subtree is skipped, so navigation continues from a skipped current node instead of returning undefined. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/tree-collection.ts)
- Given getPreviousNode is called with a value that is not in the tree, when the traversal finishes without finding it, then the result is undefined rather than the last visited node. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/tree-collection.ts)
- Given the tree and index path [0, 2] (child1-3), when getPreviousSibling is called, then it returns child1-2, and when getNextSibling is called it returns branch1-1, so sibling navigation moves within one parent and returns branch siblings without descending. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "get previous sibling"; zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "get next sibling")
- Given a tree whose root children are child1, child2 (disabled), child3, child4 (disabled) and child5, when getPreviousSibling([2]) and getNextSibling([2]) are called, then they return child1 and child5 because the scan steps over consecutive disabled siblings in each direction. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "skips disabled siblings")
- Given the same tree, when getPreviousSibling([0]) or getNextSibling([4]) is called at the first and last positions, then both return undefined, so sibling navigation does not loop. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "skips disabled siblings")
- Given the tree and index path [0, 2], when getSiblingNodes is called, then it returns all four children of branch1 including the requested node and including branch nodes, with no disabled filtering applied. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "get sibling nodes")
- Given getFirstNode or getLastNode is called with a skip predicate, when a node matches the predicate, then its whole subtree is skipped, so first and last resolve over only the visible part of the tree. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/tree-collection.ts)

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given a ListCollection built with itemToString, itemToValue and isItemDisabled callbacks, when getValues is called, then it returns the values of all items in insertion order (react, vue, solid, angular). (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/list-collection.test.ts: "get values")
- Given a collection of four items, when size is read, then it returns 4. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/list-collection.test.ts: "count")
- Given a collection, when setItems is called with two new items, then a new collection is returned whose values are only the new items, so item updates produce a replacement collection instead of mutating in place. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/list-collection.test.ts: "set items")
- Given a collection, when at is called with index 1, then it returns the Vue item object. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/list-collection.test.ts: "get value at index")
- Given a collection of four items, when at is called with the out-of-range index 5, then it returns null rather than throwing or returning undefined. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/list-collection.test.ts: "get value at index")
- Given the values ["solid", "vue"] in the wrong order, when sort is called, then it returns ["vue", "solid"] because values are ordered by their index in the collection, not alphabetically. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/list-collection.test.ts: "sort")
- Given items with a custom itemToValue, when getItemValue is called with an item, then it returns that item's value including for a disabled item (react and solid). (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/list-collection.test.ts: "item to value")
- Given items with a custom itemToString, when stringifyItem is called with the React item, then it returns "React". (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/list-collection.test.ts: "item to string")
- Given two items, when stringifyItems is called, then their labels are joined with the default ", " separator to give "React, Angular". (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/list-collection.test.ts: "items to string")
- Given a custom isItemDisabled, when getItemDisabled is called, then it returns false for the enabled React item and true for the disabled Solid item. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/list-collection.test.ts: "item to disabled")
- Given a collection, when has is called, then it returns true for a value present in the collection and false for an unknown value such as "<random>". (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/list-collection.test.ts: "has value")
- Given a collection, when insertBefore is called with an existing value, then a new collection is returned with the new item placed immediately before it (svelte before react). (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/list-collection.test.ts: "insert before / valid")
- Given a collection, when insertBefore is called with a value that is not present, then the returned collection is unchanged and the new item is dropped. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/list-collection.test.ts: "insert before / invalid")
- Given a collection, when insertAfter is called with an existing value, then a new collection is returned with the new item placed immediately after it (svelte after solid). (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/list-collection.test.ts: "insert after / valid")
- Given a collection, when insertAfter is called with a value that is not present, then the returned collection is unchanged and the new item is dropped. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/list-collection.test.ts: "insert after / invalid")
- Given an empty collection, when insertBefore or insertAfter is called with any value, then the item is inserted at index 0 instead of being dropped. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/list-collection.ts)
- Given a collection, when reorder is called with fromIndex 2 and toIndex 1, then solid moves ahead of vue and the other items keep their relative order. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/list-collection.test.ts: "reorder / valid")
- Given a collection of four items, when reorder is called with the out-of-range toIndex 5, then the moved item is appended at the end (react, vue, angular, solid) rather than the call failing. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/list-collection.test.ts: "reorder / invalid")
- Given a collection with groupBy on a type field and no groupSort, when group is called, then it returns [groupKey, items] tuples in first-seen key order with items in their original relative order, and disabled items stay in their group. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/list-collection.test.ts: "group entries"; zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/list-collection.test.ts: "group by")
- Given items interleaved by type and groupBy on type, when group is called, then items are gathered under their group key even though they are not adjacent in the source array. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/list-collection.test.ts: "group by")
- Given groupBy on type and groupSort set to the explicit array ["runtime", "framework"], when group is called, then the runtime group is emitted before the framework group. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/list-collection.test.ts: "group by / sort groups")
- Given a grouped and group-sorted collection, when indexOf is called, then indices follow the grouped and sorted order (node 0, deno 1, react 2, vue 3, solid 4) and an unknown value returns -1. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/list-collection.test.ts: "indexOf with grouped collection")
- Given a grouped and group-sorted collection, when at is called with 0 through 4, then it returns the items in grouped and sorted order rather than source-array order. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/list-collection.test.ts: "at with grouped collection")
- Given a grouped collection, when indexOf is called for the first time, then a value-to-index map is built once and cached for later lookups, and when no groupBy or groupSort is set indexOf falls back to a plain findIndex over the items array. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/list-collection.ts)
- Given a collection containing react, when upsert is called with "react" and a replacement item, then the collection keeps its size and order and find("react") returns the replacement item. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/list-collection.test.ts: "upsert / update existing item")
- Given a collection without svelte, when upsert is called with "svelte" and a new item, then the item is appended, size grows to 5, and find("svelte") returns it. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/list-collection.test.ts: "upsert / insert new item")
- Given a collection, when upsert appends a new item, then the original collection still has its original size, values and has("svelte") false, so upsert is non-mutating and returns a new collection. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/list-collection.test.ts: "upsert / preserves original collection")
- Given upsert is called with the lookup value "react" and an item whose own value is "react-new", then the item at react's position is replaced, find("react") becomes null and find("react-new") returns the new item, so the lookup value and the item's own value are independent. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/list-collection.test.ts: "upsert / update with different value should not work")
- Given upsert is called with a mode of "prepend" for a value that is not present, when the insert happens, then the item goes to the front instead of the end (default mode is "append"). (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/list-collection.ts)
- Given a Selection in multiple mode holding "1", when extendSelection is called with anchor "1" and target "2", then the result is {1, 2}, the inclusive range from anchor to target. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/selection.test.ts: "extend / include")
- Given an empty Selection in multiple mode, when extendSelection is called with anchor "5" and target "3" (target before anchor), then the result is {3, 4, 5}, so the range is resolved in collection order regardless of the direction of the drag. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/selection.test.ts: "extend / include / reverse")
- Given a Selection in multiple mode holding {1, 2, 3}, when extendSelection is called with anchor "3" and target "2", then the previous anchor-to-last-selected range is removed and the new target-to-anchor range is added, leaving {1, 2, 3} unchanged. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/selection.test.ts: "extend / toggle")
- Given a Selection in multiple mode holding "1", when extendSelection is called with anchor and target both "1", then the result is just {1}, so a zero-length range selects only the anchor. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/selection.test.ts: "extend / first")
- Given a Selection in multiple mode holding "1" over a six-item collection, when extendSelection is called with anchor "1" and target "6", then every value 1 through 6 is selected. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/selection.test.ts: "extend / last")
- Given a Selection in single mode, when extendSelection is called, then it delegates to replaceSelection with the target value so only the target ends up selected, and in "none" mode extendSelection returns the same selection untouched. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/selection.ts)
- Given an empty Selection in multiple mode, when select is called with "1" and then "2", then both values accumulate to {1, 2} without any modifier key, because multiple mode routes select through toggleSelection. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/selection.test.ts: "select")
- Given a Selection in single mode, when select is called with an already selected value and deselectable is true, then the value is toggled off, and otherwise select replaces the whole selection with that one value. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/selection.ts)
- Given a Selection in extended mode, when select is called without forceToggle, then it replaces the selection, and when forceToggle is passed it toggles instead, which is how modifier-key clicks are modelled. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/selection.ts)
- Given a Selection in multiple mode holding {1, 2, 3}, when clearSelection is called, then the returned selection is empty. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/selection.test.ts: "clearSelection")
- Given a Selection with deselectable false, when clearSelection is called, then the selection is returned with its values intact, so a required selection cannot be emptied. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/selection.ts)
- Given a Selection in multiple mode holding {1, 2, 3}, when isSelected is called, then it returns true for "1" and false for "4". (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/selection.test.ts: "isSelected")
- Given a Selection whose mode is "none", when isSelected is called with any value, then it returns false even if the value is in the underlying Set, and toggleSelection, replaceSelection, setSelection and extendSelection all return the selection unchanged. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/selection.ts)
- Given a Selection in single mode, when setSelection is called with several values, then only the first value is kept because the loop breaks after one value in single mode. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/selection.ts)
- Given a Selection, when copy, toggleSelection, replaceSelection, setSelection or clearSelection returns a new Selection, then selectionMode and deselectable are carried over to the new instance so the mode survives every state transition. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/selection.ts)
- Given a Selection, when deselect is called with a value, then a copy without that value is returned regardless of deselectable, and replaceSelection with a null value returns the selection unchanged. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/selection.ts)
- Given a Selection and a collection, when firstSelectedValue or lastSelectedValue is called, then the selected value that is earliest or latest in collection order is returned using collection.compareValue, not Set insertion order. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/selection.ts)
- Given a selectedItemMap holding a stale copy of the React item, when resolveSelectedItems is called for ["react"] against a collection that still contains React, then the collection's live item wins over the cached one. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/selection-map.test.ts: "resolves selected items from collection first")
- Given a filtered collection that no longer contains react and a selectedItemMap that does, when resolveSelectedItems is called for ["react"], then the cached item is returned, so a selected item survives the collection being filtered down. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/selection-map.test.ts: "falls back to selected item map when collection misses value")
- Given a selectedItemMap holding react and vue and a new value list of only ["react"], when deriveSelectionState is called, then selectedItems is the React item and the next map has only the "react" key, so values dropped from the selection are pruned from the cache. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/selection-map.test.ts: "derives next state and prunes removed values")
- Given the React and Solid items, when createSelectedItemMap is called, then the returned map is keyed by their values in the given order (react, solid). (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/selection-map.test.ts: "creates selected item map from selected items")
- Given a selectedItemMap with a stale React entry and a vue entry, when updateSelectedItemMap is called with values ["react"] and the fresh React item, then the react entry is overwritten with the fresh item and the vue entry is deleted. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/selection-map.test.ts: "updates selected item map with latest items and prunes stale values")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given a ListCollection constructed with items plus optional itemToValue, itemToString, isItemDisabled, groupBy and groupSort, when a callback is omitted, then a fallback is used: a string item is its own value and label, an object item falls back to its value and label properties, the label falls back to the value when absent, and disabled comes from a truthy disabled property. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/list-collection.ts)
- Given items supplied as any iterable (not just an array), when the collection is constructed, then the iterable is spread into an internal array, and the collection itself is iterable via Symbol.iterator yielding items in order. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/list-collection.ts)
- Given a collection, when find is called with null or undefined, then it returns null, and findMany silently drops values that are not present rather than inserting holes. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/list-collection.ts)
- Given a collection, when stringify is called with a value, then it looks the item up first and returns null if the value is unknown, and stringifyMany joins the found items with the given separator. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/list-collection.ts)
- Given two values in the collection, when compareValue is called, then it returns -1, 0 or 1 based on their indices, and getValueRange returns the inclusive range between them in collection order no matter which argument comes first, or an empty array if either value is missing. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/list-collection.ts)
- Given a collection, when filter is called, then the predicate receives the stringified item label, the index and the item, and the result is a new collection of the matching items. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/list-collection.ts)
- Given a collection, when remove is called, then each argument may be either a raw value string or an item object, and items whose value resolves to null are dropped from the result. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/list-collection.ts)
- Given a collection, when move, moveBefore or moveAfter is called with a value that is not present, then the same collection instance is returned unchanged, and moveBefore/moveAfter accept several values at once and move them as a block while preserving their relative order. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/list-collection.ts)
- Given a collection, when update is called with a value that is not present, then the same collection instance is returned unchanged. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/list-collection.ts)
- Given a collection, when toString is called, then it produces a comma-terminated "value:label:disabled" string per item with falsy parts omitted, and toJSON returns only { size, first, last }. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/list-collection.ts)
- Given two collections, when isEqual is called, then it deep-compares the items arrays, and copy returns a new collection that keeps the original options (including the callbacks and grouping) with either the same or replacement items. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/list-collection.ts)
- Given an unknown value, when isListCollection or isGridCollection is called, then the list check is an instanceof test while the grid check is a duck-type test for the columnCount and getRows properties, so a structurally similar object passes the grid check. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/list-collection.ts; zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/grid-collection.ts)
- Given a GridCollection of 11 items with columnCount 3, when getRows is called, then the items are chunked into rows of three with a short final row of two ([react, vue, solid], [angular, svelte, node], [deno, ts, js], [rust, go]), and the result is cached after the first call. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/grid-collection.test.ts: "get rows")
