- Given a GridCollection, when getRowCount, getCellIndex, getCell and getValueCell are used, then the row count is the item count divided by columnCount rounded up, a cell index is row times columnCount plus column, getCell returns null for an index past the end, and getValueCell returns null for an unknown value. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/grid-collection.ts)
- Given a grid row, when getFirstEnabledColumnIndex or getLastEnabledColumnIndex is called, then it scans that row inward and returns null when the row is empty or entirely disabled. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/grid-collection.ts)
- Given a TreeCollection constructed with a rootNode plus optional nodeToValue, nodeToString, isNodeDisabled, nodeToChildren and nodeToChildrenCount, when a callback is omitted, then the fallbacks treat a string node as its own value, read value, label, disabled and childrenCount off an object node, and default the label to the value. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/tree-collection.ts)
- Given a node, when isBranchNode is called, then a node counts as a branch if it has at least one child or if nodeToChildrenCount returns a number, so a lazily loaded node with a declared children count is treated as a branch before its children exist. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/tree-collection.ts)
- Given the tree, when getValues is called with no argument, then it returns all values in depth-first document order with the root excluded (branch1, child1-1, child1-2, child1-3, branch1-1, child2-1, child1, child2). (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "visit the tree")
- Given the tree, when getValues is called with the branch1 node as the root, then it returns only that subtree's values with branch1 itself excluded, so the first argument re-roots the walk. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "visit the tree")
- Given the tree, when getParentNode is called with the value child1-2, then it returns the branch1 node, so ancestor lookup accepts a value as well as an index path. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "visit the tree")
- Given the tree, when findNode is called with "branch1", then it returns the branch node with all its children intact. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "branch nodes")
- Given the tree, when getBranchValues is called, then it returns only the values of nodes that have children (branch1 and branch1-1) and excludes the root. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "branch nodes")
- Given the branch1 node passed as the walk root, when getFirstNode and getLastNode are called, then they return child1-1 and child2-1, the first and last descendants of that branch in document order, excluding the branch itself. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "branch nodes")
- Given getBranchValues is called with a depth number or a predicate over the node depth, when nodes are visited, then only branch nodes at a matching depth are returned, and a skip predicate prunes whole subtrees. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/tree-collection.ts)
- Given the tree, when getIndexPath is called with the value "child1-2", then it returns the index path [0, 1], and when getValuePath is called with that index path it returns the value path ["branch1", "child1-2"], so index paths and value paths convert both ways. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "index path and value path")
- Given getIndexPath is called with an array of values (a value path) rather than a single value, when a value in the path does not match a child at that level, then the walk stops and a partial index path is returned, and an empty value path returns an empty index path. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/tree-collection.ts)
- Given getValuePath is called with undefined, when it resolves, then it returns an empty array, and given getValue is called with an index path that does not resolve, it returns undefined. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/tree-collection.ts)
- Given a value, when getDepth is called, then it returns the length of that value's index path, and 0 when the value is not in the tree, so a missing node is indistinguishable from the root by depth alone. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/tree-collection.ts)
- Given a parent index path and a candidate index path, when contains is called, then it returns true when the candidate starts with the parent path, which is how descendant containment is tested. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/tree-collection.ts)
- Given a list of values, when the tree's sort is called, then values are ordered by comparing their index paths and values that are not in the tree are dropped. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/tree-collection.ts)
- Given the paths ["a/b/c", "a/b/d", "a/e", "f"], when filePathToTree is called, then it builds a tree under a synthetic ROOT with an empty label, reusing existing branches by segment label and setting each node's value to the joined path prefix (a, a/b, a/b/c, a/b/d, a/e, f). (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "file path tree")
- Given the tree, when remove is called with the index path [[0]], then the whole branch1 subtree disappears and only child1 and child2 remain under ROOT. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "remove branch")
- Given the tree, when remove is called with [[0, 1]], then child1-2 is removed and its siblings close up around it. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "remove child")
- Given the tree, when remove is called with [[0, 3, 0]], then the deeply nested child2-1 is removed and branch1-1 remains as a childless node. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "remove nested child")
- Given the tree, when remove is called with an index path that does not resolve to a node ([[0, 0, 0]], pointing below a leaf), then the tree comes back unchanged. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "remove non-existent node")
- Given the tree, when replace is called with [0, 0] and a new node, then child1-1 is swapped for child1-1-new in place and its siblings keep their positions. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "replace child")
- Given the tree, when replace is called with [0, 3] and a branch node carrying its own children, then branch1-1 and its subtree are swapped for branch1-1-new with child2-1-new. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "replace branch")
- Given the tree, when replace is called with the empty index path [], then the whole root is swapped for the new node, so the collection can be re-rooted. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "replace root")
- Given the tree, when replace is called with an out-of-range index path [0, 10, 0], then the tree comes back unchanged. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "replace non-existing node")
- Given the tree, when replace is called with the index path [0, 0, 0] pointing one level below the leaf child1-1, then the new node is inserted as a child of child1-1, turning a leaf into a branch rather than failing. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "convert child to branch")
- Given the tree, when move is called from [[0, 0]] to [0, 3], then child1-1 is lifted out and reinserted later among branch1's children with the target index adjusted for the removal, so it lands before branch1-1. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "moves node to different parent")
- Given the tree, when move is called from [[0, 2]] to [0, 0], then child1-3 becomes the first child of branch1 and the other children shift down. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "moves node within same parent")
- Given the tree, when move is called from [[0, 3]] to [0], then branch1-1 is promoted to the root level ahead of branch1 and takes child2-1 with it, so moving a branch carries its whole subtree. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "moves branch with children")
- Given the tree, when move is called with the non-existent source path [[0, 10]], then the tree comes back unchanged. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "handles invalid source path")
- Given the tree, when move is called from [[0, 0]] to the out-of-range target [0, 10], then child1-1 is appended as the last child of branch1 instead of the call failing. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "handles invalid target path")
- Given a tree of nodes carrying extra properties (label, customProp, disabled false), when flatten is called, then every node is emitted with its own properties preserved plus the _children, _parent and _index metadata, and indices are assigned parent-first then level by level so the emitted order (root, branch1, its children, then the remaining root children) does not match the numeric _index order. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "preserves all node properties")
- Given a flattened tree, when the parent metadata is inspected, then each child's _parent equals its parent's _index, root-level nodes point at the root's index 0, and the root node's _parent is undefined. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "includes parent references")
- Given a flattened tree, when the children metadata is inspected, then a branch's _children lists its children's indices in order and a leaf node's _children is undefined rather than an empty array. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "includes children references")
- Given a flattened tree, when flattenedToTree is called on it, then the original nested structure is rebuilt with the _children, _parent and _index metadata stripped and all custom properties kept. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "reconstructs original structure")
- Given a flatten then flattenedToTree roundtrip, when the rebuilt tree is drawn and queried, then the shape matches the original and customProp values on both a branch and a nested child survive. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "roundtrip preserves all data (flatten -> reconstruct)")
- Given a tree whose root has an empty children array, when flatten is called, then it yields a single entry with _children, _parent both undefined and _index 0, and rebuilding it produces a collection whose getValues is empty. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "handles empty tree")
- Given a three-level deep tree whose nodes carry nested data objects, when it is flattened and rebuilt, then the deepest node's nested data object is preserved by value. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "preserves complex nested structures")
- Given flattenedToTree is called with an empty array, then it throws "Cannot create tree from empty flattened array", and given no entry has an undefined _parent it throws "No root node found in flattened data". (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/tree-collection.ts)
- Given the tree, when getDescendantNodes is called with "ROOT", then it returns every leaf in document order (child1-1, child1-2, child1-3, child2-1, child1, child2) and omits the branch nodes. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "getDescendantNodes - gets all descendants of root")
- Given the tree, when getDescendantNodes is called with "branch1", then it returns that subtree's leaves (child1-1, child1-2, child1-3, child2-1) without branch1-1 itself. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "getDescendantNodes - gets all descendants of branch node")
- Given the tree, when getDescendantNodes is called with the nested branch "branch1-1", then it returns just child2-1. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "getDescendantNodes - gets all descendants of nested branch")
- Given the tree, when getDescendantNodes is called with a leaf value such as "child1-1", then it returns an empty array. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "getDescendantNodes - returns empty array for leaf nodes")
- Given the tree, when getDescendantNodes is called with a value that is not in the tree, then it returns an empty array rather than throwing. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "getDescendantNodes - returns empty array for non-existent nodes")
- Given the tree, when getDescendantNodes is called with "branch1" and { withBranch: true }, then nested branch nodes are included in document order (child1-1, child1-2, child1-3, branch1-1, child2-1). (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "getDescendantNodes - with withBranch option")
- Given the tree, when getDescendantNodes is called with { withBranch: false }, then the result matches the default and excludes branch nodes. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "getDescendantNodes - without withBranch option (excludes branch nodes)")
- Given the index path for branch1 instead of its value, when getDescendantNodes is called with it, then the same descendants are returned, so the descendant query accepts either a value or an index path. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "getDescendantNodes - using index path")
- Given the tree, when getDescendantValues is called with "branch1", then it returns the leaf values of that subtree (child1-1, child1-2, child1-3, child2-1). (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "getDescendantValues - gets all descendant values")
- Given the tree, when getDescendantValues is called with "branch1" and { withBranch: true }, then branch1-1 appears in the returned values. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "getDescendantValues - with withBranch option")
- Given the tree, when getDescendantValues is called with { withBranch: false }, then branch values are excluded, matching the default. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "getDescendantValues - without withBranch option")
- Given the tree, when getDescendantValues is called with a leaf value, then it returns an empty array. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "getDescendantValues - returns empty array for leaf nodes")
- Given the tree, when getDescendantValues is called with a value that is not in the tree, then it returns an empty array. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "getDescendantValues - returns empty array for non-existent nodes")
- Given the index path for branch1-1, when getDescendantValues is called with it, then it returns ["child2-1"], so value lookups accept index paths too. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "getDescendantValues - using index path")
- Given the tree, when getParentNodes is called with a value or index path, then it returns the ancestor chain from the outermost ancestor inward with the root node itself excluded. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/tree-collection.ts)
- Given the tree, when filter is called with a predicate matching values containing "child1", then matching nodes are kept and their ancestors are kept as scaffolding, so branch1 survives to hold child1-1, child1-2 and child1-3 while branch1-1 and child2 are dropped. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "filters nodes by value pattern")
- Given the tree, when filter keeps only the node "branch1-1", then the result preserves branch1 as its parent and branch1-1 comes back with an empty children array because its own children did not match. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "filters branch nodes only")
- Given the tree, when filter keeps only nodes that have children, then the result is ROOT with branch1 containing branch1-1 and no leaves. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "filters branch nodes only")
- Given the tree, when filter keeps only nodes with no children, then the whole original shape comes back because every leaf's ancestors are retained to reach it. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "filters leaf nodes only")
- Given the tree, when filter keeps nodes whose index path length is 1, then only the root's direct children survive and branch1 loses its children, and when the predicate is length 2 only branch1 and its four children remain. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "filters by depth")
- Given the tree, when filter matches only the deeply nested child2-1, then the full ancestor chain ROOT to branch1 to branch1-1 to child2-1 is preserved. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "preserves tree structure for parent nodes")
- Given the tree, when filter matches nothing, then the result is just the root node with no children. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "returns empty structure when no nodes match")
- Given the tree, when filter matches either branches or values containing "child2", then the result keeps branch1 with branch1-1 and child2-1 plus the top-level child2. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "filters with complex conditions")
- Given the tree, when filter removes every child of a node that originally had children, then that node keeps its children key as an empty array, a node that never had children gains no children key, and a retained leaf such as child2-1 comes back with no children property at all. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-collection.test.ts: "preserves children key as empty array when filtering results in no matching children")
- Given a file-tree-shaped collection with nodeToValue reading id and nodeToString reading name, when replace is called with [0, 1] and a new node, then only that child of node_modules is swapped and the surrounding document order is untouched. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-skip.test.ts: "replace")
- Given the same tree, when insertBefore is called with [0, 0] and a node, then the node is inserted as the first child of node_modules ahead of node_modules/zag-js. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-skip.test.ts: "insert before")
- Given the same tree, when insertAfter is called with [0, 2] and a node, then the node is inserted after node_modules/@types and its subtree, so it becomes the last child of node_modules. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/tests/tree-skip.test.ts: "insert after")
- Given insertBefore or insertAfter is called with an index path whose parent cannot be resolved, then the method returns undefined instead of a collection, so callers have to handle a missing result. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/tree-collection.ts)
- Given remove, replace, insertBefore, insertAfter, move and filter on a TreeCollection, when any of them is called, then a new TreeCollection is returned over a newly built root node while the original collection keeps its rootNode, and the internal create step only sets a children key when the node had children or the operation produced some. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/tree-collection.ts)
- Given a TreeCollection, when visit is called, then the root node is skipped, a skip predicate receiving { value, node, indexPath } prunes whole subtrees, and an onEnter callback may return "skip" or "stop" to prune or halt the walk. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/tree-collection.ts; zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/tree-visit.ts)
- Given a TreeCollection, when isSameNode or isRootNode is called, then nodes are compared by their resolved value rather than by object identity, so two distinct objects with the same value are treated as the same node. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/tree-collection.ts)
- Given two TreeCollections, when isEqual is called, then it deep-compares the root nodes, and toJSON returns the value list excluding the root. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/tree-collection.ts)
- Given a Selection and a collection, when canSelect is called, then it returns true for every mode other than "none" before the disabled check is even reached, so a disabled item can still be added to a selection in single, multiple and extended modes. The disabled check only takes effect in "none" mode, where selection is blocked anyway, which makes the guard effectively dead. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/selection.ts)
- Given a Selection, when isEqual is called with another Selection, then the two are compared as arrays in iteration order, so the same values inserted in a different order compare as unequal. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/selection.ts)
- Given none of the assigned collection test files, then no test exercises groupSort as a comparator function, groupSort "asc" or "desc", the collection search timer expiry, getNextValue or getPreviousValue with a step or clamp argument, grid navigation with loop true, getBranchValues with a depth argument, getParentNodes, getValueRange, compareValue, setSelection, deselect, firstSelectedValue, lastSelectedValue, extended selection mode, or the deselectable false path, so those behaviors are described from source only and are not verified by tests. (zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/list-collection.ts; zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/grid-collection.ts; zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/selection.ts; zag: packages/utilities/collection/src/tree-collection.ts)

## focus-trap

### Roles and attributes

- The trap sets no attributes of its own on the container or on any tabbable node; it only reads `aria-controls` and `aria-expanded` to decide whether an out-of-container element counts as inside the boundary. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/src/focus-trap.ts)
- Given `followControlledElements` defaults to `true`, an element referenced by `aria-controls` from inside a container is treated as part of the trap only while the controller has `aria-expanded="true"`. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/src/focus-trap.ts)
- The trap observes its containers and discovered portal containers with `MutationObserver` filtered to `attributeFilter: ["aria-controls", "aria-expanded"]` plus `childList` and `subtree`, so the tabbable set is recomputed when portalled controlled content mounts or toggles. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/src/focus-trap.ts)
- `trapFocus()` (the public wrapper every machine uses) applies a different default set from the raw `FocusTrap` class: `escapeDeactivates: false`, `allowOutsideClick: true`, `preventScroll: true`, `delayInitialFocus: false`, and `fallbackFocus` pinned to the first resolved element, so machine-level traps neither self-deactivate on Escape nor block outside clicks. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/src/index.ts)

### Keyboard

- Given a container with two buttons and focus on the last tabbable, when Tab is pressed, then the event is default-prevented and focus wraps to the first tabbable. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/tests/focus-trap.test.ts: "traps forward Tab from the last tabbable")
- Given focus on the first tabbable, when Shift+Tab is pressed, then the event is default-prevented and focus wraps backward to the last tabbable. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/tests/focus-trap.test.ts: "traps backward Shift+Tab from the first tabbable")
- Given a container holding one radio group of three same-named radios where only the checked radio is a tab stop, when Tab is pressed on it, then the event is default-prevented and focus stays on that same radio rather than moving to a sibling radio. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/tests/focus-trap.test.ts: "cycles correctly when there is only one effective tab stop")
- Given two containers in one trap, when Tab is pressed on the only tabbable of container A, then focus moves to the first tabbable of container B; Tab again wraps back to A, and Shift+Tab from A wraps to B. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/tests/focus-trap.test.ts: "wraps Tab forward and backward across containers")
- Given the default `escapeDeactivates`, when Escape is pressed on a node inside the container, then the event is default-prevented and the trap reports `active === false`. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/tests/focus-trap.test.ts: "deactivates on Escape by default")
- Given `escapeDeactivates: false`, when Escape is pressed inside the container, then the event is not default-prevented and the trap stays active. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/tests/focus-trap.test.ts: "does not deactivate on Escape when disabled")
- Escape handling ignores the key while `event.isComposing` is true, so an IME composition that ends with Escape does not deactivate the trap; no test covers this path. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/src/focus-trap.ts)
- `isKeyForward` and `isKeyBackward` are overridable, and when the nav key is not literally Tab the trap moves focus manually inside the active group instead of calling `preventDefault`, because only real Tab events are prevented; no test covers custom nav keys. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/src/focus-trap.ts)
- Positive `tabindex` values are only supported in single-container traps: `updateTabbableNodes` throws when any container group reports a positive tabindex and more than one container is configured; no test covers this throw. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/src/focus-trap.ts)

### Pointer

- Given the default configuration, when `mousedown` fires on an element outside the container, then the event is default-prevented and the trap stays active. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/tests/focus-trap.test.ts: "blocks outside click by default")
- Given `allowOutsideClick: true`, when `mousedown` fires outside the container, then the event is not default-prevented and the trap stays active. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/tests/focus-trap.test.ts: "allows outside click when allowOutsideClick is true")
- Given `clickOutsideDeactivates: true`, when `mousedown` fires outside the container, then the trap deactivates. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/tests/focus-trap.test.ts: "deactivates on outside click when clickOutsideDeactivates is true")
- Given `persistentElements: [() => toast]`, when `mousedown` fires on the toast, then the event is not default-prevented and the trap stays active. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/tests/focus-trap.test.ts: "does not block pointerdown on a persistent element")
- Given `persistentElements` is set, when `mousedown` fires on a different outside element, then that element is still treated as escaping and the event is default-prevented. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/tests/focus-trap.test.ts: "still treats other outside elements as escaping when persistentElements is set")
- Given a trigger inside the container with `aria-controls="listbox-1"` and `aria-expanded="true"` and the listbox portalled to the body, when `mousedown` fires on an option inside that listbox, then the event is not default-prevented and the trap stays active. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/tests/focus-trap.test.ts: "treats an expanded aria-controls target outside the container as inside the trap")
- Given the same setup but with `aria-expanded="false"`, when `mousedown` fires on the portalled option, then the event is default-prevented, so a collapsed controller does not extend the boundary. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/tests/focus-trap.test.ts: "does not follow aria-controls when the controller is collapsed")
- Given `followControlledElements: false` with an expanded controller, when `mousedown` fires on the portalled option, then the event is default-prevented, so the `aria-controls` link is ignored entirely. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/tests/focus-trap.test.ts: "ignores aria-controls when followControlledElements is false")
- The trap listens on `mousedown`, `touchstart` and `click` (all capture, non-passive) plus `focusin` and two `keydown` handlers; the capture-phase `click` handler also calls `stopImmediatePropagation` on blocked outside clicks so no app handler sees them. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/src/focus-trap.ts)
- Pointer interaction is tracked separately from keyboard: `handlePointerDown` sets `lastInteractionType = "pointer"` and `handleTabKey` sets it back to `"keyboard"`, and that value is what decides whether return focus asks for `focusVisible`. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/src/focus-trap.ts)

### Focus management

- Given a container with two buttons and `delayInitialFocus: false`, when the trap activates, then the first tabbable receives focus. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/tests/focus-trap.test.ts: "activates and focuses the first tabbable node")
- Given `initialFocus` pointing at the second button, when the trap activates, then the second button receives focus instead of the first. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/tests/focus-trap.test.ts: "respects initialFocus when provided")
- Given `initialFocus: false` and focus sitting on an outside trigger, when the trap activates, then focus is left on the trigger and nothing inside the container is focused. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/tests/focus-trap.test.ts: "respects initialFocus=false")
- Given a container with no tabbable children and `fallbackFocus` set to the container itself, when the trap activates, then the container receives focus. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/tests/focus-trap.test.ts: "uses fallbackFocus when there are no tabbables")
- Given a container with no tabbables and no `fallbackFocus`, when `activate()` is called, then it throws. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/tests/focus-trap.test.ts: "throws when there is no valid focus target")
- Given `initialFocus` pointing at a node that was never appended to the document, when the trap activates, then it does not throw and focus lands on the `fallbackFocus` node instead. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/tests/focus-trap.test.ts: "falls back cleanly when initialFocus points to a disconnected node")
- Given focus was on an outside trigger before activation, when the trap is deactivated, then after one macrotask focus returns to that trigger. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/tests/focus-trap.test.ts: "restores focus on deactivate"; zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/tests/focus-trap.test.ts: "still returns focus normally when nothing else claims it first")
- Given `setReturnFocus` pointing at a custom button, when the trap is deactivated, then focus returns to that custom button rather than the pre-activation trigger. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/tests/focus-trap.test.ts: "respects setReturnFocus")
- Given the last interaction inside the trap was a Tab keydown (after an earlier `mousedown`, proving the tracking is live rather than a default), when the trap deactivates, then the return-focus call passes `{ focusVisible: true }` in its `FocusOptions`. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/tests/focus-trap.test.ts: "passes focusVisible when the deactivation follows a keyboard interaction")
- Given the last interaction inside the trap was a `mousedown`, when the trap deactivates, then the return-focus call omits `focusVisible` entirely so no focus ring is forced. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/tests/focus-trap.test.ts: "omits focusVisible when the deactivation follows a pointer interaction")
- Given the app moves focus to a brand-new outside element after `deactivate()` but before the deferred return-focus timer runs, when the timer fires, then the trap leaves focus where the app put it and does not steal it back. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/tests/focus-trap.test.ts: "does not steal focus back if something else legitimately claimed it before return focus fires")
- Given focus is reclaimed by a node that belongs to the trap's own (now inert) container after `deactivate()`, when the timer fires, then return focus still runs and focus lands on the original trigger, because the trap's own containers do not count as a legitimate outside claim. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/tests/focus-trap.test.ts: "still returns focus if the reclaimed element is inside one of the (now inert) containers")
- Given `delayInitialFocus: true`, when the trap activates, then nothing is focused synchronously and the first tabbable is focused on the next macrotask. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/tests/focus-trap.test.ts: "defers initial focus to the next tick when true")
- Given `activate({ checkCanFocusTrap })` returning a pending promise, when the trap activates, then initial focus is withheld until the promise settles, and it lands on the first tabbable afterwards. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/tests/focus-trap.test.ts: "waits for checkCanFocusTrap before giving initial focus")
- Given `deactivate({ checkCanReturnFocus })` returning a pending promise, when a tick passes, then focus has not returned to the trigger; after the promise resolves it takes two further ticks (an extra internal `delay()` hop inside `finishDeactivation`) before focus lands on the trigger. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/tests/focus-trap.test.ts: "waits for checkCanReturnFocus before returning focus")
- Given focus is on the second button and that button is then removed from the DOM, when the mutation is observed, then the trap refocuses the initial focus node (the first button). (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/tests/focus-trap.test.ts: "refocuses the initial node when the focused node is removed from the DOM")
- Given `persistentElements: [() => toast]`, when focus is programmatically moved to the toast, then the trap does not pull it back inside the container. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/tests/focus-trap.test.ts: "does not pull focus back when moved to a persistent element")
- On any focus escape the trap calls `stopImmediatePropagation` on the `focusin` event and then re-derives a destination from the most-recently-focused node, preferring the adjacent tabbable in that node's own container and only crossing containers when the positive-tabindex heuristics say focus escaped for a navigational reason. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/src/focus-trap.ts)
- `tryFocus` always passes `preventScroll: !!config.preventScroll`, records the node as most-recently-focused by hand (because the programmatic `focus()` API fires no `focusin`), and calls `select()` when the node is a selectable input. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/src/focus-trap.ts)

### Dismissal and layering

- Given two traps sharing one `trapStack`, when the second activates, then the first reports `paused === true` while staying `active`, the second reports `active` and unpaused; when the second deactivates the first is unpaused and still active. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/tests/focus-trap.test.ts: "pauses the previous trap when a new one activates, and unpauses it on deactivate")
- Given an active trap, when `pause()` is called, then `paused` is true and its listeners are detached so an outside `mousedown` is no longer default-prevented; `unpause()` restores both the flag and the interception. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/tests/focus-trap.test.ts: "supports manual pause and unpause")
- Given a parent trap paused by a child trap with `setReturnFocus: () => trigger`, when the child deactivates, then the parent unpauses synchronously and reclaims its own initial focus first, and only on the next macrotask does the child's deferred return focus move focus to the trigger. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/tests/focus-trap.test.ts: "still returns focus to the child's target after the parent reclaims its own initial focus on unpause")
- Given a dialog trap paused by a popover trap, and the dialog's only tabbable/fallback element removed while the popover is still open, when the popover deactivates, then the automatic `unpause()` of the dialog trap does not throw, the dialog trap stays active, and it is genuinely functional afterwards (a later outside `mousedown` is still default-prevented rather than the listeners being silently never attached). (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/tests/focus-trap.test.ts: "does not throw when auto-unpausing an outer trap whose focus target is gone")
- `unpause()` wraps both `updateTabbableNodes()` and `commitInitialFocus()` in bare `try {} catch {}` blocks, so a container that transiently has nothing focusable mid re-render degrades to a no-op instead of throwing out of the stack housekeeping. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/src/focus-trap.ts)
- Activating a trap moves it to the end of its `trapStack` (splicing out an existing entry first) and pauses whichever trap was previously last; deactivating splices it out and unpauses the new last entry. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/src/focus-trap.ts)
- Deactivation clears the pending `delayInitialFocusTimer`, drops all listeners, sets `active` and `paused` to false, disconnects the mutation observer, and clears the discovered portal-container set. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/src/focus-trap.ts)

### Notes and edge cases

- Every test element is run through a `markVisible` helper that stubs `offsetWidth`, `offsetHeight` and `getClientRects` to non-zero values; this is a jsdom-specific workaround, because jsdom reports zero layout for every element and the tabbable scan would otherwise treat the whole container as hidden and make the trap throw. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/tests/focus-trap.test.ts)
- The suite also stubs a global `CSS.escape` in `beforeEach`, because jsdom does not provide it and the `aria-controls` selector lookups need it. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/tests/focus-trap.test.ts)
- No test covers `display: none` or `visibility: hidden` elements inside a trap; visibility is only ever faked through the `markVisible` stub, so hidden-element exclusion is delegated entirely to the untested `getTabbables`/`getFocusables` helpers in dom-query. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/tests/focus-trap.test.ts; zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/src/focus-trap.ts)
- Firefox quirk, source-only: when the user Tabs out of an iframe, Firefox briefly focuses the `Document`, so `handleFocus` treats a `Document` target as non-escaping and leaves focus alone; no test covers iframe focus at all. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/src/focus-trap.ts)
- Shadow DOM traversal is delegated to a `getShadowRoot` option threaded into `getTabbables`/`getFocusables`, and container matching falls back to `event.composedPath()` when `container.contains()` fails; no test covers shadow roots. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/src/focus-trap.ts)
- `getNodeForOption` accepts a string selector for `initialFocus`, `fallbackFocus` and `setReturnFocus`, throwing a distinct error for an invalid selector and another for a valid selector matching no node (unless a fallback is allowed); none of these throws are tested. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/src/focus-trap.ts)
- `fallbackFocus` may not return `false` (only `initialFocus` and `setReturnFocus` support opting out that way), and `getInitialFocusNode` throws "needs to have at least one focusable element" both when nothing resolves and when the resolved node is disconnected and the fallback is also missing. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/src/focus-trap.ts)
- `trapFocus()` swallows activation errors in a bare `try {} catch {}` and resolves its elements inside a `requestAnimationFrame`, so a machine that mounts a trap over an empty container silently gets no trap rather than an exception. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/src/index.ts)
- The afterEach teardown deactivates traps in reverse order with `{ returnFocus: false }`, which is the only way to unwind a shared trap stack without triggering return-focus races between tests. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-trap/tests/focus-trap.test.ts)

## dismissable

### Roles and attributes

- Each layer node gets `--layer-index` set to its zero-based stack position and `--nested-layer-count` set to the number of nested layers of its own type; both are written as inline CSS custom properties on every `syncLayers()` pass. (zag: packages/utilities/dismissable/src/layer-stack.ts)
- A layer that has a parent layer of the same type gets `data-nested="<type>"`; a layer that has at least one nested layer of its own type gets `data-has-nested="<type>"`; both attributes are removed before being recomputed so stale values never linger. (zag: packages/utilities/dismissable/src/layer-stack.ts)
- Layer type is one of `dialog`, `popover`, `menu`, `listbox` or any other string, and defaults to `dialog` when `trackDismissableElement` is called without `type`. (zag: packages/utilities/dismissable/src/layer-stack.ts; zag: packages/utilities/dismissable/src/dismissable-layer.ts)
- Extra `layerStyleTargets` (for example a dialog backdrop and positioner when the layer node is the content) receive the same `--layer-index`, `--nested-layer-count`, `data-nested` and `data-has-nested`, plus a `--z-index` copied from the primary node's computed `z-index`. (zag: packages/utilities/dismissable/src/layer-stack.ts; zag: packages/utilities/dismissable/src/dismissable-layer.ts)
- While any pointer-blocking layer is on the stack, `document.body` gets `style.pointer-events: none` and a `data-inert` attribute, both applied in a `queueMicrotask` and both reverted (restoring the original inline value, and dropping the `style` attribute entirely when it ends up empty) once no pointer-blocking layer remains. (zag: packages/utilities/dismissable/src/pointer-event-outside.ts)
- Every layer node gets its own inline `pointer-events` set to `none` when it sits below the topmost pointer-blocking layer and `auto` otherwise, and a per-node `MutationObserver` watching `attributeFilter: ["style"]` re-asserts that value if anything else rewrites the node's style. (zag: packages/utilities/dismissable/src/pointer-event-outside.ts)
- `persistentElements` are polled through `waitForElement` with a 1000 ms timeout and, once found, pinned to `pointer-events: auto` so they stay clickable through a pointer-blocking layer. (zag: packages/utilities/dismissable/src/pointer-event-outside.ts)
- The layer dismissal handshake is a cancelable, bubbling `CustomEvent` named `layer:request-dismiss`, whose detail carries `originalLayer`, `targetLayer`, `originalIndex` and `targetIndex`. (zag: packages/utilities/dismissable/src/layer-stack.ts)

### Keyboard

- Given a mounted node and `defer: true` (what every machine passes), when a microtask has elapsed and Escape is dispatched on the document, then `onDismiss` is called exactly once; registration is deliberately deferred to the microtask rather than a frame so Escape works before the first paint. (zag: packages/utilities/dismissable/tests/dismissable-layer.test.ts: "registers escape handler on the microtask when the node is already available")
- Given a node getter that is still null at call time (the real machine path, where effects run before the framework commits content), when the node commits and one microtask elapses, then Escape calls `onDismiss` once without waiting a frame. (zag: packages/utilities/dismissable/tests/dismissable-layer.test.ts: "registers on the microtask tick, without waiting a frame, once the node commits")
- Given the node has still not committed by the microtask, when it commits and a frame elapses, then Escape calls `onDismiss` once, so the frame is a fallback rather than the primary path. (zag: packages/utilities/dismissable/tests/dismissable-layer.test.ts: "falls back to a frame when the node has still not committed by the microtask")
- Given cleanup runs before the node ever commits, when the node commits and both a microtask and a frame elapse, then Escape does not call `onDismiss` and the node is never the topmost layer. (zag: packages/utilities/dismissable/tests/dismissable-layer.test.ts: "does not register when cleanup runs before the node commits")
- Given a registered layer, when cleanup runs and a frame elapses, then Escape no longer calls `onDismiss` and the node is no longer the topmost layer. (zag: packages/utilities/dismissable/tests/dismissable-layer.test.ts: "cleanup removes the layer and unregisters escape")
- Escape is handled on a document-level capture-phase `keydown` listener, is ignored while `event.isComposing` is true (so an IME composition cancel does not dismiss the layer), and only acts when the node is the topmost layer. (zag: packages/utilities/dismissable/src/escape-keydown.ts; zag: packages/utilities/dismissable/src/dismissable-layer.ts)
- Escape dismissal calls `event.preventDefault()` itself before invoking `onDismiss`, and a consumer `onEscapeKeyDown` handler that calls `preventDefault` first suppresses the dismissal entirely. (zag: packages/utilities/dismissable/src/dismissable-layer.ts)

### Pointer

- Pointer-down-outside dismissal is skipped when the node sits below a pointer-blocking layer or when the event target is inside a registered branch, then forwards to `onPointerDownOutside` and `onInteractOutside`, and only dismisses when neither handler prevented the event. (zag: packages/utilities/dismissable/src/dismissable-layer.ts)
- Focus-outside dismissal is skipped only for branch targets (it does not consult pointer-blocking layers), then forwards to `onFocusOutside` and `onInteractOutside` before dismissing, so the three triggers differ: pointer-down-outside is gated on both blocking layers and branches, focus-outside on branches only, and Escape on being topmost. (zag: packages/utilities/dismissable/src/dismissable-layer.ts)
- The `exclude` predicate handed to `trackInteractOutside` treats a target as inside when it is contained by any configured exclude container, by any resolved `persistentElements` entry, or by any nested layer of this node. (zag: packages/utilities/dismissable/src/dismissable-layer.ts)

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given the same DOM node added twice (React Strict Mode or any double-register race), when the stack is inspected, then it holds one layer, reports zero nested layers of that type, sets no `data-has-nested`, and writes `--layer-index: 0` and `--nested-layer-count: 0`. (zag: packages/utilities/dismissable/tests/layer-stack.test.ts: "does not duplicate the same DOM node (Strict Mode / double-register)")
- Given two distinct layer objects added for the same node, when the top layer's `dismiss` is invoked, then the second (latest) object's callback runs, so re-adding replaces rather than shadows the earlier registration. (zag: packages/utilities/dismissable/tests/layer-stack.test.ts: "re-adding the same node keeps the latest layer object at the top")

### Dismissal and layering

- Given a layer with a `styleTargets` backdrop, when the layer is added, then the backdrop mirrors `--layer-index: 0`, `--nested-layer-count: 0` and a `--z-index` equal to the primary node's computed `zIndex`, and carries neither `data-nested` nor `data-has-nested`. (zag: packages/utilities/dismissable/tests/layer-stack.test.ts: "mirrors stack metadata to extra elements")
- Given a mirrored backdrop, when the layer is removed from the stack, then `--layer-index` and `--z-index` are cleared back to empty strings on the backdrop. (zag: packages/utilities/dismissable/tests/layer-stack.test.ts: "clears mirrored styles when the layer is removed")
- Given a `styleTargets` entry that resolves to the layer node itself, when the layer is added, then the mirroring pass skips it and the node still carries its own `--layer-index: 0` from the primary write. (zag: packages/utilities/dismissable/tests/layer-stack.test.ts: "skips mirroring when target is the same node as the layer")
- Given two layers of the same type stacked parent-then-child, when the stack syncs, then the parent gets `--layer-index: 0`, `--nested-layer-count: 1`, `data-has-nested="dialog"` and no `data-nested`, while the child gets `--layer-index: 1`, `--nested-layer-count: 0`, `data-nested="dialog"` and no `data-has-nested`. (zag: packages/utilities/dismissable/tests/layer-stack.test.ts: "sets data-nested / data-has-nested and CSS vars on parent and child")
- Given a parent layer with a nested child, when the parent is removed from the stack, then the child's `dismiss` is called exactly once, so removal cascades downward through nested layers. (zag: packages/utilities/dismissable/tests/layer-stack.test.ts: "dismisses nested layers when removing a parent from the stack")
- Given a layer with no `requestDismiss`, when `layerStack.dismiss(node)` is called, then the layer's `dismiss` runs once. (zag: packages/utilities/dismissable/tests/layer-stack.test.ts: "invokes layer.dismiss when the request-dismiss event is not prevented")
- Given a layer whose `requestDismiss` calls `event.preventDefault()`, when `layerStack.dismiss(node)` is called, then `dismiss` is never invoked, so a layer can veto a cascade dismissal. (zag: packages/utilities/dismissable/tests/layer-stack.test.ts: "does not invoke layer.dismiss when requestDismiss prevents default")
- Given a non-blocking bottom layer under a pointer-blocking child, when the stack is queried, then `hasPointerBlockingLayer()` is true, `pointerBlockingLayers()` has length 1, `topMostPointerBlockingLayer().node` is the child, `isBelowPointerBlockingLayer` is true for the bottom and false for the child, and `isTopMost` is true only for the child. (zag: packages/utilities/dismissable/tests/layer-stack.test.ts: "isBelowPointerBlockingLayer and isTopMost reflect stack order and pointerBlocking flags")
- Given a registered branch element with a nested span, when `isInBranch` is asked about the span, then it is true; after `removeBranch`, it is false. (zag: packages/utilities/dismissable/tests/layer-stack.test.ts: "isInBranch is true when target is inside a registered branch")
- Given a parent layer and a nested child layer holding a button, when `isInNestedLayer` is asked about that button relative to the parent, then it is true, while asking about the parent node itself is false. (zag: packages/utilities/dismissable/tests/layer-stack.test.ts: "returns true when target is inside a nested layer node")
- Given a parent is removed while a child layer remains, when `isInNestedLayer(child, document.body)` is asked immediately, then it returns true because `recentlyRemoved` is non-empty; after a double-`requestAnimationFrame` tick it returns false. (zag: packages/utilities/dismissable/tests/layer-stack.test.ts: "treats interactions as inside while recentlyRemoved is non-empty, then clears after nextTick")
- Given a mounted node and `defer: true`, when a microtask elapses, then `layerStack.isTopMost(node)` is true, so stack registration and Escape registration land on the same tick. (zag: packages/utilities/dismissable/tests/dismissable-layer.test.ts: "adds the layer to the stack on the microtask when the node is already available")
- `remove()` deliberately holds the removed node in a global `recentlyRemoved` set for two frames (`nextTick`), which makes every `isInNestedLayer` query answer true during that window so a focus move out of a closing nested layer cannot cascade into dismissing its parent. (zag: packages/utilities/dismissable/src/layer-stack.ts)
- Layer cleanup removes the layer from the stack, re-runs `assignPointerEventToLayers()` for the survivors, clears the removed node's inline `pointer-events` and disconnects its style observer, then runs the escape and interact-outside cleanups. (zag: packages/utilities/dismissable/src/dismissable-layer.ts)
- `trackDismissableBranch` registers a node as a branch through the same `whenNode` deferral and always warns when the branch node is missing, unlike `trackDismissableElement` whose warning can be turned off with `warnOnMissingNode: false`. (zag: packages/utilities/dismissable/src/dismissable-layer.ts)

### Notes and edge cases

- `layerStack` is module-level global mutable state (`layers`, `branches`, `recentlyRemoved`), so the test suite has to drain three double-rAF ticks in `afterEach` to stop one test's pending `recentlyRemoved` cleanup from producing a false `isInNestedLayer` positive in the next. (zag: packages/utilities/dismissable/tests/layer-stack.test.ts)
- The pointer-events observer is only installed when `window.MutationObserver` exists, and silently does nothing otherwise. (zag: packages/utilities/dismissable/src/pointer-event-outside.ts)
- `disablePointerEventsOutside` refuses to touch the body when `data-inert` is already present, which is how two concurrent pointer-blocking layers avoid each stashing the other's mutated value as the "original" `pointer-events`. (zag: packages/utilities/dismissable/src/pointer-event-outside.ts)
- `layerStack.clear()` removes only `layers[0]`, relying on the nested-dismiss cascade from that removal to take the rest down; it throws if the stack is empty. (zag: packages/utilities/dismissable/src/layer-stack.ts)
- No test exercises the `debug: true` option, which `console.log`s the original event on every pointer-down-outside and focus-outside dismissal. (zag: packages/utilities/dismissable/src/dismissable-layer.ts)

## interact-outside

### Roles and attributes

- This utility ships no tests at all: `packages/utilities/interact-outside` has only `src`, no `tests` directory, so everything below is read from source. (zag: packages/utilities/interact-outside/src/index.ts)
- It sets no attributes and writes no CSS variables; its entire contract is the pair of cancelable `CustomEvent`s it dispatches on the tracked node: `pointerdown.outside` and `focus.outside`, both `bubbles: false` and `cancelable: true`. (zag: packages/utilities/interact-outside/src/index.ts)
- Each event's detail carries `originalEvent`, `contextmenu` (true when the original event is a context-menu gesture), `focusable` (for pointer events, whether anything in the composed path is focusable; for focus events, whether the target itself is focusable), and `target`. (zag: packages/utilities/interact-outside/src/index.ts)
- Consumer handlers are attached to the node as `{ once: true }` listeners for that event type immediately before the event is fired, so calling `preventDefault()` inside `onPointerDownOutside`, `onFocusOutside` or `onInteractOutside` is the documented way to veto the consequence. (zag: packages/utilities/interact-outside/src/index.ts)
- Listeners are registered on the node's own document plus, defensively, on the parent window (only when the node's window has a `frameElement`) and on every child frame's document, each wrapped in `try {}`/`catch {}` so cross-origin frames fail silently. (zag: packages/utilities/interact-outside/src/index.ts; zag: packages/utilities/interact-outside/src/frame-utils.ts)
- `followControlledElements` defaults to `true`, and when on, a target inside an element controlled via `aria-controls` by something inside the node counts as inside, which is what keeps nested menus, select dropdowns and other portalled content from reading as outside. (zag: packages/utilities/interact-outside/src/index.ts)

### Pointer

- `pointerdown` is registered on capture, but only after a `setTimeout(..., 0)`, so the pointer-down that opened the layer cannot immediately close it again. (zag: packages/utilities/interact-outside/src/index.ts)
- A target is treated as inside (no event fired) when it is not an HTMLElement, is disconnected from the DOM, is contained by the node, has an event point that falls within the node's bounding rect (the password-manager-overlay case), is a controlled element, or is rejected by the custom `exclude` predicate. (zag: packages/utilities/interact-outside/src/index.ts)
- A pointer event whose coordinates land on a scrollbar is treated as inside, checked both against the nearest overflow ancestor of the node and against the nearest overflow ancestor of whatever element has `aria-controls="<node id>"`; the scrollbar hit box is the ancestor's client box widened by a hard-coded 16 px on whichever axis is scrollable. (zag: packages/utilities/interact-outside/src/index.ts)
- Touch quirk: when `event.pointerType === "touch"`, the utility does not act on the pointerdown at all; it flushes any queued handlers and instead waits for a single `click` on the document, parent window and every frame, because touch pointerdown is not a reliable dismissal signal. (zag: packages/utilities/interact-outside/src/index.ts)
- The `defer` option maps to a `requestAnimationFrame` hop before evaluating the target, but it is deliberately ignored on touch devices (`defer && !isTouchDevice()`), so touch interactions are always evaluated synchronously within the click handler. (zag: packages/utilities/interact-outside/src/index.ts)
- When the node lives in a shadow root, the target is taken from `composedPath()[0]` rather than `event.target`, because the retargeted `event.target` would be the shadow host. (zag: packages/utilities/interact-outside/src/index.ts)

### Focus management

- `focusin` is registered on capture on the document, the parent window and every frame, but only when the device is not a touch device: `isTouchDevice()` suppresses focus-outside tracking entirely. (zag: packages/utilities/interact-outside/src/index.ts)
- Safari quirk: `focusin` events are ignored entirely while a pointer press is in flight (tracked by an `isPointerDown` flag cleared on the next `pointerup`), because Safari does not focus buttons on pointerdown and focusin-based dismissal would otherwise race with pointer-based interaction. (zag: packages/utilities/interact-outside/src/index.ts)

### Notes and edge cases

- `trackInteractOutside` resolves its node through an optional `requestAnimationFrame` hop and returns a composed cleanup that clears the pending pointerdown timer, flushes the touch-path click listeners and removes every registered listener. (zag: packages/utilities/interact-outside/src/index.ts)
- `isEventPointWithin` bails out when the node's bounding rect has zero width or height, so a collapsed or unmeasured node never swallows outside pointer events. (zag: packages/utilities/interact-outside/src/index.ts)
- The trigger lookup uses an unescaped attribute selector, `doc.querySelector('[aria-controls="' + node.id + '"]')`, so an id containing a quote or other selector metacharacter would throw. (zag: packages/utilities/interact-outside/src/index.ts)
- `isPointerEvent` is duck-typed as `"clientY" in event`, so any mouse or touch event carrying coordinates goes down the pointer path regardless of its constructor. (zag: packages/utilities/interact-outside/src/index.ts)

## remove-scroll

### Roles and attributes

- Locking marks `document.body` with a bare `data-scroll-lock=""` attribute, and that marker is always on `body` even when the element actually locked is `html`. (zag: packages/utilities/remove-scroll/src/index.ts; zag: packages/utilities/remove-scroll/tests/index.test.ts: "applies the scroll lock and clears it on cleanup")
- Locking writes `--scrollbar-width: <px>` on `document.documentElement`, computed as `window.innerWidth - documentElement.clientWidth`. (zag: packages/utilities/remove-scroll/src/index.ts)
- The locked scroll container gets inline `overflow: hidden` plus a scrollbar-width padding on one side; the side is `paddingLeft` when the document element's `getBoundingClientRect().left` rounded plus `scrollLeft` is non-zero (the RTL body-scrollbar case) and `paddingRight` otherwise. (zag: packages/utilities/remove-scroll/src/index.ts)
- Scrollbar compensation padding is skipped entirely when either `html` or `body` has `scrollbar-gutter: stable` (or a value starting `stable `), because the browser already reserves the space, and also skipped when the measured scrollbar width is zero. (zag: packages/utilities/remove-scroll/src/index.ts)

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given no active lock, when `preventBodyScroll(document)` runs, then `data-scroll-lock` is present and `body.style.overflow === "hidden"`; the returned release clears both back to absent and empty string. (zag: packages/utilities/remove-scroll/tests/index.test.ts: "applies the scroll lock and clears it on cleanup")
- Given two calls to `preventBodyScroll`, when the first release runs, then the lock is still applied (`overflow` still `hidden`) because the count only reaches zero on the second release, which is what fully unlocks. (zag: packages/utilities/remove-scroll/tests/index.test.ts: "returns a cleanup when already locked (ref-counted)")
- Given two locks, when the first release is called three times, then the count is decremented only once and the lock remains; the second release then fully unlocks. (zag: packages/utilities/remove-scroll/tests/index.test.ts: "releases are idempotent (calling twice does not double-decrement)")
- Given a lock that was fully released, when `preventBodyScroll` is called again, then the lock re-applies and its release unlocks again, so the per-document state is genuinely deleted rather than left at a stale count. (zag: packages/utilities/remove-scroll/tests/index.test.ts: "can lock again after fully releasing")
- Given the React Strict Mode mount-cleanup-mount sequence where setup runs a second time before the first cleanup fires, when both releases eventually run, then the lock is fully cleared and `body.style.overflow` is back to empty. (zag: packages/utilities/remove-scroll/tests/index.test.ts: "simulates the React Strict Mode mount-cleanup-mount sequence without leaking")
- Given two independent callers (a dialog and a drawer), when the dialog releases first, then the lock stays applied for the drawer, and only the drawer's release unlocks. (zag: packages/utilities/remove-scroll/tests/index.test.ts: "nested locks across separate callers (e.g. dialog + drawer) unlock cleanly")
- Given an already-released lock, when its release is called again, then it does not throw and the page stays unlocked. (zag: packages/utilities/remove-scroll/tests/index.test.ts: "does not throw when called repeatedly even with no scroll lock active")
- Given no argument at all, when `preventBodyScroll()` is called, then it falls back to the global `document` and locks it. (zag: packages/utilities/remove-scroll/tests/index.test.ts: "default `document` argument falls back to global")
- Given two distinct `Document` instances, when each is locked, then both bodies carry `data-scroll-lock` and releasing one leaves the other locked, because the ref-count map is keyed on the Document instance (a `WeakMap<Document, LockState>`). (zag: packages/utilities/remove-scroll/tests/index.test.ts: "isolates locks per document")
- Given a lock-then-release cycle with `document.body.removeAttribute` spied, when the release runs, then `removeAttribute` is called with `data-scroll-lock`; this test is a leak-detection smoke check whose name ("warns when called from a stale state object should not regress") does not describe what it asserts. (zag: packages/utilities/remove-scroll/tests/index.test.ts: "warns when called from a stale state object should not regress (smoke)")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given the default document where `html` does not establish its own scroll container, when the lock applies, then `body.style.overflow` is `hidden` and `documentElement.style.overflow` is not. (zag: packages/utilities/remove-scroll/tests/index.test.ts: "locks body by default")
- Given `documentElement.style.overflowY = "auto"` (the app-shell layout where `html` owns the viewport scroll), when the lock applies, then `documentElement.style.overflow` is `hidden` and `body.style.overflow` is not, so the utility picks whichever of `html`/`body` is the real overflow element. (zag: packages/utilities/remove-scroll/tests/index.test.ts: "locks html instead when it establishes its own scroll container (app-shell layout)")
- Given the `/scroll-lock/html-scroller` page where `html` establishes the scroll container, when the dialog trigger is clicked, then `body` carries the `data-scroll-lock` marker while the element actually set to `overflow: hidden` is `html`, not `body`. (zag: e2e/scroll-lock.e2e.ts: "locks <html> instead of <body> when html establishes the scroll container")
- Given the same page with an external `document.body.style.overflowY = "hidden"` already applied (a body lock that cannot actually stop the page scrolling, because `html` owns the scroller), when the dialog opens, then zag still locks `html`; closing the dialog clears the `data-scroll-lock` marker. (zag: e2e/scroll-lock.e2e.ts: "locks immediately when an external <body> lock cannot affect the page")
- iOS quirk: `isIos()` selects a completely different lock strategy, because iOS is the only platform that ignores `overflow: hidden` on `document.body`; instead the body is pinned with `position: fixed`, `overflow: hidden`, `right: 0`, and negative `top`/`left` offsets computed from `scrollX`/`scrollY`. (zag: packages/utilities/remove-scroll/src/index.ts)
- iOS quirk: the negative offsets subtract `Math.floor(visualViewport.offsetTop)` and `offsetLeft` to account for a zoomed or keyboard-shifted visual viewport, with `?? 0` fallbacks because iOS 12 has no `visualViewport`. (zag: packages/utilities/remove-scroll/src/index.ts)
- iOS quirk: the iOS cleanup restores the stashed inline styles and then calls `win.scrollTo({ left: scrollX, top: scrollY, behavior: "instant" })` to put the page back where it was, a restoration step the non-iOS path does not need; none of this is covered by the jsdom tests, which never stub `isIos()`. (zag: packages/utilities/remove-scroll/src/index.ts; zag: packages/utilities/remove-scroll/tests/index.test.ts)
- Restoration is exact rather than blanket: `setStyle`/`setStyleProperty` snapshot the previous inline value of each property they touch, reassign it on cleanup, and remove the `style` attribute entirely when the element's inline style ends up empty. (zag: packages/utilities/dom-query/src/set.ts; zag: packages/utilities/remove-scroll/src/index.ts)
- The scroll-container choice uses `isOverflowElement`, which tests the concatenated computed `overflow + overflowY + overflowX` against an overflow regex and rejects `display` values that cannot establish a scroll box. (zag: packages/utilities/dom-query/src/overflow.ts)
- `setStyle` short-circuits to a no-op cleanup when every property already holds the requested value, so a second lock attempt on an already-hidden scroller returns nothing to restore. (zag: packages/utilities/dom-query/src/set.ts)
- The jsdom suite has to reset `data-scroll-lock`, the whole `style` attribute, `--scrollbar-width`, `overflow` and `overflow-y` by hand in `afterEach`, since module-level lock state is per-Document and survives between tests. (zag: packages/utilities/remove-scroll/tests/index.test.ts)
- E2E model helper: `gotoHtmlScroller()` navigates to `/scroll-lock/html-scroller`. (zag: e2e/models/scroll-lock.model.ts)
- E2E model helper: `clickTrigger()` clicks the element with test id `dialog-trigger`. (zag: e2e/models/scroll-lock.model.ts)
- E2E model helper: `clickClose()` clicks the element with test id `dialog-close`. (zag: e2e/models/scroll-lock.model.ts)
- E2E model helper: `seeZagLockEventually()` retry-asserts that `body` has the `data-scroll-lock` attribute with an empty string value. (zag: e2e/models/scroll-lock.model.ts)
- E2E model helper: `seeNoZagLockEventually()` retry-asserts that `body` does not have `data-scroll-lock=""`. (zag: e2e/models/scroll-lock.model.ts)
- E2E model helper: `isHtmlLocked()` evaluates `document.documentElement.style.overflow === "hidden"` in the page. (zag: e2e/models/scroll-lock.model.ts)
- E2E model helper: `isBodyLocked()` evaluates `document.body.style.overflow === "hidden"` in the page. (zag: e2e/models/scroll-lock.model.ts)
- The scroll-lock e2e spec pins no browser-specific behavior: it has no `browserName` branches, `test.skip` or `test.fixme`, so both cases run on every configured browser. (zag: e2e/scroll-lock.e2e.ts)

## aria-hidden

### Roles and attributes

- This utility ships no tests at all: `packages/utilities/aria-hidden` has only `src`, no `tests` directory, so everything below is read from source. (zag: packages/utilities/aria-hidden/src/aria-hidden.ts)
- `hideOthers(target, parentNode = target.ownerDocument.body)` walks every sibling branch outside the target and sets `aria-hidden="true"` on each, marking them with `data-aria-hidden=""` so the utility can tell its own work apart from pre-existing attributes. (zag: packages/utilities/aria-hidden/src/aria-hidden.ts)
- `inertOthers` does the same walk but sets the `inert` attribute to an empty string and marks with `data-inerted=""`. (zag: packages/utilities/aria-hidden/src/aria-hidden.ts)
- `suppressOthers` picks `inertOthers` when `HTMLElement.prototype` owns an `inert` property and falls back to `hideOthers` otherwise, marking with `data-suppressed=""`; this is the browser-support branch, so older engines get `aria-hidden` and modern ones get real inertness. (zag: packages/utilities/aria-hidden/src/aria-hidden.ts)
- The walk never touches the target's own ancestors: every ancestor chain up from each target is collected into a keep set first, and only nodes outside that set get the attribute. (zag: packages/utilities/aria-hidden/src/walk-tree-outside.ts)
- Elements controlled via `aria-controls` from inside the target are also kept when `followControlledElements` is true (the default), so portalled dropdowns belonging to the dialog are not hidden from screen readers. (zag: packages/utilities/aria-hidden/src/walk-tree-outside.ts)
- Live regions are exempt by design: a node is skipped when its `localName` is `script`, `output`, `status` or `next-route-announcer`, when its `role` is `status`, when it has any `aria-live` attribute, or when it matches `[data-live-announcer]`. (zag: packages/utilities/aria-hidden/src/walk-tree-outside.ts)
- Attribute application is ref-counted per node in two parallel `WeakMap`s (a global counter and a per-marker-name counter), so overlapping dialogs each add a claim and only the last release removes the attribute. (zag: packages/utilities/aria-hidden/src/walk-tree-outside.ts)
- A node that already carried the control attribute before the first claim is recorded in an `uncontrolledNodes` map and has its attribute left in place on release, so the utility never strips an author's own `aria-hidden="true"` or `inert`. (zag: packages/utilities/aria-hidden/src/walk-tree-outside.ts)
- The marker attribute and the control attribute are counted separately, so the marker can be removed on a different release than the attribute itself. (zag: packages/utilities/aria-hidden/src/walk-tree-outside.ts)
- When the global `lockCount` drops to zero, all the counter maps are thrown away and re-created, which is the only mechanism that stops the module-level `WeakMap` state from accumulating stale counts. (zag: packages/utilities/aria-hidden/src/walk-tree-outside.ts)

### SSR and hydration

- The `ariaHidden(targetsOrFn, { defer })` wrapper defaults `defer` to `true`, deferring the whole walk to a `requestAnimationFrame` so it runs after the framework has committed portalled content; passing `defer: false` runs it synchronously. (zag: packages/utilities/aria-hidden/src/index.ts)
- The wrapper filters out null targets and bails without hiding anything when the resolved target list is empty, so a not-yet-mounted dialog does not hide the page. (zag: packages/utilities/aria-hidden/src/index.ts)

### Notes and edge cases

- A target that is not contained by the parent node is retried through its shadow host chain (`unwrapHost`), and if that also fails the utility logs `console.error("[zag-js > ariaHidden] target ... in not contained inside ...")` and drops that target rather than throwing. (zag: packages/utilities/aria-hidden/src/walk-tree-outside.ts)
- Each per-node attribute write is wrapped in `try {}`/`catch {}` and a failure logs `console.error("[zag-js > ariaHidden] cannot operate on ", node, e)`, so one hostile node cannot abort the walk. (zag: packages/utilities/aria-hidden/src/walk-tree-outside.ts)
- The "already hidden" test differs by attribute kind: for `aria-hidden` the value must literally be `"true"`, while for `inert` any present value other than `"false"` counts. (zag: packages/utilities/aria-hidden/src/walk-tree-outside.ts)
- There is a duplicated `counterMap = new WeakMap()` assignment in the zero-lock reset path, which is harmless but shows the reset was written twice. (zag: packages/utilities/aria-hidden/src/walk-tree-outside.ts)
- The implementation is a fork of `theKashey/aria-hidden`, credited in a header comment, so upstream behavior is the reference for anything not spelled out here. (zag: packages/utilities/aria-hidden/src/aria-hidden.ts)

## focus-visible

### Roles and attributes

- This utility ships no tests at all: `packages/utilities/focus-visible` has only `src`, no `tests` directory, so everything below is read from source. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-visible/src/index.ts)
- It sets no attributes and writes no CSS variables; it exposes the current interaction modality as one of `"keyboard"`, `"pointer"` or `"virtual"` and reports changes through subscriber callbacks. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-visible/src/index.ts)
- `isFocusVisible()` is true only for the `keyboard` and `virtual` modalities; `pointer` and the initial `null` (no interaction yet, which is the case during focus-trap autofocus) both read as not focus-visible. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-visible/src/index.ts)
- Per window it installs capture-phase `keydown`, `keyup` and `click` listeners on the document, a capture-phase `focus` and a bubble-phase `blur` on the window, and a `beforeunload` teardown registered `{ once: true }`. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-visible/src/index.ts)
- Pointer tracking prefers `pointerdown`/`pointermove`/`pointerup` when `window.PointerEvent` exists and falls back to `mousedown`/`mousemove`/`mouseup` otherwise. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-visible/src/index.ts)
- Setup is idempotent per window, keyed by a module-level `Map<Window, GlobalListenerData>`, and teardown restores the original `HTMLElement.prototype.focus` from that map. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-visible/src/index.ts)

### Keyboard

- A keydown or keyup switches modality to `keyboard` only when the key passes `isValidKey`, which rejects `metaKey`, `ctrlKey`, `altKey` (except on Mac, where Alt produces characters), and the bare `Control`, `Shift` and `Meta` keys. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-visible/src/index.ts)
- For text inputs, only `Tab` and `Escape` make focus visible: `isKeyboardFocusEvent` suppresses the change for any other key when the modality is `keyboard` and the event is a `KeyboardEvent`. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-visible/src/index.ts)
- "Text input" is inferred as well as passed: an active element that is an `HTMLInputElement` whose `type` is not one of checkbox, radio, range, color, file, image, button, submit or reset, or an `HTMLTextAreaElement`, or any `contentEditable` element, all count. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-visible/src/index.ts)

### Pointer

- WebKit quirk: trusted `pointermove`/`mousemove` events whose `clientX`/`clientY` match the last recorded position are ignored, because WebKit fires them when content scrolls under a stationary cursor. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-visible/src/index.ts)
- Any pointer event sets the modality to `pointer`, but only `mousedown`/`pointerdown` marks `hasEventBeforeFocus` and notifies subscribers; moves and ups update the modality silently. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-visible/src/index.ts)
- A click that `isVirtualClick` identifies (a screen-reader or assistive-tech activation) sets the modality to `virtual` and returns early without running the label logic. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-visible/src/index.ts)
- Label activation is tracked explicitly: on a real click inside a `<label>` with an enabled associated control that is not already focused, the control is remembered as `pendingLabelControl`, so the browser's subsequent default focus of that control is not mistaken for a virtual interaction. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-visible/src/index.ts)
- Interactive content nested inside a label (anchors with href, `audio[controls]`, button, details, embed, iframe, `img[controls]`, `img[usemap]`, input, select, textarea, `video[controls]`) does not arm the label path, unless that interactive element is the label's control itself. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-visible/src/index.ts)

### Focus management

- A focus event that arrives with no preceding keyboard or pointer event switches the modality to `virtual`; this is what catches iOS form next/previous button navigation. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-visible/src/index.ts)
- Firefox quirk: focus events targeting the `window` or the `document` are ignored, because Firefox fires two extra focus events (window then document) the first time the user clicks into an iframe, which would otherwise raise a spurious keyboard focus ring. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-visible/src/index.ts)
- Untrusted focus events (`e.isTrusted === false`) and events arriving while the exported `ignoreFocusEvent` flag is set are ignored, the latter so programmatic focus reverts do not produce focus rings. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-visible/src/index.ts)
- A focus event whose target is the remembered `pendingLabelControl` does not trip the virtual-modality branch. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-visible/src/index.ts)
- A window blur resets `hasEventBeforeFocus` and `pendingLabelControl` and sets `hasBlurredWindowRecently`, which suppresses the virtual-modality guess on the focus event that arrives when the user tabs back into the window. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-visible/src/index.ts)
- `HTMLElement.prototype.focus` is monkey-patched per window so every programmatic focus pre-sets `hasEventBeforeFocus`, keeping the modality at whatever the user last did (for example `pointer` after a click that opened a dialog) instead of flipping to `virtual` on autofocus or focus-trap focus. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-visible/src/index.ts)
- The patch is installed with `Object.defineProperty` rather than plain assignment because plain assignment does not work in happy-dom, and both the patch and the restore are wrapped in `try {}`/`catch {}` so a non-configurable or already-patched property degrades to event-listener-only tracking. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-visible/src/index.ts)

### Notes and edge cases

- `trackFocusVisible` fires its `onChange` immediately with `autoFocus || isFocusVisible()`, so an autofocused element is reported as focus-visible on subscription regardless of the real modality. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-visible/src/index.ts)
- `trackInteractionModality` fires its `onChange` immediately with the current modality and notifies on every modality change without the text-input key filtering that `trackFocusVisible` applies. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-visible/src/index.ts)
- `setInteractionModality(modality)` forces the modality and notifies all subscribers with a `null` event, which is the escape hatch for callers that know the interaction kind out of band. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-visible/src/index.ts)
- Modality, subscriber set and per-window listener map are all module-level globals shared across every component in the page, so there is exactly one modality for the whole document. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-visible/src/index.ts)
