- The implementation credits Adobe's `useFocusVisible` from react-spectrum as its source, so upstream behavior is the reference for anything not spelled out here. (zag: packages/utilities/focus-visible/src/index.ts)

## popper

### Roles and attributes

- This utility ships no tests at all: `packages/utilities/popper` has only `src`, no `tests` directory, so everything below is read from source. (zag: packages/utilities/popper/src/get-placement.ts)
- The floating element receives `--x` and `--y` as pixel values, each rounded to the device pixel ratio (`Math.round(value * dpr) / dpr`) and written only when the new value differs from the last by at least 0.5 px. (zag: packages/utilities/popper/src/get-placement.ts)
- The floating element receives `--reference-width` and `--reference-height` (the anchor's rounded rect) and `--available-width` and `--available-height` (the floored available space from the size middleware), each written only past the same 0.5 px change threshold. (zag: packages/utilities/popper/src/get-placement.ts)
- The floating element receives `--z-index`, copied from the computed `z-index` of its first element child, and computed exactly once per floating node to avoid a forced reflow on every position update. (zag: packages/utilities/popper/src/get-placement.ts)
- The floating element receives `--transform-origin` from the transformOrigin middleware, which also returns the same string as middleware data. (zag: packages/utilities/popper/src/middleware.ts)
- The arrow part is located by the selector `[data-part=arrow]` inside the floating element, and the arrow middleware stack is rebuilt whenever the floating element is a different node. (zag: packages/utilities/popper/src/get-placement.ts)
- `getPlacementStyles().arrow` returns `position: absolute`, `width` and `height` both `var(--arrow-size)`, and declares `--arrow-size-half: calc(var(--arrow-size) / 2)` and `--arrow-offset: calc(var(--arrow-size-half) * -1)`. (zag: packages/utilities/popper/src/get-styles.ts; zag: packages/utilities/popper/src/middleware.ts)
- `getPlacementStyles().arrowTip` returns `background: var(--arrow-background)`, `top: 0`, `left: 0`, `width: 100%`, `height: 100%`, `position: absolute`, `zIndex: inherit`, and a rotation transform chosen by placement side: 45deg for bottom, 135deg for left, 225deg for top, 315deg for right. (zag: packages/utilities/popper/src/get-styles.ts)
- `getPlacementStyles().floating` returns the configured `strategy` as `position` (default `absolute`), `isolation: isolate`, `top: 0px`, `left: 0px`, `zIndex: var(--z-index)`, and `transform: translate3d(var(--x), var(--y), 0)`. (zag: packages/utilities/popper/src/get-styles.ts)
- `sameWidth` swaps the floating element's `min-width: max-content` for `width: var(--reference-width)`; `fitViewport` adds `max-width: var(--available-width)` and `max-height: var(--available-height)`. (zag: packages/utilities/popper/src/get-styles.ts)
- `isValidPlacement` accepts exactly `top|bottom|left|right` optionally suffixed with `-start` or `-end`, and `getPlacementDetails` splits a placement into `{ side, align, hasAlign }`. (zag: packages/utilities/popper/src/placement.ts)

### Positioning

- Defaults are `strategy: "absolute"`, `placement: "bottom"`, `listeners: true`, `restoreStyles: false`, `applyStyles: true`, `gutter: 8`, `flip: true`, `slide: true`, `overlap: false`, `sameWidth: false`, `fitViewport: false`, `overflowPadding: 8`, `arrowPadding: 4`. (zag: packages/utilities/popper/src/get-placement.ts)
- The main-axis offset is `gutter + arrowHeight / 2` when the gutter is a number, and falls back to half the arrow height when no gutter is given; `offset.mainAxis` overrides `gutter`. (zag: packages/utilities/popper/src/get-placement.ts)
- Cross-axis offset comes from `offset.crossAxis`, falling back to the `shift` option but only for placements with no alignment suffix; `alignmentAxis` always takes `shift`. (zag: packages/utilities/popper/src/get-placement.ts)
- The offset middleware is skipped entirely when both `offset` and `gutter` are explicitly null. (zag: packages/utilities/popper/src/get-placement.ts)
- Flip is enabled by default with `padding: overflowPadding`; passing an array to `flip` supplies explicit `fallbackPlacements` instead of the default flip behavior. (zag: packages/utilities/popper/src/get-placement.ts)
- The shift middleware runs when either `slide` or `overlap` is on, mapping `slide` to `mainAxis`, `overlap` to `crossAxis`, `overflowPadding` to `padding`, and always installing `limitShift()` as the limiter. (zag: packages/utilities/popper/src/get-placement.ts)
- The size middleware runs unless `sizeMiddleware: false` and neither `sameWidth` nor `fitViewport` need it, so those two options force it back on. (zag: packages/utilities/popper/src/get-placement.ts)
- `boundary` accepts a function (called to resolve the element), the literal string `"clipping-ancestors"` (mapped to floating-ui's `clippingAncestors`), or a value passed straight through; it is threaded into flip, shift, size and hide. (zag: packages/utilities/popper/src/get-placement.ts)
- `hideWhenDetached` installs floating-ui's `hide` with `strategy: "referenceHidden"` and a boundary defaulting to `clippingAncestors`, and when the reference is hidden the floating element gets inline `visibility: hidden` and `pointer-events: none`, both removed again when it reappears. (zag: packages/utilities/popper/src/get-placement.ts)
- `listeners: true` expands to autoUpdate with `ancestorResize`, `ancestorScroll`, `elementResize` and `layoutShift` all on; passing an object uses it verbatim, and a falsy value installs no observers at all. (zag: packages/utilities/popper/src/get-placement.ts)
- Auto-update observers are torn down and re-created only when the anchor identity or the floating node actually changes, where anchor identity is the element itself, or a virtual element's `contextElement`, or the virtual object. (zag: packages/utilities/popper/src/get-placement.ts)
- `applyStyles: false` skips every inline style write while still awaiting the computed position and calling `onComplete` with the dpr-rounded `x` and `y`. (zag: packages/utilities/popper/src/get-placement.ts)
- `restoreStyles: true` snapshots the floating element's `transform`, `visibility`, `pointer-events`, `--x`, `--y`, `--z-index`, `--reference-width`, `--reference-height`, `--available-width`, `--available-height` and `--transform-origin`, plus the arrow's `top`, `right`, `bottom` and `left`, and restores them on cleanup, removing the `style` attribute when nothing is left. (zag: packages/utilities/popper/src/get-placement.ts)
- A custom `updatePosition` hook replaces the built-in update entirely and is handed `{ updatePosition, floatingElement }`, with `onPositioned({ placed: true })` fired afterwards. (zag: packages/utilities/popper/src/get-placement.ts)
- `onPositioned({ placed: false })` fires on cleanup, so a consumer can distinguish a positioned floating element from a torn-down one. (zag: packages/utilities/popper/src/get-placement.ts)
- A virtual anchor is supported through `getAnchorRect`, which is wrapped into a floating-ui `VirtualElement` whose `getBoundingClientRect` returns a synthesized rect; the synthesized rect falls back to a hand-rolled object with a `toJSON` when `DOMRect` is not a constructor (older or non-browser environments). (zag: packages/utilities/popper/src/get-anchor.ts)
- The arrow middleware always runs: when no `[data-part=arrow]` element exists, a throwaway detached `div` is created so floating-ui's `arrow` has something to measure. (zag: packages/utilities/popper/src/get-placement.ts)
- The arrow element is positioned by writing inline `left`/`top` from the arrow middleware data and setting the placement-side property to `calc(100% + var(--arrow-offset))`, which pushes the arrow outside the floating box on the anchor side. (zag: packages/utilities/popper/src/middleware.ts)

### Animation and presence

- Before any placement is computed, the floating styles set `pointer-events: none` and `transform: translate3d(0, -100vh, 0)`, parking the element off-screen so an unpositioned popper cannot flash at the top-left corner or intercept clicks. (zag: packages/utilities/popper/src/get-styles.ts)
- Adjacent transform origin is computed per side so a scale animation grows out of the arrow: `top` gets `<arrowCenterX>px calc(100% + <offset>px)`, `bottom` gets `<arrowCenterX>px -<offset>px`, `left` gets `calc(100% + <offset>px) <arrowCenterY>px`, and `right` gets `-<offset>px <arrowCenterY>px`. (zag: packages/utilities/popper/src/middleware.ts)
- When `overlap` is on, the side axis is vertical, and the absolute shift on y exceeds the side offset (so the floating element now covers the anchor), the transform origin switches to the anchor's vertical center instead of the arrow. (zag: packages/utilities/popper/src/middleware.ts)

### Notes and edge cases

- `getPlacement(reference, floating, { defer })` wraps the whole setup in a `requestAnimationFrame` when `defer` is set, and returns a cleanup that runs both the frame cancel and the inner teardown. (zag: packages/utilities/popper/src/get-placement.ts)
- Both the anchor and the floating element may be passed as getters and are re-resolved on every update, and `opts.getAnchorElement?.()` takes precedence over the positional anchor argument. (zag: packages/utilities/popper/src/get-placement.ts)
- `updatePosition` returns early without positioning when the floating element is missing, and again when neither an anchor nor a `getAnchorRect` resolves a reference. (zag: packages/utilities/popper/src/get-placement.ts)
- The `rects` middleware exists only to surface floating-ui's reference and floating rects as middleware data for consumers. (zag: packages/utilities/popper/src/middleware.ts)
- Every CSS variable name is declared once in `middleware.ts` via a `toVar` helper that pairs the `--name` with its `var(--name)` reference, so the variable and reference spellings cannot drift. (zag: packages/utilities/popper/src/middleware.ts)

## live-region

### Roles and attributes

- This utility ships no tests at all: `packages/utilities/live-region` has only `src`, no `tests` directory, so everything below is read from source. (zag: packages/utilities/live-region/src/index.ts)
- Each announcement creates a fresh `<span>` with the fixed id `__live-region__` and `data-live-announcer="true"`. (zag: packages/utilities/live-region/src/index.ts)
- The region gets `aria-live` set to the configured level (`polite` by default) and a redundant `role`: `status` for polite, `alert` for assertive. (zag: packages/utilities/live-region/src/index.ts)
- The region is visually hidden with inline styles `border: 0`, `clip: rect(0 0 0 0)`, `height: 1px`, `margin: -1px`, `overflow: hidden`, `padding: 0`, `position: absolute`, `width: 1px`, `white-space: nowrap`, `word-wrap: normal`. (zag: packages/utilities/live-region/src/index.ts)
- The region is appended to the configured `root` element, falling back to `document.body`. (zag: packages/utilities/live-region/src/index.ts)
- `debug: true` additionally creates a visible overlay with id `__live-region-debug__`, `data-live-announcer-debug="true"` and `aria-hidden="true"`, pinned to the bottom of the viewport with `position: fixed`, `z-index: 2147483647` and `pointer-events: none`, and mirrors each message into it. (zag: packages/utilities/live-region/src/index.ts)

### Accessibility tooling

- `announce(message, delay)` removes any existing `__live-region__` node first and appends a brand-new one, which is the trick that makes screen readers re-announce an identical message. (zag: packages/utilities/live-region/src/index.ts)
- The message text is written in a `setTimeout` after the region is appended (delay defaults to 0, overridable per call), so the region exists in the accessibility tree before its content changes. (zag: packages/utilities/live-region/src/index.ts)
- The deferred write checks `region.isConnected` first and does nothing if the region was removed in the meantime, so a destroyed announcer cannot resurrect text. (zag: packages/utilities/live-region/src/index.ts)
- `destroy()` removes both the live region and the debug region if either is present. (zag: packages/utilities/live-region/src/index.ts)
- The returned object's `toJSON()` returns the id string `__live-region__`, which keeps a live region stored in machine context from bloating serialized state snapshots. (zag: packages/utilities/live-region/src/index.ts)
- The timer comes from the target document's own `defaultView` (falling back to the global `window`), so an announcer created for an iframe document schedules on that iframe's window. (zag: packages/utilities/live-region/src/index.ts)
- The fixed ids mean one live region per document: a second `createLiveRegion` announcing into the same document reuses and replaces the same `__live-region__` node rather than adding a second one. (zag: packages/utilities/live-region/src/index.ts)

## dom-query

### Roles and attributes

- `getInitialFocus` reads three author attributes: `[data-autofocus]` and `[autofocus]` opt an element in, and `[data-no-autofocus]` opts it out. (zag: packages/utilities/dom-query/src/initial-focus.ts)

### Keyboard

- Given a trigger followed by portalled content at the end of the body, and focus on the last item in that content, when Tab is pressed, then `onFocus` is not called and focus stays on the last item, so tabbing out of portalled content does not loop back into it. (zag: packages/utilities/dom-query/tests/proxy-tab-focus.test.ts: "does not loop into portalled content when the trigger is the last page tabbable")
- Given a trigger, a following page button, and portalled content after both, and focus on the last content item, when Tab is pressed, then `onFocus` is called with the page button after the trigger and focus lands there, not on whatever follows the portal in DOM order. (zag: packages/utilities/dom-query/tests/proxy-tab-focus.test.ts: "tabs from the last content item to the next tabbable after the trigger")
- Given focus on the page button that follows the trigger, when Shift+Tab is pressed, then `onFocus` is called with the last item inside the portalled content and focus lands there. (zag: packages/utilities/dom-query/tests/proxy-tab-focus.test.ts: "shift+tabs from the next after trigger into the last content item")
- Given focus on the trigger, when Tab is pressed, then `onFocus` is called with the first item in the portalled content and focus lands there. (zag: packages/utilities/dom-query/tests/proxy-tab-focus.test.ts: "tabs from the trigger into the first content item")
- Given the container and trigger are passed as getters that resolve to nothing at setup time, when the content mounts later and Tab is pressed from its last item, then the getters are resolved on the keydown and focus moves to the button after the trigger. (zag: packages/utilities/dom-query/tests/proxy-tab-focus.test.ts: "resolves container and trigger getters on keydown")
- `proxyTabFocus` installs a single capture-phase `keydown` on the document, ignores every key but Tab, calls `event.preventDefault()` only once it has a destination, and falls back to `elementToFocus.focus()` when no `onFocus` callback is supplied. (zag: packages/utilities/dom-query/src/proxy-tab-focus.ts)
- When the content has no tabbable elements at all, both Tab and Shift+Tab still redirect (to the next tabbable after the trigger, and to the trigger respectively), so an empty popover does not trap the user. (zag: packages/utilities/dom-query/src/proxy-tab-focus.ts)
- `onFocusEnter` fires only on the two entering transitions (Tab from the trigger into the content, and Shift+Tab from the element after the trigger back into the content), never on the exiting ones; no test covers it. (zag: packages/utilities/dom-query/src/proxy-tab-focus.ts)
- The edge lookup uses `getTabbableEdges(content, { includeContainer: true })`, so a container that is itself tabbable counts as its own first or last stop. (zag: packages/utilities/dom-query/src/proxy-tab-focus.ts)
- `isValidTabEvent` reports false when the active element is the container's first tabbable and Shift is held, when it is the last tabbable and Shift is not held, and when the container has no tabbable edges at all; it ships with no test. (zag: packages/utilities/dom-query/src/initial-focus.ts)

### Focus management

- Given `enabled: false`, when `getInitialFocus` runs, then it returns `undefined` and nothing is chosen. (zag: packages/utilities/dom-query/tests/initial-focus.test.ts: "returns undefined when disabled")
- Given a `getInitialEl` returning the second button, when `getInitialFocus` runs, then it returns that button, so the explicit override beats every other rule. (zag: packages/utilities/dom-query/tests/initial-focus.test.ts: "prefers getInitialEl when provided")
- Given the second button carries `data-autofocus`, when `getInitialFocus` runs, then it returns the second button rather than the first tabbable. (zag: packages/utilities/dom-query/tests/initial-focus.test.ts: "prefers data-autofocus over first tabbable")
- Given a close button and a help button both carrying `data-no-autofocus` ahead of a submit button, when `getInitialFocus` runs, then it returns the submit button. (zag: packages/utilities/dom-query/tests/initial-focus.test.ts: "skips elements with data-no-autofocus")
- Given one element carrying both `data-no-autofocus` and `data-autofocus`, when `getInitialFocus` runs, then it returns that element, so the opt-in wins over the opt-out. (zag: packages/utilities/dom-query/tests/initial-focus.test.ts: "lets data-autofocus win over data-no-autofocus")
- Given every tabbable in the root carries `data-no-autofocus`, when `getInitialFocus` runs, then it returns the root element itself. (zag: packages/utilities/dom-query/tests/initial-focus.test.ts: "falls back to root when every tabbable has data-no-autofocus")
- Given a root with no tabbable children at all, when `getInitialFocus` runs, then it returns the root element itself. (zag: packages/utilities/dom-query/tests/initial-focus.test.ts: "falls back to root when there are no tabbables")
- Given a `filter` rejecting anything whose role starts with `menuitem`, when `getInitialFocus` runs over a `role="menuitem"` button followed by a plain button, then it returns the plain button. (zag: packages/utilities/dom-query/tests/initial-focus.test.ts: "respects the filter option")
- The resolution order is fixed: explicit `getInitialEl`, then `[data-autofocus],[autofocus]` by `querySelector`, then the first filtered tabbable without `data-no-autofocus`, then the root, then `undefined`; note the `filter` option applies only to the third step, not to the `data-autofocus` lookup. (zag: packages/utilities/dom-query/src/initial-focus.ts)

### SSR and hydration

- Given `defer` is off and a mounted node, when `whenNode` is called, then `fn` runs synchronously with that node. (zag: packages/utilities/dom-query/tests/when-node.test.ts: "runs synchronously when defer is off")
- Given `defer: true` and a getter that currently returns a node the framework is about to replace, when the old node is removed, a new one mounted, and a microtask elapses, then `fn` runs exactly once and receives the newly committed node, not the doomed one. (zag: packages/utilities/dom-query/tests/when-node.test.ts: "waits for the commit even when a node already exists")
- Given `defer: true` and a getter returning null at call time, when the node mounts and a microtask elapses, then `fn` runs with that node. (zag: packages/utilities/dom-query/tests/when-node.test.ts: "runs on the microtask tick when the node commits after the call")
- Given `defer: true` and a node still missing at the microtask, when it mounts and a frame elapses, then `fn` runs with it, confirming the frame is a second-chance fallback after the microtask. (zag: packages/utilities/dom-query/tests/when-node.test.ts: "falls back to a frame when the node is still missing at the microtask")
- Given a getter that never returns a node, when both a microtask and a frame elapse, then `fn` is never called and `onMissing` is called exactly once. (zag: packages/utilities/dom-query/tests/when-node.test.ts: "never calls fn without a node, and reports via onMissing")
- Given `defer` is off and an absent node, when `whenNode` is called, then `fn` is not called and `onMissing` fires immediately. (zag: packages/utilities/dom-query/tests/when-node.test.ts: "calls onMissing immediately when not deferred and the node is absent")
- Given `defer: true` and cleanup called before the node commits, when the node mounts and both a microtask and a frame elapse, then `fn` is never called. (zag: packages/utilities/dom-query/tests/when-node.test.ts: "cleanup cancels pending work before the node commits")
- Given `fn` returned an inner cleanup, when the outer cleanup is called, then the inner cleanup runs exactly once, and not before. (zag: packages/utilities/dom-query/tests/when-node.test.ts: "cleanup runs the cleanup returned by fn")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given a stubbed navigator reporting platform `Linux x86_64` and a Firefox X11 user agent, when `isLinux()` is called, then it is true. (zag: packages/utilities/dom-query/tests/platform.test.ts: "should detect desktop linux")
- Given a stubbed navigator reporting platform `Linux x86_64` and a `CrOS x86_64` Chrome user agent, when `isLinux()` is called, then it is true, so ChromeOS counts as Linux. (zag: packages/utilities/dom-query/tests/platform.test.ts: "should detect chrome os")
- Given a stubbed navigator whose `userAgentData.platform` is `Chrome OS`, when `isLinux()` is called, then it is true, so the modern `userAgentData` spelling with a space is matched as well as `CrOS`. (zag: packages/utilities/dom-query/tests/platform.test.ts: "should detect chrome os via userAgentData")
- Given a stubbed navigator whose `userAgentData.platform` is `Android` (with a `Linux armv81` legacy platform and 5 touch points), when `isLinux()` is called, then it is false. (zag: packages/utilities/dom-query/tests/platform.test.ts: "should exclude android via userAgentData")
- Given a stubbed navigator reporting platform `Linux armv8l` and an `Android 14; Pixel 8` user agent, when the platform helpers run, then `isLinux()` is false and `isAndroid()` is true. (zag: packages/utilities/dom-query/tests/platform.test.ts: "should exclude android")
- Given stubbed navigators for macOS (`MacIntel`, Safari user agent) and Windows (`Win32`, Chrome user agent), when the platform helpers run, then `isLinux()` is false for both and `isMac()` is true for the mac stub. (zag: packages/utilities/dom-query/tests/platform.test.ts: "should be false on mac and windows")
- `getPlatform()` prefers `navigator.userAgentData.platform` and falls back to the deprecated `navigator.platform`; `getUserAgent()` prefers a synthesized `brand/version` string built from `userAgentData.brands` and falls back to `navigator.userAgent`. (zag: packages/utilities/dom-query/src/platform.ts)
- iPad detection has a Safari-specific branch: `isIPad()` is true when the platform starts with `iPad` or when the platform is Mac and `navigator.maxTouchPoints > 1`, which is how desktop-mode iPadOS Safari is caught. (zag: packages/utilities/dom-query/src/platform.ts)
- `isSafari()` requires an Apple platform and an `apple` vendor string, and `isWebKit()` requires an `AppleWebKit` user agent while explicitly excluding Chrome; only `isLinux`, `isAndroid` and `isMac` are covered by tests, so `isSafari`, `isWebKit`, `isFirefox`, `isChrome`, `isIPhone`, `isIPad`, `isIos`, `isApple` and `isTouchDevice` are all unverified. (zag: packages/utilities/dom-query/src/platform.ts; zag: packages/utilities/dom-query/tests/platform.test.ts)
- Every helper is guarded by `isDom()` (a `typeof document !== "undefined"` check) and returns false outside the browser, which is what keeps them safe to call during SSR. (zag: packages/utilities/dom-query/src/platform.ts)
- The `proxyTabFocus` and `getInitialFocus` suites both stub `offsetWidth`, `offsetHeight` and `getClientRects` on every element through a local `markVisible` helper, because jsdom reports zero layout for everything and the tabbable scan would otherwise find no candidates. (zag: packages/utilities/dom-query/tests/proxy-tab-focus.test.ts; zag: packages/utilities/dom-query/tests/initial-focus.test.ts)
- `getNextTabbableAfterTrigger` scans the whole `document.body` tabbable list, finds the trigger's index, and returns the first later tabbable that is not inside the content container, returning null when the trigger itself is not in the list. (zag: packages/utilities/dom-query/src/proxy-tab-focus.ts)

## date-utils

### Roles and attributes

- The package exports no DOM parts; it is a pure calendar-math layer over `@internationalized/date` whose `DateValue` is `CalendarDate | CalendarDateTime | ZonedDateTime`. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/src/index.ts; zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/src/types.ts)
- Week and month grid API: `getStartOfWeek(date, locale, firstDayOfWeek?)` and `getEndOfWeek` map a numeric `firstDayOfWeek` (0=sun through 6=sat) onto the `@internationalized/date` day names, `getDaysInWeek(weekIndex, from, locale, firstDayOfWeek?)` returns exactly 7 consecutive days starting at that week's start, `getMonthDays(from, locale, numOfWeeks?, firstDayOfWeek?)` returns an array of week rows (defaulting to `getWeeksInMonth`), `getWeekDays(date, startOfWeekProp, timeZone, locale)` returns the 7 weekday header cells, `getWeekdayFormats(locale, timeZone)` builds a formatter returning `{ value, short, long, narrow }`, `getMonthNames(locale, format?, referenceDate?)` returns month labels, and `getWeekOfYear(date, locale)` returns the ISO 8601 week number. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/src/date-month.ts)
- Year API: `getYearsRange({ from, to })` expands an inclusive year list, `getDefaultYearRange(referenceDate, min?, max?)` defaults to Gregorian 1900-2099 converted into the reference date's calendar, `normalizeYear(year)` expands partial year strings, and `getDecadeRange(year)` returns the 10 years of the containing decade. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/src/date-year.ts)
- Constraint API: `constrainValue(date, min?, max?)` clamps the whole date to the range, while `constrainSegments(date, min?, max?)` clamps only the out-of-range year, then month, then day, so later segments survive; both return the original object identity when no change is needed and re-apply the clamped date onto the original type so time and time zone are kept. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/src/constrain.ts)
- Equality API: `isDateEqual(a, b)` compares by day when neither side has an `hour`, otherwise by `CalendarDateTime` comparison, and short-circuits nullish operands with a strict `===` so `null` and `undefined` are not interchangeable. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/src/assertion.ts)
- Formatting API: `formatSelectedDate(start, end, locale, timeZone)` and `formatVisibleRange(start, end, locale, timeZone)` build labels through `getDayFormatter`/`getMonthFormatter`, which pass `era: getEraFormat(date)` and `calendar: date.calendar.identifier` into `Intl.DateTimeFormat`. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/src/format.ts; zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/src/formatter.ts)
- Era API: `getEraFormat(date)` returns `"short"` for every non-Gregorian, non-ISO calendar and for Gregorian dates whose `era` is `"BC"`, and `undefined` for ordinary AD Gregorian dates, so BC dates and Persian/Buddhist/Japanese dates render an era designator while modern Gregorian dates do not. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/src/get-era-format.ts)
- Pagination API: `getNextPage`/`getPreviousPage` shift the visible duration and realign the start date, `getNextRow`/`getPreviousRow`, `getSectionStart`/`getSectionEnd`, and `getNextSection`/`getPreviousSection` move the focused date within a page; all funnel through `getAdjustedDateFn`, which constrains the focused date and realigns the start date when focus escapes the visible window. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/src/pagination.ts)
- Locale input API: `isValidCharacter(char, separator, locale?)`, `ensureValidCharacters(value, separator, locale?)`, and `getLocaleSeparator(locale)` gate typed characters in date fields; `parseDateString(date, locale, timeZone)` parses a partially typed string using a regex derived from the locale's numeric date parts; `getDateRangePreset(preset, locale, timeZone)` resolves named ranges such as `thisQuarter` and `lastYear`. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/src/locale.ts; zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/src/parse-date.ts; zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/src/preset.ts)

### RTL and i18n

- Given the default `en` locale and a reference date of Wednesday 2024-08-21, when `getWeekDays` is called with no explicit `weekStartDay`, then the first column is Sunday 2024-08-18, matching the locale's own week start. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/get-start-of-week.test.ts: "en locale")
- Given the `en` locale, when `weekStartDay` is passed explicitly as 0 then the first column is 2024-08-18 and when it is 1 then the first column is Monday 2024-08-19, so the explicit prop overrides locale resolution. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/get-start-of-week.test.ts: "en locale")
- Given the `fr` locale and the same reference date, when `getWeekDays` is called with no explicit `weekStartDay`, then the first column is Monday 2024-08-19, so week start is resolved per locale rather than hardcoded to Sunday. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/get-start-of-week.test.ts: "fr locale")
- Given the `fr` locale, when `weekStartDay` is 0, 1, or 2, then the first column is 2024-08-18, 2024-08-19, or Tuesday 2024-08-20 respectively, so the explicit prop also overrides a non-Sunday locale default. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/get-start-of-week.test.ts: "fr locale")
- Given locale `en` and time zone `UTC`, when `getWeekdayFormats` formats CalendarDate 2020-01-01, then it returns `long: "Wednesday"`, `short: "Wed"`, `narrow: "W"`, and echoes the original `value` carrying calendar identifier `gregory` and era `AD`. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/get-weekday-formats.test.ts: "getWeekdayFormats")
- Given locale `en-US`, time zone `UTC`, and the date 2023-01-10, when `getWeekDays` runs with an undefined start-of-week, then it returns seven entries from Sunday 2023-01-08 through Saturday 2023-01-14, each with long, short, and narrow labels, and the narrow labels collide (`S` for both Saturday and Sunday, `T` for both Tuesday and Thursday) so narrow labels alone cannot identify a column. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/get-week-days.test.ts: "should get week dates")
- Given locale `en`, when `getMonthNames` is called with no format, then it returns the twelve long English month names from January to December. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/get-month-names.test.ts: "en / returns the list of month names")
- Given locale `en` and format `"short"`, when `getMonthNames` runs, then it returns Jan through Dec. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/get-month-names.test.ts: "en / returns the list of month names in short format")
- Given locale `ru`, when `getMonthNames` runs with the default long format, then it returns the Russian nominative lowercase month names январь through декабрь, confirming the labels come from `Intl` rather than a bundled English table; the test name says "numeric format" but no numeric format is exercised. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/get-month-names.test.ts: "en / returns the list of month names in numeric format")
- Given locale `fa-IR` and a reference date converted into `PersianCalendar`, when `getMonthNames` runs, then it returns 12 names, the first is not "January", and the first contains فروردین (Farvardin), so month labels follow the reference date's calendar system and not the Gregorian months. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/get-month-names.test.ts: "fa-IR / returns Persian month names when given a Persian referenceDate")
- Given locale `en` and a Gregorian reference date, when `getMonthNames` runs, then it returns 12 months starting at "January", so passing a Gregorian reference date takes the same path as passing none. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/get-month-names.test.ts: "en / returns 12 Gregorian months when referenceDate is Gregorian")
- Given a Gregorian reference date 2024-06-15, when `getDefaultYearRange` runs with no min or max, then the range is exactly `{ from: 1900, to: 2099 }`. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/year-range.test.ts: "getDefaultYearRange returns 1900-2099 for Gregorian")
- Given a reference date converted to `PersianCalendar`, when `getDefaultYearRange` runs, then the default Gregorian bounds are converted into Persian years so `from` lands between 1200 and 1900 and `to` lands below 1500, confirming the bounds are calendar-relative rather than literal numbers. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/year-range.test.ts: "getDefaultYearRange converts to target calendar years")
- Given explicit min 2000-01-01 and max 2050-12-31, when `getDefaultYearRange` runs, then the range is `{ from: 2000, to: 2050 }`, so explicit bounds win over the calendar-converted defaults. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/year-range.test.ts: "getDefaultYearRange respects min/max")
- Given locale `en-US` and time zone `UTC`, when `formatSelectedDate` formats the single date 2023-01-10, then the label is "Tuesday, January 10, 2023" with weekday, long month, numeric day, and numeric year, and no era designator for an AD Gregorian date. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/format.test.ts: "formatSelectedDate / selected date")
- Given start 2023-01-10 and end 2023-01-12, when `formatSelectedDate` formats the range, then the label is "Tuesday, January 10 – Thursday, January 12, 2023", with the shared year lifted out of the start side by the `formatRangeToParts` splitting logic. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/format.test.ts: "formatSelectedDate / selected date")
- Given a start date that is not the first of its month, when `formatVisibleRange` formats 2023-01-10 through 2023-01-12, then it falls through to the day formatter's range output "Tuesday, January 10 – Thursday, January 12, 2023" rather than a month-level label. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/format.test.ts: "formatVisibleRange / visible range")
- Given separator `"/"` and no locale, when `isValidCharacter` is given the digits "5" or "0", then it returns true; and with separator ". " the digit "0" is also accepted. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/locale.test.ts: "accepts digits")
- Given a single-character separator, when `isValidCharacter` is given that same character ("/" with "/", "." with ".", "-" with "-"), then it returns true. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/locale.test.ts: "accepts single-char separator")
- Given separator `"/"`, when `isValidCharacter` is given "a" or "!", then it returns false. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/locale.test.ts: "rejects non-digit, non-separator characters")
- Given the cs-CZ multi-character separator ". ", when `isValidCharacter` is given either "." or " ", then both are accepted because membership is tested per character of the separator string; this is called out in the test as a cs-CZ regression. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/locale.test.ts: "accepts each character of a multi-char separator (cs-CZ regression)")
- Given the multi-character separator ". ", when `isValidCharacter` is given "a", then it still returns false, so widening the separator does not admit letters. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/locale.test.ts: "rejects letters even with multi-char separator")
- Given a `null` or empty-string char, when `isValidCharacter` runs, then it returns true, so absent input never blocks the field. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/locale.test.ts: "accepts null or empty char")
- Given multi-character input such as "20.10.2000", when `isValidCharacter` runs, then it returns true unconditionally because any string longer than one character is treated as a paste or IME commit and passed through unfiltered. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/locale.test.ts: "accepts multi-char data (paste/IME passthrough)")
- Given locales `en-US`, `ar-EG`, and `hi-IN-u-nu-deva`, when `isValidCharacter` is given the ASCII digit "5", then it is accepted in all three, so ASCII digits stay valid in every numbering system. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/locale.test.ts: "accepts ASCII digits in any locale")
- Given locale `ar-EG`, when `isValidCharacter` is given the Arabic-Indic digits ٥ (U+0665) or ٠ (U+0660), then they are accepted, so the locale's native numerals are typable. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/locale.test.ts: "accepts Arabic-Indic numerals in ar locale")
- Given locale `hi-IN-u-nu-deva`, when `isValidCharacter` is given the Devanagari digits ५ (U+096B) or ० (U+0966), then they are accepted. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/locale.test.ts: "accepts Devanagari numerals in hi deva locale")
- Given locale `bn-IN-u-nu-beng`, when `isValidCharacter` is given the Bengali digit ৫ (U+09EB), then it is accepted. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/locale.test.ts: "accepts Bengali numerals in bn beng locale")
- Given a locale, when `isValidCharacter` is given a digit from a different numbering system (Devanagari ५ in `en-US`, Arabic-Indic ٥ in `hi-IN-u-nu-deva`), then it returns false, so the allowed digit set is exactly ASCII plus the locale's own numerals. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/locale.test.ts: "rejects non-locale numerals when locale is provided")
- Given locales `ar-EG` and `hi-IN-u-nu-deva`, when `isValidCharacter` is given "a" or "!", then it returns false, so locale awareness does not loosen the letter and symbol rejection. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/locale.test.ts: "still rejects letters and symbols when locale is provided")
- Given no locale argument, when `isValidCharacter` is given ASCII "5" then it is accepted and Arabic-Indic ٥ is rejected, so the fallback path uses the ASCII-only `\d` test. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/locale.test.ts: "falls back to ASCII-only when no locale is given")
- Given locale `ar-EG` and separator "/", when `ensureValidCharacters` filters "٢٠/١٠/٢٠٠٠", then the string is returned unchanged with its Arabic-Indic numerals intact. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/locale.test.ts: "preserves Arabic-Indic numerals in ar locale")
- Given locale `en-US`, when `ensureValidCharacters` filters "0५1", then the Devanagari digit is stripped and the ASCII digits survive as "01". (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/locale.test.ts: "strips foreign numerals not in the locale's numbering system")
- Given the cs-CZ separator ". ", when `ensureValidCharacters` filters "20. 10. 2000", then the full string including the spaces is preserved; this is tracked as a regression test. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/locale.test.ts: "preserves full cs-CZ format with spaces (regression)")
- Given the cs-CZ separator ". ", when `ensureValidCharacters` filters the space-free short form "20.10.2000", then it is preserved unchanged. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/locale.test.ts: "preserves cs-CZ short form without spaces (regression)")
- Given separator ". ", when `ensureValidCharacters` filters "abc20.10", then the leading letters are dropped and "20.10" remains. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/locale.test.ts: "strips letters but keeps digits and separator chars")
- Given separator "/", when `ensureValidCharacters` filters "01/02/2024", then it is preserved unchanged. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/locale.test.ts: "preserves valid en-US format")
- Given separator "/", when `ensureValidCharacters` filters "20.10.2000", then every dot is stripped and the result is the run-together "20102000", so a locale mismatch between separator and typed text silently mangles the value rather than rejecting it. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/locale.test.ts: "strips dots when separator is slash")
- Given locale `en-US`, when `getLocaleSeparator` runs, then it returns "/". (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/locale.test.ts: "returns / for en-US")
- Given locale `cs-CZ`, when `getLocaleSeparator` runs, then it returns the two-character ". ", so the separator is not assumed to be a single character. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/locale.test.ts: "returns dot-space for cs-CZ")
- Given locale `de-AT`, when `getLocaleSeparator` runs, then it returns ".". (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/locale.test.ts: "returns dot for de-AT")
- Given locale `en-US` and the input "03", when `parseDateString` runs, then it yields month 3 with the day and year filled in from today's date, so a partially typed field resolves against the current date. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/parse-date.test.ts: "with month")
- Given locale `en-US` and the input "03/28", when `parseDateString` runs, then it yields month 3, day 28, and the current year. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/parse-date.test.ts: "with just month/day")
- Given locale `en-US` and the input "03/28/2023", when `parseDateString` runs, then it yields month 3, day 28, year 2023. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/parse-date.test.ts: "with just month/day/year")
- Given locale `en-US` and the two-digit year input "03/28/23", when `parseDateString` runs, then the year normalizes to 2023. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/parse-date.test.ts: "with just month/day/year [shortform]")
- Given locale `de-DE` and the input "10.1.23", when `parseDateString` runs, then it reads day-first to yield day 10, month 1, year 2023, so segment order follows the locale's numeric date pattern. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/parse-date.test.ts: "with just month/day/year [shortform - different locale]")
- Given locale `de-DE` and the malformed three-digit year input "10.1.293", when `parseDateString` runs, then the year is right-padded to 2930 rather than rejected. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/parse-date.test.ts: "with just month/day/year [malformed year - different locale]")
- Given locale `cs-CZ` and the input "20. 10. 2000" with dot-space separators, when `parseDateString` runs, then it yields day 20, month 10, year 2000. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/parse-date.test.ts: "cs-CZ full format with dot-space separators")
- Given locale `cs-CZ` and the space-free input "20.10.2000", when `parseDateString` runs, then it still yields day 20, month 10, year 2000, so the optional-literal regex tolerates a missing space. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/parse-date.test.ts: "cs-CZ short form without spaces")
- Given locale `sk-SK` and the input "20. 10. 2000", when `parseDateString` runs, then it yields day 20, month 10, year 2000. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/parse-date.test.ts: "sk-SK full format with dot-space separators")
- Given locale `en-US` and time zone `UTC`, when `getDateRangePreset("thisWeek")` runs on Thursday 2024-03-14, then the range is Sunday 2024-03-10 through Saturday 2024-03-16, so week boundaries come from the locale. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/preset.test.ts: "thisWeek")
- Given locale `en-US`, when `getDateRangePreset("lastWeek")` runs on 2024-03-14, then the range is the full previous locale week 2024-03-03 through 2024-03-09. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/preset.test.ts: "lastWeek")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given a two-digit year string "23", when `normalizeYear` runs, then it returns "2023" by attaching the current century, and any result more than 10 years in the future is pushed back a century. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/normalize-year.test.ts: "with 2 digits"; zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/src/date-year.ts)
- Given a three-digit year string "123", when `normalizeYear` runs, then it returns "1230" by right-padding with a zero rather than interpreting it as year 123. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/normalize-year.test.ts: "with 3 digits")
- Given an already four-digit year "2023", when `normalizeYear` runs, then it is returned unchanged. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/normalize-year.test.ts: "with 4 digits")
- Given January 4 of 2023 and of 2024, when `getWeekOfYear` runs with locale `en`, then both return 1, pinning the ISO 8601 rule that Jan 4 always falls in week 1 regardless of weekday. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/get-week-of-year.test.ts: "returns 1 for Jan 4 (always in week 1 per ISO 8601)")
- Given 2023-01-02, when `getWeekOfYear` runs, then it returns 1. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/get-week-of-year.test.ts: "returns week 1 for a date in the first week of the year")
- Given 2023-12-31, when `getWeekOfYear` runs, then the result is asserted only to be between 52 and 53 inclusive, so the exact year-end week number is deliberately left loose. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/get-week-of-year.test.ts: "returns 52 or 53 for last days of December")
- Given the year 2023, when `getDecadeRange` runs, then it returns 2020 through 2029. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/get-decade-range.test.ts: "returns the ten years of the decade")
- Given any year inside a decade, when `getDecadeRange` runs, then the output is anchored to the decade start: 2020 and 2029 produce identical arrays and 2030 produces an array beginning at 2030. (zag: packages/utilities/date-utils/tests/get-decade-range.test.ts: "is anchored to the decade, not the year passed in")
