### Focus management

- Given a store tracking a held key, when the window fires blur, then pressedKeys and pressedCodes are both emptied so a key held while the window loses focus does not stay stuck. (zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/tests/store.test.ts: "clears pressedCodes on blur")
- Given a store listening on a target, when the window fires either blur or contextmenu, then pressed keys, pressed codes, the fired-command set and all in-progress sequences are cleared; contextmenu is handled because opening a native context menu swallows the matching keyup. (zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/src/store.ts)
- Given a command with options.target set to an element, when the keyboard event originates outside that element, then the command is skipped; the target must contain focus to see the event at all. (zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/tests/store.test.ts: "should fire targeted commands only when the event originates within the target"; zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/src/types.ts)

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given a store created with defaultOptions { capture: false, enableOnContentEditable: true }, when a command registers with no options of its own, then it inherits both defaults while keeping the built-in preventDefault true. (zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/tests/store.test.ts: "applies store-level default options during registration")
- Given a store with those same defaults, when a command registers with its own capture and enableOnContentEditable, then the command values win over the store defaults. (zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/tests/store.test.ts: "lets command-level options override store defaults")
- Given a command registered before init(), when init() later supplies defaultOptions { capture: false }, then the already-registered command is re-resolved and picks up the new default, so registration order relative to init does not matter. (zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/tests/store.test.ts: "re-applies defaults to commands registered before init")
- Given a store with the hotkey "Q" registered, when the physical KeyQ is pressed on a layout that produces "a", then isPressed("Q") is true and getPressedCodes contains "KeyQ", so pressed-state queries are layout independent through the code path. (zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/tests/store.test.ts: "matches physical code when logical key differs (layout-independent letter)")
- Given a sequence hotkey such as "a>b", when isPressed is asked about it, then the answer is always false because a sequence is progressive and "all keys held at once" does not apply. (zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/tests/store.test.ts: "returns false for key sequences (not a chord)")
- Given the symbol hotkey "/" and Control held while "/" is pressed, when isPressed("/") is read, then it is false, so isPressed applies the same modifier strictness as chord matching. (zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/tests/store.test.ts: "for symbol hotkeys, rejects extra Control (matches chord semantics)")
- Given a store with a command registered, when a modifier key such as Shift is pressed on its own, then isPressed("shift") is true and getCurrentlyPressed contains "Shift". (zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/tests/store.test.ts: "should report a held modifier via isPressed")
- Given a store with no commands registered at all but with a subscriber attached, when Shift is pressed, then the subscriber fires and getCurrentlyPressed reports ["Shift"], so key-state tracking works without any command; the store falls back to attaching a capture listener for subscriber-only use. (zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/tests/store.test.ts: "should track pressed keys with no commands registered"; zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/src/store.ts)
- Given a command registered with enabled false, when the hotkey is pressed then nothing happens, and after enable(id) the same hotkey fires the action once. (zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/tests/store.test.ts: "should fire a command enabled after being registered as disabled")
- Given a store with an active subscriber, when destroy() is called, then all listeners detach, state.listening is false and getCurrentlyPressed stays empty for later key events; subscribers are cleared before clear() so clear() cannot restart listening. (zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/tests/store.test.ts: "should detach all listeners on destroy even with active subscribers"; zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/src/store.ts)
- Given a subscriber that caused a capture-phase listener to attach, when a command with capture false is registered afterwards, then the store re-attaches so a bubble-phase listener also exists and the command fires. (zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/tests/store.test.ts: "should fire a bubble-phase command registered after a subscriber")
- Given a command with options.target set to a grid element, when the event comes from a button outside the grid then nothing fires, and when it comes from a button inside the grid then the action fires once. (zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/tests/store.test.ts: "should fire targeted commands only when the event originates within the target")
- Given a command whose options.target is a function, when the function returns null then the command is skipped on that event, and when it later returns an element containing the event target then the action fires; the function is re-resolved on every event. (zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/tests/store.test.ts: "should skip a command while its target resolves to null")
- Given a command targeted at a shadow host and a composed event dispatched from inside the shadow root, when the event is evaluated, then containment is decided from event.composedPath() so the command fires across the shadow boundary. (zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/tests/store.test.ts: "should match containment across shadow boundaries"; zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/src/utils.ts)
- Given a global command and a target-scoped command on the same hotkey with conflictBehavior "allow", when the event originates inside the target then only the scoped action runs, and when it originates outside then only the global action runs, because a target adds 100 to the command priority and only the highest-priority tier executes. (zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/tests/store.test.ts: "should prefer a targeted command over a global one on the same hotkey"; zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/src/store.ts)
- Given the same hotkey registered once globally and once with a target, when both register, then no conflict warning is logged, and registering a second global command on that hotkey does warn exactly once, so conflict detection compares the target as part of the identity. (zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/tests/store.test.ts: "should not warn when the same hotkey is registered on different targets")
- Given an in-progress sequence "g > h" scoped to "a" with g already pressed, when the scope is removed and re-added and h is then pressed, then the action does not fire, because every scope mutation (setScope, addScope, removeScope, toggleScope) clears all sequence state. (zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/tests/store.test.ts: "should reset in-progress sequences when scopes change"; zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/src/store.ts)
- Given a store whose activeScopes is ["reader"], a command scoped to ["editor"] and an unscoped command, when the editor hotkey is pressed then nothing fires, and when the global hotkey is pressed then it fires once, because an unscoped command defaults to scope "*" which always matches. (ark: packages/react/src/providers/hotkeys/hotkeys.test.tsx: "should only fire commands within an active scope"; ark: packages/solid/src/providers/hotkeys/hotkeys.test.tsx: "should only fire commands within an active scope"; ark: packages/svelte/src/lib/providers/hotkeys/hotkeys.test.ts: "should only fire commands within the active scope")
- Given useHotkeys registering two commands with labels and categories, when useHotkeyRegistrations is read, then it lists each command's id, hotkey string as written (not normalized), label and category. (ark: packages/react/src/providers/hotkeys/hotkeys.test.tsx: "should expose registered commands with their metadata"; ark: packages/solid/src/providers/hotkeys/hotkeys.test.tsx: "should expose registered commands with their metadata")
- Given a child component that registers one hotkey, when the child unmounts, then useHotkeyRegistrations in the parent drops back to zero entries. (ark: packages/react/src/providers/hotkeys/hotkeys.test.tsx: "should update when a command unregisters"; ark: packages/solid/src/providers/hotkeys/hotkeys.test.tsx: "should update when a command unregisters")
- Given a React component reading useHotkeyRegistrations, when an unrelated prop changes or a registered hotkey fires, then the returned array is referentially identical to the previous one, because the snapshot is cached against a version string built from each command's id, hotkey and label. (ark: packages/react/src/providers/hotkeys/hotkeys.test.tsx: "should return a stable reference while commands are unchanged"; ark: packages/react/src/providers/hotkeys/use-store-snapshot.ts)
- Given useHotkeys called with an empty commands array, when the component renders, then nothing registers and the registration count is zero. (ark: packages/react/src/providers/hotkeys/hotkeys.test.tsx: "should treat an empty command list as a no-op")
- Given useHotkeys whose commands array grows then shrinks across renders, when each render settles, then the registration count tracks 1, 2, 1 as commands are added and removed. (ark: packages/react/src/providers/hotkeys/hotkeys.test.tsx: "should handle commands being added and removed")
- Given the Solid equivalent where commands come from an accessor reading a signal, when the signal toggles, then the registration count tracks 1, 2, 1; Solid takes a MaybeAccessor of props where React takes a plain object re-read each render. (ark: packages/solid/src/providers/hotkeys/hotkeys.test.tsx: "should react to an accessor of commands")
- Given a command whose enabled flag toggles between renders, when it flips from false to true, then the same single registration id stays on the store rather than being unregistered and re-registered. (ark: packages/react/src/providers/hotkeys/hotkeys.test.tsx: "should keep a single registration when toggling enabled")
- Given useHotkey with a reactive enabled option, when enabled is false the hotkey does nothing, and after it flips to true the hotkey fires once. (ark: packages/react/src/providers/hotkeys/hotkeys.test.tsx: "should respect the enabled option"; ark: packages/solid/src/providers/hotkeys/hotkeys.test.tsx: "should respect a reactive enabled option")
- Given two commands where only one command's label changes, when the render settles, then only the changed command's _registrationOrder advances and the untouched command keeps its original order, so reconciliation is per command and field by field. (ark: packages/react/src/providers/hotkeys/hotkeys.test.tsx: "should not re-register commands that did not change"; ark: packages/solid/src/providers/hotkeys/hotkeys.test.tsx: "should not re-register commands that did not change")
- Given a component that re-renders for an unrelated reason, when the render settles, then the registered command's _registrationOrder is unchanged. (ark: packages/react/src/providers/hotkeys/hotkeys.test.tsx: "should not re-register when an unrelated render occurs")
- Given a command whose hotkey prop changes from "ctrl+k" to "Control+K", when the render settles, then _registrationOrder is unchanged because the reconciler compares normalizeHotkey output rather than the raw string. (ark: packages/react/src/providers/hotkeys/hotkeys.test.tsx: "should treat equivalent hotkey spellings as unchanged"; ark: packages/solid/src/providers/hotkeys/hotkeys.test.tsx: "should treat equivalent hotkey spellings as unchanged")
- Given two components that both call useHotkey without naming a store, when each registers, then both land on one module-level default store created lazily on first use, and after one component unmounts its command no longer fires while the other's still does. (ark: packages/react/src/providers/hotkeys/hotkeys.test.tsx: "should fall back to a shared store"; ark: packages/react/src/providers/hotkeys/use-hotkey-store.ts)
- Given a store with conflictBehavior "allow" and two commands on "ctrl+k", when both register, then both ids stay registered. (ark: packages/react/src/providers/hotkeys/hotkeys-options.test.tsx: "should keep both registrations when allowed"; ark: packages/solid/src/providers/hotkeys/hotkeys-options.test.tsx: "should keep both registrations when allowed")
- Given a store with conflictBehavior "replace" and two commands on "ctrl+k", when both register, then only the later id survives and the earlier one is dropped. (ark: packages/react/src/providers/hotkeys/hotkeys-options.test.tsx: "should drop the earlier registration when replacing"; ark: packages/solid/src/providers/hotkeys/hotkeys-options.test.tsx: "should drop the earlier registration when replacing"; ark: packages/svelte/src/lib/providers/hotkeys/hotkeys.test.ts: "should drop the earlier registration when replacing")
- Given a store with the default conflictBehavior, when two commands claim "ctrl+k", then console.warn is called and both registrations are kept. (ark: packages/react/src/providers/hotkeys/hotkeys-options.test.tsx: "should warn but keep both by default"; ark: packages/solid/src/providers/hotkeys/hotkeys-options.test.tsx: "should warn but keep both by default"; ark: packages/svelte/src/lib/providers/hotkeys/hotkeys.test.ts: "should keep both registrations by default")
- Given conflictBehavior "error", when a second command claims a hotkey already registered with the same target, then register() throws instead of warning; this branch has no test. (zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/src/store.ts)
- Given a store with a command registered, when a subscriber's selector output is unchanged by an event, then its callback is not invoked, because notifySubscribers compares the selected value by identity against the last one. (zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/src/store.ts)
- Given a subscriber or command action that throws, when it runs, then the error is caught and logged with console.error instead of breaking the event dispatch for other commands. (zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/src/store.ts)
- Given several commands that all match one event, when dispatch runs, then matches are sorted by priority descending then by registration order ascending, and only the commands sharing the highest priority execute; priority is 1000 for a sequence, 100 per modifier, 10 per key and 100 for a target. (zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/src/parser.ts; zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/src/store.ts)
- Given a command with options.requireReset true, when the hotkey fires, then the command id is remembered and further keydowns are ignored until a keyup clears the fired set, so the action runs once per physical press rather than on every auto-repeat. (zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/src/store.ts)
- Given a command with eventType "keyup", when the key is released, then the action runs before the key is removed from pressedKeys, so the action still sees the key as held. (zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/src/store.ts)
- Given a store created without a target, when init() is called without one, then it throws "target is required for initialization". (zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/src/store.ts)
- Given commands registered before init() whose hotkey contains "mod" or "controlormeta", when init() resolves the real platform, then only those commands are re-parsed and re-prioritized, so a store built during module evaluation still resolves mod correctly once the DOM exists. (zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/src/store.ts)
- Given useIsKeyPressed watching "shift", when Shift is held then the value is true and when it is released then the value returns to false. (ark: packages/react/src/providers/hotkeys/hotkeys.test.tsx: "should track whether a key is pressed"; ark: packages/solid/src/providers/hotkeys/hotkeys.test.tsx: "should track whether a key is pressed"; ark: packages/svelte/src/lib/providers/hotkeys/hotkeys.test.ts: "should track pressed keys and modifiers")
- Given usePressedKeys, when Shift is held then the list is ["Shift"] and when it is released then the list is empty. (ark: packages/react/src/providers/hotkeys/hotkeys.test.tsx: "should expose currently pressed keys"; ark: packages/solid/src/providers/hotkeys/hotkeys.test.tsx: "should expose currently pressed keys")
- Given React's useIsKeyPressed, when it subscribes, then it goes through useSyncExternalStore with store.isPressed as the selector, where Solid and Svelte wrap the same store.subscribe through their own useSyncExternalStore shim and return an accessor or a getter function instead of a plain value. (ark: packages/react/src/providers/hotkeys/use-is-key-pressed.ts; ark: packages/solid/src/providers/hotkeys/use-is-key-pressed.ts; ark: packages/svelte/src/lib/providers/hotkeys/use-is-key-pressed.svelte.ts)

### Forms

- Given commands for the plain key "s", the chord "ctrl+s" and the plain key "p" with enableOnFormTags true, when focus is inside an input and s is typed, then the input receives the character "s" and the plain command does not fire. (ark: packages/react/src/providers/hotkeys/hotkeys-options.test.tsx: "should ignore a single-key hotkey while typing in an input"; ark: packages/solid/src/providers/hotkeys/hotkeys-options.test.tsx: "should ignore a single-key hotkey while typing in an input"; ark: packages/svelte/src/lib/providers/hotkeys/hotkeys.test.ts: "should ignore a single key while typing but still fire modifiers and opt-ins")

(zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/src/parser.ts; zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/src/types.ts)
- Given an event whose target reports isContentEditable, when enableOnContentEditable is not true, then the command is skipped regardless of tag name. (zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/src/parser.ts)

### SSR and hydration

- Given React's usePlatform, when it runs on the server, then getServerSnapshot returns "windows" so the markup is stable, and the client snapshot re-detects the real platform after hydration; no test covers the server path. (ark: packages/react/src/providers/hotkeys/use-platform.ts)
- Given Solid's usePlatform, when it runs, then the signal starts at "windows" and is only updated inside onMount, so the server render and the first client render agree. (ark: packages/solid/src/providers/hotkeys/use-platform.ts)
- Given Svelte's usePlatform, when it runs, then $state starts at "windows" and detection happens in an $effect, which does not run on the server. (ark: packages/svelte/src/lib/providers/hotkeys/use-platform.svelte.ts)
- Given Svelte's useHotkeys with no id prop, when it generates an instance id, then it uses a random prefix rather than $props.id(), which is safe only because a hotkey id is never rendered and registration happens in an $effect that does not run on the server; React instead uses useId. (ark: packages/svelte/src/lib/providers/hotkeys/use-hotkeys.svelte.ts; ark: packages/react/src/providers/hotkeys/use-hotkeys.ts)
- Given the hotkey store's init, when the environment provider's getRootNode() is used as the listener target, then React initializes inside useSafeLayoutEffect, Solid inside onMount and Svelte inside $effect, so no framework touches the document during render. (ark: packages/react/src/providers/hotkeys/use-hotkey-store.ts; ark: packages/solid/src/providers/hotkeys/use-hotkey-store.ts; ark: packages/svelte/src/lib/providers/hotkeys/use-hotkey-store.svelte.ts)

### Notes and edge cases

- Given the public entry point, when it is imported, then it exports parseHotkey, normalizeHotkey, isHotKey, isHotkeyEqual, formatHotkey, getPlatform, createHotkeyStore/HotkeyStore, createHotkeyRecorder/HotkeyRecorder, validateHotkey and assertValidHotkey. (zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/src/index.ts)
- Given a hotkey string, when parseHotkey runs, then it returns { keys, codes, alt, ctrl, meta, shift, isSequence } plus sequenceSteps for a sequence, where "+" is the modifier separator and ">" is the sequence separator. (zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/src/parser.ts; zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/src/utils.ts)
- Given a hotkey written with the alias "mod" or "ControlOrMeta", when it is parsed, then it resolves to Meta on mac and Control everywhere else; the accepted modifier spellings are ctrl/control, alt/option, shift, and meta/cmd/command/win/windows. (zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/src/modifier.ts)
- Given a hotkey key name, when keyToCode maps it, then single uppercase letters become KeyX, digits become DigitX, F1-F20 map to themselves, the named navigation keys map to themselves, and the punctuation set maps to Space, Minus, Equal (both "=" and "+"), BracketLeft, BracketRight, Semicolon, Quote, Backquote, Backslash, Comma, Period and Slash; anything else has no code and so can only match on the logical key. (zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/src/key-to-code.ts)
- Given a parsed hotkey with several keys, when matchesHotkey runs, then it succeeds if ANY of the steps matches the event, so a multi-key chord is an OR of alternatives rather than a requirement that all keys be held. (zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/src/parser.ts)
- Given a store, when it is used, then its API is init, destroy, register, unregister, enable, disable, setEnabled, clear, setScope, addScope, removeScope, toggleScope, getActiveScopes, getState, isPressed, getCurrentlyPressed, getPressedCodes and subscribe(selector, callback). (zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/src/store.ts)
- Given the store's default command options, when nothing overrides them, then preventDefault is true, stopPropagation false, enableOnFormTags false, enableOnContentEditable false and capture true. (zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/src/store.ts)
- Given commands with mixed capture settings, when listeners are attached, then the store attaches a capture listener, a bubble listener or both, and re-attaches whenever the required set changes; with no commands but at least one subscriber it still attaches a capture listener. (zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/src/store.ts)
- Given validateHotkey, when it inspects a hotkey string, then an empty string is an error, an unrecognized modifier segment is an error, an empty sequence step is an error prefixed with its step number, and a modifier-only hotkey, a duplicate modifier or an unrecognized key name is a warning rather than an error; assertValidHotkey throws only on errors. There are no tests for validate.ts at all. (zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/src/validate.ts)
- Given format.test.ts, when the file is read end to end, then several describe blocks are duplicated verbatim under the same names (two "formatHotkey / Windows" style blocks, two "formatHotkey / styles / symbols", two "formatHotkey / styles / text", two "formatHotkey / styles / mixed / Mac"), so a number of assertions run twice and the useShortNames cases assert no behavioral difference at all. (zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/tests/format.test.ts)
- Given the hotkeys tests, when they run, then matching.test.ts, store.test.ts, smoke.test.ts, format.test.ts and recorder.test.ts all declare `// @vitest-environment jsdom`, so every platform and layout quirk is simulated through synthesized KeyboardEvent objects rather than exercised in a real browser; no Playwright coverage exists for this package. (zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/tests/matching.test.ts; zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/tests/store.test.ts)
- Given matching.test.ts, when it builds events, then getModifierState is hand-written on a plain object, so the AltGraph behavior under test is the test author's model of Windows AltGr and macOS Option rather than observed browser output. (zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/tests/matching.test.ts)
- Given the modifier handling as a whole, when platforms are compared, then the Mac versus Windows split shows up in four distinct places: mod resolves to Meta against Control, display uses ⌃⌥⇧⌘ against Ctrl/Alt/Shift/Win (Super on linux), macOS Option sets only altKey while Windows AltGr sets ctrlKey and altKey together, and macOS Firefox reports AltGraph for a bare Option press so the AltGraph guard additionally requires ctrlKey. (zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/src/parser.ts; zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/src/format.ts; zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/src/modifier.ts)
- Given a hotkey bound to a symbol key, when the event carries a modifier that transformed the character (macOS Option+/ producing "÷" while code stays "Slash"), then matching falls back to the physical code, but only while a modifier is held, so an international layout that simply puts a different character on that key does not false-positive. (zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/src/parser.ts)
- Given a React component reading useHotkeyRegistrations or usePressedKeys, when the version string is unchanged, then the previously built array is returned from a ref cache; Solid and Svelte instead return accessors and rebuild on read, so React is the only framework that guarantees referential stability. (ark: packages/react/src/providers/hotkeys/use-store-snapshot.ts; ark: packages/solid/src/providers/hotkeys/use-hotkey-registrations.ts)
- Given a command id that another component already registered on the same store, when useHotkeys registers over it, then a dev warning explains that the earlier command silently stops firing and suggests a unique id, an omitted id, or a separate store; commands without an id are keyed as `${instanceId}:${index}` so two components never collide. (ark: packages/react/src/providers/hotkeys/use-hotkeys.ts; ark: packages/svelte/src/lib/providers/hotkeys/use-hotkeys.svelte.ts)
- Given the three framework wrappers, when their prop shapes are compared, then React takes plain objects, Solid takes MaybeAccessor props resolved with runIfFn and returns accessors, and Svelte takes MaybeFunction props and returns getter functions; Solid's useHotkey wraps its command in a createMemo while React relies on a fresh array each render plus field-by-field reconciliation. (ark: packages/react/src/providers/hotkeys/use-hotkey.ts; ark: packages/solid/src/providers/hotkeys/use-hotkey.ts)
- Given Vue, when the hotkeys provider is looked for, then there is none: hotkeys hooks exist only for React, Solid and Svelte. (ark: packages/react/src/providers/hotkeys/index.ts)
- Given the Svelte hotkeys tests, when they assert behavior, then they drive prebuilt .svelte example components and match on rendered text such as "Save (modifier)" or a `li[data-fired]` attribute, rather than calling the hooks directly as the React and Solid suites do; there is no separate Svelte hotkeys-options test file. (ark: packages/svelte/src/lib/providers/hotkeys/hotkeys.test.ts)
- Given the Solid hotkeys suite, when compared with React's, then Solid has no equivalent of the keyup eventType test, the sequence test, the stable-reference test, the empty-command-list test, the add/remove test, the enabled-toggle registration test, the shared default store test, the recorder record/clear tests, or the explicit platform override test, so those behaviors are only pinned in React. (ark: packages/solid/src/providers/hotkeys/hotkeys.test.tsx)

- The smoke suite drives five table-driven `it(`${id}: ${hotkey}`)` blocks whose names are generated at runtime, covering standard modifier chords (clipboard, undo, redo and the Shift variants from Linear, Notion, VS Code, Slack, GitHub and Figma), single-key shortcuts, function keys, arrow-key combinations, and symbol and punctuation shortcuts, with 59 table entries in total. (zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/tests/smoke.test.ts: "${id}: ${hotkey}")
- The smoke suite additionally pins named sequence cases (VS Code `g>g`, GitHub `g>i` and `g>p`, and the chorded `Control+k>Control+s` and `Control+k>Control+c`), coexistence cases distinguishing Ctrl+S from Ctrl+Shift+S and a single key from its modified version, and four negative cases where a handler must not fire (plain S against Ctrl+S, a plain letter while Ctrl is held, Ctrl+P against Ctrl+Shift+P, and a sequence whose second key is wrong). (zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/tests/smoke.test.ts: "VS Code: g>g (go to top - vim)"; zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/tests/smoke.test.ts: "GitHub: g>i (go to issues)"; zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/tests/smoke.test.ts: "GitHub: g>p (go to pull requests)"; zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/tests/smoke.test.ts: "VS Code-style: Control+k>Control+s (open keyboard shortcuts)"; zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/tests/smoke.test.ts: "VS Code-style: Control+k>Control+c (add line comment)"; zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/tests/smoke.test.ts: "distinguishes Ctrl+S from Ctrl+Shift+S"; zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/tests/smoke.test.ts: "distinguishes single key from modified version"; zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/tests/smoke.test.ts: "Ctrl+S does not fire on plain S"; zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/tests/smoke.test.ts: "plain letter does not fire when Ctrl is held"; zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/tests/smoke.test.ts: "Ctrl+Shift+P does not fire on Ctrl+P"; zag: packages/utilities/hotkeys/tests/smoke.test.ts: "sequence does not fire if wrong second key")

## factory

### Roles and attributes

- Given an ark.div with asChild wrapping an ark.span, when it renders, then the parent element is absent from the DOM and only the child element is rendered. (ark: packages/react/src/components/factory.test.tsx: "should render only the child"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/factory.test.tsx: "should render only the child"; ark: packages/svelte/src/lib/components/factory/factory.test.ts: "should render only the child")
- Given a parent with id "parent" and data-part "parent" and a child with id "child" and data-part "child", when asChild merges them, then the child's id and data-part win, so for ordinary attributes the child overrides the parent. (ark: packages/react/src/components/factory.test.tsx: "should override existing props"; ark: packages/svelte/src/lib/components/factory/factory.test.ts: "should override existing props")
- Given a parent with style background red and class "parent" and a child with style color blue and class "child", when asChild merges them, then the merged element carries both declarations and both class names in the order "child parent", so class and style are concatenated rather than replaced. (ark: packages/react/src/components/factory.test.tsx: "should merge styles and classes"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/factory.test.tsx: "should merge styles"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/factory.test.tsx: "should merge classes"; ark: packages/svelte/src/lib/components/factory/factory.test.ts: "should merge styles and classes")
- Given the merged element, when its text content is checked, then the child's children survive the merge. (ark: packages/react/src/components/factory.test.tsx: "should merge styles and classes")
- Given mergeProps, when it merges two prop objects, then any key starting with "on" whose values are both functions is composed into a call-all of the later then the earlier handler, "className" and "class" are joined with whitespace after trimming, "style" is merged as objects (or string-concatenated with a ";" when both are strings, with one side serialized when only one is a string), "data-ownedby" is joined as a de-duplicated whitespace-separated set, and every other key takes the later value unless it is undefined. (zag: packages/core/src/merge-props.ts)
- Given props carrying symbol keys (Svelte attachments), when mergeProps runs, then symbol keys are copied straight over from the later object with no composition. (zag: packages/core/src/merge-props.ts)
- Given React's factory with asChild false, when it renders, then it calls createElement(Component, { ...restProps, ref }, children) so the element is rendered normally with the ref attached directly. (ark: packages/react/src/components/factory.ts)

### Pointer

- Given an asChild pair where both the parent and the child declare onClick, when the rendered element is clicked, then both handlers run, so event handlers compose instead of overriding. (ark: packages/react/src/components/factory.test.tsx: "should merge events"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/factory.test.tsx: "should merge events"; ark: packages/svelte/src/lib/components/factory/factory.test.ts: "should merge events")

### Focus management

- Given an ark.span with asChild and a stable useCallback ref, when the parent re-renders, then the callback ref is not called again, so a stable callback ref is never detached and re-attached by an unrelated parent render. (ark: packages/react/src/components/factory.test.tsx: "should not detach stable asChild callback ref on parent re-render")
- Given an asChild parent with a ref and a react.lazy child that also has a ref, when the element mounts, then both the parent ref and the child ref receive the same DOM node, so refs compose through the lazy unwrapping. (ark: packages/react/src/components/factory.test.tsx: "should compose refs through a react.lazy child")
- Given React's factory, when asChild is used, then the child's own ref is read through a getter-aware helper that handles React 18 dev, React 19 dev and the plain props.ref case, and is composed with the forwarded ref through useComposedRefs; when no outer ref was forwarded the child's own ref is passed through untouched. (ark: packages/react/src/components/factory.ts)

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given nested ark elements where both the outer and middle element set asChild, when they render, then the outermost props reach the innermost element, so asChild composes down through a chain. (ark: packages/react/src/components/factory.test.tsx: "should propagate asChild")
- Given nested ark elements where the middle element sets asChild={false}, when they render, then the outer element's data-testid does not reach the innermost element, so the chain stops at the opted-out level. (ark: packages/react/src/components/factory.test.tsx: "should stop propagate asChild"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/factory.test.tsx: "should stop propagate asChild")

### SSR and hydration

- Given a child handed across the RSC boundary as a react.lazy wrapper (which isValidElement rejects), when asChild renders it, then the factory unwraps it through Children.toArray, the parent element is not rendered, and class, style and text are merged onto the real child exactly as for a plain element child. (ark: packages/react/src/components/factory.test.tsx: "should unwrap a react.lazy child from the RSC flight protocol"; ark: packages/react/src/components/factory.ts)
- Given a pending react.lazy child inside a Suspense boundary, when it has not resolved, then the fallback renders and the child is absent, and once the chunk resolves the child appears carrying the parent's data-part. (ark: packages/react/src/components/factory.test.tsx: "should suspend until a pending react.lazy child resolves")
- Given Vue's factory, when asChild is false, then self-closing tags (br, hr, img, input, area, textarea) are rendered with no default slot at all, specifically to avoid a hydration mismatch. (ark: packages/vue/src/components/factory.ts)
- Given Svelte's factory, when asChild is not supplied, then it branches on the tag: void SVG tags go through a dedicated Svg component, void HTML tags render with no children snippet, textarea is special-cased with no children, and everything else renders the children snippet inside svelte:element. (ark: packages/svelte/src/lib/components/factory/factory.svelte)

### Notes and edge cases

- Given asChild with two sibling element children, when it renders, then nothing is rendered at all, because getAsChild looks for a single valid element and finds an array instead. (ark: packages/react/src/components/factory.test.tsx: "should leave non-lazy invalid children untouched")
- Given asChild with a bare text child, when it renders, then nothing is rendered, so an invalid asChild child fails silently with no element and no warning. (ark: packages/react/src/components/factory.test.tsx: "should render nothing when asChild has no valid child")
- Given the four framework factories, when their asChild APIs are compared, then React and Vue take a boolean asChild and read the single child element, Solid takes asChild as a render function receiving a props callback (asChild={(props) => <ark.span {...props({...})} />}), and Svelte takes an asChild snippet receiving the same kind of props callback; the Solid and Svelte forms therefore require the author to spread the merged props explicitly and cannot be propagated implicitly the way React's boolean can. (ark: packages/react/src/components/factory.ts; ark: packages/solid/src/components/factory.tsx; ark: packages/svelte/src/lib/components/factory/factory.svelte; ark: packages/vue/src/components/factory.ts)
- Given Solid's factory, when asChild is used, then the props callback strips "ref" out of the parent props before merging, so a parent ref is not forwarded through asChild the way React composes it. (ark: packages/solid/src/components/factory.tsx)
- Given Solid's factory without asChild, when it renders, then it uses solid-js/web Dynamic rather than a per-tag component. (ark: packages/solid/src/components/factory.tsx)
- Given Vue's factory with asChild, when it renders, then it delegates to a Dynamic component that flattens Fragment children, skips Comment nodes to find the first real child, deletes that child's ref, merges attrs with the child's props and clones the vnode with its props emptied first so cloneVNode does not merge the child's props a second time. (ark: packages/vue/src/utils/dynamic.ts)
- Given every factory, when a tag is accessed off the ark proxy, then the wrapped component is memoized per tag in a Map, and calling ark(...) as a function wraps an arbitrary component type. (ark: packages/react/src/components/factory.ts; ark: packages/solid/src/components/factory.tsx; ark: packages/vue/src/components/factory.ts)
- Given React's wrapped component, when it is created, then it is wrapped in both memo and forwardRef and given a displayName taken from the underlying component. (ark: packages/react/src/components/factory.ts)
- Given the Solid factory suite, when compared with React's, then Solid has no test for prop override, no asChild propagation test, no ref test and no lazy/RSC tests, and the Svelte suite covers only render-only-child, prop override, style/class merge and event merge; the asChild ref and RSC behavior is pinned in React alone. (ark: packages/solid/src/components/factory.test.tsx; ark: packages/svelte/src/lib/components/factory/factory.test.ts)
- Given the Svelte factory suite, when it asserts merged styles, then it compares color as "rgb(0, 0, 255)" rather than "blue", matching how jsdom serializes a style string; Solid does the same. (ark: packages/svelte/src/lib/components/factory/factory.test.ts; ark: packages/solid/src/components/factory.test.tsx)

- Given a Vue `asChild` factory wrapping a plain child element that already has a class, then the merged class list contains each class exactly once with no duplication. (ark: packages/vue/src/components/factory.test.tsx: "should not duplicate the class of a plain child element")
- Given a plain child element with its own click handler under a Vue factory that also has one, then each handler is invoked exactly once per click. (ark: packages/vue/src/components/factory.test.tsx: "should call each handler of a plain child element once")
- Given a Vue slot whose first node is a comment (a `v-if` placeholder), then the props are applied to the first non-comment child instead. (ark: packages/vue/src/components/factory.test.tsx: "should apply props to the first non-comment child")
- Given reactive props on a Vue factory, when they change, then the same child DOM element is patched in place rather than replaced, and its class list reflects the new value. (ark: packages/vue/src/components/factory.test.tsx: "should patch reactive props onto the same child element")
- Given a Vue slot that renders only a comment, then the markup is left untouched as `<!--v-if-->` rather than throwing or injecting a wrapper. (ark: packages/vue/src/components/factory.test.tsx: "should render comment-only children untouched")

## portal

### Dismissal and layering

- Given a Portal nested inside a parent div, when it renders, then the content lands under the test container's base element (document.body) and is NOT inside the parent div. (ark: packages/react/src/components/portal/portal.test.tsx: "should render portal children next to the body")
- Given a Portal with disabled set, when it renders inside a parent div, then the content stays inside the parent div and is still visible, so disabling the portal degrades to rendering in place rather than to rendering nothing. (ark: packages/react/src/components/portal/portal.test.tsx: "should not render portal children next to the body if marked as `disabled`")
- Given a Portal whose container prop is a ref to a sibling div, when it renders, then the container is non-empty and holds the portal content. (ark: packages/react/src/components/portal/portal.test.tsx: "should render portal children inside a custom element")
- Given a Portal with both a container ref and disabled set, when it renders, then the container div is empty while the content is still visible in its original position, so disabled wins over container. (ark: packages/react/src/components/portal/portal.test.tsx: "should not render portal children inside a custom element if marked as `disabled`")
- Given an EnvironmentProvider whose value returns a shadow root, when a Portal inside it renders, then the content is mounted directly into that shadow root (shadowRoot.innerHTML is exactly the portal markup) instead of into document.body. (ark: packages/react/src/components/portal/portal.test.tsx: "should render portal children inside a shadow root")
- Given no container, when the mount node is resolved, then the environment's root node is asked for its own getRootNode(), and the shadow root is used when that is one, otherwise the owner document's body. (ark: packages/react/src/components/portal/portal.tsx)

### SSR and hydration

- Given React's Portal, when it renders on the server, then useSyncExternalStore's server snapshot reports isServer true and the children are rendered inline with no createPortal call, and the portal only takes effect after hydration. (ark: packages/react/src/components/portal/portal.tsx)

### Notes and edge cases

- Given a Portal whose child is a bare string, when it renders, then the text is visible. (ark: packages/react/src/components/portal/portal.test.tsx: "should render portal without element children")
- Given a Portal with one element child, when it renders, then that element is visible. (ark: packages/react/src/components/portal/portal.test.tsx: "should render portal with element children")
- Given a Portal with two element children, when it renders, then both are visible, because the implementation maps over children and calls createPortal per child rather than portalling a single wrapper. (ark: packages/react/src/components/portal/portal.test.tsx: "should render portal with multiple element children"; ark: packages/react/src/components/portal/portal.tsx)
- Given a Portal with a container ref, when it mounts, then its children render twice, because the container state starts as the ref's current value (null on the first pass) and an effect sets it after the ref is attached. (ark: packages/react/src/components/portal/portal.test.tsx: "should render twice if container was specified")
- Given a Portal with no container, when it mounts, then its children render exactly once. (ark: packages/react/src/components/portal/portal.test.tsx: "should render once if container was not specified")
- Given Ark's component set, when portals are compared across frameworks, then only React and Svelte ship a Portal component: Solid is expected to use solid-js/web's own Portal and Vue its own Teleport, so there is no Ark-level portal contract or test coverage for those two. (ark: packages/react/src/components/portal/portal.tsx; ark: packages/svelte/src/lib/components/portal/portal.svelte)
- Given Svelte's Portal, when it renders, then it defaults container to globalThis.document?.body, waits for tick() and then imperatively mount()s the children snippet into the container carrying the full context map through getAllContexts, unmounting on cleanup; when disabled it renders the snippet inline instead. Unlike React's it has no shadow-root resolution through the environment provider and no server-render branch beyond the optional-chained document access. (ark: packages/svelte/src/lib/components/portal/portal.svelte)
- Given the Svelte Portal, when it is used, then there is no test file for it at all. (ark: packages/svelte/src/lib/components/portal/portal.svelte)

## field

### Roles and attributes

- Given the field anatomy, when parts are enumerated, then they are root, errorText, helperText, input, label, select, textarea and requiredIndicator, each rendered with the matching data-scope="field" and data-part attribute. (ark: packages/react/src/components/field/field.anatomy.ts)
- Given Field.Root, when it renders, then it carries data-part="root", role="group", id `field::<id>`, and data-disabled, data-invalid and data-readonly set only when those flags are true. (ark: packages/react/src/components/field/use-field.ts; ark: packages/react/src/components/field/field.test.tsx: "should set textbox as disabled")
- Given Field.Label, when it renders, then it carries data-part="label", id `field::<id>::label`, data-disabled, data-invalid, data-readonly and data-required mirroring the root state, and an htmlFor pointing at the target item control when target is set or at the root control id otherwise. (ark: packages/react/src/components/field/use-field.ts)
- Given any control part (Input, Textarea, Select), when it renders, then it gets the shared control props: id, required, disabled, readOnly, aria-invalid when invalid, data-invalid, data-required, data-readonly, aria-describedby pointing at the helper text id when a helper text element exists, and aria-errormessage pointing at the error text id only when the field is invalid AND an error text element exists. (ark: packages/react/src/components/field/use-field.ts)
- Given Field.HelperText, when it renders, then it carries data-part="helperText", id `field::<id>::helper-text` and data-disabled when the field is disabled. (ark: packages/react/src/components/field/use-field.ts; ark: packages/react/src/components/field/field.test.tsx: "should set textbox as disabled")
- Given Field.ErrorText, when it renders, then it carries data-part="errorText", id `field::<id>::error-text` and aria-live="polite", and it renders nothing at all unless the field is invalid. (ark: packages/react/src/components/field/use-field.ts; ark: packages/react/src/components/field/field-error-text.tsx)
- Given Field.RequiredIndicator, when the field is required, then it renders a span with data-part="requiredIndicator" and aria-hidden true whose default content is "*", and when the field is not required it renders the optional fallback prop instead. (ark: packages/react/src/components/field/field-required-indicator.tsx; ark: packages/react/src/components/field/field.test.tsx: "should set textbox as required")
- Given Field.Root with target="amount" and two Field.Items, when the structure is snapshotted, then the label's for attribute is `field::<id>::item::amount`, the currency select's id is `field::<id>::item::currency` and the amount input's id is `field::<id>::item::amount`, so each item namespaces its control id by its value. (ark: packages/react/src/components/field/field.test.tsx: "should render the correct html structure"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/field/field.test.tsx: "should render the correct html structure"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/field/tests/field-item.test.tsx: "should render the correct html structure"; ark: packages/svelte/src/lib/components/field/tests/field-item.test.ts: "should render the correct html structure")
- Given a Field.Item, when it builds its context, then it clones the parent field context but replaces ids.control with `field::<parent control id>::item::<value>` and ids.label with that control id plus "::label", and re-derives getLabelProps, getInputProps, getSelectProps and getTextareaProps from it while inheriting every other parent value unchanged. (ark: packages/react/src/components/field/field-item.tsx)
- Given a Field.Item with a custom control rendered through Field.Context and getInputProps(), when it renders, then the custom input's id contains "item::custom" and the label's for attribute equals that id, so arbitrary controls can join the item scoping. (ark: packages/react/src/components/field/field.test.tsx: "should scope control id for custom controls via Field.Context")
- Given Field.Root with no target and a mix of one Field.Item and one direct Field.Input, when the structure is snapshotted, then the label's for attribute and the direct input's id are the plain root control id while the item's select keeps its `item::currency` id. (ark: packages/react/src/components/field/field.test.tsx: "should work when mixing Field.Item with a direct control under Field.Root"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/field/field.test.tsx: "should work when mixing Field.Item with a direct control under Field.Root"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/field/tests/field-item.test.tsx: "should work when mixing Field.Item with a direct control under Field.Root")
- Given the same mixed layout in Svelte, when the structure is snapshotted, then the direct control's id is `field::<id>::control` rather than the bare generated id that React, Solid and Vue produce, so the Svelte port uses a different id scheme for the root control. (ark: packages/svelte/src/lib/components/field/tests/field-item.test.ts: "should work when mixing Field.Item with a direct control under Field.Root"; ark: packages/svelte/src/lib/components/field/tests/field-item.test.ts: "should focus the item control when target is set in mixed usage")
- Given Field.Root with target="currency" and a mix of an item and a direct input, when the structure is snapshotted, then the label points at the item control id while the direct input keeps the root control id, so target redirects only the label. (ark: packages/react/src/components/field/field.test.tsx: "should focus the item control when mixing Field.Item with a direct control and target is set"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/field/field.test.tsx: "should focus the item control when target is set in mixed usage"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/field/tests/field-item.test.tsx: "should focus the item control when target is set in mixed usage"; ark: packages/svelte/src/lib/components/field/tests/field-item.test.ts: "should focus the item control when target is set in mixed usage")
- Given a field, when aria-describedby is asserted on the control, then it is present once a helper text element with the expected id exists in the document or shadow root; presence is detected with getElementById plus a MutationObserver on the root subtree, so the attribute appears asynchronously and the tests wait for it. (ark: packages/react/src/components/field/field.test.tsx: "should set aria-describedby to the ids of the error and helper text"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/field/field.test.tsx: "should set aria-describedby to the ids of the error and helper text"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/field/tests/field.test.tsx: "should set aria-describedby to the ids of the error and helper text"; ark: packages/react/src/components/field/use-field.ts)

### Focus management

- Given a field with a label and an input, when the label text is clicked, then the input receives focus through the native label-for association. (ark: packages/react/src/components/field/field.test.tsx: "should focus on input when label is clicked"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/field/field.test.tsx: "should focus on input when label is clicked"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/field/tests/field.test.tsx: "should focus on input when label is clicked")
- Given Field.Root with target="amount" and items for currency and amount, when the label is clicked, then the amount input (not the first item) receives focus. (ark: packages/react/src/components/field/field.test.tsx: "should focus the target input when label is clicked"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/field/field.test.tsx: "should focus the target input when label is clicked"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/field/tests/field-item.test.tsx: "should focus the target input when label is clicked"; ark: packages/svelte/src/lib/components/field/tests/field-item.test.ts: "should focus the target input when label is clicked")
