### Notes and edge cases

- Given a Field.Item rendered outside any Field.Root, when it mounts, then it throws "Field.Item must be used within Field.Root" in all four frameworks. (ark: packages/react/src/components/field/field.test.tsx: "should throw when Field.Item is used outside Field.Root"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/field/field.test.tsx: "should throw when Field.Item is used outside Field.Root"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/field/tests/field-item.test.tsx: "should throw when Field.Item is used outside Field.Root"; ark: packages/svelte/src/lib/components/field/tests/field-item.test.ts: "should throw when Field.Item is used outside Field.Root")
- Given Field.Input, Field.Textarea and Field.Select used with no Field.Root around them, when they render in Vue, then all three still render, so the control parts tolerate a missing field context. (ark: packages/vue/src/components/field/tests/field.test.tsx: "should render input, textarea, and select outside Field.Root"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/field/tests/field-standalone.test.vue)
- Given the id snapshots across frameworks, when they are compared, then the generated field id differs by framework runtime (React `_r_9_`, Solid `cl-8`, Vue `v-0`, Svelte `c1`), so any conformance suite must match ids by shape rather than by literal value. (ark: packages/react/src/components/field/field.test.tsx: "should render the correct html structure"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/field/field.test.tsx: "should render the correct html structure"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/field/tests/field-item.test.tsx: "should render the correct html structure"; ark: packages/svelte/src/lib/components/field/tests/field-item.test.ts: "should render the correct html structure")
- Given the Vue error-text case, when it asserts the accessible error message, then it must await nextTick() first, because Vue applies the aria wiring on the next tick; the React and Solid equivalents assert synchronously. (ark: packages/vue/src/components/field/tests/field.test.tsx: "should display error text when error is present")
- Given the Vue and Svelte suites, when compared with React's, then neither runs axe, neither has the custom-control Field.Context test, neither has the NumberInput-inside-item test and neither has the stable-callback-ref test; the Solid suite additionally lacks axe and the custom-control test but is the only one that pins reactive invalid propagation into Field.Item. (ark: packages/vue/src/components/field/tests/field.test.tsx; ark: packages/svelte/src/lib/components/field/tests/field-item.test.ts; ark: packages/solid/src/components/field/field.test.tsx)
- Given the Vue and Svelte field suites, when their fixtures are inspected, then every scenario is a separate .test.vue or .test.svelte single-file component mounted by the .ts test, whereas React and Solid declare the markup inline in the test file. (ark: packages/vue/src/components/field/tests/field-item-basic.test.vue; ark: packages/svelte/src/lib/components/field/tests/field-item-basic.test.svelte)
- Given useField's helper-text and error-text detection, when the field lives inside a shadow root, then presence is resolved against the environment's root node (document or shadow root) rather than the global document. (ark: packages/react/src/components/field/use-field.ts)

## fieldset

### Roles and attributes

- Ark's Fieldset composes Root, Legend, HelperText and ErrorText around native `fieldset` semantics, and the root is discoverable as `role="group"` named by its legend. (ark: packages/react/src/components/fieldset/fieldset.test.tsx: "should render aria-labelledby on the fieldset")
- Given a fieldset with a legend, then the group element carries `aria-labelledby` referencing the legend's generated id. (ark: packages/react/src/components/fieldset/fieldset.test.tsx: "should render aria-labelledby on the fieldset"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/fieldset/fieldset.test.tsx: "should render aria-labelledby on the fieldset"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/fieldset/tests/fieldset.test.tsx: "should render aria-labelledby on the fieldset")
- Given a fieldset with helper text, then the group's `aria-describedby` contains the helper-text id. (ark: packages/react/src/components/fieldset/fieldset.test.tsx: "should set aria-describedby with helper text"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/fieldset/fieldset.test.tsx: "should set aria-describedby with helper text"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/fieldset/tests/fieldset.test.tsx: "should set aria-describedby with helper text")
- Given an invalid fieldset, then `aria-describedby` contains both the error-text and the helper-text ids, so the error is announced in addition to the description rather than replacing it. (ark: packages/react/src/components/fieldset/fieldset.test.tsx: "should set aria-describedby with error text when invalid"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/fieldset/fieldset.test.tsx: "should set aria-describedby with error text when invalid"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/fieldset/tests/fieldset.test.tsx: "should set aria-describedby with error text when invalid")

### Forms

- Given `disabled` on the fieldset root, then a Field input nested inside it is disabled, so disabled state propagates from the fieldset through the field context. (ark: packages/react/src/components/fieldset/fieldset.test.tsx: "should set textbox as disabled"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/fieldset/fieldset.test.tsx: "should set textbox as disabled"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/fieldset/tests/fieldset.test.tsx: "should set textbox as disabled")
- Given a fieldset, then its helper text always renders and remains reachable alongside the nested field's own helper text. (ark: packages/react/src/components/fieldset/fieldset.test.tsx: "should display helper text"; ark: packages/react/src/components/fieldset/fieldset.test.tsx: "should have helper text accessible"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/fieldset/fieldset.test.tsx: "should display helper text"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/fieldset/fieldset.test.tsx: "should have helper text accessible"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/fieldset/tests/fieldset.test.tsx: "should display helper text"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/fieldset/tests/fieldset.test.tsx: "should have helper text accessible")
- Given `invalid`, then the fieldset's error text renders, and with no error it is absent from the DOM. (ark: packages/react/src/components/fieldset/fieldset.test.tsx: "should display error text when error is present"; ark: packages/react/src/components/fieldset/fieldset.test.tsx: "should not display error text when no error is present"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/fieldset/fieldset.test.tsx: "should display error text when error is present"; ark: packages/solid/src/components/fieldset/fieldset.test.tsx: "should not display error text when no error is present"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/fieldset/tests/fieldset.test.tsx: "should display error text when error is present"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/fieldset/tests/fieldset.test.tsx: "should not display error text when no error is present")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given a `Field.Textarea` with a `defaultValue` nested inside a fieldset, when a `Fieldset.Context` consumer counts its renders, then the count stays under ten and never reaches the fifty-render tripwire, pinning a controlled-value feedback loop between the fieldset context and a defaulted textarea. (ark: packages/react/src/components/fieldset/fieldset.test.tsx: "should not re-render in a loop when a textarea with defaultValue is nested")
- Only React runs axe over the fieldset; Solid and Vue omit the accessibility case, and Vue's suite is written as a `.tsx` test even though the rest of its components use `.vue` fixtures. (ark: packages/react/src/components/fieldset/fieldset.test.tsx: "should have no a11y violations"; ark: packages/vue/src/components/fieldset/tests/fieldset.test.tsx)

## environment

### Roles and attributes

- `EnvironmentProvider` takes a value function returning a document or shadow root, and `useEnvironmentContext` exposes `getRootNode`, which every machine uses instead of the global `document` so components work inside shadow DOM and inside iframes. (ark: packages/react/src/providers/environment/environment.test.tsx)

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given `EnvironmentProvider value={() => document}`, when a child reads `getRootNode()` from the context, then it resolves to a real node rather than an empty value. (ark: packages/react/src/providers/environment/environment.test.tsx: "should have access to the environment values")
- Given the Solid provider, then the consumer renders the stringified root node `[object Document]`, so Solid's context is a signal accessor (`environment().getRootNode()`) where React's is a plain object. (ark: packages/solid/src/providers/environment/environment.test.tsx: "should have access to the environment values")
- Given the Vue provider, then the test only asserts that the consumer renders without throwing, so Vue's environment wiring is the weakest covered of the three. (ark: packages/vue/src/providers/environment/environment.test.ts: "should have access to the environment values")

## ark-utils

### Notes and edge cases

- `createSplitProps<Target>()(source, keys)` is Ark's typed prop splitter: it returns the picked group and the rest, returns an empty first group when no keys are requested, and deliberately fails typechecking both when a required key is omitted and when an unknown key is passed (both cases are asserted with `@ts-expect-error`, so the test is a type test as much as a runtime one). (ark: packages/react/src/utils/create-split-props.test.ts: "should split props"; ark: packages/react/src/utils/create-split-props.test.ts: "should create an empty object when no keys are required"; ark: packages/react/src/utils/create-split-props.test.ts: "should throw TS error on incomplete keys"; ark: packages/react/src/utils/create-split-props.test.ts: "should throw TS error on extra keys"; ark: packages/solid/src/utils/create-split-props.test.ts: "should split props"; ark: packages/solid/src/utils/create-split-props.test.ts: "should create an empty object when no keys are required"; ark: packages/solid/src/utils/create-split-props.test.ts: "should throw TS error on incomplete keys"; ark: packages/solid/src/utils/create-split-props.test.ts: "should throw TS error on extra keys")
- `runIfFn(valueOrFn, ...args)` passes a plain value through untouched and calls a function value with the supplied argument, and its type tests pin argument inference, rejection of a wrong argument type, return-type inference with and without explicit annotations, and inference through a function that itself returns a function. (ark: packages/react/src/utils/run-if-fn.test.ts: "should pass through a non function value"; ark: packages/react/src/utils/run-if-fn.test.ts: "should call a function value"; ark: packages/react/src/utils/run-if-fn.test.ts: "should infer the argument type"; ark: packages/react/src/utils/run-if-fn.test.ts: "should infer an invalid argument type"; ark: packages/react/src/utils/run-if-fn.test.ts: "should infer the return type"; ark: packages/react/src/utils/run-if-fn.test.ts: "should infer the return type with explicit typings"; ark: packages/react/src/utils/run-if-fn.test.ts: "should infer the return type even if it is a nested function")
- The identical seven `runIfFn` cases are duplicated verbatim in Solid and Vue, which is how Ark keeps the render-prop helper consistent across adapters. (ark: packages/solid/src/utils/run-if-fn.test.ts: "should pass through a non function value"; ark: packages/solid/src/utils/run-if-fn.test.ts: "should infer the return type even if it is a nested function"; ark: packages/vue/src/utils/run-if-fn.test.ts: "should pass through a non function value"; ark: packages/vue/src/utils/run-if-fn.test.ts: "should infer the return type even if it is a nested function")
- `getActivity(React)` returns undefined when the React namespace has no `Activity` export and returns the export when it exists, which is how Ark feature-detects React 19's `<Activity>` without a version check. (ark: packages/react/src/utils/react-activity.test.ts: "returns undefined when React does not export Activity"; ark: packages/react/src/utils/react-activity.test.ts: "returns Activity when React exports it")
- `composeRefs(...refs)` applies a node to both callback refs and object refs in one pass. (ark: packages/react/src/utils/compose-refs.test.tsx: "should compose callback and object refs")
- Given a callback ref that returns a cleanup function, then composeRefs returns a disposer that runs that cleanup exactly once. (ark: packages/react/src/utils/compose-refs.test.tsx: "should run callback ref cleanups")
- Given no ref returns a cleanup, then composeRefs returns undefined rather than a no-op function, so React 18 and React 19 ref semantics are both honored. (ark: packages/react/src/utils/compose-refs.test.tsx: "should not return a cleanup function when no ref provides one")
- Given one ref uses the cleanup convention and a sibling is a plain callback ref, then the plain ref is not called with null during attach but is called with null when the disposer runs; the same holds for an object ref, whose `current` is reset to null. (ark: packages/react/src/utils/compose-refs.test.tsx: "should reset a plain callback ref to null when a sibling ref returns a cleanup"; ark: packages/react/src/utils/compose-refs.test.tsx: "should reset an object ref to null when a sibling ref returns a cleanup")
- Given a mix of cleanup refs, plain callback refs and object refs, then every kind is torn down on dispose. (ark: packages/react/src/utils/compose-refs.test.tsx: "should clean up every ref type when mixed together")
- Given undefined or null entries among the refs, then they are ignored, and when every ref is nullish nothing happens and no cleanup is returned. (ark: packages/react/src/utils/compose-refs.test.tsx: "should ignore undefined and null refs"; ark: packages/react/src/utils/compose-refs.test.tsx: "should do nothing and return no cleanup when every ref is nullish")
- Given a plain callback ref alongside a cleanup ref, then it is called exactly twice in total, once with the node and once with null, and never again during cleanup. (ark: packages/react/src/utils/compose-refs.test.tsx: "should not call a plain callback ref again on cleanup beyond the initial null call")
- Given stable ref identities across a re-render, then the refs stay attached and the callback ref is not re-invoked. (ark: packages/react/src/utils/compose-refs.test.tsx: "should keep stable refs attached across re-renders")
- Given one constituent callback ref is swapped for another, then the old ref is detached with null and the new one is attached with the node. (ark: packages/react/src/utils/compose-refs.test.tsx: "should reattach refs when a constituent callback ref changes")
- Given the ref set changes while one member uses the cleanup convention, then the old bundle's cleanup runs, the plain ref is detached with null and then reattached with the node, in that order. (ark: packages/react/src/utils/compose-refs.test.tsx: "should tear down the old cleanup-ref bundle and set up the new one when the ref set changes")
- Given the component unmounts while a sibling ref uses the cleanup convention, then plain callback and object refs are still detached. (ark: packages/react/src/utils/compose-refs.test.tsx: "should detach plain callback and object refs on unmount when a sibling ref uses cleanup")
- `composeRefs` exists only in the React package: Solid and Vue have no equivalent test because their ref models do not need it. (ark: packages/react/src/utils/compose-refs.test.tsx)

## anatomy

### Roles and attributes

- `createAnatomy(name).parts(...).build()` returns, per part, an `attrs` object of exactly `data-scope` and `data-part`, and a `selector` string combining a self selector and a descendant selector: `&[data-scope="x"][data-part="y"], & [data-scope="x"][data-part="y"]`. (zag: packages/anatomy/src/create-anatomy.ts; zag: packages/anatomy/tests/create-anatomy.test.ts: "should allow to set parts")
- Given a camelCase scope or part name, then both are kebab-cased in the emitted attributes and selector, so `createAnatomy("hoverCard").parts("toggleButton")` yields `data-scope="hover-card"` and `data-part="toggle-button"`. (zag: packages/anatomy/tests/create-anatomy.test.ts: "should convert string to kebab case if needed")
- Given a duplicated part name, then the built anatomy contains it once. (zag: packages/anatomy/tests/create-anatomy.test.ts: "should filter duplicate values")
- Given `extendWith`, then the extra parts are appended to the built anatomy, and duplicates between the base and the extension are collapsed. (zag: packages/anatomy/tests/create-anatomy.test.ts: "should allow to extend the anatomy"; zag: packages/anatomy/tests/create-anatomy.test.ts: "should filter duplicates parts when extending")
- Given `rename("segmented-control")`, then every part's `data-scope` and selector switch to the new scope while the part names stay, which is exactly how Ark builds SegmentGroup out of radio-group. (zag: packages/anatomy/tests/create-anatomy.test.ts: "should rename component scope")
- Given `.parts(...)` is called twice, then it throws with a message pointing at `.extendWith(...)`, and calling `.parts` on an already-built instance throws too. (zag: packages/anatomy/tests/create-anatomy.test.ts: "should not allow to invoke .parts more than once"; zag: packages/anatomy/tests/create-anatomy.test.ts: "should not allow to invoke .parts when extending")
- Given `keys()`, then it returns the declared part names in order, including parts added by `extendWith`. (zag: packages/anatomy/tests/create-anatomy.test.ts: "should return correct keys"; zag: packages/anatomy/tests/create-anatomy.test.ts: "should return correct keys when extended")
- The anatomy also exposes `omit(...)`, which returns a new instance without the named parts; it has no test. (zag: packages/anatomy/src/create-anatomy.ts)
- The convention this establishes across every machine: each rendered element carries `data-scope="<machine>"` plus `data-part="<part>"`, and all state is expressed as additional `data-*` attributes on those same elements, so styling never depends on class names. (zag: packages/anatomy/src/create-anatomy.ts)

## machine-runtime

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given a transition target that names a sibling of the source state, then it resolves relative to the transition's source state. (zag: packages/core/tests/state.test.ts: "resolves relative targets from transition source state")
- Given a name that exists both as a sibling of the source and as a child of it, then the sibling wins - the case reproduced from the color picker, whose `open` state has both a child `idle` and a root-level sibling `idle`. (zag: packages/core/tests/state.test.ts: "prefers sibling over child when both exist with same name")
- Given a dot-prefixed target, then it resolves to a child of the source state, and drills into that child's `initial` state when it is compound. (zag: packages/core/tests/state.test.ts: "dot-prefixed target resolves to child state"; zag: packages/core/tests/state.test.ts: "dot-prefixed target drills down to initial child")
- Given a bare target name, then it never resolves to a child of the source state. (zag: packages/core/tests/state.test.ts: "bare name never resolves to child of source")
- Given a dotted absolute path, then it is used as-is without relative resolution. (zag: packages/core/tests/state.test.ts: "resolves absolute path targets without relative resolution")
- Given a root-level handler with no source state, then resolution still works. (zag: packages/core/tests/state.test.ts: "resolves with undefined source (root-level handler)")
- Given a relative target that names a compound state, then resolution drills down to its initial child. (zag: packages/core/tests/state.test.ts: "drills down to initial child on relative resolution")
- Given a target that matches no state, then the raw value is returned rather than throwing. (zag: packages/core/tests/state.test.ts: "returns raw value for unknown target")
- Given a state that targets itself, then resolution returns that same state. (zag: packages/core/tests/state.test.ts: "self-targeting resolves to the same state")
- Given a `#id`-prefixed target, then it resolves by state id anywhere in the tree, and throws when the id is unknown. (zag: packages/core/tests/state.test.ts: "resolves # prefixed target by state id"; zag: packages/core/tests/state.test.ts: "throws when # prefixed target id is unknown")
- Given a `#id` target naming a compound state, then resolution continues into that state's initial child. (zag: packages/core/tests/state.test.ts: "resolveStateValue can transition by #id to a state with initial child")
- `getStateChain` returns every ancestor path from the outermost state down to the leaf. (zag: packages/core/tests/state.test.ts: "getStateChain returns the full ancestry paths")
- `getStateDefinition` returns the definition (including tags) for a dotted path. (zag: packages/core/tests/state.test.ts: "getStateDefinition returns the leaf state definition")
- `findTransition` looks for a handler on the current leaf first, then bubbles to the parent, then to the machine root, reporting which source matched. (zag: packages/core/tests/state.test.ts: "findTransition resolves from nearest state then bubbles to parent and root")
- `getExitEnterStates` computes the minimal exit and enter sets for a sibling transition (only the differing leaf), and with `reenter` on the same leaf it exits the whole chain outward and re-enters it inward. (zag: packages/core/tests/state.test.ts: "getExitEnterStates computes minimal exit/enter set for sibling transitions"; zag: packages/core/tests/state.test.ts: "getExitEnterStates reenters full chain when reenter=true on same leaf")
- `matchesState` is true for an exact match and for any ancestor of the current state, false for an unrelated state, and false for an undefined state. (zag: packages/core/tests/state.test.ts: "matchesState checks exact and descendant state matches")
- `hasTag` reads tags from the leaf and from every ancestor, and is false for a tag that belongs only to a different branch. (zag: packages/core/tests/state.test.ts: "hasTag checks tags on leaf and ancestor states")
- `createMachine` throws `[zag-js] Duplicate state id: "..."` when two states share an id, `[zag-js] Compound state "x" has child states but no "initial" property` when an initial is missing, and `[zag-js] Compound state "x" has initial "y" which is not a child state` when the initial names a nonexistent child, so these are eager authoring errors rather than runtime surprises. (zag: packages/core/tests/state.test.ts: "createMachine throws when state ids are duplicated"; zag: packages/core/tests/state.test.ts: "throws when compound state has children but no initial"; zag: packages/core/tests/state.test.ts: "throws when initial references a nonexistent child state")
- `mergeProps` concatenates `data-ownedby` tokens across sources and deduplicates them, while every other data attribute keeps last-wins override semantics. (zag: packages/core/tests/merge-props.test.ts: "combines data-ownedby tokens"; zag: packages/core/tests/merge-props.test.ts: "dedupes data-ownedby tokens"; zag: packages/core/tests/merge-props.test.ts: "keeps normal override behavior for other data attributes")
- The replace tracker gives each claim on a key a token: a lone claim is never replaced, a later claim on the same key replaces the earlier one, only the newest of many claims survives, keys are independent of each other, and a token belonging to another key reads as replaced. (zag: packages/core/tests/replace-tracker.test.ts: "a lone claim is not replaced"; zag: packages/core/tests/replace-tracker.test.ts: "a later claim replaces the earlier one"; zag: packages/core/tests/replace-tracker.test.ts: "only the newest of many claims survives"; zag: packages/core/tests/replace-tracker.test.ts: "keys are independent"; zag: packages/core/tests/replace-tracker.test.ts: "a token from another key is treated as replaced")
- This is what backs the `replaces: "open"` marker used by dialog, popover, menu, tooltip, hover-card, combobox and floating-panel when they send open and close events. (zag: packages/machines/popover/src/popover.connect.ts; zag: packages/core/tests/replace-tracker.test.ts)

### Notes and edge cases

- The core state module and the framework adapters share one behavioral suite: every adapter runs the same "uniform coverage" block, so the runtime contract is asserted identically in React, Preact, Solid, Vue, Svelte and vanilla. (zag: packages/frameworks/react/tests/machine.test.ts; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/machine.test.ts)
- Several packages ship no tests at all and are therefore unspecified by this document: `packages/store` (the proxy-based reactive store the machines build on), `packages/utilities/json-tree-utils`, `packages/utilities/stringify-state` and `packages/types`. (zag: packages/store/src; zag: packages/utilities/json-tree-utils/src; zag: packages/utilities/stringify-state/src)

## framework-adapters

### Roles and attributes

- React's `normalizeProps` is the identity function: React prop names (`className`, `htmlFor`, `onFocus`, camelCase styles) are already the target shape, so the adapter only supplies types. (zag: packages/frameworks/react/src/normalize-props.ts)
- Vue's normalizer rewrites `htmlFor` to `for`, `className` to `class`, `onDoubleClick` to `onDblclick`, `onChange` to `onInput`, `onFocus` to `onFocusin`, `onBlur` to `onFocusout`, `defaultValue` to `value` and `defaultChecked` to `checked`; other `on*` handlers are re-cased to `on<Event>`; a preserve-list keeps `viewBox`, `preserveAspectRatio` and the SVG stroke and clip attributes intact; everything else is lowercased; and a string `children` becomes `innerHTML` while a non-primitive `children` logs a development warning. (zag: packages/frameworks/vue/src/normalize-props.ts)
- Solid's normalizer maps `onFocus` to `onFocusIn`, `onBlur` to `onFocusOut`, `onDoubleClick` to `onDblClick`, `onChange` to `onInput`, plus the same default-value and class mappings, drops `readOnly` when it is false, hyphenates style object keys while leaving custom properties starting with `--` untouched, and turns a string `children` into `textContent`. (zag: packages/frameworks/solid/src/normalize-props.ts)
- Svelte's normalizer lowercases prop names except for a preserve-list, maps the same eight React-shaped names to Svelte's lowercase event names (`onfocusout`, `oninput`, `onfocusin`, `ondblclick`), and serializes a style object into a `style` string with camelCase keys hyphenated and `--` custom properties preserved. (zag: packages/frameworks/svelte/src/normalize-props.ts)
- The vanilla normalizer applies the same prop map, drops `undefined` values entirely, preserves case only for `viewBox` and `preserveAspectRatio`, lowercases everything else, and exposes a `toStyleString` helper for callers that render to an HTML string instead of going through `spreadProps`. (zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/src/normalize-props.ts)
- Given the vanilla normalizer, then `htmlFor` becomes `for`, `className` becomes `class`, `defaultValue` becomes `value` and `defaultChecked` becomes `checked`. (zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/normalize-props.test.ts: "htmlFor -> for"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/normalize-props.test.ts: "className -> class"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/normalize-props.test.ts: "defaultValue -> value"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/normalize-props.test.ts: "defaultChecked -> checked")
- Given the vanilla normalizer, then `onFocus` becomes `onFocusin`, `onBlur` becomes `onFocusout`, `onChange` becomes `onInput` and `onDoubleClick` becomes `onDblclick`. (zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/normalize-props.test.ts: "onFocus -> onFocusin"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/normalize-props.test.ts: "onBlur -> onFocusout"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/normalize-props.test.ts: "onChange -> onInput"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/normalize-props.test.ts: "onDoubleClick -> onDblclick")
- Given a style object, then the vanilla normalizer passes it through untouched, preserves CSS custom properties, and leaves null and undefined style values for `spreadProps` to handle. (zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/normalize-props.test.ts: "passes style object through untouched"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/normalize-props.test.ts: "preserves CSS custom properties"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/normalize-props.test.ts: "leaves null and undefined style values to spreadProps")
- Given SVG attributes, then `viewBox` and `preserveAspectRatio` keep their case while other attributes are lowercased. (zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/normalize-props.test.ts: "preserves viewBox case"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/normalize-props.test.ts: "preserves preserveAspectRatio case"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/normalize-props.test.ts: "lowercases other attributes")
- Given mixed values, then `undefined` props are filtered out while `null` and `false` are kept, because null means "remove the attribute" and false is a meaningful boolean. (zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/normalize-props.test.ts: "filters out undefined values"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/normalize-props.test.ts: "keeps null values"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/normalize-props.test.ts: "keeps false boolean values"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/normalize-props.test.ts: "handles complex prop object")
- Solid's `mergeProps` handles a single argument, combines event handlers, concatenates CSS classes, concatenates and dedupes `data-ownedby` tokens, merges style objects, accepts function sources (Solid getters), lets the last value overwrite event listeners when asked, composes with Solid's own `mergeProps`, and merges a function source with a plain override object. ### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Every adapter asserts the same baseline: the machine reports its initial state, runs root and state entry actions once on mount, exposes state plus context, transitions on `send`, exposes state tags, handles reenter transitions, runs actions in a deterministic order, exposes computed values, fires watchers on context changes, evaluates basic and composed guards, supports controlled context, and runs state effects with cleanup. (zag: packages/frameworks/react/tests/machine.test.ts: "initial state"; zag: packages/frameworks/react/tests/machine.test.ts: "initial entry action"; zag: packages/frameworks/react/tests/machine.test.ts: "current state and context"; zag: packages/frameworks/react/tests/machine.test.ts: "send event"; zag: packages/frameworks/react/tests/machine.test.ts: "state tags"; zag: packages/frameworks/react/tests/machine.test.ts: "reenter transition"; zag: packages/frameworks/react/tests/machine.test.ts: "action order"; zag: packages/frameworks/react/tests/machine.test.ts: "computed"; zag: packages/frameworks/react/tests/machine.test.ts: "watch"; zag: packages/frameworks/react/tests/machine.test.ts: "guard: basic"; zag: packages/frameworks/react/tests/machine.test.ts: "guard: composition"; zag: packages/frameworks/react/tests/machine.test.ts: "context: controlled"; zag: packages/frameworks/react/tests/machine.test.ts: "effects"; zag: packages/frameworks/solid/tests/machine.test.ts: "initial state"; zag: packages/frameworks/vue/tests/machine.test.ts: "initial state"; zag: packages/frameworks/svelte/tests/machine.test.ts: "initial state"; zag: packages/frameworks/preact/tests/machine.test.ts: "initial state"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/machine.test.ts: "initial state")
- The shared "uniform coverage" block asserts: root entry, exit and effect cleanup all run; an internal transition with no target runs its actions without re-entering; guard fallback picks the next passing transition; a reenter transition works without an explicit target; unknown events are no-ops; effect setup and cleanup stay balanced through state churn; a reenter restarts state effects exactly once; the event object has a defined baseline before the first send; multi-action transitions run in declaration order; a transition whose guards all fail performs no transition and no actions; and several sends in one tick are processed deterministically. (zag: packages/frameworks/react/tests/machine.test.ts: "root lifecycle runs entry, exit and effect cleanup"; zag: packages/frameworks/react/tests/machine.test.ts: "internal transition without target runs actions without reentry"; zag: packages/frameworks/react/tests/machine.test.ts: "guard fallback selects the next passing transition"; zag: packages/frameworks/react/tests/machine.test.ts: "reenter transition works without explicit target"; zag: packages/frameworks/react/tests/machine.test.ts: "unknown events are no-ops"; zag: packages/frameworks/react/tests/machine.test.ts: "effect setup and cleanup stay balanced during state churn"; zag: packages/frameworks/react/tests/machine.test.ts: "reenter restarts state effects exactly once per reenter"; zag: packages/frameworks/react/tests/machine.test.ts: "event baseline before first send"; zag: packages/frameworks/react/tests/machine.test.ts: "multi-action transition order is deterministic"; zag: packages/frameworks/react/tests/machine.test.ts: "all guards false results in no transition and no actions"; zag: packages/frameworks/react/tests/machine.test.ts: "rapid sends in same tick are processed deterministically")
- Solid, Svelte, Preact and vanilla additionally assert that events sent after teardown are ignored, which React does not test. - Given a Svelte machine rendered with `svelte/server` in a node environment, then root exit actions do not run during server rendering, so SSR never fires teardown side effects. (zag: packages/frameworks/svelte/tests/ssr.test.ts: "does not run root exit actions during server rendering")

### Notes and edge cases

- The vanilla adapter's `bindable` is the reference implementation of Zag's controlled/uncontrolled value primitive: it initializes from `defaultValue`, prefers `value` over `defaultValue`, updates through `set`, passes the previous value to a functional `set`, handles repeated updates, respects an external controlled `value`, fires `onChange` when toggling back to the initial value, uses the controlled value as `prev` for a functional set, and survives switching between controlled and uncontrolled. (zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/bindable.test.ts: "initializes with defaultValue"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/bindable.test.ts: "initializes with value over defaultValue"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/bindable.test.ts: "updates value with set"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/bindable.test.ts: "set with function receives previous value"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/bindable.test.ts: "multiple updates"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/bindable.test.ts: "respects external value prop"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/bindable.test.ts: "fires onChange when toggling back to initial value"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/bindable.test.ts: "uses controlled value as prev when set is a function"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/bindable.test.ts: "switches between controlled and uncontrolled")
- `bindable`'s `onChange` fires on a real value change, does not fire when the value is unchanged, and fires on an explicit invoke. (zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/bindable.test.ts: "fires on value change"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/bindable.test.ts: "does not fire when value is same"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/bindable.test.ts: "fires on invoke")
- Equality defaults to `Object.is` and can be replaced with a custom `isEqual`, and the hash used for change detection defaults to a string representation and can be replaced with a custom hash. (zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/bindable.test.ts: "uses custom equality function"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/bindable.test.ts: "default equality uses Object.is"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/bindable.test.ts: "returns string representation by default"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/bindable.test.ts: "uses custom hash function")
- `bindable` exposes a `ref` holding the current value that updates on set, `bindable.cleanup` is a no-op, and `bindable.ref` creates a simple ref that works for primitives and objects. (zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/bindable.test.ts: "exposes ref with value"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/bindable.test.ts: "ref updates on set"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/bindable.test.ts: "is a no-op function"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/bindable.test.ts: "creates simple ref with default value"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/bindable.test.ts: "get and set work correctly"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/bindable.test.ts: "works with objects")
- `createRefs` builds a ref bag from an object, supports get and set per key, handles several refs at once, and works with DOM element values. (zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/bindable.test.ts: "creates refs from object"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/bindable.test.ts: "get returns current value"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/bindable.test.ts: "set updates value"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/bindable.test.ts: "handles multiple refs"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/bindable.test.ts: "works with DOM element refs")
- The vanilla `spreadProps` is the only adapter that must implement DOM patching by hand, and its tests define the contract every declarative framework gets for free: it sets attributes (lowercasing names), removes them when the value is null or undefined, and removes attributes absent from the new props. (zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/spread-props.test.ts: "sets attributes on element"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/spread-props.test.ts: "lowercases attribute names"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/spread-props.test.ts: "removes attributes when null"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/spread-props.test.ts: "removes attributes when undefined"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/spread-props.test.ts: "removes old attributes not in new props")
- `spreadProps` adds event handlers, removes the old handler when it changes, removes all handlers through its cleanup function, and supports several event types at once. (zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/spread-props.test.ts: "adds event handlers"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/spread-props.test.ts: "removes old event handlers on update"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/spread-props.test.ts: "cleanup function removes event handlers"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/spread-props.test.ts: "handles multiple event types")
- `spreadProps` writes `value`, `checked` and `selected` as DOM properties rather than attributes, sets `checked: false` as an empty-string property, and clears DOM properties and the class property when they leave the prop set. (zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/spread-props.test.ts: "sets value as property on input"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/spread-props.test.ts: "sets checked as property on checkbox"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/spread-props.test.ts: "checked: false sets the property to empty string"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/spread-props.test.ts: "sets selected as property on option"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/spread-props.test.ts: "clears DOM properties when removed from attrs"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/spread-props.test.ts: "clears class property when removed from attrs")
- `spreadProps` reconciles, touching only changed attributes, sets truthy booleans as attributes and removes falsy ones, and preserves `viewBox` and `preserveAspectRatio` case on SVG elements including SVG children. (zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/spread-props.test.ts: "only updates changed attributes"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/spread-props.test.ts: "sets truthy boolean as attribute"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/spread-props.test.ts: "removes falsy boolean attribute"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/spread-props.test.ts: "preserves viewBox case for SVG elements"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/spread-props.test.ts: "preserves preserveAspectRatio case for SVG elements"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/spread-props.test.ts: "handles SVG child elements")
- `spreadProps` applies a style object as individual inline properties including custom properties, skips null and undefined values, removes properties that disappear, removes all of them when style is dropped, never clobbers inline styles set outside of `spreadProps`, scopes the properties it applied per machine id, and falls back to setting the whole `style` attribute when style is a raw string. (zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/spread-props.test.ts: "applies style object as individual properties"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/spread-props.test.ts: "applies css custom properties"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/spread-props.test.ts: "skips null and undefined values"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/spread-props.test.ts: "removes properties that are no longer present"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/spread-props.test.ts: "removes all applied properties when style is dropped from attrs"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/spread-props.test.ts: "does not clobber inline styles set outside of spreadProps"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/spread-props.test.ts: "scopes applied properties per machineId"; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/spread-props.test.ts: "sets the whole attribute when style is a raw string")

## Test infrastructure notes

### Playwright setup

- The e2e suite lives in one top-level `e2e/` directory, `testDir: "./e2e"` with `testMatch: "*.e2e.ts"`, output in `e2e/results`, the HTML report in `e2e/report` and a JUnit file at `e2e/junit.xml` on CI. (zag: playwright.config.ts)
- Timeouts are 30s per test with a 10s `expect` timeout; retries are 2 on CI and 1 locally; workers are 1 on CI and 50 percent of cores locally; `fullyParallel` is on locally and off on CI; `forbidOnly` is on for CI. (zag: playwright.config.ts)
- Failure artifacts are configured for debuggability rather than speed: `trace: "retain-on-failure"`, `screenshot: "only-on-failure"`, `video: "retain-on-failure"`. (zag: playwright.config.ts)
- The browser context is pinned to `locale: "en-US"` and `timezoneId: "UTC"`, which is what makes the date-picker, date-input and number-input formatting assertions stable; locale-specific cases then opt in through the example's controls panel. (zag: playwright.config.ts)
- The reporter is `github` plus `junit` on CI and `list` locally, with the HTML reporter always on but never auto-opened. (zag: playwright.config.ts)

### One e2e suite, five framework example apps

- `playwright.config.ts` maps a `FRAMEWORK` environment variable to one of five example apps and ports: react to `examples/next-ts` on 3000, vue to `examples/nuxt-ts` on 3001, solid to `examples/solid-ts` on 3002, svelte to `examples/svelte-ts` on 3003 and preact to `examples/preact-ts` on 3004; an unknown value throws with the list of valid ones. (zag: playwright.config.ts)
- `getWebServer()` returns a Playwright `webServer` entry that runs `pnpm dev` in that example's directory with the resolved `PORT`, sets `baseURL` to the same URL, and reuses an already-running server unless on CI. (zag: playwright.config.ts)
- Root scripts expose one command per framework (`e2e-react`, `e2e-vue`, `e2e-solid`, `e2e-svelte`, `e2e-preact`), each just setting `FRAMEWORK` before `playwright test`, plus `pw-test`, `pw-test-debug` and `pw-test-ui` that default to react. (zag: package.json)
- Because every spec navigates to route paths only (`/menu/basic`, `/date-picker/range`, and so on), the identical spec files run unchanged against all five frameworks: the example apps are responsible for exposing the same routes and the same testids. This is the core mechanism a multi-framework conformance suite needs. (zag: playwright.config.ts; zag: e2e/menu.e2e.ts)
- A handful of specs branch on the framework at runtime rather than skipping, for example the toast-versus-dialog case that returns early unless `process.env.FRAMEWORK === "react"`. (zag: e2e/toast.e2e.ts: "interacting with toast does not close dialog")
- `examples-smoke.e2e.ts` iterates `exampleRoutes` exported from the shared package and, for every route, asserts the response is ok, waits for network idle, and asserts that no `pageerror` was emitted, so every example page in every framework is at least proven to mount without a runtime error. (zag: e2e/examples-smoke.e2e.ts: "${route.path} loads without runtime errors")

### The page-object model pattern

- Every component has a model class in `e2e/models/<name>.model.ts` extending a shared `Model` base, and specs interact only through the model: a spec's body reads as `await I.clickTrigger(); await I.seeDropdown()`, never as raw locators. This is what keeps the same spec readable across five frameworks. (zag: e2e/models/model.ts; zag: e2e/menu.e2e.ts)
- Models name methods in two families: imperative `click*`, `press*`, `hover*`, `type*`, `focus*`, `drag*` for actions, and assertion-shaped `see*` / `dontSee*` for expectations. Assertions live inside the model, so the vocabulary of what a component can be observed to do is the model's public surface.
- Locators are almost always built from the anatomy contract rather than test ids: `[data-scope=<machine>][data-part=<part>]`, often refined by `data-value`, `data-index`, `data-type`, `data-channel`, `data-axis`, `data-stage` or `data-view`. Testids appear only where an example needs to expose something the anatomy does not (hidden inputs, output panels, submit counters). (zag: e2e/models/select.model.ts; zag: e2e/models/date-picker.model.ts)
- Several models encode timing knowledge that the machine defines, for example the number-input model's `waitForTick(n)` computing `50ms * n + 300ms` from the machine's spin interval and delay, and the tooltip model's `hoverTrigger` waiting 1000ms for the open delay by default. (zag: e2e/models/number-input.model.ts; zag: e2e/models/tooltip.model.ts)

### The shared Model base class

- `Model` is constructed with a Playwright `Page` and immediately subscribes to `console` and `pageerror`, recording every message so that tests can assert on logs. (zag: e2e/models/model.ts)
- `controls` returns the example app's controls-panel driver with `num(id, value)`, `bool(id, value = true)`, `select(id, value)` and `date(id, value)`, each addressing a control by testid; `num` selects the existing text, presses Backspace, fills and presses Enter, so it works with controlled number inputs. (zag: e2e/models/model.ts; zag: e2e/_utils.ts)
- `clickViz()` clicks the "Visualizer" link, `clickControls()` opens the controls panel, `clickOutside()` force-clicks `body`. (zag: e2e/models/model.ts)
- `checkAccessibility(selector?)` runs axe through `@axe-core/playwright`, scoped by default to `[data-part=root]`, always disabling the `color-contrast` rule plus any extra rules passed in, and asserting `results.violations` is empty. (zag: e2e/models/model.ts; zag: e2e/_utils.ts)
- `pressKey(key, times = 1)` repeats a key press n times; `pressKeyDown` and `pressKeyUp` hold and release arrow keys; `type(value)` types through the keyboard; `rightClick(selector)` clicks with the right button.
- Caret helpers: `seeCaretAt(position)` reads `selectionStart` from the active element, `moveCaretTo(start)` calls `setSelectionRange`, `selectPartialText(text)` selects a substring inside the focused input, and `seeSelectedText(text)` retries an assertion on the current selection.
- Pointer and viewport helpers: `moveCursorTo(point)`, `mouseup()`, `resizeWindow(size)`, `attachFile(selector, path)`, `wait(time)`.
- Content helpers: `click(text)` clicks by text, `clickButton(name, options)` clicks a button by accessible name with optional modifiers, `seeTextValue(selector, value)`, `see(text, context?)` and `dontSee(text, context?)` scope a text assertion to an optional container.
- Console helpers: `seeInConsole(text, timeout = 5000)` polls the recorded messages for a substring, `dontSeeInConsole(text, timeout = 500)` asserts the opposite, and `clearConsoleMessages()` resets the buffer. These are what let e2e tests assert framework-level regressions such as "Maximum update depth exceeded". (zag: e2e/models/model.ts; zag: e2e/floating-panel.e2e.ts: "should not report maximum update depth errors when resizing controlled page")

### The shared e2e helpers (e2e/_utils.ts)

- `part(name)` and `testid(name)` build escaped attribute selectors, escaping regex-significant characters so part names like `item-group` work.
- `a11y(page, selector = "[data-part=root]", disableRules = [])` waits for the selector, runs AxeBuilder scoped to it with color-contrast disabled, and asserts no violations.
- `controls(page)` is the controls-panel driver described above.
- `rect(locator)` returns the bounding box augmented with `midX`, `midY`, `maxX` and `maxY`, which every drag, swipe and geometry assertion is built on.
- `approximatelyEqual(a, b, tolerance = 1)` and `isInViewport(viewport, el)` support tolerance-based and containment assertions; `isInViewport` compares an element's box against a scroll container's box and is how scroll-into-view is verified for menu, combobox and select.
- `repeat(count, fn)` sequences an async action n times; `retry(fn, { maxAttempts = 3, delay = 100, backoffMultiplier = 1.5 })` retries with exponential backoff.
- `paste(node, value)` dispatches a synthetic `ClipboardEvent` carrying a DataTransfer, and `nativeInput(node, value)` sets the value through the native `HTMLInputElement`/`HTMLTextAreaElement` value setter and dispatches an `insertFromPaste` InputEvent, which is how paste is simulated where the real clipboard is unavailable.
- `pointer` exposes `down`, `up` and `move` built on `dispatchEvent` with `pointerType: "mouse"`, used where a real mouse gesture would be flaky.
- `textSelection(page)` returns `window.getSelection().toString()`.
- Three swipe implementations exist for three different quirks: `mouseSwipe` drives real mouse move, down, move (with step count derived from duration) and optional release; `touchSwipe` constructs real `Touch` and `TouchEvent` objects in-page and advances by `requestAnimationFrame`; `touchPointerSwipe` dispatches `PointerEvent`s with `pointerType: "touch"` and a pressure value. Both in-page variants tag the target element with a temporary random attribute so the page-side code can re-select it.
- `moveCaret(input, start, end)` and `getCaret(input)` read and write selection ranges through the element, throwing when the target is not an input or textarea.

### Unit test tooling

- Zag's root `vite.config.ts` enables only `globals: true`, so most utility packages run in the default node environment; packages that need a DOM set their own config. (zag: vite.config.ts)
- The React adapter's package config adds `@vitejs/plugin-react`, `environment: "jsdom"`, `css: false`, a setup file, and `retry: 2` - the only place in the repo where unit tests are allowed to retry. (zag: packages/frameworks/react/vite.config.ts)
- The Svelte adapter's config adds the Svelte plugin, `environment: "jsdom"` and `resolve.conditions: ["browser"]`; its SSR test opts out per-file with a `// @vitest-environment node` pragma and renders through `svelte/server`. (zag: packages/frameworks/svelte/vite.config.ts; zag: packages/frameworks/svelte/tests/ssr.test.ts)
- Machine-level unit tests are pure function tests over utils modules (`date-picker.utils`, `image-cropper` crop and transform, `pagination.utils`, `splitter.utils`, `marquee.utils`, `number-input/cursor`, `file-upload.utils`, `drawer.stack`, `date-input` placeholders and formatting), deliberately avoiding the DOM; behavior that needs a browser is pushed to the Playwright suite instead. (zag: packages/machines/date-picker/tests/date-picker.utils.test.ts; zag: packages/machines/number-input/tests/cursor.test.ts)
- Ark runs Vitest per framework package through each package's `vite.config.mts`: react and vue use `environment: "happy-dom"`, solid uses `jsdom`, each with a `src/setup-test.ts` that imports `@testing-library/jest-dom/vitest` and `vitest-axe/extend-expect`, and v8 coverage. `resolve.conditions: ["source"]` makes tests run against source rather than build output. (ark: packages/react/vite.config.mts; ark: packages/react/src/setup-test.ts; ark: packages/solid/vite.config.mts)
- Ark's root `test` script runs each package's `test:ci` sequentially across react, solid, svelte and vue, so the same component suite is executed once per framework. (ark: package.json)
- Ark tests use each framework's own testing-library binding (`@testing-library/react`, `@solidjs/testing-library`, `@testing-library/vue`, `@testing-library/svelte`) with a shared `@testing-library/user-event`, which is why the same assertion is spelled `render(<C />)`, `render(() => <C />)`, `render(C, { props })` and `render(C)` respectively. (ark: packages/react/src/components/dialog/tests/dialog.test.tsx; ark: packages/vue/src/components/dialog/tests/dialog.test.ts)

### How the adapters are tested for parity

- Each framework package under `packages/frameworks/*` carries the same two core suites, `machine.test.ts` and `nested-states.test.ts`, with a shared "uniform coverage" block whose test names are identical across react, preact, solid, vue, svelte and vanilla; parity is therefore enforced by name-for-name duplication rather than by a shared runner. (zag: packages/frameworks/react/tests/machine.test.ts; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/machine.test.ts)
- Each package has its own `tests/render.ts` (or a Svelte harness component) that adapts `renderMachine` to that framework's rendering API, so the test bodies stay nearly identical while the mounting differs. (zag: packages/frameworks/react/tests/render.ts; zag: packages/frameworks/svelte/tests/ssr.test.ts)
- Framework-specific concerns get their own files instead of being forced into the shared suite: React has `strict-mode.test.tsx`, `stable-apis.test.ts` and `replaces.test.tsx`; Solid and Svelte have `merge-props.test.ts`; Svelte has `ssr.test.ts`; vanilla has `normalize-props.test.ts`, `spread-props.test.ts` and `bindable.test.ts`. (zag: packages/frameworks/react/tests/strict-mode.test.tsx; zag: packages/frameworks/svelte/tests/merge-props.test.ts; zag: packages/frameworks/vanilla/tests/spread-props.test.ts)
- Vue and Svelte carry visibly thinner coverage than React and Solid (three nested-state cases instead of seven, no dedicated replace or stable-API suites), and several Ark Vue component cases are skipped outright, so parity in this codebase is aspirational in places rather than complete. (zag: packages/frameworks/vue/tests/nested-states.test.ts; ark: packages/vue/src/components/menu/tests/menu.test.ts)
- On the Ark side, parity is pursued by giving each framework the same test names over a per-framework fixture file (`basic.tsx`, `*.test.vue`, `*.test.svelte`), with Vue and Svelte splitting the fixture into a component file plus a `.test.ts` that mounts it. Differences that survive - `useForwardPropsEmits` and `v-model` in Vue, `splitProps` and accessor props in Solid, runes and attachments in Svelte - are exactly the adapter seams a new library has to decide about. (ark: packages/vue/src/components/checkbox/tests/checkbox.test.vue; ark: packages/solid/src/components/menu/tests/menu.test.tsx; ark: packages/svelte/src/lib/components/field/tests/field-item.test.ts)

### Page-object models, method by method

### e2e/models/switch.model.ts
- `goto(url = "/switch/basic")` - navigates to the switch example route.
- `root` / `label` / `control` / `input` - locators for `[data-scope='switch'][data-part='...']` and the input nested inside root.
- `checkAccessibility()` - runs axe over the default root part selector.
- `clickCheckbox()` - clicks the root part.
- `clickLabel(times = 1)` - force-clicks the label part n times.
- `focusCheckbox()` - calls `.focus()` on the hidden input directly.
- `seeCheckboxIsChecked()` - asserts the input is checked.
- `seeCheckboxIsFocused()` - asserts the input has focus and the control has `data-focus=""`.
- `seeCheckboxIsNotFocused()` - asserts the input lacks focus and the control lacks `data-focus`.
- `seeCheckboxIsDisabled()` - asserts the input is disabled and the control has `data-disabled=""`.
- `trackBlur()` - exposes a page function and attaches a blur listener to the input that increments a counter.
- `expectBlurCount(count)` - asserts the recorded blur count.

### e2e/models/radio-group.model.ts
- `goto(url = "/radio-group/basic")` - navigates to the radio-group example.
- `root` / `label` - locators for the scoped root and label parts.
- `getRadio(value)` - returns the `radio`, `label`, `input` and `control` locators for one option, resolved by `data-testid` (`radio-<value>`, `label-<value>`, `input-<value>`, `control-<value>`).
- `clickRadio(value)` - clicks that option's item element.
- `clickMain()` - clicks the page `main` element to move focus out of the group.
- `tabToFirstRadio()` - clicks main then presses Tab, the canonical "tab into the group" gesture.
- `seeRadioIsChecked(value)` - asserts `data-state="checked"` on the item, its label and its control.
- `seeRadioIsFocused(value)` - asserts the option's input has focus and its control has `data-focus=""`.
- `seeRadioIsFocusVisible(value)` - asserts `data-focus-visible=""` on the control.
- `seeRadioIsNotFocusVisible(value)` - asserts `data-focus` present but `data-focus-visible` absent.
- `seeRadioIsDisabled(value)` - asserts `data-disabled=""` on the control and a disabled input.
- `seeRadioIsNotFocused(value)` - asserts the option's input lacks focus.
- `seeRadioIsNotFocusable()` / `seeRadioIsFocusable()` - tabs into the group then asserts the "apple" input is or is not focused.
- `seeRootHasLabelledBy()` - reads the label's generated id and asserts root's `aria-labelledby` matches it.

### e2e/models/toggle-group.model.ts
- `__item(item)` - private locator resolving "bold" | "italic" | "underline" to the nth `[data-part=item]`.
- `clickItem(item)` - clicks that item.
- `outsideButton` - private locator for the `button` named "Outside" used as the external tab stop.
- `clickOutsideButton()` - clicks and then focuses the outside button.
- `seeOutsideButtonIsFocused()` - asserts the outside button has focus.
- `seeItemIsFocused(item)` / `seeItemIsNotFocused(item)` - asserts item focus state.
- `__selected(item)` / `__notSelected(item)` - private assertions for `data-state="on"` and `"off"`.
- `seeItemIsSelected(items[])` / `seeItemIsNotSelected(items[])` - asserts the on/off state for a list of items in parallel.

### e2e/models/slider.model.ts
- `goto(url = "/slider/basic")` - navigates to the slider example.
- `getThumb(index = 0)` - locator for `[data-part='thumb'][data-index='<i>']`.
- `control` / `track` / `output` - locators for the control, track and `value-text` parts.
- `focusThumb(index?)` - focuses a thumb directly.
- `seeValueText(value)` - asserts the value-text part's text.
- `getTrackPoint(percent)` - private geometry helper: reads `data-orientation`, measures control and thumb boxes, insets the usable range by half a thumb for "contain" alignment, and maps a 0-1 percentage to a page point, inverting the axis for vertical sliders.
- `mousedownAt(percent)` - moves the mouse to the computed track point and presses.
- `mousemoveTo(percent)` - moves the mouse to another computed track point without releasing.
- `seeThumbIsFocused(index = 0)` - asserts a thumb has focus.

### e2e/models/angle-slider.model.ts
- `goto(url = "/angle-slider/basic")` - navigates to the angle-slider example.
- `thumb` / `control` / `output` - scoped locators for those parts.
- `focusThumb()` - focuses the thumb.
- `getCurrentValue()` - reads the value-text content, defaulting to "0deg".
- `seeValueText(value)` - asserts the value-text content.
- `clickControlAtAngle(angle)` - converts a degree value (0 at top, clockwise) into a point on a circle at 80 percent of the control radius and clicks it.
- `dragThumbFromEdgeToAngle(targetAngle)` - presses at 80 percent width / 20 percent height of the thumb box (deliberately off-center), drags to the computed target angle point and releases, to prove the grab offset is preserved.

### e2e/models/rating-group.model.ts
- `goto()` - navigates to `/rating-group/basic`.
- `control` / `hiddenInput` / `label` - locators for the control part, the `hidden-input` testid and the label part.
- `getRating(value)` - locator for the nth `[data-part=item]`, one-based.
- `hoverOut()` - hovers the page `main` element to leave the group.
- `clickRating(value)` / `clickLabel()` / `focusRating(value)` - basic interactions.
- `hoverRating(value)` - hovers the item and additionally dispatches a `pointermove` with button 0, because the machine listens for pointermove rather than pointerenter.
- `seeRatingIsHighlighted(value)` - asserts `data-highlighted=""`.
- `seeRatingIsDisabled(value)` - asserts `data-disabled=""`.
- `seeRatingIsFocusable(value)` - asserts `tabindex="0"`.
- `seeControlIsDisabled()` - asserts `data-disabled=""` on the control.
- `seeRatingIsFocused(value)` - asserts item focus.
- `seeInputHasValue(value)` - asserts the hidden input's value.
- `seeAllRatingsAreDisabled()` / `seeAllRatingsAreReadonly()` - evaluates across all items and asserts every one has `dataset.disabled === ""` or `dataset.readonly === ""`.

### e2e/models/clipboard.model.ts
- `goto()` - navigates to `/clipboard/basic`.
- `checkAccessibility(selector?)` - axe over the given selector.
- `getTrigger()` - locator for the trigger part.
- `getContent(text)` - locator for text inside the indicator part.
- `focusTrigger()` / `clickTrigger()` - interactions on the trigger.
- `seeTriggerIsFocused()` - asserts trigger focus.
- `seeContent(text)` / `dontSeeContent(text)` - asserts the indicator text is or is not hidden, using `isHidden()` rather than visibility so the swapped indicator variant is checked.

### e2e/models/number-input.model.ts
- `goto()` - navigates to `/number-input/basic`.
- `input` / `incButton` / `decButton` / `scrubber` - private locators resolved by testid (`input`, `inc-button`, `dec-button`, `scrubber`).
- `type(value, options?)` - focuses the input then either `fill(value)` (atomic set) or `pressSequentially` when a delay option is given; the distinction matters because `fill` bypasses per-key machine handling.
- `typeSequentially(value, options?)` - presses each character in turn without refocusing.
- `seeInputHasValue(value)` - asserts the exact input value.
- `seeInputValueIsApprox(expected, tolerance = 1)` - reads the numeric value and asserts it is within tolerance, used for long-press spinning.
- `seeInputIsInvalid()` - asserts `aria-invalid="true"` on the input.
- `seeInputIsValid()` - evaluates `el.checkValidity()` in the page and asserts true.
- `focusInput()` / `selectInput()` - focuses, or selects all text in, the input.
- `clickInc()` / `clickDec()` - clicks the increment or decrement trigger.
- `scrubBy(x)` - hovers the scrubber, presses, moves horizontally by x in x steps, then releases.
- `waitForTick(n)` - waits `50ms * n + 300ms`, matching the machine's spin interval and initial delay.
- `mousedownInc()` / `mousedownDec()` - hovers the trigger and holds the mouse down without releasing, to start a spin.

### e2e/models/pin-input.model.ts
- `goto(url = "/pin-input/basic")` - navigates to a pin-input example.
- `getInput(index)` - private locator for the testid `input-<index>` (one-based).
- `clearButton` / `allInputs` - locators for the `clear-button` testid and all `[data-part=input]` elements.
- `fillInput(index, value)` - fills one slot.
- `focusInput(index)` / `clickInput(index)` - focuses or clicks one slot.
- `clickClear()` - clicks the clear button.
- `paste(value)` - writes the value to the real clipboard via `navigator.clipboard.writeText` then presses ControlOrMeta+v.
- `fillAll(...values)` - presses each value as a key in sequence, simulating real typing rather than programmatic fills.
- `seeInputIsFocused(index)` / `seeInputIsNotFocused(index)` - focus assertions per slot.
- `seeInputHasValue(index, value)` - asserts one slot's value.
- `seeValues(...values)` - asserts every slot's value in order.
- `seeClearButtonIsFocused()` - asserts focus is on the clear button, used for roving-tabindex tests.
- `seeInputHasAttribute(index, attr, value?)` - asserts an attribute equals a value, or equals the empty string when no value is given.
- `dontSeeInputHasAttribute(index, attr)` - asserts the attribute is absent.
- `seeTabbableCount(expected)` - counts inputs with `tabindex="0"` and asserts the total, proving only one slot is tabbable.
- `clickButton(testId)` - clicks any button by testid, used for the controlled example's set and reset buttons.

### e2e/models/editable.model.ts
- `goto()` - navigates to `/editable/basic`.
- `preview` / `input` / `submitTrigger` / `editTrigger` / `cancelTrigger` - locators by testid (`preview`, `input`, `save-button`, `edit-button`, `cancel-button`).
- `focusPreview()` - focuses the preview and then waits for `input:focus`, encoding the expectation that focusing the preview hands focus to the input.
- `typeSequentially(value)` - presses keys one at a time into the input.
- `clickEdit()` / `clickSubmit()` / `clickCancel()` - clicks the respective trigger.
- `dblClickPreview()` - double-clicks the preview for dblclick activation mode.
- `seeInput()` / `dontSeeInput()` - visibility assertions on the input.
- `seeInputIsFocused()` - asserts the input has focus.
- `seeInputHasValue(value)` - asserts the input's value.
- `seePreviewHasText(text)` - asserts the committed preview text.

### e2e/models/password-input.model.ts
- `goto(url = "/password-input/basic")` - navigates to the password-input example.
- `input` / `visibilityTrigger` - scoped locators for `[data-scope=password-input]` input and visibility-trigger parts.
- `clickVisibilityTrigger()` - clicks the visibility toggle.
- `canSeePassword()` - asserts the input's `type` attribute is `text`.
- `cantSeePassword()` - asserts the input's `type` attribute is `password`.
- `caretIsAt(start, end = start)` - reads `selectionStart`/`selectionEnd` from the input and asserts both, used to prove the caret survives a type swap.

### e2e/models/tags-input.model.ts
- `goto(url = "/tags-input/basic")` - navigates to a tags-input example.

- `paste(value)` - focuses the input, writes to the real clipboard, then presses ControlOrMeta+V.
- `addTag(value)` - types the value, presses Enter, then asserts the input cleared and kept focus, so the helper itself encodes the post-add contract.
- `editTag(value)` - fills the currently open tag editor, presses Enter and asserts focus returned to the main input.
- `clickControl()` / `clickTag(value)` / `doubleClickTag(value)` - pointer interactions on the control and tags.
- `focusInput()` - focuses the main input.
- `deleteLastTag()` - presses Backspace twice, the highlight-then-delete rhythm.
- `clickOutside()` - force-clicks the body.
- `clickTagClose(value)` / `clickClearTrigger()` - force-clicks the tag delete or clear trigger.
- `seeTagIsHighlighted(value)` - asserts `data-highlighted=""` on the tag.
- `seeTag(value)` / `dontSeeTag(value)` - visibility assertions per tag.
- `seeNoTags()` - asserts zero item elements.
- `seeInputIsFocused()` / `seeInputHasValue(value)` - main input assertions.
- `seeTagInputIsFocused(value)` / `dontSeeTagInput(value)` / `seeTagInputHasValue(value)` - per-tag editor assertions.
- `seeNoHighlightedTag()` - counts `[data-part=item][data-selected]` and asserts zero.
- `seeClearTriggerIsFocused()` - asserts focus on the clear trigger.

### e2e/models/autoresize.model.ts
- `goto(url = "/autoresize/basic")` - navigates with `waitUntil: "networkidle"` and waits for the textarea to be visible, so height measurements are stable.
- `textarea` / `clearButton` / `valueOutput` - the first textarea, the button named /clear/i, and the `value` testid element.
- `focusTextarea()` - clicks the textarea and asserts it took focus.
- `typeInTextarea(value)` - focuses then types via the keyboard.
- `pasteInTextarea(value)` - focuses, writes to the clipboard, then presses ControlOrMeta+v.
- `clear()` - clicks the clear button.
- `getTextareaHeight()` - evaluates `getBoundingClientRect().height`.
- `seeTextareaHasValue(value)` - asserts the textarea value.
- `seeStateValue(value)` - asserts the rendered state output equals `JSON.stringify(value)`.
- `seeTextareaGrew(fromHeight, minDelta = 5)` - polls the height for up to 5s and asserts it exceeded the baseline by more than minDelta.

### e2e/models/file-upload.model.ts
- `goto()` - navigates to `/file-upload/basic`.
- `getDropzone()` / `getTrigger()` / `getHiddenInput()` / `getItem()` / `getDeleteTrigger()` - locators for the dropzone, trigger, `input` testid, first item and first item-delete-trigger parts.
- `focusDropzone()` / `focusTrigger()` / `clickTrigger()` - basic interactions.
- `seeDropzoneIsFocused()` - asserts dropzone focus.
- `seeItem(fileName)` - asserts the first item is visible and contains the file name.
- `seeDeleteTrigger()` - asserts the delete trigger is visible.
- `seeTriggerIsDisabled()` / `seeHiddenInputIsDisabled()` - disabled assertions.
- `openFilePicker()` - starts waiting for the `filechooser` event, clicks the trigger, and returns the chooser.
- `openFilePickerWithKeyboard()` - same but focuses the trigger and presses Enter.
- `waitForNextFrame()` - awaits one `requestAnimationFrame` inside the page, used to prove no second picker opened.
- `trackFileChooserEvents()` - registers a `filechooser` listener and returns a live counter object.
- `uploadFile(path)` - opens the picker and sets files on it.
- `uploadFileViaDropzone(path)` - clicks the dropzone to open the picker, then sets files.
- `uploadFileViaDragAndDrop(path)` - primes the hidden input with `setInputFiles`, then in-page builds a DataTransfer from `input.files` and dispatches `dragover` and `drop` on the dropzone, finally waiting for the item to appear.
- `seeFileDetails(fileName, fileSize?)` - asserts the item contains the name and optionally the formatted size.
- `deleteFile()` - clicks the first delete trigger.
- `seeNoFiles()` - asserts the first item is not visible.

### e2e/models/accordion.model.ts
- `constructor(page)` - extends the shared `Model` base with the Playwright page, inheriting console-message capture and the generic key/click helpers.
- `goto()` - navigates to `/accordion/basic`.
- `checkAccessibility(selector?)` - runs the axe helper over `selector`, defaulting to `[data-part=root]`, with the color-contrast rule disabled, and asserts zero violations.
- `getTrigger(id)` - locator for `[data-testid=<id>:trigger]`.
- `getContent(id)` - locator for `[data-testid=<id>:content]`.

- `seeTriggerIsFocused(id)` - asserts that item's trigger is the focused element.
- `seeContent(id)` - asserts that item's content is visible.
- `dontSeeContent(id)` - asserts that item's content is not visible.

### e2e/models/dialog.model.ts
- `constructor(page, id)` - extends `Model`; the `id` selects which dialog instance in the nested story this model drives, by suffixing every test id.
- `checkAccessibility()` - runs axe over `[role=dialog]` with the color-contrast rule disabled and asserts zero violations.
- `goto(url = "/dialog/nested")` - navigates to the nested dialog story by default, or any other dialog story URL.
- `trigger` (private getter) - locator for `[data-testid='trigger-<id>']`.
- `content` (private getter) - locator for `[data-testid='positioner-<id>']`, so content visibility is asserted through the positioner element.
- `closeTrigger` (private getter) - locator for `[data-testid='close-<id>']`.
- `clickTrigger(opts)` - clicks the trigger, optionally with a click `delay` in ms (used as 17ms to let a parent dialog settle before opening a child).
- `clickClose()` - clicks the close trigger.
- `seeCloseIsFocused()` - asserts the close trigger is the focused element.
- `seeContent()` - asserts the positioner is visible.
- `dontSeeContent()` - asserts the positioner is not visible.
- `seeTriggerIsFocused()` - asserts the trigger is the focused element, used for focus-restore assertions.

### e2e/models/drawer.model.ts
- `constructor(page)` - extends `Model`; all locators are part-based (`[data-part=...]`) rather than test-id based, so one model works across every drawer story.
- `checkAccessibility()` - runs axe over `[data-part=content]` with the color-contrast and `scrollable-region-focusable` rules disabled and asserts zero violations.
- `goto(url = "/drawer/basic")` - navigates to the basic drawer story by default, or to `/drawer/draggable-false`, `/drawer/snap-points`, `/drawer/swipe-area`, `/drawer/indent-effect` and so on.
- `trigger` (private getter) - locator for `[data-part=trigger]`.
- `content` (private getter) - locator for `[data-part=content]`.
- `backdrop` (private getter) - locator for `[data-part=backdrop]`.
- `grabber` (private getter) - locator for `[data-part=grabber]`.
- `swipeAreaEl` (private getter) - locator for `[data-part=swipe-area]`.
- `noDragArea` (private getter) - locator for `[data-no-drag]`, the story element that opts out of dragging.
- `scrollable` (private getter) - locator for `[data-testid=scrollable]`, the scrollable region inside the content.
- `clickTrigger(opts)` - clicks the trigger, optionally with a click `delay`.
- `clickBackdrop()` - clicks the backdrop element directly.
- `mouseDragGrabber(direction, distance = 100, duration = 500, release = true)` - real mouse drag on the grabber via `mouseSwipe`: moves to the grabber's bounding-box centre, `mouse.down()`, then `mouse.move()` to centre plus or minus `distance` on the y axis in `max(duration / 10, 1)` interpolated steps so Playwright emits that many `mousemove` events, then `mouse.up()` only when `release` is true, leaving the button held down otherwise so a mid-drag state can be inspected.
- `touchDragGrabber(direction, distance = 100, duration = 500)` - synthesized touch drag on the grabber via `touchSwipe`: tags the grabber with a random `data-zag-touch-swipe` attribute to get a stable selector, then inside `page.evaluate` constructs real `Touch` objects (identifier 0, target the grabber, matching clientX/clientY and pageX/pageY) and dispatches a bubbling cancelable `touchstart` at the centre, `max(floor(duration / 16), 1)` `touchmove` events interpolated linearly toward the end point with one `requestAnimationFrame` await between each, and a final `touchend` whose `touches`/`targetTouches` lists are empty while `changedTouches` holds the last point. Never releases early; there is no `release` parameter.
- `touchPointerDragGrabber(direction, distance = 100, duration = 500)` - synthesized pointer-event drag on the grabber via `touchPointerSwipe`: tags it with `data-zag-touch-pointer-swipe`, then dispatches `PointerEvent`s with `pointerId: 1`, `pointerType: "touch"`, `isPrimary: true`, `button: 0`, `composed: true` - a `pointerdown` with `buttons: 1` and `pressure: 0.5` at the centre, `max(floor(duration / 16), 1)` interpolated `pointermove` events one per animation frame, then a `pointerup` with `buttons: 0` and `pressure: 0` at the end point.
- `dragContent(direction, distance = 100, duration = 500, release = true)` - the same real-mouse `mouseSwipe` gesture but anchored on the content's bounding-box centre instead of the grabber.
- `selectTitleText()` - inside the content, walks the DOM with a `TreeWalker` filtered to non-blank text nodes, takes the first one, and installs a `Range` over its contents as the window selection; throws if no selectable text node or no selection object exists.
- `getSelectedText()` - returns `window.getSelection()?.toString()` or an empty string.
- `hasSelectionInContent()` - returns true only when a non-collapsed selection exists and its range's `commonAncestorContainer` is contained by the content element.
- `dragNoDragArea(direction, distance = 100, duration = 500, release = true)` - the real-mouse `mouseSwipe` gesture anchored on the `[data-no-drag]` element.
- `swipeArea(direction, distance = 100, duration = 500, release = true)` - swipes the swipe-area part; when `release` is false it uses the real-mouse `mouseSwipe` so the button stays held, and when `release` is true it uses the synthesized `touchSwipe` gesture instead, because the swipe area's pointerdown handler explicitly ignores `pointerType === "touch"` and its touch path is what the opening gesture exercises.
- `seeContent()` - asserts the content part is visible.
- `dontSeeContent()` - asserts the content part is not visible.
- `seeBackdrop()` - asserts the backdrop is visible.
- `dontSeeBackdrop()` - asserts the backdrop is not visible.
- `seeTriggerIsFocused()` - asserts the trigger is the focused element.
- `seeContentIsFocused()` - asserts the content element itself is focused (it is `tabindex="-1"`).
- `getContentVisibleHeight()` - returns `0` when the content is not visible, otherwise `content.clientHeight` minus the parsed numeric value of the computed `--drawer-translate` custom property, treating an unparsable value as `0`; this is the canonical measure of how much of the drawer is on screen.
- `getContentFullHeight()` - returns `content.clientHeight`, or `0` when the content is not visible.
- `scrollContent(distance)` - adds `distance` to the scrollable region's `scrollTop` via `evaluate`, bypassing wheel events.
- `isScrollableAtTop()` - returns whether the scrollable region's `scrollTop` is exactly `0`.
- `clickOutside()` - overrides the base helper to click the `body` with `force: true` at position (5, 5), so the click lands outside the drawer even when an overlay covers the centre of the page.
- `waitForOpenState()` - asserts the content is visible and then awaits `Promise.allSettled` over every animation returned by `content.getAnimations()`, so the enter animation is finished before measurements.
- `waitForClosedState()` - asserts the content has `data-state="closed"`.
- `waitForSnapComplete()` - awaits `Promise.allSettled` over the content's current animations without re-asserting visibility, used after a drag to let the snap transition settle.
- `waitForVisibleHeightNear(targetHeight, tolerance = 4, timeout = 2000)` - polls `getContentVisibleHeight()` until its absolute difference from `targetHeight` is at most `tolerance`, failing after `timeout` ms.

### e2e/models/popover.model.ts
- `goto()` - navigates to `/popover/basic`.

### e2e/models/tooltip.model.ts
- `checkAccessibility()` - runs axe over `main` rather than the root part, since a tooltip has no single root.

- `getTrigger(id)` / `getContent(id)` - private locators built from `<id>-trigger` and `<id>-tooltip` testids, so several tooltips can be addressed.
- `wait(ms)` - raw `page.waitForTimeout`.
- `hoverTrigger(id, { wait = true })` - hovers a trigger and by default waits 1000ms for the open delay; passing `wait: false` proves the immediate-switch path between tooltips.

- `seeContent(id)` / `dontSeeContent(id)` - visibility assertions per tooltip.
